e: You write pricing rules. About every five minutes MAYA reads your bookings, runs your rules on every night whose bookings changed, and sends the prices that changed to your property system (with Mews, nothing is sent yet). Once a day, just after midnight at your property, it runs them on every night up to 396 nights ahead. Nothing is sent until you say so. The change log shows the latest changes and why each one happened.

A rule is a sentence you fill in: when a night looks like this, change the price by that much.

Here is one from The Harbour Inn, a 20-room property we use in every example: when a night is more than 80% full, raise the price by 10%. On the **Rules** tab that rule is a name ("Busy nights"), a condition (**Sellable occupancy (%)**, **Greater than**, 80), a direction (**Increase the rate**) and an amount (10%). That is the whole rule.

Sellable occupancy is rooms booked divided by rooms you can sell that night. When The Harbour Inn has 17 of its 20 rooms booked for November 14, that night is 85% full, so "Busy nights" fires and Standard goes from $150 to $165. When it has 16 booked, the night is exactly 80% full, which is not more than 80%, so the rule waits.

A rule can watch four things about a night:

| What a rule can watch | On screen | In plain words |
|---|---|---|
| Sellable occupancy | **Sellable occupancy (%)** | how full the night is |
| Booking speed | **Booking speed (recommended)** | how fast the night is booking compared with your own similar past nights |
| Booking window | **Booking window (days to stay)** | how many days away the night is |
| Pickup count | **Pickup count (advanced)** | how many more rooms were booked for the night, or how much room revenue it gained, in the last 1, 3 or 7 days |

A rule can combine up to four of these, one of each kind. All of them have to be true at once for the rule to fire. You build rules by filling in dropdowns, not by writing code. [Build your first rule](@30) walks through it click by click.

**1. You set the rules**

You add a rule on the **Rules** tab. With Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations, setup also adds starter rules built from your own booking history, when there is about 60 days of it. They are added for you and switched on, but while you are in simulation they only show what they would do. Nothing is sent. You can switch any of them off or delete them before you go live. Later, **Get suggestions from my data** can offer more as cards, which you accept or turn down. Each rule has an **On/Off** switch.

**Example: What this looks like on screen**

The **Rules** tab lists every rule in a table: its name, how many times it has fired, its conditions, the room types it applies to, the price change, and its **On/Off** switch. Under the table, **+ Add a rule** opens the builder. Above it, a panel called **How rules behave** plays two short animations.

**2. MAYA runs them**

About every five minutes, MAYA reads your bookings and room types from your property system, refreshes your own rates from it about once an hour, runs every rule on each night whose bookings changed or that a change of yours reaches, and sends the prices that changed. In the first cycles after midnight at your property it runs every rule on every night from tonight to 395 nights ahead, nearest first. Sending only happens once you have gone live, and never to Mews yet. Until then MAYA runs everything and sends nothing.

This all happens on MAYA's side, day and night, whether or not anyone has MAYA open. Nobody needs to be signed in, and the office computer being off or your own internet being down does not stop it. What stops it is MAYA being unable to reach your property system's service (read [Connection lost](@101)), or a subscription that has stopped.

Nothing, most of the time. Each stretch of runs that changed nothing is counted into one quiet line in the **Change Log**, such as "Prices checked 47 times from Sep 24, 10:05 AM to 1:55 PM, nothing needed to change." You only see the runs that changed a price unless you click **Show All Cycles**.

**3. You watch the log**

Every price change is recorded: which room type, which night, from what to what, which rule acted and why. For a booking speed change, a **Show the numbers** button opens the past nights this night was compared with and the counts behind the change.

Each change reads like this: Standard · stay 2026-11-14: $150.00 up to $165.00 (+10%), then a sentence such as "It was 85% full, past the 80% mark you set." The **Calendar** tab shows the result: each night's current price per room type.

MAYA reads only what pricing needs:

- **Bookings**: the stay dates, the room type, the nightly rate, and the date the booking was made. Cancellations are read the same way and taken off the count.
Bookings

- **Room types**, and with Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations how many rooms each has. Mews does not normally report room counts, so on Mews MAYA uses one room count for every room type, which we set with you. [Your room count and what you pay](@60) says why that matters.
Room types

- **Your own rates** for each night, read from your property system about once an hour, so your rate is the starting point a rule works from. This applies to Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations. Mews rates are not read.

- **Property details**: with Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations, the property's name, time zone and currency are read once, at connection. With Mews we set them with you when we connect it.

Property details

One nightly price per room type, and nothing else.

**Cloudbeds:** MAYA writes each room type's base rate. Rate plans set up to follow it move with it by Cloudbeds' own rules. [Cloudbeds](@12) has the details.

**ThinkReservations:** MAYA writes the rate type named Best Available. Name your main rate type Best Available to be sure it is the one written. Only prices that changed go out. A night whose price has not changed since MAYA last sent it is not sent again. On your first live run, every night in the 396-night window that has a price is sent once, including nights your rules left at your own rate. A price of 0 is never sent. For a free night, type 0 in MAYA and set 0 in your property system yourself.

- Reservations. MAYA never creates, changes or cancels a booking. So when a rule raises or cuts tonight's price, guests who have already booked keep the rate they booked at. The new price is for bookings made after it reaches your system.

- Minimum stays, closed-to-arrival, closed-to-departure or close-outs.
- Guests, guest profiles or guest messages.

- Booking.com, Expedia or any other channel directly. Your property system and channel manager carry your base rate to them, as they do today.

**Sellable occupancy** is rooms booked divided by rooms you can sell that night. Only room types you have ticked as rooms count, and rooms you have marked out of service come off first. Twelve Standard rooms, three out of service, eight booked: 89%. [Sellable occupancy](@32) has a slider to try.
Sellable occupancy

**Booking speed** is how many bookings a night received in the past day, week or month, compared with how many your own similar past nights had received by the same point before arrival. MAYA turns that into one of seven levels, from Stalled to Surging, and a rule can fire on any of them. After a booking speed or pickup count rule changes a night, it counts only the bookings made since then, while that change is still on the price, and so does every weaker rule that moves the price the same way. So one burst of bookings brings one raise, not one from every rule. Occupancy and booking window rules are not limited this way. [Booking speed](@34) explains the levels, and [after the rule acts](@34#after-the-rule-acts) explains the counting.
Booking speed

From your own rates, your own rules and your own past bookings. Nothing from outside your property.

- With Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations, the starting price for a night is your own rate, read from your system.
- With Mews, no rates are read, so a Mews night has no starting price until you type one. What a guest paid is never a starting price, on any system. [Mews](@14#where-a-nights-starting-price-comes-from) has the detail.
- A night your system has no rate for is not priced and not sent until it has one. The day card says "No rate in Cloudbeds for this night yet" (or your system's name). Load a rate there, or type a price in MAYA.
- A rule raises or cuts the starting price by a percentage or a fixed amount, and the result stays between that room type's floor and ceiling. [Floors and ceilings](@28) says where they come from.

- MAYA does not read competitor rates, rate shoppers, weather, events or market data. There is no feed to switch on.

**Good to know: How a wedding counts** · With Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations, a wedding of 20 rooms on one booking counts once for booking speed, both now and on the past nights it is compared with. Mews records each room as a booking of its own, so with Mews the same wedding counts as 20 bookings. Occupancy rules and pickup count rules both count all 20 rooms, with every system.

You set the rules, and MAYA runs them against your bookings and your own past years. Each cycle it counts your bookings, compares a night with your own past nights, checks each rule you wrote, and sends the result. That is all it does. Nothing in it adjusts itself over time or builds a picture of your hotel. A rule never changes by itself. The starter rules are added at setup where you can see them, and later suggestions come as cards for you to accept or turn down.

You can check any change by hand. The change log names the rule behind it and says why it acted, and on a booking speed change the **Show the numbers** button opens the past nights it was compared with and the counts behind the change.

There is no forecast of occupancy or demand anywhere in MAYA. Your rules act on what is already on the books: how full a night is now, how many days away it is, how many rooms it gained in the last 1, 3 or 7 days, and how fast it is booking compared with your own similar past nights at the same point. Booking speed describes the pace so far, not where the night will end up.

So a price moves after bookings arrive, not before them. When you know something your bookings cannot show yet, such as a festival or a wedding in town, type a price for those nights. [Hold a price for an event](@68) shows how.

- **You write the rules.** The starter rules from your history are added for you during setup and switched on, but while you are in simulation they only show what they would do. You can switch any of them off or delete them before you go live. A rule that is switched off holds the changes it already made. A deleted rule undoes them.

- **You can type a price** for any room type, for tonight or any night up to 399 days ahead, from the **Calendar** tab. Your typed price becomes the night's new starting point. The changes your rules had already made there are set aside, and any rule that fires after that works from your number. No rule raises a night set to 0, and a 0 is not sent, so set the night to 0 in your property system too.

Floors and ceilings hold every rule

Your rules run over tonight and the next 395 nights. Nights further out keep the rates the old tool last wrote until they enter that window, and then those rates become their starting point. Look over your far-out rates before you switch the old tool off, or load the rates you want.

With Mews, MAYA sends no prices yet, so the two never clash, and the old tool keeps setting the rates guests see.

**Example: What a brand-new hotel can expect**

You open in March with no history. Occupancy and booking window rules work straight away, because they read your bookings and the calendar, not your past. Set your floor and ceiling in the five questions: the floor goes to every room type, and the ceiling to every room type that has not sold above it. Add a Busy nights rule and a Last minute rule. When you are ready, email us and we switch the property live. The **Turn them on for real** button only appears once MAYA has built starter rules from your history, so a brand-new property goes live by email.

Booking speed rules are quiet at first. Once bookings arrive, a night with no similar past nights is read from momentum: how nearby nights are filling now (compared with a year ago, once there is one). Those readings stay between Slower Than Normal and Faster Than Normal. MAYA will not build starter rules until about 60 days of stays are on record. After your first couple of months, click **Get suggestions from my data** on the **Rules** tab and MAYA proposes the starter rules from what it has read so far. Over the first year, each night finds more similar nights to compare with, and booking speed rules can reach every level.

It skips a room type that may not be a room. A limit still at $1.00 or $99,999.99 stops nothing in most currencies (in yen or rupiah, the default ceiling can hold real rates down), and shows in the **Guardrails** column of the **Rate Simulator** tab. Per room, per month, and the price per room drops as the property grows. There is no minimum: 5 rooms is $27.50 a month. Yearly billing saves 10% from 21 rooms up. Prices are in US dollars and exclude tax. Every size gets the same MAYA.

Find the row your room count lands in. Every room in the property pays that row's rate.

| Rooms | Per room, per month | Yearly |
|---|---|---|
| 1 to 20 | $5.50 | 12 times the monthly price, paid once a year |
| 21 to 40 | $5.00 | 10% off |
| 41 to 60 | $4.00 | 10% off |
| 61 to 80 | $3.00 | 10% off |
| 81 to 500 | $2.50 | 10% off |

The whole property bills at one bracket: the one its room count falls into. There is no minimum charge and no other fee. Any adjustment for a room count change shows on your next invoice. Prices exclude tax, and any tax that applies is yours to pay under the Terms. Each property is its own subscription.

20 rooms: $110 a month. 21 rooms: $105 a month, or $1,134 a year with 10% off.

The calculator on the get-maya.com home page uses the same brackets. Both use the room count you type. After you connect, MAYA checks it against the rooms in your system, and how it counts them depends on the system: read [how the bill is worked out](#how-the-bill-is-worked-out-after-you-sign-up).

**Example: Some worked examples** · The Harbour Inn has 20 rooms: 20 times $5.50 is $110 a month, or $1,320 a year paid once. A 21-room property is in the next bracket: 21 times $5.00 is $105 a month, or $1,134 a year with the 10% off. 40 rooms: $200 a month or $2,160 a year. 100 rooms: $250 a month or $2,700 a year. A 3-room B&B pays $16.50 a month.

You may have spotted that 21 rooms costs less than 20. That is on purpose. The bracket is a step: when a property crosses into the next bracket, every one of its rooms moves to the lower rate. There is no blended or "first 20 rooms at one price, the rest at another" arithmetic to work out. One room count, one rate, one number.

You choose at signup, on the **Billing** control of the payment screen, between **Monthly** and **Yearly**.

- **Monthly** bills the bracket price each month, in advance, at the start of each month of service.
Monthly

- **Yearly** is one invoice for twelve months at the per-room rate, less 10% from 21 rooms up. The screen says so beside the button: **save 10%** for 21 rooms and up, and **pay once a year** for 1 to 20 rooms, because the smallest bracket has no yearly discount.

The yearly price is still worked out per room, per month, and then multiplied by twelve. The **Billing** page shows it as one price per year. To switch between monthly and yearly later, open **Update card, receipts & cancellation** on the **Billing** page and change the plan in Stripe's portal. A switch starts a new billing period that day. Moving to yearly charges the full year at once, less a credit for the unused part of your month. [Switching between monthly and yearly](@61#switching-between-monthly-and-yearly) has the detail.
Yearly

**Commitment.** There is no contract term beyond the period you have paid for. A monthly plan can be cancelled any time and ends at the next renewal date. A yearly plan runs to the end of the year you paid for, with no refund for the rest of it. Read [Cancelling, restarting and leaving](@62).

Accounts created directly at maya-rms.com (ThinkReservations, Mews, or Cloudbeds by code) get no trial unless a code grants one. Every property, trial or not, starts in simulation, where MAYA runs your rules and sends nothing, so you can watch before anything reaches your system. Read [Codes and the free trial](@9).

**Do I pay while I am in simulation?** Yes. Your subscription runs from checkout, or from the end of the trial, whether your property is in simulation or live. Going live costs nothing extra, and there is no other fee.

**Careful** · A card is always collected, trial or not. Unless you cancel before the trial ends, it becomes a paid subscription and the card is charged. Cancelling takes effect at the end of the paid period, and there are no refunds for part of a period.

What you pay is not refunded, including for part of a billing period, rooms or features you did not use, a move to a smaller plan, or time when MAYA or your property system was down. Cancelling stops the next renewal, and MAYA keeps working to the end of the period you paid for. Lowering your room count gives a credit against future invoices, never money back. A free trial costs nothing if you cancel before it ends.

The Terms name the exceptions. If we end your subscription for our own reasons, on 30 days' notice, or stop offering MAYA altogether, we refund the unused part of the period you paid for. And where the law gives you a refund, you get it. Read [Terms and legal](@110#fees-cancelling-and-refunds-in-brief), and clauses 3.5, 7.10 and 12.3 of the [Terms of Service](https://www.get-maya.com/terms).

A code is something we give you. It can grant a trial of some number of days, a percentage off (for a set number of months, or for as long as you stay), or a dollar amount off each month (for a set number of months, or for as long as you stay). The payment screen tells you exactly what your code grants the moment you type it, and the price panel re-prices in front of you.

Four things to expect:

- One code per property. A code cannot be used twice on the same property.
- A code's trial replaces the Marketplace trial. The two never stack.
- There is no referral programme. Recommending MAYA to another hotel earns nothing today, and discounts come only from codes we issue.

Each property is its own subscription at its own bracket. Two 15-room properties are two subscriptions at $5.50 a room, not one 30-room property at $5.00. Brackets are never pooled. If your Cloudbeds login covers several properties, one card is taken for the first and offered for each of the others, and you pay for them one at a time. There is no volume discount beyond what a code grants. Read [Paying for a group of properties](@10).

One checkbox: **I agree to the Terms of Service and acknowledge the Privacy Policy**. You see it when you create an account, when you accept an invitation, and once more whenever a new version is in force. MAYA records who ticked it, when, where in the app and from which browser, plus your IP address everywhere except when you create an account directly. The Terms are at get-maya.com/terms and the Privacy Policy at get-maya.com/privacy.

Every agreement in the app goes through the same box. Its text is "I agree to the Terms of Service and acknowledge the Privacy Policy", with the two document names as links. Both open in a new tab, so reading them never loses what you typed into the form. The box starts unticked, and the button under it stays greyed out until you tick it.

The two verbs are deliberate. The Terms of Service are a contract between your business and Modern Hospitality Solutions, so you agree to them. The Privacy Policy is a description of what happens with data, not a bargain, so you acknowledge that you have seen it. The wording is the same in every place the box appears.

| Moment | What you see |
|---|---|
| Creating an account at maya-rms.com/login | The box under the password fields. **Create Account** is greyed out until it is ticked. |
| Creating an account after **Connect App** in Cloudbeds | The same box on the same form. |
| Accepting a team invitation | The box on the "Set your password" page. **Set password & continue** waits for it. |
| A new version of the Terms or Privacy Policy is in force | A screen headed "Before you continue", once, over whatever page you opened. |
| Starting checkout with nothing on file | The same "Before you continue" screen, and checkout carries on by itself once you tick it. |

When a new version of either document is published, every signed-in person is asked once. It never covers the sign-in page or the invitation page, which carry their own box. When you tick and continue, the screen goes away and you are exactly where you were going. Nothing navigates.

Three messages can appear on it:

- **"The terms have been updated. Reload the page to see them."** You left a tab open across a new release, so the wording on your screen is older than the version MAYA would record. Reload the page and the current text and version load.
"The terms have been updated. Reload the page to see them."

- **"We couldn't save that just now. Please try again."** The record could not be written. Try once more. If it keeps failing, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Terms%20screen).
"We couldn't save that just now. Please try again."

- **"Not signed in"** means your session ended before the tick was saved, for example because you signed out in another tab. Press **Sign out** under the button, sign in again, and the screen asks once more.

**Good to know: Why you might be asked twice** · If MAYA cannot check whether your acceptance is on file, it lets you through and asks again later. A property is never locked out of its pricing by this record. So an occasional second ask means the check could not be made at that moment, not that your first tick was lost.
"Not signed in"

When you tick the box, MAYA records:

- Your email and account.
- The version number of the Terms and of the Privacy Policy you saw.
- Where it happened: creating an account, claiming a Cloudbeds property, accepting an invitation, or the "Before you continue" screen.
- The property, where there is one (a Marketplace claim records it against each property you claimed).
- Your browser's identifying string.
- Your IP address, when you claim a Cloudbeds property, accept an invitation or use the "Before you continue" screen (it is not recorded when you create an account at maya-rms.com without coming from the Marketplace).
- The time.

A second click, a retry, or the same tick from another tab writes nothing extra. The Privacy Policy describes the same record in its own words.

Above the pay button on Stripe's checkout page there is a line of text, not a box, because your acceptance is already on file. "Charged for room-count changes" refers to the room count check described on [Your room count and what you pay](@60): if your property system shows more rooms than you pay for and you do not set the count yourself within 7 days of being told, MAYA raises it and the difference lands on your next invoice.

For Mews, the dialog also says, above that line: "MAYA doesn't send rates to Mews yet, so nothing is sent. The hotel only shows as live." That is what happens. **6. Continue to payment**

"Your subscription is on hold. Email us at info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com and we'll get it running again."

Update your card from billing and the subscription restarts where it left off."** The property's subscription is unpaid: the bank's retries ran out, but it is still alive in Stripe, so a new one is not started beside it. "We couldn't start checkout just now. Please try again in a moment."

Cloudbeds Marketplace arrivals get 7 days free at their first signup, card required, nothing charged until the trial ends. Everyone else may need a code. The payment screen tells you, and codes come from us. A code can give free days, a percentage off or a dollar amount off. One code per property, and a code's own trial replaces the Marketplace trial rather than adding to it. A restart gets no free days at all, from the Marketplace or a code.

One way in comes with a trial: clicking **Connect App** in the Cloudbeds Marketplace. The trial is 7 days. The number is a setting on our side and can change, and the payment screen always shows the current one before you add a card. It reads "Try MAYA free for 7 days. Nothing is charged until the trial ends, and you can cancel any time." Its button reads **Set up payment**.

A card is always taken, trial or not. That is what lets the subscription start on its own when the trial ends. Until then the price panel reads "Nothing today" and names the date and amount of your first charge, and the **Billing** page shows "Your trial ends in 5 days" (counting whole days) and a **Trial ends** row. Cancel from the **Billing** page before that date and nothing is charged.

Every trial comes with a property's first signup only: the Marketplace trial and a code's own free days alike. Restarting a cancelled subscription is billed when checkout completes, whatever code you type, as [Cancelling, restarting and leaving](@62#restarting) explains. A code's discount still applies to a restart.

**Good to know: The reminder before the first charge** · The Terms say that we or our payment processor email a reminder before the first charge. MAYA sends no reminder of its own. Any reminder comes from Stripe, and whether and when it arrives depends on Stripe's settings. The date is always on your **Billing** page, and not receiving an email does not stop the charge.

Whether you need a code depends on your property system. The payment screen asks which system you use, and the code field is required or optional to match.

- **Cloudbeds through the Marketplace:** never needs a code at first sign-up. A code you type anyway is checked and honoured. Restarting after a cancellation may ask for one. [Cancelling, restarting and leaving](@62#restarting) explains.
Cloudbeds through the Marketplace

- **Cloudbeds from inside MAYA, ThinkReservations, Mews:** a code may be needed. The field tells you: **Your code** with the helper "MAYA is invite-only for now" means required. **Your code (optional)** with "Got a discount or trial code? Enter it here" means you can leave it blank.
Cloudbeds from inside MAYA, ThinkReservations, Mews

- ****Something else**:** always needs a code, and there is nothing to connect afterwards. [Which systems MAYA works with](@11) lists the three that work.

Codes come from us. If you need one, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Signup%20code) with your property's name and system.
Something else

A code is one of three kinds, and any kind can also carry some free days at the start. The moment a code is accepted, a green line under the field says exactly what it grants, in one of these shapes.

| Kind | What the screen says |
|---|---|
| Free days | "14 days free, then your normal rate. We'll ask for a card now but won't charge it until the trial ends." |
| A percentage off for a set number of months | "20% off for your first 3 months." |
| A percentage off for as long as you stay | "20% off, for as long as you stay." |
| Dollars off each month, for a set number of months | "$25.00 off each of your first 3 months." |
| Dollars off each month, for as long as you stay | "$25.00 off every month, for as long as you stay." |
| A discount with free days in front | "14 days free, then 20% off for your first 3 months." |

When you restart a subscription, the green line leaves the free days out, because a restart gets none. A discount with free days in front reads as the discount alone, for example "20% off for your first 3 months." A code that only gives free days reads "This code's 14 free days don't apply to a restart, so it doesn't change your price."

The price panel re-prices as you type: the list price is struck through, the discounted first invoice stands beside it, and a line says how long it lasts and what follows. [Setting up payment](@8) shows the panel.

A code is 3 to 40 characters: letters, digits and dashes. Capitals do not matter. The field upper-cases as you type. MAYA checks the code a moment after you stop typing ("Checking…" appears), and checks it again if you switch between **Monthly** and **Yearly**, because a limited discount is worth a different number on a yearly invoice.

You can check a code up to 20 times in 10 minutes. After that: "Too many code attempts. Wait a few minutes and try again."

Each message means one thing.

- **"We don't recognize that code"**, followed by a suggestion to check it for typos. The code does not exist as typed. Compare it letter by letter with what you were sent.
"We don't recognize that code"
- **"That code has been turned off."** We have withdrawn it. Email us.
"That code has been turned off."
- **"That code has expired."** Its end date has passed.
"That code has expired."
- **"That code has already been used the maximum number of times."** It had a limit and the limit is reached.
"That code has already been used the maximum number of times."

- **"This property already used that code."** One code, one property, once. This includes restarting a cancelled subscription, because the old code is spent. This one does not show under the field: it appears in a red box above the pay button after you press it.
"This property already used that code."

- **"Your session expired"**, followed by a prompt to sign in again. Your sign-in ran out while the screen was open. Sign in and come back. Nothing you typed on the screen is kept, so type the details again.
"Your session expired"

- **"Couldn't check that code"**, with a suggestion to try again. MAYA could not reach the code check. Wait a moment and type the last character again.

A required field left empty shows no message. The pay button stays greyed out until a code is accepted.

A typed code is always checked, even when the field is optional. A mistyped code stops checkout rather than being ignored, so you never find out on your card statement that a discount did not apply.
"Couldn't check that code"

They never stack. On a Marketplace property, a code that carries free days replaces the 7-day trial with its own number of days. A code that carries a discount and no free days keeps the 7-day trial and discounts the invoices that follow it. On a restart there is no trial to combine with: the code's discount applies and its free days do not. A code cannot be added after checkout. If you have one, type it before you pay, or [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Code%20after%20signup).

On **Yearly** you pay once a year, so MAYA reshapes some discounts to fit that one invoice. What happens depends on the kind of discount.

- **A percentage for fewer than 12 months** is spread over the year. "20% off your first 3 months" is taken as 5% off your first year (20% of 3 months is 5% of 12), and the green line ends "which is the same saving."
A percentage for fewer than 12 months
- **A percentage for 12 months or more, or for as long as you stay,** is not changed.
A percentage for 12 months or more, or for as long as you stay,

- **Dollars off for a set number of months** becomes the whole total, taken once off your first yearly invoice, however many months the code covers. "$25.00 off your first 3 months" is taken as $75.00 off your first invoice. $25.00 off for 24 months is taken as $600.00 off the first invoice only, and the green line says so.
Dollars off for a set number of months

- **Dollars off for as long as you stay** becomes 12 months' worth off every yearly invoice: $25.00 a month is $300.00 off each year. The green line still reads "$25.00 off every month, for as long as you stay."

**Example: The Harbour Inn with a 3-month code**

The Harbour Inn has 20 rooms, so $110 a month. A code for 20% off the first 3 months makes the first three invoices $88 and the fourth $110. On **Yearly** the same code makes the first year $1,254 instead of $1,320, which is the same $66 saving, and the second year $1,320.
Dollars off for as long as you stay

The redemption is recorded when your checkout completes. The **Billing** page does not show which code you used today. Its price hint says "with your code applied" only while a discount from your code is on Stripe's next invoice, so a code that only granted free days, or a discount that has run out, does not show there. [The billing page](@59) explains the numbers. Two properties in a group each need their own redemption. A code with a use limit counts each property once.

When the trial ends, the subscription converts on its own and the card is charged. If the card fails, MAYA keeps working while your bank retries, and stops if the retries run out. [Cards, payments and invoices](@61) covers that path.

A property that never pays keeps its rules and settings. If it came from the Cloudbeds Marketplace, its imported booking history may be deleted after 180 days without anyone using MAYA for it. Reconnecting reads the history again. [Cancelling, restarting and leaving](@62) has what is kept and what is not.

**Not yet** · No trial without the Marketplace or a code, and no trial of any kind on a restart. No code after checkout. No volume or multi-property discount beyond what a code grants. Codes are issued by us, not by a form.

One **Connect App** in Cloudbeds can hand MAYA every property your Cloudbeds login covers. You pay for them one at a time (the screen says **Property 2 of 3**), the same card is offered for each, and each property is its own subscription, with its own billing period, rules and settings. **Not now** parks a property until you are ready, and the **Billing** page is where you pick it up.

**Cloudbeds:** If your Cloudbeds login covers several properties, one click on **Connect App** in the Marketplace connects all of them. You create one MAYA account (or sign in to one you have), and every property attaches to it with you as its Hotel Admin. All of them start in simulation. From maya-rms.com directly it works the other way round: you pay first, then connect one property at a time, and a Cloudbeds login that covers several properties is refused at the connect step, after you have paid. So for a group, start with **Connect App** in the Marketplace, before paying anything.

**ThinkReservations:** There is no group hand-over for ThinkReservations. Each property is connected and paid for on its own, and a ThinkReservations login that covers several properties is refused at the connect step. [Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=ThinkReservations%20group) and we set the rest up with you.

**Mews:** Mews properties are connected by us, one at a time, each with its own payment. [Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Connecting%20Mews) for each one.

After you create your account, the payment screen comes up for the first property, headed with its name and "is connected". Above the heading a small line reads **Property 1 of 3**. You pay, and the same screen returns for the next property, **Property 2 of 3**, and so on. Properties come up oldest first, by when Cloudbeds handed them over.

A property you set aside with **Not now** counts as done for the numbering, so after skipping the first the next reads **Property 2 of 3**, not **Property 1 of 2**.

While the payment screen is up, MAYA reads the booking history of the property on screen. One unpaid import runs at a time, for the property you are looking at, so the next property's history starts loading when you reach it.

Every property in the group bills on one billing account in Stripe, so the card taken for the first is offered again for each of the others. You can pick it from a list rather than typing it again. The Terms line above Stripe's pay button says so: your card "may be charged for room-count changes and offered for your other properties".

Each property is still its own subscription:

- **Its own bracket.** Two 15-room properties are two subscriptions at $5.50 a room, not one 30-room property at $5.00. Brackets are never pooled, and there is no group discount beyond what a code grants.
Its own bracket
- **Its own invoice.** One invoice per property, each on its own renewal date. There is no combined invoice.
Its own invoice
- **Its own billing period.** Each property's payment screen has its own **Monthly** and **Yearly** buttons, so one property can be monthly and another yearly.
Its own billing period
- **Its own trial.** Each Marketplace property gets the 7-day trial at its own checkout.
Its own trial

- **Its own rules, limits, team, settings and simulation state.** Going live on one changes nothing on another.

To switch one property between monthly and yearly later, open that property's **Billing** page and click **Update card, receipts & cancellation**. In a Cloudbeds Marketplace group, the owner's portal lists every property's subscription, so choose the one for that property. If you cannot tell which is which, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Switch%20one%20property). A General Manager or Hotel Admin of only that property gets Stripe's screen for changing that one property's plan. [Switching between monthly and yearly](@61#switching-between-monthly-and-yearly) says what a switch charges.
Its own rules, limits, team, settings and simulation state

**Cloudbeds:** **Different cards: yes, when you pay.** Once you have paid for one property, Stripe's page for the next offers the same card, and you can type a different card there instead. That property is then charged to the card you paid for it with. Both cards are saved on the same billing account. To move one property to a different card after you have paid for it, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Card%20for%20one%20property).

**Different companies: not inside one group.** Every property you pay for through the Cloudbeds Marketplace bills on the same billing account in Stripe, the one that belongs to your MAYA login. That account has one billing email and, if you add them, one billing address and one business tax ID. So each property gets its own invoice, but every invoice is addressed the same way.
Different companies: not inside one group
**Billing a property separately.** From the screens, a Marketplace property goes on a different billing account only when someone else pays for it from their own MAYA login.
Billing a property separately

**Before your group is connected**, the other company can connect its property itself. Someone there clicks **Connect App** in the Cloudbeds Marketplace with a Cloudbeds login that covers only that property, and creates their own MAYA account. Once they pay, it bills on their account with their card. They can invite you from its **Team** page, so it also appears in your **Property** selector.
Before your group is connected

**Once the property is on your MAYA account**, there is no screen to move it. Connecting it again from another login leaves it where it is, and a restart after cancelling uses the same billing account. If you have not paid for it yet, set it aside with **Not now** so nothing is charged. Either way, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Separate%20billing) and tell us who should pay for it.

**ThinkReservations:** Outside the Cloudbeds Marketplace, each property's checkout opens a billing account for that property alone. So each ThinkReservations property can have its own card and billing details. When we set up your group with you, tell us who pays for which property.
Once the property is on your MAYA account

Under the pay button, a link reads **Not now**, followed by "set this property up later". Beside it a small **?** says "You can come back to it from Billing any time." Clicking it skips the property: it leaves the payment queue, its history import pauses where it is, and the next property comes up. Nothing is charged for a property you set aside, and it does not appear in the **Property** selector until it is paid for.

The link is offered only while another property is waiting to be paid for, or one is already set up. Setting aside the last property with nothing live would leave you on a payment screen with nothing to pay for, so on that property the link does not appear. Only a General Manager or Hotel Admin can set a property aside.

If the property cannot be set aside, a message above the pay button says why:
- **"This is the only property left to set up."** The last property cannot be set aside. Pay for it, or leave the page.
"This is the only property left to set up."
- **"This property is already set up."** or **"This property is already paid for."** There is nothing to set aside. Reload the page.
"This property is already set up."
- **"This property isn't waiting on a Marketplace setup."** It did not come from the Marketplace, so there is nothing to park.
"This property isn't waiting on a Marketplace setup."
- **"That property isn't yours."** Sign in with the account that claimed it.
"That property isn't yours."
- **"This needs General Manager access or higher on this property."** Your role on this property is below General Manager. Ask its Hotel Admin or a General Manager to set it aside.
"This needs General Manager access or higher on this property."

- **"That property no longer exists."** Reload the page.

If the request itself does not go through, the same place shows one of these instead:
"That property no longer exists."
- **"Something went wrong on our side. Try again in a moment."** MAYA could not finish the request. Try again in a moment.
"Something went wrong on our side. Try again in a moment."
- **"Couldn't set that aside just now."** The request failed and no reason came back. Try again.
"Couldn't set that aside just now."
- **Your browser's own words**, such as "Failed to fetch" or "Load failed". The connection dropped. Check your internet connection, then try again.
Your browser's own words

Open **Billing** from any property you have set up. At the bottom, a section headed **Properties not set up yet** lists each parked property with "Set aside" and the date, and a **Set up** button. Click it (it reads "Opening…") and the payment screen opens with that property first. If it fails: "Could not pick that property back up." or "Could not reach MAYA. Try again."

Each property has its own **Billing** page, showing only that property's subscription. The whole group bills on the owner's one account in Stripe, and the full billing portal would show every property's subscription and the card. So a General Manager or Hotel Admin of one property who does not also manage every other property on that account gets a narrower screen: **Update card, receipts & cancellation** opens only Stripe's screen for changing that property's plan.

On that screen there is no card, no invoice list and no way to cancel. For those, ask the owner, or [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Group%20billing). If Stripe refuses even the narrow screen, the page says "Billing for a shared group is still being set up. Ask the account owner, or try again later."

The properties do not all stop at once. Each one is charged on its own renewal date, so a failing card fails one property at a time, as each renewal comes round. Each property then follows its own path: "Payment overdue" while the bank retries, with MAYA still working on it, then "Unpaid" and stopped if the retries run out. A property whose renewal has not come yet keeps running as normal.

Only the owner can fix it, because the card belongs to the owner's billing account. The owner adds a working card in the full portal and saves it as the default. Every property already "Unpaid" is then paid on the new card straight away and moved onto it. A subscription can keep the card it was set up with, so for any other property the owner also [emails us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Move%20to%20a%20new%20card) which properties to move onto the new card (or all of them), and we move each one. Read [Moving to another card](@61#moving-to-another-card). A General Manager of only one property cannot reach the card from their **Billing** page, so they ask the owner or [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Group%20card).

Cancelling one property's subscription leaves the others running. For a connected property, the owner cancels it from the full portal on their own **Billing** page. A General Manager of only that property cannot cancel from their screen (the section above explains why), so they ask the owner or [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Cancel%20one%20property). If the property has not been connected yet, the payment screen carries a link **Manage billing or cancel for** that property's name, which opens Stripe straight onto cancelling that one subscription. [Cancelling, restarting and leaving](@62) has the rest.

MAYA connects to one property system per property. Cloudbeds: connect from the Cloudbeds Marketplace or from inside MAYA, and MAYA reads your bookings and sends prices back. ThinkReservations: connect from inside MAYA, and MAYA reads and sends. Mews: we connect it for you, and MAYA reads your bookings and shows prices but sends nothing to Mews yet. Any other system: not yet.

Your property system is where your bookings and your rates live. MAYA reads bookings from it about every five minutes, runs your rules, and (for Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations) sends the prices that changed back to it. This page says which systems work today, what each one can do, and what to expect if yours is not on the list.

|  | Cloudbeds | ThinkReservations | Mews |
|---|---|---|---|
| How you connect | From the Cloudbeds Marketplace, or from inside MAYA | From inside MAYA | We connect it for you |
| Free trial without a code | Yes, for Marketplace arrivals (7 days) | No | No |
| A code may be needed | Only when you create your account at maya-rms.com rather than arriving from the Marketplace | Yes, a code may be needed | Not applicable (we set it up) |
| What MAYA reads | Bookings, room types, rate plans, property name, time zone, currency | Bookings, room types, rate types, property name, time zone, currency | Bookings and room categories |
| What MAYA sends | One nightly price per room type | One nightly price per room type | Nothing yet |
| Which rate is changed | Each room type's base rate | Your Best Available rate type | None |

**Cloudbeds:** Cloudbeds is the complete path. Install MAYA from the Cloudbeds Marketplace with one click, or sign in with your Cloudbeds account from inside MAYA after paying. MAYA reads your bookings, room types, rate plans and property details. Once you go live, it writes one nightly price per room type to that room type's base rate. Read the full [Cloudbeds page](@12).

**ThinkReservations:** ThinkReservations connects from inside MAYA: pick **Think Reservations**, sign in on their site, and you are brought back. MAYA reads bookings, room types, your list of rooms and rate types, and sends nightly prices to your Best Available rate type. It counts each room type's rooms from that list, so occupancy is read per room type. Read the full [ThinkReservations page](@13).

When a property is live, MAYA sends the prices that changed to your property system every cycle, for tonight and the next 395 nights. One number goes to one rate per room type. Your system's own derived rates, channels and booking engine follow from there by its own rules. On Cloudbeds, MAYA also asks Cloudbeds to let it know if the app is uninstalled. MAYA never sends anything else: no bookings, no availability, no minimum stays, no close-outs. Read [what MAYA reads and writes](@15) for the full list.

Until you go live, no price is sent. Every property starts in simulation, where MAYA runs your rules and writes down what it would have sent. Read [simulation mode](@54).

- **About every five minutes**, MAYA reads new and changed bookings from your system, runs your rules on the nights they changed, and (when live) sends the prices that changed. Once a day it runs them on every night up to 396 nights ahead. A very large first read can take a few cycles to finish.
About every five minutes
- **Once a day**, MAYA re-reads the whole booking window, so a booking that was missed in between is picked up within the day.
Once a day
- **Nothing to install.** You sign in on your system's own website (Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations), or we enter your keys (Mews). Nothing runs on your computers.
Nothing to install

- **Your password is never seen by MAYA.** Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations hand MAYA a token that lets it read and write on your behalf. If prices stop updating after you change your password there, a General Manager or Hotel Admin can reconnect from the **PMS** tab.
Your password is never seen by MAYA

- **One connection per property.** MAYA holds one property system per property. There is no screen for a second one.

**Good to know: Nothing to open on your network** · MAYA talks to your system's online service directly, over the internet, the same service its own website uses. There is nothing to install on a front-desk computer and nothing to open or allow on your network.
One connection per property

Booking history works the same way. The bookings MAYA has already read stay with the property, filed under your old system's room types. MAYA reads bookings only from the system it is connected to (and has no history import for Mews yet). It cannot read a system you have left, or a file. So older bookings that live only in a system you no longer use are not read. Read [how much history you need](@1#how-much-history-you-need).

These systems are on the roadmap on get-maya.com: StayNTouch, Little Hotelier, WebRezPro, Opera Cloud, ResNexus and Maestro. No dates are promised for any of them, or for sending prices to Mews.

If you run one of them, join the waitlist on get-maya.com. The waitlist asks only for your email, so also [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Notify%20me%20when%20my%20system%20is%20ready) with the name of your system, and we will tell you when it is ready.

Opera Cloud is on that roadmap. Older Opera versions, Guesty and any other system not named here are not supported today and are not on the roadmap. MAYA cannot read bookings from a spreadsheet or a file. It needs a live connection to one of the three systems above.

**Not yet: Not yet** · Two systems on one property, a system not named above, and a spreadsheet or file import are not possible today. For a second property on a different system, email us and we will set it up as its own property in MAYA.

**Example: What connecting looks like for The Harbour Inn**

The Harbour Inn runs Cloudbeds. Sam, the Hotel Admin, opens the Cloudbeds Marketplace, finds MAYA and clicks **Connect App**. Cloudbeds hands Sam over to MAYA, where Sam creates an account and sets up payment with the free trial. Then Sam picks **Hold My Hand** (the guided setup) or **Let Me Drive** (straight to the dashboard). The history import runs on its own either way.

Install MAYA from the Cloudbeds Marketplace, or sign in with your Cloudbeds account from inside MAYA. MAYA reads your bookings, room types, rate plans and property details, and once you go live it writes one nightly price per room type to that room type's base rate. Plans that follow the base rate move by Cloudbeds' own rules, and packages are left alone. Your bookings, availability and settings in Cloudbeds are never changed.

Both ways end with the history import and a review of what MAYA found. The Marketplace way comes with a free trial (7 days), needs no code, and connects several properties at once ([paying for a group of properties](@10)). From inside MAYA you pay first, a code may be needed, and one property connects at a time.

1. **In Cloudbeds, open the Marketplace, find MAYA and click **Connect App**.** Approve the permissions Cloudbeds lists. They come from MAYA's Marketplace listing.
2. **Create your MAYA account, or switch to **Sign in** if you have one.** The page says "Your Cloudbeds property is connected. Create your account to finish setting it up."
3. **Click **Set up payment**.** Nothing is charged until the trial ends, and you can cancel any time.

**Good to know: The hand-over link lasts 24 hours** · If the page says "That connection link has expired. Reconnect the app from the Cloudbeds Marketplace.", click **Connect App** in Cloudbeds again for a fresh link.

2. **Sign in on Cloudbeds' site and approve, within 15 minutes.** MAYA asks to read bookings, write bookings, read rooms, read and write rates, read property details, and read taxes and fees.
3. **You are back in MAYA.** It names the property from Cloudbeds (adding "(2)" if that name is taken), reads its time zone and currency, and starts the history import.

Your property's name, time zone and currency are read once, at connect. If you change them in Cloudbeds, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Time%20zone%20or%20currency).

Cloudbeds sends availability and restrictions (such as minimum stays) with your room types and nightly rates, and guest names with bookings. MAYA uses none of them and keeps none of them. It never asks for room blocks, allotments or other guest details.

A few Cloudbeds details:

- Bookings count when **Confirmed**, **Checked In**, **Checked Out** or **Confirmation Pending**, even before they are given a room. **Cancelled** and **No Show** come off on the next read.

- The **booking date** is the one Cloudbeds reports. MAYA does not shift it to another time zone.
- A **virtual room type** is read like any other. If it makes your room count too high, you can untick **Counts as a room** for it on the **PMS** tab. Unticking it also stops bookings made on that room type counting towards occupancy and booking speed. If guests book it, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Cloudbeds%20virtual%20room%20type) before you untick it.
- **Blocked rooms** are not read. Record them under **Rooms out of service** on the **PMS** tab.

Once you go live, MAYA sends the prices that changed every cycle, for tonight and the next 395 nights, to each room type's **base rate**. Plans that follow it (derived plans, such as a non-refundable rate at 10% off) move by Cloudbeds' own rules. MAYA never writes to any other plan and never creates one.

**Example: Which of my Cloudbeds rate plans will MAYA change?**

1. **Does the plan follow another plan?** MAYA never writes to it. It follows its parent.
2. **Does it have a public name, like a package or a promotion?** MAYA never writes to it.
3. **Neither?** Then it is the base rate, and MAYA changes it.

At The Harbour Inn, Standard has "Standard Rate" (the base), "Non-refundable" (follows it at 10% off) and "Bed and Breakfast" (a package). MAYA writes to "Standard Rate" only.

A room type with no base rate is priced on the calendar but not sent, and the change log says "MAYA can't find a base rate for Deluxe in Cloudbeds, so its rates can't be changed". Once you add one, the held prices go out on a later cycle. Read [when your property system does not accept a price](@57).

**Careful: MAYA sends the number as it is** · MAYA reads and writes the same rate field. If your base rate includes tax, so do MAYA's prices. MAYA does not add or remove tax.

MAYA never writes bookings, availability, restrictions, minimum stays, close-outs, taxes, room types or settings, and never sends a price of 0 (set a comp night to 0 in Cloudbeds yourself). The "write reservations" permission MAYA asks for when you connect from inside MAYA is never used.

To reconnect, a General Manager or Hotel Admin clicks **Reconnect Cloudbeds** on the **PMS** tab and signs in at Cloudbeds. Rules, history and settings are untouched. Any login that reaches this property works, a group login included, however you first connected. A login that does not reach it stops with "This login is for a different property." before anything changes. MAYA never sees your Cloudbeds password, so after a password change, reconnect only if prices stop updating.

ThinkReservations connects from inside MAYA and receives prices, so a ThinkReservations property gets the full path: the history import, starter rules, the calendar, going live and sending. This page covers how to connect, what MAYA reads, which rate type it writes to, and what works differently from Cloudbeds, including how you connect, how rooms are counted, how a send is checked, and how a disconnect or a reconnect shows up.

There is one way in. You create your MAYA account, pay, and then connect. ThinkReservations has no marketplace listing for MAYA, so there is no free trial without a code, and a code may be needed at checkout. Read [codes and the free trial](@9).

1. **Create your account and pay.** At checkout, choose **Think Reservations** as your system. If the code field is required, enter the code we gave you.
2. **On the screen titled **Connect your property system**, click **Connect →** beside Think Reservations.** The card says **Sign in with your Think Reservations account**. There is nothing to copy and nothing to set up on the ThinkReservations side.

3. **Sign in on ThinkReservations' website and approve.** MAYA asks ThinkReservations for permission to read your bookings, rooms, rates and availability, to write rates, and to stay connected without asking you to sign in again. It does not ask for guest details. Finish within 15 minutes. If it takes longer, you land on a page that says "That sign-in link ran out after 15 minutes. Start again from MAYA." with an **Open MAYA** link. Nothing is wrong and nothing was set up: go back to the connect screen and start again.
4. **You are brought back to MAYA.** MAYA names the property from ThinkReservations, reads its time zone and currency, and starts the history import. If a property with that name already exists on MAYA, a "(2)" is added. You can rename it in the questions step. Read [the history import](@23).

**Good to know: One permission MAYA asks for but does not use** · The list ThinkReservations shows you includes reading availability. MAYA asks for it but makes no availability call today. It never reads how many rooms are free on a night, and it never changes availability. Read [what MAYA reads and writes](@15).

If your ThinkReservations login can reach several hotels, the connect step stops with "This Think Reservations login covers 3 properties. MAYA signs one property up at a time right now" (with your own number) and no **Try again** link. MAYA cannot tell which of them you paid for, and picking one could price the wrong hotel. Reply to your receipt or [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=ThinkReservations%20group) and we set the properties up by hand, each as its own property in MAYA. There is no group flow for ThinkReservations yet.

On every cycle, about every five minutes, MAYA reads from ThinkReservations:

- **Bookings** made or changed since the last read. A booking that holds several rooms arrives with one entry per room. MAYA keeps each room's room type, its nights, and its nightly room charge.
Bookings

- **Room types**, by name, and your **list of rooms**, which MAYA counts room type by room type (see below).

About once an hour, MAYA reads your **rate types** (their names, whether each is standard or follows another, and which room types each covers) and your **own nightly rates** for the next 396 nights from the rate type it sends to. Once a day it re-reads the whole booking window, so a booking missed in between is picked up within the day.

At connect, MAYA reads the property's **name, time zone and currency** once. They are not refreshed afterwards. If you change your time zone or currency in ThinkReservations later, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Time%20zone%20or%20currency) and we change it in MAYA.
Room types

The **booking date** is the moment ThinkReservations recorded the booking, read on your property's own calendar. A booking made at 11 pm at a property in California is dated that day, not the next.

ThinkReservations sends guest details with every booking even though MAYA does not ask for them. MAYA drops them before anything is stored: names, emails, phone numbers, addresses, dietary notes, arrival times and special requests never reach MAYA's database. Read [what MAYA reads and writes](@15).

MAYA keeps a booking when ThinkReservations lists it as **scheduled**, **checked in** or **checked out**. A booking marked **cancelled** or **no show** is removed on the next read, and its nights come off the count. Cancelling changes the booking, so the cancellation arrives in the same five-minute read as everything else.

Nights run from check-in up to, but not including, check-out. A same-day booking is one night. Each room in a booking is one booked room on each of its nights.

For occupancy, each room counts. For booking speed, a booking counts once however many rooms it holds. A 4-room booking for one night is 4 booked rooms and 1 booking. Read [booking speed](@34).

On every cycle MAYA reads ThinkReservations' list of rooms and counts the rooms in each room type, so each room type has its own count. The **Room types** block on the **PMS** tab shows it as units beside each one. A room is left out when ThinkReservations marks it as inactive, as not a room, or as not included in occupancy. A room you do not sell online still counts, because it can still be sold at the desk. A room type with no rooms in the list counts as 0.

If a count looks wrong, check those three settings on the rooms in ThinkReservations. MAYA reads the change on the next cycle. If ThinkReservations cannot send the list of rooms on a cycle, MAYA keeps the counts it already has.

Sellable occupancy divides by these counts, and so does the room count on your bill, over the room types ticked as rooms. Read [your room count and what you pay](@60).

The Harbour Inn has 12 Standard rooms, 6 Deluxe and 2 Suites in ThinkReservations, so MAYA reads 12, 6 and 2, and the property measures 20 rooms for its bill. On Fri, Nov 13 2026, 9 Standard and 5 Deluxe rooms are booked: Standard reads 75% full and Deluxe 83%.

**Rooms out of service** works on top of the counts: 3 Standard rooms out of service for that night leave 9 to sell, so Standard reads 100%.

ThinkReservations marks each rate type as standard or as following another rate type (derived). MAYA sends its prices to your **Best Available** rate type: the standard rate type whose name contains "Best Available". A rate type called "Best Available Non-Refundable" has those words too, and MAYA may write to it instead, so give exactly one standard rate type a name with "Best Available" in it.

If no rate type is called Best Available, MAYA uses the one standard rate type that covers the most room types. That could be a non-refundable or a package rate type, because ThinkReservations marks those standard too. If two standard rate types tie for that, neither is used, and nothing is sent until one of them is named Best Available. A room type the chosen rate type does not cover is not sent to. MAYA never hands a room type's price to a non-refundable or package rate type instead.

Derived rate types reprice themselves from their parent by ThinkReservations' own rules, so writing the Best Available rate is the whole job. A non-refundable rate that follows Best Available at 10% off moves when MAYA moves Best Available. MAYA never writes to a derived rate type and never creates a rate type. A non-refundable or package rate type is written to only when it is the one chosen above, so name your main rate type Best Available.

**Example: Which of my ThinkReservations rate types will MAYA change?**

For your property, ask in this order:

1. **Is there a standard rate type called Best Available?** If yes, that is the one MAYA changes, for every room type it covers.
2. **If not, which standard rate type covers the most room types?** If exactly one does, MAYA changes that one.

At The Harbour Inn, "Best Available" covers Standard, Deluxe and Suite. "Non-Refundable" follows Best Available at 10% off. "Romance Package" is a package. MAYA writes each room type's price to Best Available. Non-Refundable follows on its own. Romance Package is untouched.

If no rate type MAYA can send to covers a room type, that room type is priced on the calendar but not sent, and the change log shows a "Prices not reaching Think Reservations" entry: "MAYA can't find a base rate for Deluxe in Think Reservations, so its rates can't be changed", with the action "Add a base rate for this room type in Think Reservations." Add the room type to your Best Available rate type in ThinkReservations. MAYA re-reads your rate types and sends the held prices on a later cycle. Read [when your property system does not accept a price](@57).

ThinkReservations does not apply a price the instant it receives it. It answers "accepted" and applies the price shortly after, and there is no job for MAYA to ask about afterwards, as there is with Cloudbeds. So MAYA checks by reading. About once an hour it reads your rates from ThinkReservations, and a send counts as landed when that read finds MAYA's price there.

Until a send has been read back, a rate you change in ThinkReservations on that night is not kept as a manual price, because MAYA cannot yet tell your change from a price of its own that has not landed. Once the send has been read back and is at least 60 minutes old, a rate you change there is kept, exactly as on Cloudbeds. Read [rates you change in your property system](@51).

If ThinkReservations accepts a batch and then never applies it, MAYA's calendar shows MAYA's price while ThinkReservations still holds the old one. The next time that night's price changes, MAYA sends it again. Nothing is sent again at the same price on its own. If a night in ThinkReservations still shows the old rate an hour after MAYA's calendar changed, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=ThinkReservations%20rate%20not%20applied) the night and room type and we check it.

**Careful: A price of 0 is never sent** · MAYA does not send a price of 0 to ThinkReservations. A night you set to 0 in MAYA is a comp night that you set to 0 in ThinkReservations yourself. The save says so: "Saved. MAYA doesn't send a price of 0 to Think Reservations, so set the night to 0 there yourself."

If ThinkReservations lets MAYA read but refuses the write, the change log shows "Think Reservations won't let MAYA change Standard rates because MAYA doesn't have permission to update rates", with the action "Give MAYA permission to update rates in Think Reservations, then reconnect on the PMS tab." Reads, pricing and the calendar carry on. The held prices go out on the cycle after you reconnect.

A refused write never disconnects a ThinkReservations property. The connection stays up, and only the sending waits.

ThinkReservations does not tell MAYA when access has been removed. MAYA reads the refusal when its next call fails. A failed read is tried again with a growing wait, up to an hour between tries, and nothing is priced or sent while reads fail. When ThinkReservations refuses to renew MAYA's access, the **Connection** card on the **PMS** tab reads **Error** and the banner "MAYA has lost its connection to Think Reservations" appears for a General Manager or Hotel Admin, with a **Reconnect Think Reservations** button. If it still reads **Error** an hour later, every General Manager and Hotel Admin gets one email saying so. Read [emails MAYA sends](@63#the-connection-down-email). Until the status changes, the tab can still read **Connected** while calls are failing.

To reconnect, click **Reconnect Think Reservations** on the banner or on the **PMS** tab, sign in on ThinkReservations' site with a login that reaches this hotel and no other, and you are back on the dashboard's **PMS** tab with the note "Reconnected." Your rules, history and settings are untouched. Finish signing in within 15 minutes. If it takes longer, you see "That sign-in link ran out after 15 minutes. Start again from MAYA." Nothing has changed: click **Open MAYA** and start again from the **PMS** tab. Syncing resumes within about five minutes, or up to an hour if reads had been failing for a while. Read [reconnecting and disconnecting](@16).

If **Last sync** stops moving after a reconnect, reconnect again with a login that reaches only this hotel. If your only login reaches several hotels (we set those properties up by hand), or you signed in to another hotel by mistake, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=ThinkReservations%20reconnect) and we sort it out.

MAYA has no disconnect button of its own. To remove MAYA's access in ThinkReservations, cancel your subscription first, then [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Disconnect%20ThinkReservations) and we walk you through it.

The **Connection** card and **Last sync** are right for ThinkReservations. The **Recent requests to Think Reservations** list and the **Health (last 24 hours)** card both read "Not tracked for this system", because MAYA keeps a log of its requests to Cloudbeds only. It does not mean syncing has stopped. **Last sync** is the number to look at. Read [the PMS tab](@53).

**Not yet: Not yet** · There is no Marketplace install for ThinkReservations, so no free trial without a code. ThinkReservations does not tell MAYA about a disconnect (MAYA finds the refusal on its next call). A login covering several hotels cannot connect on its own (we set them up by hand). The PMS tab keeps no request log for ThinkReservations.

**Example: The Harbour Inn goes live on ThinkReservations**

The Harbour Inn's Best Available rate for Standard is $150 on Fri, Nov 13 2026. That night is booking faster than similar nights did, so the starter rule "Warm-date bump" raises Standard 10%, from $150 to $165. (It is a booking speed rule, which counts bookings rather than rooms, so it can fire whatever the room count is.) On the next cycle, MAYA sends $165 to Best Available for that night. ThinkReservations answers "accepted" and applies it a moment later. The Non-Refundable rate, which follows Best Available at 10% off, now shows $148.50 in ThinkReservations without MAYA touching it.

There is no history import for Mews yet, so there are no starter rules at connect.
