The screen titled **Connect your property system** lists Mews under **Coming soon** with the label **Not yet available**. You cannot click it. Instead, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Connect%20Mews) after you pay and we connect Mews for you.

Mews connects with keys rather than a sign-in. One key identifies MAYA and we hold it, so you never need to find a client token. The other is an access token for your property, which Mews creates when your property is connected to MAYA. If your Mews account covers more than one enterprise, we also need this property's Enterprise ID.

We arrange a secure way to share keys when we connect you, so never paste them into an ordinary email. We test the keys against Mews, save them, and mark the property as connected. MAYA only ever talks to Mews' own service, and nothing is installed on your computers.

MAYA does not copy your property's name, time zone or currency from Mews, so we set them with you when we connect it. We also set how many rooms MAYA counts for each room category (more on that below). Check both under **Time zone and currency** on the **PMS** tab, and email us if either is wrong. The calendar, the booking window and every "past week" count run on the time zone.

Every property starts in simulation, and for Mews it stays effectively that way, because nothing is sent either way. Read [simulation mode](@54).

A Mews property pays the same as any other property: the same price per room, in the same brackets, monthly or yearly. There is no lower price while nothing is sent to Mews. Read [what it costs](@3).

You pay before we connect Mews, and you pick **Mews** on the payment screen. A code may be needed: the field reads **Your code** when one is required and **Your code (optional)** when it is not.

There is no free trial for Mews. The trial (7 days) comes only with the Cloudbeds Marketplace. So unless a code gives free days, your first charge is when you finish checkout. Read [codes and the free trial](@9).

On every cycle, about every five minutes, MAYA reads from Mews:

- **Bookings** (Mews calls them reservations) made or changed since the last read, with their room category, arrival and departure, and total price.
Bookings

- **Room categories** (Mews' name for room types), by name. MAYA does not read room counts from Mews yet, so it uses one number for all of them (read below).

Once a day, MAYA re-reads the whole window: 30 days back and about 13 months ahead. A booking missed in between is picked up within the day.

The **nightly rate** MAYA stores comes from the booking's total price. MAYA adds up the charges on the booking and splits the total evenly across its nights, so a 3-night stay at $450 is stored as $150 a night, even when its nights were charged at different prices. That total includes taxes, and it can include extras on the booking as well as the room, so it can sit above your room rate.

The **booking date** is the moment Mews recorded the booking as created, read on your property's own calendar.
Room categories

MAYA removes a booking only when Mews marks it **Canceled**. Every other state it reads counts as a booked room: **Confirmed**, **Started**, **Processed**, and also **Optional**, **Enquired** and **Requested**. So an option held for a group, or an enquiry not yet firm, counts towards occupancy and booking speed exactly like a confirmed booking.

If you hold many options that never firm up, occupancy and booking speed read higher than your firm bookings. There is no setting in MAYA for this yet. Cancelling an option in Mews takes it off the count on the next read. Mews records a no-show as a cancelled reservation, so a no-show comes off the count like any cancellation.

A Mews booking is one room, so one booking is one booked room on each of its nights and one booking for booking speed. Nights run from arrival up to, but not including, departure.

MAYA does not read room counts from Mews yet, so it uses one number for every category at your property. We set that number with you when we connect Mews. The **Room types** block on the **PMS** tab shows it as "units" beside each category.

Sellable occupancy is rooms booked divided by rooms you can sell, so this number is the bottom half of every occupancy figure. It is right for a category that has exactly that many rooms and off for every other. A rule that measures several categories adds their numbers together. Booking window rules that also check occupancy depend on it too.

**Example: One number for The Harbour Inn's room categories**

The Harbour Inn has 12 Standard, 6 Deluxe and 2 Suite rooms, and a Meeting Room that is unticked as not a room. On Mews, every category gets the same number, but the Meeting Room adds nothing because it is unticked. With 100, a night with 9 Standard rooms booked reads 9% full for Standard, and "Busy nights" (occupancy Greater than 80) does not fire. With 7, the three room categories add up to 21 rooms, close to the real 20, so a rule that measures all three reads close to the truth. A rule that measures Standard alone then reads 9 booked of 7, which is 129%, and fires on a night that is not full.

A Mews property has no starter rules, so the review has no go-live button. Going live would change nothing in Mews anyway. If you want the property to show as live, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Show%20my%20Mews%20property%20as%20live). Live or not, the calendar and the change log show the price your rules set for every night, which is what would have been sent.

Prices you type are saved and shown on the calendar the same way, and they are not sent either. In simulation the line after a save reads "Saved (simulation: not sent to Mews)." On a property we have set to show as live, it can read "Saved. Sending to Mews now." or "Saved. Sending to Mews on the next cycle (about 5 min)." Nothing is sent to Mews whatever that line says. If you want a price in Mews, set it there yourself.

No date is promised for sending prices to Mews. To hear when that changes, join the waitlist on get-maya.com, or [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Sending%20prices%20to%20Mews) and we will tell you.

MAYA does not read your rate plans from Mews, so it has no "your own rate" for a night. A night's starting price is a price you typed for it, and nothing else: a night nobody has typed a price for is not priced at all, whatever its bookings paid. What a guest paid is never a starting price, on any system. Read [how rules run](@39).

**Example: The Harbour Inn on Mews**

Sam types $150 for Standard on Fri, Nov 13 2026 in MAYA. The calendar shows "Manual · $150.00". "Busy nights" fires on top of it and the night goes to $165; the change log names the rule. Mews still shows whatever rate The Harbour Inn has set there. To sell at $165, Sam sets it in Mews. A Standard night Sam has not typed a price for shows a dash.

Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations properties get a history import at connect, a review of what MAYA found, and starter rules built from that history. Mews does not have that yet. A Mews property's history is what the reads cover: 30 days back at connect, growing by a day each day. If you would like us to read further back once, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Mews%20history) and we can read up to a year back. Read [the history import](@23).

**Get suggestions from my data** on the **Rules** tab reads your history the same way, so on a Mews property it is greyed out, with the note "Not available for Mews yet. MAYA can't read its booking history." Build your rules in the rule builder. Read [build your first rule](@30).

If your Mews keys stop working, MAYA's reads fail. For about the first half hour nothing on screen warns you: the **Connection** card on the **PMS** tab still reads **Connected**, and no banner appears above the calendar. Once Mews has refused MAYA's keys three reads in a row, the card reads **Error** and the panel described below appears. About an hour after that, every General Manager and Hotel Admin gets one email headed "MAYA has lost its connection to Mews", asking you to reply so we can arrange new keys. Read [emails MAYA sends](@63#the-connection-down-email).

Only refusals of the keys count. A read that fails for another reason, such as Mews being down, leaves the card at **Connected**, and a read that works starts the count again. Then the sign to look for is **Last sync** on the **PMS** tab, which stops moving.

[Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Mews%20keys) and we arrange new keys with you and save them. Leave the keys themselves out of the email: we set up a secure way to share them. There is no button for this in MAYA.

When we remove the keys, the **Connection** card reads **Disconnected** and reads stop, and no email is sent. Whenever the card reads **Error** or **Disconnected**, the **PMS** tab and the banner above the calendar show "Mews needs its keys re-entered", with the words "Ask us to re-enter the Mews keys: email [info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com)." Every role sees the same panel, and the address opens an email to us. We arrange new keys with you. Read [reconnecting and disconnecting](@16).

The **Connection** card changes when we save or remove your keys, and to **Error** when Mews refuses MAYA's keys three reads in a row. It can read **Connected** while reads fail for any other reason. The **Recent requests to Mews** list and the **Health (last 24 hours)** card both read "Not tracked for this system", because MAYA keeps a log of its requests to Cloudbeds only. **Last sync** is the number to look at. **Counts as a room** and **Rooms out of service** work the same as on any property. Read [the PMS tab](@53).

**Not yet: Not yet** · For Mews there is no sending (including prices you type), no read of your own rates, no room count per room category (one number is used for all), no warning on screen for about the first half hour after the keys stop working or when reads fail for another reason (watch **Last sync**), no history import and no starter rules at connect, no **Get suggestions from my data**, no go-live, connect or reconnect from the app (email us), and no way to leave options and enquiries out of the count. No date is promised for any of these.

MAYA reads your bookings (nights, room type, nightly rate, booking date), your room types (and, on Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations, how many rooms each has), your rate plans, and your property's name, time zone and currency. It writes only one nightly price per room type to one rate plan (on Cloudbeds, MAYA also asks Cloudbeds to let it know if the app is uninstalled). On Mews it does not copy your rate plans or property details, and it writes nothing. It never stores guest names, emails, phone numbers, addresses or card details.

This page is the full list, for anyone who needs to answer "what exactly does MAYA touch?" before connecting, or who wants to check afterwards. Where the three systems differ, the tabs say how. The short version: MAYA reads the shape of your bookings and your rates, and it writes nightly prices. Everything else in your system is yours alone.

**Cloudbeds:** About every five minutes: bookings made or changed since the last read, with every room in the booking and each room's own nightly rate, and your room types with the number of units in each.

About once an hour: your rate plans, with each room type's own nightly rate for the next 396 nights from its base rate plan.

Once a day: the whole booking window again, and your taxes and fees (Cloudbeds requires the request, but MAYA keeps none of it and uses none of it).

Once, at connect: the property's name, time zone and currency, and which properties your login covers.

Arrives but is never used or kept: availability and restrictions (minimum stays, closed to arrival or departure), which come with your room types and nightly rates, and guest names, which come with bookings.

**ThinkReservations:** About every five minutes: bookings made or changed since the last read, with each room and its room charges, your room types by name, and your list of rooms, which MAYA counts room type by room type. A room marked as inactive, as not a room, or as not included in occupancy is left out.

About once an hour: your rate types (name, standard or derived, which room types each covers) and your own nightly rates for the next 396 nights from the rate type MAYA sends to.

Once a day: the whole booking window again.

Once, at connect: the property's name, time zone and currency, and which hotels your login covers.

Once a day: the whole window again.

Once, at connect: your property's details, only to check the keys work. MAYA keeps none of them. We set the property's name, time zone and currency with you.

Never asked for: your rate plans, availability, restrictions or guest details. Guest fields that come with a booking are dropped before anything is stored. Read the [Mews page](@14).

**Mews:** Nothing. MAYA does not send prices to Mews yet, including prices you type.

Until you go live, no price is written. Every property starts in simulation. Read [going live](@55).

MAYA never creates, changes or cancels a booking. So when a rule raises or cuts a night's price, guests who have already booked keep the rate they booked at. The new price is for bookings made after it reaches your system. MAYA never changes availability, so it cannot cause an overbooking. It never changes restrictions, minimum stays, close-outs, taxes, room types, rate plans or property settings. It never sends a price of 0. Read [how prices reach your property system](@56).

**Good to know: Two permissions asked for but never used** · When you connect Cloudbeds from inside MAYA, the permission list includes writing reservations. When you connect ThinkReservations, it includes reading availability. MAYA asks for both and uses neither. Nothing in MAYA creates, changes or cancels a booking, and nothing uses how many rooms are free on a night.

Simulation is the read-only way to use MAYA. Every property starts in it and stays in it until a General Manager or Hotel Admin goes live. In simulation MAYA reads your system and runs your rules. The results show on the calendar and in the change log, and no price is sent. On Cloudbeds, the only thing written is the notification subscription, set up when you connect. Read [simulation mode](@54).

MAYA has no read-only connection. When you connect Cloudbeds from inside MAYA, or connect ThinkReservations, the permissions it asks for include changing rates, because it needs that once you are live.

For each room in a booking, MAYA keeps one line per night: the night, the room type, the date the booking was made, the days between the two, and that room's nightly rate. It also keeps a short record of the booking's shape: its reference in your system, its status, its dates, how many adults and children, and the channel it came from. Where your system sends them, the record also holds the room the booking was given and the rate plan it was booked on. On ThinkReservations it also keeps the booking's subtotal, tax and total amounts. No price is worked out from these amounts. Bookings read by the history import keep no record at all beyond the line per night.

MAYA never stores guest names, emails, phone numbers, addresses, notes, dietary or special requests, payment details or loyalty numbers. Where your system lets MAYA choose, it does not ask for them: MAYA never asks Cloudbeds for guest details, and never asks ThinkReservations for customer records. Where they arrive anyway (a guest name on a Cloudbeds booking, a customer block on a ThinkReservations booking, a Mews booking's guest fields), MAYA keeps only the fields on a short list and drops the rest before anything is stored. A new field your system adds is dropped by default.

The same promise is in the [Privacy Policy](https://www.get-maya.com/privacy) and the [Terms](https://www.get-maya.com/terms). Read [privacy, security and your data](@109).

MAYA reads your rate plans for two reasons: to find the one plan per room type it writes to, and to read your own nightly rates from that plan about once an hour. Your own rate is what a rule starts from on a night MAYA has not sent to yet. Read [how rules run](@39).

MAYA writes to one plan per room type and never to any other.

- **Cloudbeds**: the room type's base rate, the plan that does not follow another plan and has no public name. Derived plans (a non-refundable rate at 10% off, say) follow the base by Cloudbeds' own rules, so they move when MAYA moves the base. Packages, promotions and long-stay plans are never written to. Read [which rate plan MAYA changes in Cloudbeds](@12#what-maya-writes-the-base-rate).
Cloudbeds

- **ThinkReservations**: your Best Available rate type, the standard rate type with "Best Available" in its name. If no rate type has that name, MAYA uses the one standard rate type that covers the most room types. Derived rate types reprice themselves from it. A non-refundable or package rate type is written to only if it is the one chosen, so give exactly one standard rate type a name with "Best Available" in it. Read [which rate type MAYA sends to in ThinkReservations](@13#which-rate-type-maya-sends-prices-to).
ThinkReservations

- **Mews**: none.

There is no setting to choose a different plan, in MAYA or with us. On Cloudbeds, it follows from how your plans are built. MAYA writes to the base rate, so a plan you want to move with MAYA's prices should follow the base rate.

On ThinkReservations, it follows from the name. MAYA sends to the standard rate type whose name contains "Best Available", so you choose by giving that name to the standard rate type you want (and to no other). MAYA reads your rate types about once an hour, so a renamed rate type is picked up within about an hour.

MAYA never creates a rate plan or a rate type. Set up any new rate structure in your system first. If a room type has no plan MAYA can write to, it is priced on the calendar and not sent, and the change log says so. Read [when your property system does not accept a price](@57).
Mews

The Harbour Inn's Standard room in Cloudbeds has "Standard Rate" (the base), "Non-refundable" (follows Standard Rate at 10% off) and "Bed and Breakfast" (a package). MAYA writes $165 to Standard Rate for Fri, Nov 13 2026. Cloudbeds moves Non-refundable to $148.50 on its own. Bed and Breakfast stays where it was. Your booking engine and channels read Standard Rate as they always have.

On Cloudbeds, MAYA asks for your taxes and fees once a day, because Cloudbeds requires it of pricing tools like MAYA. MAYA keeps none of it and uses none of it. No price is worked out from your taxes, and nothing about tax is sent. If your property has not given MAYA permission to read them, Cloudbeds turns the request down and MAYA carries on as normal.

On ThinkReservations and Mews, MAYA does not read your tax settings at all. A ThinkReservations booking does arrive with its own tax amount. MAYA keeps it with the booking and works out no price from it. Read [what a stored booking looks like](#what-a-stored-booking-looks-like).

MAYA reads and writes the same rate field in your system, so prices come out on whatever basis your base rate is on. If your base rate in Cloudbeds is entered with tax included, MAYA's prices are with tax included. If it is entered without, so are MAYA's. The same holds for ThinkReservations. MAYA does not add or remove tax, and it shows you the number it works with.

**Careful: MAYA sends the number as it is** · On Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations, a price you type in MAYA goes to your system exactly as typed, on that same basis (except 0, which you set there yourself). If your rates are entered without tax, type prices without tax. Nothing is sent to Mews.

MAYA reads your property's name, time zone and currency at connect and does not read them again. On Mews it copies none of the three, and we set them with you when we connect. The name you can change yourself in the questions step. The time zone and currency cannot be changed inside MAYA. If you change either in your system, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Time%20zone%20or%20currency) and we change it in MAYA. The time zone matters more than it looks: the calendar, the 396-night window, the booking window and every "past week" count run on it. Read [time, weekends, currency and holidays](@106).

Cloudbeds reports the number of rooms in each room type, and MAYA re-reads it on every cycle, so a wing you open shows up on the next read. On ThinkReservations, MAYA counts the rooms in each room type from your list of rooms on every cycle, and keeps the counts it has if the list cannot be read. MAYA does not read room counts from Mews yet, so it uses one number for every Mews room category, which we set with you when we connect (100 until then). That number cannot differ by category, so occupancy is exact only when your categories are the same size. The count is what sellable occupancy divides by and what your bill is based on. Read [room types and rooms out of service](@52) and [your room count and what you pay](@60).

**Not yet: Not yet** · MAYA does not use, keep or write availability or restrictions on any system (on Cloudbeds they arrive with your room types and nightly rates and are dropped). It does not read or write room blocks or allotments. It does not read rate plans from Mews or send anything to Mews. Time zone and currency are not re-read after connect (email us). Mews room counts are not read, and a count for each room category is not possible there yet (one number covers them all).

When the connection breaks, a General Manager or Hotel Admin reconnects it in one click, signing in with a login for this property only (on Mews, you email us and we arrange new keys). A banner shows for some breaks but not all, so the sign to watch is **Last sync** on the **PMS** tab. When the connection has read Disconnected or Error for about an hour, the General Managers and Hotel Admins get one email. While the connection is down, MAYA reads no bookings and sends nothing, and the rates already in your system stay exactly as they are. Disconnecting on purpose happens in your property system, not in MAYA, and it does not cancel your subscription or delete anything.

When the connection is broken, the **PMS** tab shows a panel headed "MAYA has lost its connection to Cloudbeds" (or Think Reservations). The same panel appears as a banner at the top of the dashboard, whichever tab is open, from the moment the dashboard opens.

The address opens an email to us. Read [Mews: what works today](@14).

When the **Connection** card has read **Disconnected** or **Error** for about an hour, every General Manager and Hotel Admin on the property gets one email, headed "MAYA has lost its connection to Cloudbeds" (or your system). On Mews it asks you to reply, and we arrange new keys with you. Our team is told at the same time.

One email per outage. If the connection comes back and breaks again later, the next email follows about an hour after the new break. The five-minute cycle skips a disconnected property: no bookings are read, no scheduled pricing runs and nothing is sent.

A connection that reads **Error** is not skipped. MAYA keeps trying it, waiting longer after each failed try, up to an hour between tries, and nothing is read, priced or sent while the tries fail. The first try that works turns the card back to **Connected**, and the cycle carries on as normal with no reconnect needed.

- **Rates already in your system stay as they are.** MAYA never puts back your old rates when it disconnects or when you cancel. If you want different rates while MAYA is disconnected, set them in your system.

- **Your rules, history, settings, room type answers, floors and ceilings and manual prices stay in MAYA.**

1. **Open the **PMS** tab (or the banner) and click **Reconnect Cloudbeds**** (or **Reconnect Think Reservations**). Only a General Manager or Hotel Admin sees the reconnect button.
2. **Sign in on your system's website and approve.** Use a login that reaches this property. It does not have to be the login that connected MAYA first. On ThinkReservations, use one that reaches no other hotel. Before you use any other login, read "Which login to use", below.
3. **You are back on the MAYA dashboard.** It opens on the **PMS** tab of the property you reconnected, with a short note: "Reconnected." Close it with the ×. The banner stops showing once the connection reads as connected, which is right away.

Syncing resumes on the next cycle, within about five minutes, or up to an hour if reads had been failing for a while. (After each failed read MAYA waits longer before trying again, up to an hour, and reconnecting does not cut that wait short.) The first read after a reconnect picks up the bookings you missed. Prices that changed while you were disconnected go out on that cycle like any changed price, and prices that were held for a missing permission go out on that cycle too, rather than a day later.

If your Cloudbeds property started in the Cloudbeds Marketplace (you first connected by clicking **Connect App** in Cloudbeds), there is a second way: click **Connect App** for MAYA in the Marketplace again. You land on the MAYA sign-in page with "Your Cloudbeds connection is active again. Sign in to pick up where you left off." Sign in and carry on.

If you connected Cloudbeds from inside MAYA instead (you paid first, then connected), **Connect App** in the Marketplace finds your property too, by its Cloudbeds property, and never adds a second one. Sign in to MAYA first, in the same browser, as the property's General Manager or Hotel Admin. Then **Connect App** reconnects it, and you land on its **PMS** tab with the note "Reconnected." Signed out, or with any other role, you see "This property is already in MAYA, so nothing new was added. Reconnecting it needs General Manager access or higher on it. Sign in to MAYA with that access and click Reconnect Cloudbeds on the PMS tab." and nothing changes. **Reconnect Cloudbeds** in MAYA is the simplest way either way.

A login that reaches this property and no other always works. What any other login does depends on your system.

The **Connection** card shows one word. What each one means:

| Word | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| **Connected** | The connection is working as far as MAYA can tell. Some breaks, and a stopped subscription, still read Connected (see "When there is no banner") | Nothing, as long as **Last sync** is a few minutes old |
| **Pending** | Connected but not paid for yet, or set up but not switched on | Finish payment, or wait for us |
| **Degraded** | MAYA is still reading and sending. One calm line says the connection needs a refresh soon and prices are still updating. (Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations only.) | If it is still there in an hour, reconnect with a login for this property only. It does no harm |
| **Error** | Your system refused to renew MAYA's access. On Mews: Mews refused MAYA's keys three reads in a row. MAYA keeps trying, and the card goes back to **Connected** by itself once a try works | Reconnect if it has not cleared within a couple of hours (on Mews, email us) |
| **Disconnected** | Access has been withdrawn, or the app was uninstalled | Reconnect |
| unknown | MAYA could not read the status | Reload the page. If it stays, email us |

The banner appears for **Error** and **Disconnected**. **Degraded** shows the calm line instead, with the quiet reconnect link for a General Manager or Hotel Admin. A break that leaves the card at **Connected** shows no banner (see "When there is no banner", above). **Error** or **Disconnected** for about an hour also sends the email (see "The email after an hour"). For what to check in each case, read [connection lost](@101).

**Cloudbeds:** Cloudbeds tells MAYA when the property disables or uninstalls the app, usually within seconds. MAYA marks the connection **Disconnected** at once and the property leaves the cycle. If that message does not reach MAYA, MAYA finds out on its next read, within about five minutes, and the card reads **Disconnected** or **Error**. Either way, reconnect. One case is not caught: when the Cloudbeds user who approved MAYA is deactivated or deleted, the tab may still read **Connected** while **Last sync** stops moving. A user at the property who is still active reconnects.

**Mews:** Mews connects with keys, so there is nothing to revoke from Mews' side that MAYA is told about. If the keys stop working, reads fail and back off. Once three reads in a row have been refused as bad keys, about half an hour after the first, the status changes to **Error** and the banner appears. A read that fails for another reason, such as Mews being down, does not count, and a read that works starts the count again. MAYA keeps trying, up to an hour between tries, and once we save new keys the status reads **Connected** again. When we remove the keys at your request, the status reads **Disconnected**. Read [Mews: what works today](@14).

MAYA has no disconnect button of its own. You disconnect in your property system.

**Cloudbeds:** In Cloudbeds, go to **Marketplace**, then **My Apps**, find MAYA and disconnect it there. Cloudbeds tells MAYA, and MAYA marks the connection **Disconnected**. If you did it by accident, click **Reconnect Cloudbeds** in MAYA. Clicking **Connect App** again there works too (for a property you connected from inside MAYA, sign in to MAYA first as its General Manager or Hotel Admin; see "Reconnecting", above).

**ThinkReservations:** To remove MAYA's access in ThinkReservations, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Disconnect%20ThinkReservations) and we walk you through it.

**Mews:** [Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Disconnect%20Mews) and we remove the keys. If you only revoke them in your Mews dashboard, MAYA's reads start failing but do not stop. They are tried again with a growing wait, up to an hour between tries, until we remove the keys. Nothing is priced while they fail. After three refused reads the **PMS** tab reads **Error**, and about an hour later your General Managers and Hotel Admins get the connection-down email. So if you revoke them in Mews, email us as well.

**Careful: Cancel first, then disconnect** · Disconnecting does not cancel your subscription, and cancelling does not disconnect your system. To stop completely, cancel on the **Billing** page first, then disconnect in your system. Read [cancelling, restarting and leaving](@62).

If your system still lets MAYA read but refuses the price write, the connection stays up and only sending waits. The change log shows "Cloudbeds won't let MAYA change Standard rates because MAYA doesn't have permission to update rates", with the action "Give MAYA permission to update rates in Cloudbeds, then reconnect on the PMS tab." Restore the permission in your system, then click the **Reconnect** link on the **PMS** tab. The held prices go out on the next cycle. Read [when your property system does not accept a price](@57).

Everything. Disconnecting deletes nothing, and neither does cancelling, so a property that paid and comes back finds its history, rules and settings intact. Reconnecting never resets anything.

There is one exception, and it only touches properties that never paid. If a property connected through the Cloudbeds Marketplace has never paid for MAYA and nobody has used it for 180 days, its imported booking history, its stored connection and its credentials may be deleted. The property, its members, rules and settings stay. When that owner comes back, the banner reads "Your rules and settings are still here, and your booking history comes back once you reconnect." and reconnecting reads the history again. The same rule is in the [Terms](https://www.get-maya.com/terms), section 8.8.

MAYA sends each room type's price to one rate plan, its base rate, and never to any other. Rates that follow the base rate move on their own by your system's rules. Packages and named promotional plans are left alone. If a room type has no base rate MAYA can send to, nothing is sent for it. Once you are live, the change log says so for that room type. Before you go live the change log says nothing about it, because nothing is sent in simulation. So check your rate plans by hand with the steps below.

**Cloudbeds:** For each room type, look at its rate plans in Cloudbeds and ask, in this order:
1. **Does the plan follow another plan?** Cloudbeds calls this derived. If yes, MAYA never writes to it.
Does the plan follow another plan?
2. **Does the plan have a public name?** Packages, promotions and long-stay plans do. If yes, MAYA never writes to it.
Does the plan have a public name?

3. **What is left?** The one plan that follows nothing and has no public name is the base rate. That is the one MAYA changes.

Once you are live, a room type with only derived plans is reported in the change log as "Cloudbeds won't let MAYA change Deluxe rates because that rate follows another rate plan", with the action "In Cloudbeds, give this room type a base rate of its own that doesn't follow another plan." A room type with only packages is reported as "MAYA can't find a base rate for Deluxe in Cloudbeds". Fix it in Cloudbeds. MAYA re-reads your rate plans and sends the held prices on a later cycle. Before you go live neither message appears, so ask the three questions above for every room type yourself.
What is left?

Once you are live, a room type not covered by that rate type is reported in the change log as "MAYA can't find a base rate for Deluxe in Think Reservations, so its rates can't be changed", with the action "Add a base rate for this room type in Think Reservations." Add the room type to Best Available. MAYA re-reads your rate types and sends the held prices on a later cycle. Before you go live this message does not appear, so check in ThinkReservations that Best Available covers every room type you want priced.

**Mews:** MAYA does not read or write Mews rate plans. Nothing to set up.

Read [when your property system does not accept a price](@57) for every sentence the change log can show.

A night whose rate in your system is 0 reads as closed: your rules leave it alone and nothing is sent for it, unless you have typed a price for it in MAYA. So if you close a night by setting it to 0 in your system, also clear any price you typed for it in MAYA. Otherwise MAYA may keep your typed price and send it once you are live.

A night with no rate loaded at all starts from the newest booking's rate for that night when there is one, otherwise from the starting point used the last time your rules ran on that night, and is otherwise left unpriced. So before you go live, load a rate on the base rate plan for every night you sell in the next 396. Nights further out are read as they enter the window, one a day. A night with no rate and no booking stays unpriced, and nothing is sent for it.

**Good to know: Only the base rate plan is read** · MAYA reads the nightly rate from the base rate plan it writes to, and from no other plan. A rate loaded only on a package does not count as a loaded rate.

The time zone sets what "today" is, which nights are in the 396-night window, and what "past week" means for booking speed. If it is wrong, your system may refuse the price for tonight with "Cloudbeds wouldn't take Standard rates for a night that had already begun at the property".

Sellable occupancy is rooms booked divided by rooms you can sell that night. MAYA divides by the units of every room type ticked as a room, minus rooms out of service. So two things need to be right: which types count, and how many units each has.

**Which types count.** Your system lists every bookable thing as a room type, so a meeting room, a car park or a spa slot can appear. Untick **Counts as a room** for anything nobody sleeps in. It can still be priced. On the review, a room type whose name has a word like Meeting, Conference or Parking is already unticked. Any room type whose name or bookings do not read like a bedroom's (a name like Spa or Tennis Court, or only one-night bookings when your other rooms get longer stays) gets a card asking whether it is a room. Room types added after your first history read arrive ticked, so untick any that are not rooms on the **PMS** tab. Read [room types and rooms out of service](@52).
Which types count

**How many units.**

**Cloudbeds:** The units come from Cloudbeds on every read, so there is usually nothing to do. A virtual room type (one that sells rooms from another type) counts like any other, with the units Cloudbeds gives it, so your count can read higher than the rooms you have. Unticking it takes out its units, but also leaves out any bookings Cloudbeds records on it. If you sell one, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Virtual%20room%20type) before you untick it, and we check which room type its bookings are counted under.
How many units

**Mews:** Mews does not report room counts, so every room category gets the one number we set with you when we connect. If your room categories are all the same size, occupancy reads right. If they differ, we set the average: whole-property occupancy reads close, and occupancy for one category is off. The room count you are billed for is checked against this number, so 100 for each category can raise your bill. Check the units on the **PMS** tab. If they read 100, or look wrong, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Mews%20room%20counts).

MAYA does not read room blocks, out-of-order rooms or allotments from any system. A room you have blocked in your system still counts as sellable in MAYA until you record it under **Rooms out of service** on the **PMS** tab: the room type, from and to dates, how many units, and an optional reason. Those units come off the sellable count for those nights only. Nothing is sent to your system for that.

An allotment held for a group without bookings is invisible to MAYA. It neither reduces the sellable count nor counts as bookings. If a block matters to your pricing, record it as rooms out of service.

Try what a block does to a rule. Set 12 rooms, 3 out of service and 8 booked, and see how an occupancy rule reads.

Twelve rooms, three out of service, eight booked: 89% sellable occupancy, so a Greater than 80 rule fires.

MAYA never writes to any of these, so leave them as they are:

- Availability, restrictions, minimum stays, closed to arrival or departure, and close-outs.
- Bookings, guests and payments.
- Taxes and fees. On Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations, MAYA reads and writes the same rate field, so if your base rate is entered with tax included, MAYA's prices are with tax included. On Mews, a starting price taken from a booking includes tax (and can include extras on the booking). A price you type is used as you type it. MAYA does not add or remove tax.
- Room types and property settings.
- Rate plans other than the base rate. Derived plans follow it by your system's own rules. MAYA never creates a rate plan.

MAYA reads your bookings about every five minutes, your own rates about once an hour (Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations), and the whole booking window once a day. A new booking, a cancellation, a date change or a room move shows in MAYA on the next read. A rate you change in your system is read within the hour. Blocked rooms, allotments and restrictions are not read at all, and property details are read once, when you connect, and never again (on Mews, we set them with you).

Three clocks set how soon a change in your system reaches MAYA. This page names them, then lists every change you can make and which clock it rides on. Where a system is different, its tab says so.

| Clock | What is read | How often |
|---|---|---|
| The cycle | Bookings made or changed since the last read, and your room types | About every five minutes |
| The rates read | Your own nightly rate on the base rate plan, for tonight and the next 395 nights, and your rate plans | About once an hour, or when your hotel day changes (Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations only) |
| The daily re-read | Every booking in the window, 30 days back and about 13 months ahead | Once a day |

"Next read" below means the next cycle, up to about five minutes on a healthy connection. "Within the hour" means the next rates read.

**Cloudbeds:**

| You do this in Cloudbeds | MAYA picks it up |
|---|---|
| Make a booking | Next read. A booking waiting in the unassigned list counts too |
| Cancel a booking, or mark it no-show | Next read. Its nights come off the count |
| Take a room off a booking that holds several, or cancel one of its rooms | Next read. That room's nights come off the count. The booking's other rooms stay as they were |
| Add a room to a booking | Next read. The new room is counted. The rooms already counted are not counted again, and the booking is still one booking for booking speed |

**ThinkReservations:**

| You do this in ThinkReservations | MAYA picks it up |
|---|---|
| Make a booking | Next read |
| Cancel a booking, or mark it no-show | Next read. Cancelling changes the booking, so it arrives with everything else |
| Change a booking's dates | Next read. New nights are added and dropped nights removed |
| A guest checks out early (stay shortened) | Next read, once ThinkReservations shows the shorter stay. The nights it no longer covers count as free rooms again. If the booking still shows the old check-out date, MAYA still counts those nights as booked |
| Move a booking to another room type | Next read |
| Change a rate on a night MAYA has never sent to | Within the hour, and always before MAYA's first send to that night. Your rate becomes the night's starting point |

**Mews:**

| You do this in Mews | MAYA picks it up |
|---|---|
| Make a reservation, an option, an enquiry or a request | Next read. Every state but Canceled counts |
| Cancel a reservation | Next read. Its nights come off the count. Mews records a no-show as a cancelled reservation, so a no-show comes off too |
| Change a reservation's dates | Next read |
| A guest checks out early (stay shortened) | Next read, once Mews shows the shorter stay. The nights it no longer covers count as free rooms again. If the reservation still shows the old departure date, MAYA still counts those nights as booked |
| Move a reservation to another room category | Next read |
| Confirm an option | Nothing changes. Both count as booked |
| Change a rate | Not read. MAYA does not read Mews rates |
| Add a room category | Next read, with the one number set for your property's categories |

Three kinds of booking people ask about:

- **An extended stay or a date change.** The added nights belong to the same booking and keep the date it was first made. They count as booked rooms from the next read, but for booking speed they are an old booking, so they rarely show in **Past day** or **Past week**.
An extended stay or a date change

- **A day-use booking** (in and out the same day). It is not skipped. In ThinkReservations and Mews it counts as one night on its date. In Cloudbeds it counts on each date Cloudbeds lists a room rate for, so on its date when Cloudbeds lists one. Either way it reads as a booked room that night.
A day-use booking

- **A comp, house-use or owner stay at $0.** It counts by its status, like any booking: a booked room for occupancy and a booking for booking speed. It adds $0 to the calendar's revenue and lowers the ADR. Read [Comp, house-use and day-use bookings](@22#comp-house-use-and-day-use-bookings).
A comp, house-use or owner stay at $0

A test booking counts like any other booking while it is in your system. What happened depends on whether a read found it before you cancelled it:

- **Cancelled before the next read** (within about five minutes). The read finds it already cancelled, so it is never counted and no price moves.
Cancelled before the next read

- **Still there at a read.** It counts as a booked room and a new booking on its nights, and your rules run with it on that cycle. The next read after you cancel it takes it off the count.

If your rules ran with it, here is what happens to what they did:
Still there at a read

- **A rule with only occupancy and booking window conditions** follows the count. A change that needed the test booking comes off on the cycle that reads the cancellation, and a change it was holding back can now happen.
A rule with only occupancy and booking window conditions

- **A booking speed or pickup change** comes off when its rule's undo box is ticked and the cancellation means the rule is no longer true. One test booking may not be enough, and bookings made since can keep the rule true. A cut made because a night was booking slowly never comes off this way. Read [When a price change comes off](@40).

In simulation nothing was sent. If you are live on Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations, a price it moved was sent like any other (nothing is ever sent to Mews). To put a night straight back, type the price you want on the calendar. Read [Undo a price change](@67).

To test without moving any price, book a night more than 395 nights ahead and cancel it straight away. Your rules run on tonight and the next 395 nights only.
A booking speed or pickup change

From any system: availability by night, room blocks, out-of-order rooms, allotments, restrictions, minimum stays, closed-to-arrival flags and closed-to-departure flags. Guest details that come with a booking are dropped before anything is saved. It reads your property's name, time zone and currency once at connect and never again (on Mews, we set them with you). Read [what MAYA reads and writes](@15).

- **A large property's first read** can take several cycles. Each cycle reads for a fixed slice of time and carries on from where it stopped. Until the whole window has been read, your rules run on what has arrived and nothing is sent.
A large property's first read
- **A failing connection** is tried again with a growing wait, up to an hour between tries. Nothing is priced or sent on a cycle where the read failed, so bookings are never priced on stale data.
A failing connection
- **If your system keeps asking MAYA to slow down**, MAYA waits a minute or two before calling it again, and sends move to a later cycle.
If your system keeps asking MAYA to slow down
- **Nights 396 or more days out** (past tonight and the next 395) are neither read for rates nor sent until they enter the window.
Nights 396 or more days out

- **A rate you change within an hour of MAYA's send** is not yet kept as yours, and MAYA's next price for that night can write over it. Wait an hour after a send before changing that night's rate by hand, or type the price in MAYA instead. Read [rates you change in your property system](@51).
A rate you change within an hour of MAYA's send

**Not yet: Not yet** · There is no button to read your system right now. The cycle runs on its own about every five minutes. Blocks, allotments and restrictions are not read from any system. Time zone, currency and name are read once. Mews rates and Mews room counts are never read.

Your system and MAYA use different words for the same things. MAYA's base rate is one of your rate plans (Cloudbeds) or rate types (ThinkReservations): the one per room type that MAYA writes to. A Cloudbeds reservation, a ThinkReservations reservation and a Mews reservation are all bookings in MAYA. A Cloudbeds room type, a ThinkReservations room type and a Mews room category are all room types in MAYA. This page is the translation table.

| MAYA says | Cloudbeds says | ThinkReservations says | Mews says | What it means in MAYA |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Booking | Reservation | Reservation, holding one booking per room | Reservation, one room each | A stay. For occupancy each room counts. For booking speed a booking counts once however many rooms it holds. On Mews every room is its own reservation, so rooms booked together count once per room |
| Room type | Room type | Room type | Room category, space category or resource category | The kind of room a price is set for. Your rules set one price per room type per night |
| Units | Units | Rooms, counted per room type | none (not reported) | How many rooms a room type has. MAYA divides by it for sellable occupancy. On ThinkReservations MAYA counts it from your list of rooms. On Mews it is one number for every room type, 100 until we set it with you |

On ThinkReservations, each rate type is standard or derived (it follows another). A package or a non-refundable rate can be standard too. MAYA writes to the standard rate type whose name contains Best Available. If none has that name, MAYA writes to the one standard rate type that covers the most room types, even if it is a package. If two tie, MAYA writes to neither. Name your main rate type Best Available and MAYA leaves your packages alone.

Your system marks each booking with a status. MAYA keeps some and removes others.

**Cloudbeds:**

| Cloudbeds status | In MAYA |
|---|---|
| Confirmed | Counts as booked |
| Checked In | Counts as booked |
| Checked Out | Counts as booked (a past night) |
| Confirmation Pending | Counts as booked. It holds a room, and Cloudbeds' own occupancy counts it |
| Cancelled (Cloudbeds spells it "canceled") | Removed on the next read |
| No Show | Removed on the next read |

Two more Cloudbeds words: a booking in the **unassigned** list (not yet placed on a physical room) counts as a booked room, and a **virtual room type** (one that sells rooms from another type) is treated like any other room type.

**ThinkReservations:**

| ThinkReservations status | In MAYA |
|---|---|
| Scheduled | Counts as booked |
| Checked in | Counts as booked |
| Checked out | Counts as booked (a past night) |
| Cancelled | Removed on the next read |
| No show | Removed on the next read |

ThinkReservations holds one **booking** per room inside a **reservation**. MAYA keeps each room's nights and room charge, and for booking speed the reservation counts once.

**Mews:**

| Mews state | In MAYA |
|---|---|
| Confirmed | Counts as booked |
| Started | Counts as booked (the guest is in the house) |
| Processed | Counts as booked (a past night) |
| Optional | Counts as booked |
| Enquired | Counts as booked |
| Requested | Counts as booked |
| Canceled | Removed on the next read |

Only Canceled removes a booking. An option, an enquiry or a request counts like a confirmed booking until it is cancelled in Mews.

Each Mews reservation holds one room. A guest who books three rooms has three reservations in Mews, so for booking speed that stay counts as three bookings. On Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations the same stay counts once. MAYA does not read Mews reservation groups.

**Complimentary, house-use and owner stays.** A booking counts by its status, not its rate. A comp or house-use booking at $0 counts as a booked room for [sellable occupancy](@32) and pickup count, and as one booking for booking speed, like any other. On the calendar it adds $0 to the night's revenue, so it lowers the ADR. There is no setting to leave $0 bookings out.
Complimentary, house-use and owner stays

**Day-use bookings (in and out the same day).** They are not skipped. In ThinkReservations and Mews, a booking with check-out on its check-in date counts as one night on that date: a booked room for occupancy, and a booking for booking speed. In Cloudbeds, a booking counts on each date Cloudbeds lists a room rate for, so a same-day booking counts on its date when Cloudbeds lists a rate for it. Either way, a day-use room reads as booked that night, even though it can still be sold for the night.
Day-use bookings (in and out the same day)

| Word | Whose | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| Marketplace, **Connect App**, **My Apps** | Cloudbeds | Where you install MAYA and where you disconnect it. MAYA has no disconnect button of its own |
| **Sign in with your Cloudbeds account**, **Sign in with your Think Reservations account** | MAYA | The other way in: from the **Connect your property system** screen after paying |
| Access code | MAYA | A code that may be needed at checkout for some systems. Marketplace installs never need one |
| Client token, Access token, Enterprise ID | Mews | The keys MAYA uses to read Mews. We set them up with you |
| Group login | Cloudbeds, ThinkReservations | A login that reaches several properties. Through the Cloudbeds Marketplace it connects all of them. From inside MAYA it is refused |
| **PMS** tab | MAYA | The tab that shows the connection, its health, the last sync and your room type settings. "PMS" is the label. These docs say "property system" |
| **Connected**, **Pending**, **Degraded**, **Error**, **Disconnected** | MAYA | The connection words on the **PMS** tab. Read [reconnecting and disconnecting](@16) |

These have no equivalent in your system.

| MAYA says | What it means |
|---|---|
| Cycle | One run for your property, about every five minutes: read bookings, refresh your rates if due, run rules, send changed prices |
| Window | Tonight and the next 395 nights. The nights your rules price and, once you are live, MAYA sends (Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations) |
| Sellable occupancy | Rooms booked divided by rooms you can sell that night, counting only room types ticked as rooms and subtracting rooms out of service |
| **Counts as a room** | The checkbox that says a room type is somewhere guests sleep |
| **Rooms out of service** | Units you take off sale for a stretch in MAYA. Your system's blocks are not read |
| Manual price, "Manual · $175.00" | A price you typed for a room type on a night |

For every other product word, read the [glossary](@105).

**Example: One sentence, three vocabularies**

The change log at The Harbour Inn says: "Cloudbeds won't let MAYA change Deluxe rates because that rate follows another rate plan". In Cloudbeds' words: the Deluxe room type's only rate plan is derived. In MAYA's words: Deluxe has no base rate. The fix is the same in both: in Cloudbeds, give Deluxe a rate plan that follows nothing and has no public name. On ThinkReservations the change log shows a different sentence for a room type with no base rate: "MAYA can't find a base rate for Deluxe in Think Reservations, so its rates can't be changed". The fix there is adding Deluxe to your Best Available rate type.

As soon as your property is connected, MAYA reads your past bookings: your current bookings first, then one year at a time back through up to ten years. You can close the page, because the import runs on its own. The first results (your starter rules and the review) are ready after three past years are in, or once everything is read if you have less than three years. Pricing comparisons reach three years back.

The import starts on its own. You do not press anything.

- **Cloudbeds, from the Marketplace**: it starts as soon as you create your MAYA account (or sign in) and claim the property, before you have paid. By the time you reach the payment screen it is usually already running, and paying does not start it over.
Cloudbeds, from the Marketplace
- **Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations, from inside MAYA**: it starts the moment your connection succeeds.
Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations, from inside MAYA

- **Mews**: there is no history import for Mews yet. See the Mews tab below.

You can start a fresh read later from the **Rules** tab with **Get suggestions from my data**. That read makes suggestions only and changes nothing on its own. Read [Getting suggestions later](@29).

**Good to know: A login that covers several properties** · If you came from the Cloudbeds Marketplace and your login covers several properties, MAYA reads one unpaid property at a time. Choosing **Not now** for a property pauses its import where it is, and it carries on from the same place when you come back to that property. From inside MAYA, a Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations login that covers several properties cannot connect yet, so nothing is imported: [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Group%20login) and we will set them up.
Mews

The progress bar names each step as it goes. In order:

1. **Reading your property setup.** Your time zone and currency (only where MAYA has nothing yet), and your room types with how many units each has. The import never changes your property's name.
Reading your property setup

2. **Reading your current bookings.** The same read MAYA makes about every five minutes from then on: bookings from 30 days ago to about 13 months ahead. For a large book this takes several passes, and the bar says so: "Reading your current bookings (part 2)".
Reading your current bookings

3. **Importing past years.** One 365-day stretch at a time, going backwards from where the current read started. Up to ten stretches, so at most about ten years. It stops earlier when a year comes back empty.
Importing past years

4. **Building your starter rules.** After the first three past years are in, MAYA reads what it has so far and writes the review cards, sets floors and ceilings that were still at their defaults, and builds your starter rules. From here the bar reads "First results ready. Importing older years", and the review can open while the rest loads.
Building your starter rules

5. **Checking your full history.** Once every year is in, MAYA reads everything again. This pass refines the review cards: it can sharpen a card, add one, or take one away. With less than three years on record, step 4 is skipped and this is the only read, so your first results come once all of your history has been read.
Checking your full history

6. **Import complete.**

**Good to know: Why three years first** · Every comparison MAYA makes for pricing (similar past nights, seasons, the checks behind a "Not a fair comparison?" answer) reaches at most three years back. So three years is the smallest history on which the review and the starter rules work as they will with the full import.
Import complete

For each past stay night MAYA keeps six things: the booking's reference number from your property system, the stay date, the room type, the nightly price, the date the booking was made, and the number of days between the two. The reference number is how a booking with several rooms counts as one booking in booking speed.

It keeps nothing about the guest. No names, no emails, no card details. For past stays nothing else about the booking is stored, only those six fields. What MAYA keeps about your current and future bookings is covered in [What MAYA reads and writes](@15).

There is no fixed time, and MAYA does not promise one. It depends on how much history your property system holds and how quickly that system answers. A small property with two years of bookings finishes far sooner than a 200-room property with ten.

The import runs on our side in short bursts and picks itself up again between them, so it does not need your browser open. Close the page, come back later, and the progress bar shows where it got to.

Two things you may see on a large book:

- "Reading your current bookings (part 2)", "(part 3)" and so on. One pass was not enough to cover the window, so it is taking another.
- A very large history can stop before ten years. MAYA reads up to a set number of room nights (one room for one night), and the limit grows with the size of your property.

You can. Here is what to expect:

- The dashboard fills in as the import goes. Your current bookings arrive in step 2, so the calendar shows real occupancy early on, while older years are still loading.
- Your rules run during the import. MAYA runs them on each night whose bookings changed, within about five minutes, and on every night up to 395 nights ahead once a day, and writes the result in the **Change Log** tab. Each stretch of runs that change nothing is counted into one line, such as "Prices checked 47 times from Sep 24, 10:05 AM to 1:55 PM, nothing needed to change."
- Your property starts in simulation, so no rule, starter or yours, changes anything in your system until you go live.
- With Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations, MAYA also reads the rate you already have for each night, about once an hour, and your rules work from it. Mews rates are not read.
The progress page has a link, **Go to my dashboard →**, at the bottom.

The progress bar sits under the five questions and on the progress page. It shows the current step on the left and, on the right, how many room-nights have been read and, once an oldest stay is known, "back to" that month (for example "back to 2019-03").

The dot beside the step pulses while the import runs, turns green when it is complete, and turns amber if it has paused or stopped.

The progress page adds three tiles: **Room-nights**, **Years covered** (the span between your oldest and newest stay, at least 1) and **Oldest stay**. It moves on by itself: to the review as soon as there is something to review, or to the dashboard if the import finished with nothing to review. If the work was already done when you arrived, it moves on straight away. Otherwise it waits a moment so you can see it finish.

If the bar reads "Import paused" or "Import stopped" with an amber dot, the import has stopped trying for now: your property system stopped answering for a long stretch, or refused MAYA's access, or a read kept ending in the same place. Your connection, your rules and everything already read are safe. When your system refused MAYA's access, reconnecting picks it up again (see below).

When it stops, an automatic alert goes to our team. Then the import tries again by itself, up to three times, each time from where it had got to. It waits an hour before the first try, four hours before the second and twelve hours before the third. While it waits, the bar says when the next try is, for example "Import paused. We've been told, and it tries again by itself around 3:40 PM." Once a try is under way, the bar shows the step it is on again.

"We've been told" appears only when the alert reached us. If the bar says "Import stopped. Email us and we'll restart it." instead, nothing reached us, so please [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Import%20stopped). A Cloudbeds Marketplace property you have not paid for yet does not try again by itself: paying for it (a free trial counts) starts the import again from where it stopped.

If your connection drops while the import runs, the dot turns amber, the bar keeps the name of the step it had reached, and the reconnect prompt appears on your dashboard. Read [Reconnect and disconnect](@16).

Reconnecting picks the import up where it left off. A General Manager or Hotel Admin clicks **Reconnect Cloudbeds** (or **Reconnect Think Reservations**) on the **PMS** tab and signs in, and the import carries on from the step it had reached, usually within a minute. Everything it had already read is kept, and an import that is still running is left to finish: reconnecting never starts a second one. This also covers an import that paused or stopped because your system kept refusing MAYA's access while the connection was down. If the dot is still amber a few minutes after you reconnect, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Restart%20my%20import) and we will restart it.

When the read has run, you have:

- your room types with their unit counts, and MAYA's first proposal for which of them are rooms,
- the review cards: closures, room types that may not be rooms, duplicates, rates that look like typos, stays with no rate, stays that point at deleted room types,
- floors and ceilings for room types that were still at their defaults,
- starter rules, if you have enough history and no rules yet.

Your property's own rates (the starting point your rules work from) are not part of the import. The regular cycle reads them once your property is paid for. A free trial counts.

Read [Checking what MAYA found](@26), [Your starter rules](@27) and [Floors and ceilings](@28).

- **Get suggestions from my data** on the **Rules** tab reads your whole history again and turns what it finds into cards you accept or reject one by one. Read [Getting suggestions later](@29).
- A Cloudbeds property from the Marketplace that never paid may have its booking history removed after 180 days without use. When you come back, reconnecting starts a fresh import, and nothing is priced until it completes. Your rules and settings are kept.

**Cloudbeds:** MAYA reads each booking with every room in it, each with its own room type and nightly rates. Every booking status is read. Confirmed, checked-in, checked-out and not-yet-confirmed stays are kept. Cancelled and no-show bookings are left out, and a booking cancelled since an earlier read has its nights removed.

A few Cloudbeds accounts refuse the detailed booking read. MAYA then reads a plainer list for your past years. From that list, a past booking's nightly price is an average of its total, and a past booking with several rooms may be counted as one room. The list holds only the kept stays, so a past booking cancelled since an earlier read keeps its nights. Current bookings are read in full either way.

MAYA counts each room type's rooms from ThinkReservations' list of rooms, so your occupancy percentages are right from the first read. A room marked inactive, as not a room, or as not included in occupancy is left out. [ThinkReservations](@13) has the details.

**Mews:** MAYA does not read Mews history yet. A Mews property has no import, no review cards, no starter rules and no floors or ceilings from data. Occupancy and booking window rules work from the bookings MAYA reads each cycle. Booking speed rules fire less often at first: with little history a reading stays within one step of Normal, so rules set to Much Faster Than Normal, Surging, Much Slower Than Normal or Stalled stay quiet. **Get suggestions from my data** is greyed out on a Mews property. Email us if you want history read by hand.

**Good to know** · MAYA reads your history on both paths. Let Me Drive skips only the questions and the guided walk through the review.

You go to [the five questions](@25), one card at a time, with the import's progress bar underneath. Every question can be skipped.

After the last question (or **Skip the rest →**), MAYA takes you to the review if the first results are in and there is something to look at. Otherwise it takes you to the progress page, which moves you on to the review by itself once there is something to review.

On the review you check what MAYA found, tick which room types are rooms, see your starter rules, and can go live. Read [Checking what MAYA found](@26).

You go straight to the dashboard. The import keeps running in the background, so the calendar fills in as you look at it. Your starter rules are still built and switched on in simulation, floors and ceilings are still filled in from your history, and the review cards are still written. With no answer to the last question, the starter rules are the usual five. To have them copy your own raises and cuts instead, answer it at maya-rms.com/onboarding/questions while nobody has changed them: [Your starter rules](@27#answering-after-they-were-built) says when that swaps them.

When there are cards waiting for your answer, a blue banner appears at the top of your dashboard with a **Review →** link. That is the same review screen Hold My Hand walks you to.

|  | Hold My Hand | Let Me Drive |
|---|---|---|
| The history import | runs | runs |
| The five questions | asked, all optional | not asked |
| Review cards (closures, room types, typos) | walked through | written, waiting on the review screen |
| Starter rules | built, on, in simulation | built, on, in simulation |
| Floors and ceilings | from your answers, then your history | from your history |
| Where you land | the review, then the dashboard | the dashboard |

Your choice is recorded for you and for the property. It does not change how rules run, what is sent, or what you pay.

There is no button to switch paths, and you do not need one. Both guided screens stay open to you:

- The review opens any time at maya-rms.com/onboarding/review. The dashboard banner links to it only while cards wait for your answer and you have not pressed **Finish** since the newest one arrived. Read [the banner on your dashboard](@26#the-banner-on-your-dashboard).
- The five questions open any time after your property is connected, at maya-rms.com/onboarding/questions.

If you chose Hold My Hand and closed the tab part way through, nothing is lost. Your next sign-in lands on the dashboard. If cards are waiting for your answer, the banner brings you back to the review. If there is no banner, open the review by its address.

Sam connects The Harbour Inn on a Tuesday evening, presses **Let Me Drive**, and lands on the calendar with the coming nights already filling in. On Wednesday morning a banner at the top of the dashboard reads "We found 3 things worth a quick look". Sam clicks **Review →**, confirms one closure, presses **Not a room** on the Meeting Room card, and sees the five starter rules waiting in simulation. Nothing about Tuesday's choice held any of that back.

Five optional questions, one card at a time: your property's name, what a room turnover costs you, the lowest rate you would take on a dead Tuesday, the most you would charge when the town is full, and what your starting rules should do. The name renames your property, and the turnover cost only shapes the floor question. The lowest rate becomes every room type's floor, and the highest becomes the ceiling of each room type whose rates read so far fit under it. A room type whose own floor or ceiling rules an answer out keeps its number, and the card names it. The last answer picks your starter rules: copies of the raises and cuts you already make, or rules that look for money left on the table. Careful: saving the floor, ceiling or last card again puts your saved floor back on every room type, over any floor set since.

The questions come after you press **Hold My Hand**. Each one is a card. Across the top you see "A few quick questions · 1 of 5 · all optional" and a **Skip the rest →** link. Under the cards sits the import's progress bar, because your history is being read while you answer.

Every card has a **Skip this question** link. A money card shows a **Continue** button once you have typed a number above zero. Press it, or press Enter in the box. While an answer saves, the button reads "Saving…".

Money amounts show your property's currency: "$" for US dollars, otherwise the currency code and a space, for example "EUR ". Whatever you type is rounded to two decimal places.

The card asks "Did we get your property's name right?" and shows the name MAYA read from your property system. Leave it and press **Looks right**, or type a better one.

A name you type wins. It renames the property everywhere in MAYA, and a later read of your system never puts the old name back.

If another property on MAYA already uses that name, the card says the name is already taken and suggests adding your city or neighbourhood.

"Ballpark: what does it cost you to turn over a room?" Cleaning, laundry, utilities and supplies for one night's stay, as a rough number. The placeholder suggests 35.

This number does one thing: it sets where the next question starts. It is saved with your answers and nothing else reads it. It is not a floor, and it never reaches a price.

The card reads "Picture a Tuesday in your slowest month. You're at 10% occupancy." and offers a rate: would you take this much for a room tonight, from someone walking in off the street? Two buttons: **I'd take $50** (the amount changes) and **Too low**.

The first offer is a little above your turnover cost ($40 if you skipped that question), and each **Too low** raises it by at least 15%, rounded up to the next $5. After two **Too low** presses a reminder appears: a night like this would otherwise earn nothing, so anything above your turnover cost is profit.

If you would rather name the number, press **I'll just type my floor**. The card changes to "What's your true floor?" with a money box.

A $35 turnover cost offers $50, then $60, $70 and $85.

A room type whose ceiling is already under your answer keeps its own floor, because a floor can't be above the ceiling. Every other room type takes your answer, and the card stays up and names each room type that did not, for example: "Your floor of $200 wasn't saved for Deluxe King: its ceiling is $150, and a floor can't be above the ceiling." Type a lower floor, or skip the question to leave it that way.

When you answer again and a ceiling answer is already saved, a floor at or above it is refused with "Your floor price needs to be below your ceiling price of $300." (your ceiling in place of $300). Nothing is saved and the card stays.

**Careful** · Your answer goes to every room type that counts as a room, the Suite included. If your room types need different floors, answer with your cheapest room type's floor and [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Floor%20and%20ceiling) to raise the others. Once you have answered, the import fills in only ceilings.

The card opens "Now the fun one" and asks you to imagine the biggest concert of the year next door, with every room in town gone. What is the most you would charge for a night? The card also asks you to bear in mind the highest you have ever actually sold a room for, as a reference point. It does not show that number. The placeholder suggests 450.

What the answer does: it becomes the ceiling of each room type whose highest rate read so far is at or below your number. A ceiling is the highest price MAYA will publish for that room type. A room type whose rates read so far go above your number keeps its ceiling as it was.

"Read so far" matters, because you answer while the import is still reading. The check uses only the rates read by the moment you save, and a room type with no rates read yet gets your ceiling.

Answer with a number above your floor. A ceiling at or under the floor you gave is refused with "Your ceiling price needs to be above your floor price of $80." (your floor in place of $80). Nothing is saved and the card stays, so type a higher number or skip the question.

A room type whose own floor is above your answer keeps its ceiling, because a ceiling can't be below the floor. Every other room type that fits takes your answer, and the card stays up and names each room type that did not, for example: "Your ceiling of $150 wasn't saved for Suite: its floor is $180, and a ceiling can't be below the floor." Type a higher number, or skip the question to leave it that way.

The last card asks "Last one: what should your starting rules do?", with two choices:

- **My pricing works, automate it** ("Copy the raises and cuts I already make, so I don't have to touch it every day."). Your starter rules copy the moves your own rates made in the past year: a raise once a night is filling up, a cut (or raise) for last-minute bookings on emptier nights, sized like yours. If nothing of yours can be copied, you get the usual five booking speed rules, and the review says why.
My pricing works, automate it

- **Find money I'm leaving on the table** ("Look in my own bookings for nights I could have priced higher."). You get the five booking speed rules, with bigger raises if many of your nights were already 90% booked two weeks out, and a raise for nights more than 80% booked if your rates stayed flat on them.

Skip it and you get the five booking speed rules as they are. [Your starter rules](@27) has each set, what in your bookings it reads and the exact limits.
Find money I'm leaving on the table

Saving it does one more thing: it writes your saved floor and ceiling answers to your room types again, as if you had answered those questions again. Your floor goes back on every active room type that counts as a room, and your ceiling on every such room type whose rates fit under it. The first time through, that repeats what questions 3 and 4 wrote.

- **Skip this question** moves to the next card and saves nothing for that one.
- **Skip the rest →** ends the questions from any card.
- After the last card, or after **Skip the rest →**, MAYA opens the review if the first results are in and there is something to look at. Otherwise it opens the progress page, which moves you on by itself.

You can reopen the questions any time after your property is connected at maya-rms.com/onboarding/questions. The cards do not show your earlier answers (the name card shows the property's current name). A new answer replaces the old one.

Saving the floor card, the ceiling card or the last card writes both your saved answers again: your floor onto every active room type that counts as a room, and your ceiling onto every such room type whose rates fit under it, over whatever limits they had. Types unticked as rooms are left alone. A room type that cannot take them (its ceiling under the floor, or its floor over the ceiling) keeps the floor and ceiling it had. The floor card names such a room type for your floor, and the ceiling card for your ceiling. When a card writes your other saved answer again, a room type that cannot take that one is not named again.

If a save fails you see "Couldn't save that" with an invitation to try again. Your earlier answers are unaffected. If your answer was saved but one room type's save failed, the card names it, for example "Your floor wasn't saved for Deluxe King. Try again in a moment."

**Not yet** · The questions do not set a floor or ceiling per room type, per night or per season, and there is no floor and ceiling editor yet. After the import there are three ways to change one: [a suggestion card](@29) for a room type still at MAYA's default ($1.00 for a floor, $99,999.99 for a ceiling), answering these questions again (every room type at once), or [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Floor%20and%20ceiling) for one room type.

**Example: Sam answers the questions at The Harbour Inn**

The name card shows "Harbour Inn", the name Cloudbeds holds. Sam types "The Harbour Inn" and presses **Looks right**. Sam types 35 for the turnover cost and sees the first offer, $50. Two presses of **Too low** take it to $60, then $70. Sam has a number in mind for a Standard on a dead night, so Sam presses **I'll just type my floor** and types 80. Every room type gets an $80 floor. Sam skips the ceiling question, so the import sets the Standard, Deluxe and Suite ceilings from their own rates: $300, $400 and $600. On the last question, the bar under the card reads "First results ready. Importing older years", so the usual five starter rules are already built. Sam picks the first card, "My pricing works", and the five are swapped for two rules copied from the inn's own rates: a raise once a night is more than 70% booked, and a cut for last-minute bookings on nights under half booked.

The review is two short screens, and the first checks your data: closures, room types that may not be rooms, duplicate room types, rates that look like typos, stays with no rate, and stays that point at deleted room types.
