Answer a card to confirm or dismiss it, or skip it and come back later. Only one card reports something already done for you: hiding an empty duplicate room type. You can undo it on the card. The second screen has the room count strip (where room types that are certainly not bedrooms arrive unticked), your starter rules and the go-live button.

The review opens on its own at the end of [the five questions](@25), or from the progress page once there is something to look at. It also opens from the dashboard banner (below), and after **Get suggestions from my data** on the **Rules** tab. You can open it directly at maya-rms.com/onboarding/review.

The cards come from the history import. MAYA reads your history twice on a first import: once after the first three years are in, and again once every year is in. If the review is open when the second read finishes, the cards refresh: one can be sharpened, added or taken away.

Anyone on the property can open the review and read it. Answering a card needs a Revenue Manager, General Manager or Hotel Admin. Below that, pressing any card button shows "Only a Revenue Manager or above can answer this.", and the card stays.

The first screen is headed "First: does this match reality?". It appears only when there are data-check cards waiting. Each card is a question with two buttons, or a single **Got it** when there is nothing to answer.

At the bottom, **Continue to recommendations**. The small print under it says that anything you skip stays available later. That is true: an unanswered card waits for you.

MAYA found at least 14 days in a row with no rooms booked, with the property clearly open in the 30 days before and the 30 days after. Up to three short interruptions (a stray booking, a brief reopening of 14 days or fewer) are bridged into one closure. The stretch before your first ever booking is not a closure, and neither is a gap that runs up to today.

The card shows the two dates and how many straight days it found. Buttons: **Yes, we were closed** and **No, we were open**.

- **Confirm**: those dates are recorded as a closed period for the whole property. From then on they are left out of every comparison MAYA makes: they are never one of a night's similar past nights, and they play no part in how your seasons are read.
Confirm

- **Dismiss**: MAYA never asks about those dates again.

A closure changes nothing about future nights. Your rules still run on every night in the window, closed or not. To keep a future night off sale, close it in your property system.
Dismiss

The same closure at the same time of year in at least two different years (starts within 21 days of each other) becomes one seasonal card, labelled like "mid-December to mid-February" or "all of August". The card says in how many different years the closure appears. The years need not be back to back. Buttons: **Yes, that's our season** and **No, we were open**.

Confirming records every instance it found. When older years reveal more instances of a confirmed season, they are added without asking again. After a **Get suggestions from my data** run, new instances are proposed as a card instead. Dismissing a season means none of its years is asked about again.

Property systems list every bookable space as a room type: event rooms, spa slots, courts, parking. MAYA asks about a type when one of two things is true:

- its name does not read like a bedroom (words like parking, boardroom, meeting, treatment, or a word like spa, court or hall with no bedroom word beside it), or
- it has at least 20 bookings, every one exactly one night, while your property's typical stay is two nights or longer.

A type that is a tiny share of your bookings (under half a percent) at an unusual rate is mentioned as extra weight, never as the reason on its own.

Buttons: **Not a room**, which takes the type out of your counts, and **It's a real room**.

- **Not a room**: the type leaves your sellable occupancy, your RevPAR (revenue per available room: a night's room revenue divided by your rooms, which sets the calendar's colours) and the room count you are billed for. A rule that changes it still prices it.
Not a room

- **It's a real room**: the type is recorded as a room, in your name, and MAYA does not ask again.

Either answer needs a Revenue Manager or higher. Below that, the button shows "Only a Revenue Manager or above can answer this." and the card stays. You can change the answer any time on the **PMS** tab under **Room types**. Read [Room types and rooms out of service](@52).
It's a real room

Two active room types shared the same name once punctuation and capitals are ignored, and one of them had no bookings at all. On a first import MAYA hides the empty one straight away, so it does not sit in your occupancy as rooms you cannot sell. The card records this and adds a line beginning "We already did this for you".

Buttons: **Good call** keeps it hidden. **Undo** makes the type active again.

After a **Get suggestions from my data** run the empty duplicate is only proposed, and nothing is hidden until you confirm.

**Careful** · Once you have pressed **Good call** there is no button to bring the type back, and a later read of your system does not reactivate it. If you need it back, email us.

For a room type with at least 30 nights on record, its single highest rate is far above what the room type normally sells for: about ten times its usual rate or more. The card names the highest rate and the usual (median) rate. Usually it is a test booking or a mistyped rate.

**Example: The exact test, for the curious**

The highest rate must be above 10 times the room type's median rate. Once the type has 200 nights or more, it must be above the larger of 10 times the median and 3 times the rate that 99 in 100 of its stays sold under.

Buttons: **Probably a typo** and **Those are real**. Either answer is recorded and changes nothing else. MAYA never builds a ceiling from a room type's single highest rate.

A mistyped high rate can still matter in one way. The ceiling you gave in the five questions only goes on a room type whose highest rate read so far fits under it. If Suite's $9,999 typo had already been read when you saved a $600 ceiling, your $600 does not go on Suite, whichever button you press here. (If the typo was read only after you saved, Suite got your ceiling like the others.) The **Guardrails** column on the **Rate Simulator** tab shows the ceiling each room type has. Email us with the room type and the ceiling you want. Read [Floors and ceilings](@28).

More than 2% of the stay nights MAYA imported came through with no rate. Usually comps or gaps in the data. The card says how many. One button, **Got it**. There is nothing to fix, and the card shows "$" whatever your currency.
Some stay nights point at room types your property system no longer has. They still count in your history totals but cannot be priced. The card says how many. One button, **Got it**.

The second screen is headed "Recommendations from your data". The heading's small print promises rules and guardrails your history supports. On a first import there are no cards here: the starter rules and your floors and ceilings are built for you (below), and the box reads "No new recommendations this time." Suggestion cards appear on this screen only after **Get suggestions from my data**. Read [Getting suggestions later](@29).

When nothing at all is waiting, the box reads "Nothing left to review" and says your data looks clean. Under it, in small text, "N items already handled" counts the cards you have answered.

Then, in order:
1. **The room count strip** (next section).
The room count strip

2. **Your starter rules**, in a box headed "While you were here, we built your first pricing rules", with the **Turn them on for real** button. The box lists the starter rules your import built, and it stays after anyone on your team runs **Get suggestions from my data**. Read [Your starter rules](@27) and [Going live](@55).
Your starter rules

The strip reads "We're counting 4 room types as rooms" and asks whether anything there is not one. One chip per active room type, with its name and how many units it has. A chip is ticked once the type counts as a room, and the number in the question counts the ticked chips.

Ticked types are what MAYA divides by for sellable occupancy, and what it counts for the revenue per room behind the calendar colours and for the room count you are billed for. Untick anything nobody sleeps in. An unticked type is still priced if a rule changes it.

- Room types whose name is certainly not a bedroom (parking, boardroom, meeting, treatment and the like) arrive unticked, as MAYA's proposal. Tick one to say it is a room.

- A tick saves at once. There is no confirm, and nothing here holds up **Finish**.
- Ticking or unticking needs a Revenue Manager or higher. Below that you see "This needs Revenue Manager access or higher on this property." On a live property a change re-prices every night of the window from the next cycle, nearest nights first.
- Thirty changes in ten minutes is the limit, per person. The same thirty also cover prices you type or clear by hand and rooms you take out of service in those ten minutes. Past it you see "That's a lot of room-type changes at once. Give it a minute and try again."
- If a tick fails to save it snaps back and you see "That didn't save" with an invitation to try again.

A blue banner appears at the top of the dashboard when your property is connected, the first results are in, there are cards waiting, and you have not finished the review since the newest card arrived. Its heading says your booking history has been read, the line under it says how many things are worth a quick look, and it ends with the link **Review →**. It shows once per page load. Pressing **Finish** (as a Revenue Manager or higher) clears it until a newer card arrives, for example from the second read of your history.

You can leave the review at any point and come back through the banner or the review's own address.

Answered closure cards, "Is X actually a room?" cards and duplicate cards are not asked again. Cards about typos, $0 rates and deleted room types can come back after **Get suggestions from my data**, because each read is a fresh look. A typo card can also come back at the second read of your first import, if the older years hold an even higher rate for that room type.

What you can still change:

| Card | Change it later? |
|---|---|
| Is X actually a room? | Yes, on the **PMS** tab under **Room types** |
| Were you closed / normally closed | Not yet. Email us |
| Hid duplicate room type | Only before you press **Good call**. After that, email us |
| Rates look like typos | Nothing to change. The answer only records your view |
| $0 rates, deleted room types | Nothing to change |

If a card answers itself with "Finding was already resolved", a colleague or another tab got there first, and the list refreshes. If it says "Only a Revenue Manager or above can answer this.", your role is below Revenue Manager, so the card cannot be answered from your login and it stays. Ask a Revenue Manager or above to answer it. Read [Messages explained](@104).

If your property has about two months of booking history or more, and no rules yet, MAYA adds starter rules during the import. Which ones depends on your answer to the last of the five questions. With no answer, five booking speed rules: two that cut a night booking slower than similar nights had, and three that raise a night booking faster. "My pricing works" gets rules that copy the raises and cuts your own rates made in the past year. "Find money I'm leaving on the table" gets the five with bigger raises where your nights filled early, and can add a raise for nearly full nights. They start switched on, in simulation, so they change nothing in your system until you go live. Turn any of them off, or delete it, from the **Rules** tab.

On the review, a green box headed "While you were here, we built your first pricing rules" lists each rule with a sentence about what it does, then the **Turn them on for real** button. If you picked "My pricing works" and there was nothing of yours to copy, a line under the heading says so. Read [Going live](@55) for that button. The box stays on the review after anyone on your team runs **Get suggestions from my data**, and so do the rules.

After that they live on the **Rules** tab like any rule you build yourself, with a **Fired** count, an **On** / **Off** switch and a **Delete** button. Every change they make is written in the **Change Log** tab with the rule's name.

These are the starter rules when you did not answer the last question. "Find money I'm leaving on the table" gets the same five, with bigger raises when your nights filled early. "My pricing works" gets them only when nothing of yours could be copied.

Each is a [booking speed](@34) rule. Booking speed compares how many bookings a night received recently with how many similar past nights had received at the same point before arrival, and reads as one of seven levels from Stalled to Surging. The **Conditions** column on the **Rules** tab shows each rule like this:

| Name | Conditions, as the Rules tab shows them (each begins "booking speed") | Price change |
|---|---|---|
| Slow-date rescue | at most Much Slower Than Normal (past month), then waits 1 week | -15% |
| Slow-date trim | Slower Than Normal (past month), then waits 1 week | -7% |
| Warm-date bump | at least Faster Than Normal (past month), then waits 3 days | +10% |
| Hot-week surge | at least Much Faster Than Normal (past week), then waits 2 days | +25% |
| Sudden-spike catcher | at least Surging (past day), then waits 1 day | +25% |
"At most Much Slower Than Normal" means Much Slower or Stalled. "Slower Than Normal" on its own means exactly that level. "At least Faster Than Normal" means Faster, Much Faster or Surging.

When a night is booking far behind similar nights (Much Slower Than Normal or Stalled, over the past month), the rule cuts it 15%. It then waits a week, counts only the bookings made in the full days since the newest cut still on the night by itself or a stronger rule, and cuts again if those are still that far behind. MAYA asks you once three of its cuts are on the same night.

When a night is booking a little behind similar nights (exactly Slower Than Normal, over the past month), the rule trims it 7%. It checks again a week after each trim, counting only the bookings made in the full days since the newest cut still on the night by itself or a stronger rule such as Slow-date rescue, and trims again if those are still behind.

When a night is booking ahead of similar nights (Faster Than Normal or more, over the past month), the rule raises it 10%. It waits 3 days, then raises again only if the bookings made since the newest raise still on the night, by itself or a stronger rule, are ahead of what a similar night gets in a whole month. If cancellations mean the rule is no longer true, the raise comes back off.

When a night's past week runs much faster than similar nights had at the same point (Much Faster Than Normal or more), the rule raises it 25%. It can raise again every 2 days while new bookings keep coming that fast, and MAYA asks you once three of its raises are on the same night.

When bookings pour in for a night within a single day (Surging, over the past day), the rule raises it 25%, and can raise again each day while the rush lasts. Your ceiling is the cap, and MAYA asks you once three of its raises are on the same night.

MAYA reads your past year of bookings, night by night, and copies the raises and cuts you made on top of your own rate. Each booking's rate is compared with what the same room type sold for on the same night to its early guests: those who booked a week or more ahead, while the night was under 40% booked. Whatever weekday, weekend and season differences your own rates hold are already in the rate every rule starts from, so comparing within the same night leaves them out and copies only the moves you made as a night filled up or got close.

For each booking, MAYA also counts how full the night already was: the rooms booked for it on earlier days, among bookings still on record, over the rooms of the room types that count as rooms.

It looks for two moves:

- **Filling-up raise.** Guests who booked once the night was more than a certain share booked paid more than its early guests. MAYA reads the bookings in steps of 10 points (more than 40% booked, more than 50%, and so on up to more than 90%). A step counts once it has 8 bookings or more. The raise starts at the lowest step where guests paid at least 5% more, as long as no higher step that counts shows less. Its size is what guests paid, in the middle, once the night was past that point. The rule: **Sellable occupancy (%)** **Greater than** that step, raise by that percent.
Filling-up raise

- **Last-minute cut** (or **Last-minute raise**). Guests who booked fewer than 7 days ahead, while the night was still under half booked, paid at least 5% less (or more) than its early guests. If only bookings fewer than 3 days ahead show it, the window is 3 days. The rule: **Booking window (days to stay)** **Less than** 7 (or 3) and **Sellable occupancy (%)** **Less than** 50, cut (or raise) by that percent.

A move needs at least 20 bookings over at least 10 nights behind it. A raise bigger than 50% or a cut bigger than 40% is left out, because a gap that size is more likely a different rate plan than a move you made. Sizes are rounded to a whole percent. Each rule's sentence on the review says how many of your nights showed it and what guests paid.
Last-minute cut

Each move is read on Friday and Saturday nights and on the other nights. If both show the same move, at the same step or window and within 3 points of each other, one rule covers every night. If they differ, each gets its own rule, and its name ends in "(Fri and Sat)" or "(Sun to Thu)": that rule applies only on those nights. If only one of them shows the move, only that one gets a rule. If neither has enough bookings on its own but all nights together do, one rule covers every night. The Rules tab does not show a rule's days, so the name is where you see them.

One raise step only. If you raise in several steps, you get one rule at the point your raises start, sized at the middle of them.

If no move of 5% or more shows up across at least 10 nights, your starter rules are the usual five. The review says so under its heading: "In the past year of your bookings, no raise or cut of 5% or more showed up across at least 10 nights, so there was nothing of yours to copy. These are the usual five starting rules."

You get the five booking speed rules, with two changes that depend on your past year:

- **Bigger raises when your nights filled early.** If at least 10 of your nights, and at least 1 in 10 of the nights read, were already 90% booked two weeks or more before arrival, the three raise rules go up a step: Warm-date bump raises 15% instead of 10%, and Hot-week surge and Sudden-spike catcher raise 30% instead of 25%. Their sentence on the review ends by saying how many nights filled that early. The two cuts stay as they are.
Bigger raises when your nights filled early

- **Nearly-full raise.** If guests who booked once a night was more than 80% booked paid within 2% of what its early guests paid (at least 20 bookings over at least 10 nights), and no filling-up raise shows in your bookings, a sixth rule is added: **Sellable occupancy (%)** **Greater than** 80, raise 10%. It is a standard rule like the ones above.

If neither shows up, you get the five as they are.
Nearly-full raise

The import often finishes before you reach the last question. When you answer it then, MAYA swaps the starter rules for the ones your answer calls for, if all of these hold:

- the starter rules on your property are exactly the ones the import built: none switched off, deleted or edited, and no other rule added,
- nobody has pressed **Get suggestions from my data** since the import,
- your property is still in simulation,
- you are a Revenue Manager or higher.

The old ones are removed with every change they made, as **Delete** would, and the new ones are switched on. The box on the review then shows the new ones. Answering again later swaps again, under the same conditions. Otherwise nothing changes, and your answer is used when anyone presses **Get suggestions from my data**. Read [Getting suggestions later](@29).

This section is about the booking speed rules.

A booking with several rooms counts once. A 20-room wedding booking is one booking for booking speed (and 20 booked rooms for occupancy). Only bookings in the room types a rule measures are counted.

Each rule waits after it adjusts a night, per night and per room type. Once the wait is over, the rule does not count the same bookings twice:

- A rule that raises counts only bookings made since the newest raise still on the night by itself or a stronger rule. A stronger rule changes the price by more, and at the same change it watches the faster speed. So Sudden-spike catcher's raise restarts Hot-week surge's count and Warm-date bump's, but Warm-date bump's raise never restarts theirs.
- The three rules that raise all raise on a fast pace, so after a raise the bookings since have to beat what a similar night gets in the rule's whole window.

- When some of the bookings behind a change cancel but bookings made since keep the rule true, the change stays and the count still runs from when it was made. Counting starts again only when a price changes.

So one burst of bookings raises a night once, by the strongest rule it makes true. A weaker rule steps in on top only when the bookings since that raise keep it true on their own. A cut rule keeps cutting a night that stays behind, and a raise rule keeps raising while real demand keeps coming.

A price you type on a night takes its adjustments off and starts the wait over from that price. After the wait, the rule reads its whole window again. Read [Setting a price yourself](@50).

Every starter rule has its undo box ticked. A raise made by Warm-date bump, Hot-week surge or Sudden-spike catcher comes off when bookings it counted cancel and the rule is no longer true for the night: the bookings it counted that are still booked no longer reach the rule's speed, and the bookings made since do not keep it true either. The change log then reads: Cancellations meant "Warm-date bump" was no longer true, so its 10% raise came off. A saved rule's box cannot be changed. For raises that cancellations never take off, add the rule again yourself with the box unticked. Read [Changing a rule](@42#changing-a-rule).

A Filling-up raise or Nearly-full raise comes off when cancellations take the night back to its step or below, and goes on again if bookings bring it back over. A Last-minute cut comes off once the night is half booked.

A booking speed cut never comes off for cancellations, because guests cancelling only make a slow night slower. A night Slow-date rescue cut stays cut until you set a price yourself (in MAYA, or by changing the rate in Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations on a night MAYA has sent to), delete the rule, or the night passes. Turning the rule off freezes the cut in place.

Once three of one of the booking speed rules' changes are on the same night, an amber banner appears at the top of the dashboard (the Rules that keep adjusting banner). It is headed with a sentence naming the rule and how many of its changes are on the price, such as ""Slow-date rescue" would have 3 cuts on each of 3 nights." While you are in simulation it says "would have". Once you are live it says "has".

The banner asks you, night by night: keep adjusting, or stop for this night. Until you answer, the rule keeps going. Read [Rules that keep adjusting](@43).

The starter rules measure and change every room type that counted as a room when they were built. A meeting room or court you had unticked is left out of both. They apply every day of the week, with no date range, except a copied rule whose name ends in "(Fri and Sat)" or "(Sun to Thu)".

A room type your system adds later is not added to them. Build a rule of your own for it.

When two booking speed or pickup rules both want to act on the same night and room type, only one fires per run: the stronger one. The bigger change to the price comes first, then, at the same change, a rule that watches booking speed, and of two that do, the faster speed (the slower one for cuts), then the pickup count harder to meet. Only after those do starter rules rank above rules you build, in this order: Sudden-spike catcher, Hot-week surge, Warm-date bump, Slow-date rescue, Slow-date trim. So a rule of yours that raises 30% fires before Hot-week surge's 25%.

Filling-up raise, Last-minute cut and Nearly-full raise are standard rules, which never compete: each applies whenever its conditions hold, on top of whatever else applies.

MAYA builds them once per first import, and only when all of these hold:

- at least 60 past nights on record had a booking (about two months of history),
- the property has no rules at all, not even one switched off (someone built a rule before the import finished, or an earlier import left one),
- at least one room type counts as a room,
- the history import ran at all. Mews has no import yet, so no starter rules.

The rules copied for "My pricing works", and the checks for "Find money", read the past year only: nights from 365 days ago up to yesterday. On a very large property they read its newest nights, up to about 50,000 booked room-nights. Once your property is live, they count only bookings made two or more days before MAYA first tried to send a price to your system, because a later booking may carry MAYA's price rather than yours.

**Good to know** · A night with fewer than five similar past nights reads at most one step from Normal, so Slow-date rescue, Hot-week surge and Sudden-spike catcher stay quiet on it. Slow-date trim and Warm-date bump can still fire. A night with no usable history reads nothing, and no booking speed rule fires on it.

- The **On** / **Off** switch on the **Rules** tab. Off freezes what the rule has done: the changes it made stay on those nights, and it makes no new ones. On again picks up from the next run.
- **Delete** opens a dialog headed with the rule's name. **Delete Rule and Undo Its Changes** removes the rule and every price change it made, so the next run prices those nights as if it had never existed. **Turn It Off and Keep Its Changes** is the switch, from the dialog. Deleting cannot be undone.

You need to be a Revenue Manager or higher for either.

A Filling-up raise, Last-minute cut or Nearly-full raise for every night can be rebuilt exactly in the rule builder, from the conditions above. One limited to "(Fri and Sat)" or "(Sun to Thu)" cannot, because the builder has no weekday choice.

To rebuild a booking speed one your way, the rule builder's **Speed** dropdown, **Measured over** and **Then waits (advanced)** can set the same condition, window and wait as four of the five. Slow-date trim is the exception. The builder turns a slow level into "at most", so the closest you can build is "at most Slower Than Normal", which also fires on Much Slower and Stalled nights. When everything else is equal, a rule you build ranks below the starter rules you keep, so a rebuilt copy can wait behind one where the original would not.

**Good to know** · A starter rule can be edited like any rule: **Edit** on its row opens it in the rule builder, to change its number, its wait or its room types. Slow-date trim's "exactly Slower Than Normal" stays as it is unless you pick another speed. Read [Change a rule](@72).

An illustration with made-up numbers, not your property. Each example assumes at least five similar past nights.

**Example: Slow-date rescue on a Tuesday six weeks out**

Similar Tuesdays at The Harbour Inn had about 20 bookings in the month before this point. This one has 8. That reads Much Slower Than Normal (6 to 10 would, and 5 or fewer would read Stalled, which the rule also fires on). Standard drops 15%, from $150 to $127.50. A week later, MAYA counts only the bookings made in the 6 full days after the day of the cut, up to yesterday, and compares them with the same days of the similar Tuesdays. If those still read Much Slower or Stalled, it cuts again, to $108.38. At three cuts on the night the amber banner asks whether to carry on.

Similar nights had about 5 bookings in the month. This one has 9: Faster Than Normal (10 or more would read Much Faster or Surging, and the rule fires on those too). Standard rises 10%, from $150 to $165. Three days later MAYA counts only the bookings made since the raise. If those alone read Faster Than Normal against the 5 a similar night gets in a whole month, it raises again, to $181.50. If 4 of the 9 cancel, the 5 left read Normal, and unless bookings made since keep the rule true, the raise comes off.

**Example: Hot-week surge on a Saturday**

Similar Saturdays had about 5 bookings in the week at this point. This one has 10: Much Faster Than Normal (10 to 17 would). Suite rises 25%, from $300 to $375. Two days later the rule counts only the bookings made since the raise. It raises again only if those alone read Much Faster against the 5 a similar Saturday gets in a whole week.

A night that usually gets about 1 booking in a day gets 5 today: Surging. Standard rises 25%, from $150 to $187.50. Tomorrow the rule counts only the bookings made since its raise. Hot-week surge now counts only those too, because Sudden-spike catcher is the stronger rule: the same 25%, at the faster speed. A raise by Hot-week surge earlier today would not have changed what Sudden-spike catcher counts. If the bookings since read Surging, its 25% stacks on top, up to the ceiling.

A floor is the lowest price MAYA will publish for a room type, and a ceiling is the highest. Each night's price is held between them, and a price you type outside them is refused. Every room type starts at 1.00 and 99,999.99 in your property's currency, which stop nothing in most currencies. If a room type sells above 99,999.99 (in yen or rupiah, say), set a real ceiling before you go live. Real ones come from your answers to the five questions, from your own rates during the import, or from a suggestion card you accept or change.

The **Change Log** tab says so when it happens: "That would have gone past your $300.00 ceiling for Standard, so it stopped there." or "That would have dropped under your $80.00 floor for Standard, so it stopped there." Amounts are in your property's currency.

A limit also stops rules from piling up beyond it. A booking speed or pickup rule that raises does not fire on a night already at its ceiling, and one that cuts does not fire on a night already at its floor. It starts no wait, and the attempt does not count towards the three-times question. When the night's price moves back inside the limits, the rule can fire again.

$200, up 10% to $220, then up 25% to $275. The $300 ceiling is not reached, so $275 is published.

Standard's base rate for a Saturday in August is $200. Its ceiling is $300. "Busy nights" raises it 10% to $220. Hot-week surge then raises it 25% to $275. Warm-date bump's 10% on top would be $302.50, so the published price is $300 and the change log says it stopped there. Sudden-spike catcher, which would raise it again, does not fire while the night sits at $300.

The other way: Standard at $150 with an $80 floor. Slow-date rescue cuts 15% four times over four weeks: $127.50, $108.38, $92.12, then $78.30, which is under the floor, so $80.00 is published. A fifth cut does not fire.

There is no settings page that lists floors and ceilings. You meet them in four places:

- The **Rate Simulator** tab's room table has a **Guardrails** column showing each room type's floor and ceiling. Only room types ticked as rooms are listed there. For an unticked type, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Floor%20and%20ceiling) to check its limits.
- The **Change Log** tab, in the sentences above.
- The **Rules that keep adjusting** banner, in a line like "If it keeps cutting, the price can fall to your $80.00 floor for Standard." When the limit is still the default, the line reads "Your ceiling for Suite is still MAYA's $99,999.99 default, so the price can climb that far." with a "?" beside it.
- The manual price editor, when a price you type is outside them.

There are three ways a floor or ceiling gets set, and no editor beyond them.

1. **The five questions.** The lowest rate you would take on a dead Tuesday becomes the floor of every active room type that counts as a room. The most you would charge becomes the ceiling of each such room type whose highest rate read so far fits under it. A type you have unticked as a room (a parking bay, a meeting room), and one nobody has answered for whose name is plainly not a bedroom, keeps its own floor and ceiling, and MAYA sends no price for it unless one of your rules changes it or you type a price for one of its nights. If you answer while the import is still reading, a room type whose higher rates arrive later can keep that ceiling: check the **Guardrails** column once the import is complete, and email us to lift one. Read [The five questions](@25).
The five questions

2. **The import, from your own rates.** Once the first three years are in, and again when the full history is in, MAYA fills in a floor and a ceiling for every room type still at its defaults, using the history numbers in the next section (with the exceptions it lists). This happens without a card. It never overwrites a limit that has already been set.
The import, from your own rates

3. **A suggestion card.** After **Get suggestions from my data** on the **Rules** tab, the review shows a card for each room type still at a default: "Set a floor for "Standard"?" or "Set a ceiling for "Suite"?". The suggested amount sits in a box labelled **Amount to set**. Accept it with the **Set it to 80** button, or type your own number first and the button follows it. **No thanks** leaves the default. Read [Getting suggestions later](@29).

The banner's **Ask MAYA for a floor** and **Ask MAYA for a ceiling** buttons take you to the **Rules** tab, where the suggestions button is.
A suggestion card

During the import, your answers to the five questions are applied first, and then the history numbers below fill whatever is still at a default. On a card, your answer is offered where it fits. For a floor, the number from your history is offered only if you never answered. If your answer does not fit, there is no floor card.

**Floor**

- On a card: your own answer from the five questions, if you gave one.
- Otherwise, a floor of about 40% of what the room type usually sells for. It needs at least 30 nights of history for that room type.
Floor

**Ceiling**

- On a card: your own answer, if you gave one and it sits above nearly all of the room type's past rates. A ceiling lower than that would pin the room type down, so the next line is used instead.
- Otherwise, about one and a half times the room type's normal top rate. It needs at least 200 nights of history for that room type. It is never built on the single highest rate, so one mistyped rate cannot become your ceiling.
Ceiling

A room type whose name or bookings look unlike a bedroom (the same tests as the "Is X actually a room?" card) never gets a floor or ceiling from its own rates, and never gets a floor or ceiling card, even after you confirm it is a real room. It stays at $1.00 and $99,999.99 unless the five questions or an email set one. MAYA also skips a ceiling that would land at or under the floor, and a floor that would land at or above the ceiling.

The rationale on a card tells you which line it came from: "You said the lowest rate you'd accept is $80, so MAYA suggests that as the floor." or "Standard has typically sold for $150 a night, so MAYA suggests a floor of $60."

- A floor must be above 0.
- A ceiling must be at least the floor. A card that would break this is refused with an error. The five questions check it too: a ceiling answer at or under your floor answer is refused, and nothing is saved. An answer that one room type's own floor or ceiling rules out is saved on every other room type, and the card names the room type that kept its number and says why. Read [The five questions](@25).
- One floor and one ceiling per room type. Not per night, per season, per weekday or for weekends.
- Amounts are in your property's currency, to two decimal places. The defaults are plain numbers in your currency too: 1.00 and 99,999.99, whatever the currency.

In most currencies the default ceiling stops nothing. In a currency where a room sells for more than 99,999.99, such as yen, won, rupiah or dong, it does. Until a room type has a real ceiling, any price your base rate and rules reach above 99,999.99 is published at 99,999.99, even when your own rate for the night is higher. A price you type above it is refused. So before you go live, give every room type a real ceiling: answer the ceiling question in the five questions, accept a suggestion card, or [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Ceiling%20in%20my%20currency) with the numbers. The import sets one from your own rates for a room type with 200 nights of history or more.

The limits apply to you too, with one exception.

- A price you type under the floor is refused: "Below this room type's floor of $80.00." Over the ceiling: "Above this room type's ceiling of $300.00." Nothing is saved. Read [Setting a price yourself](@50).
- The exception is 0. A night set to 0 is a comp night. It is saved, no rule raises it, and MAYA does not send 0 to your property system, so you set the night to 0 there yourself. That is why a floor cannot be 0: a comp night is a per-night choice, not a limit.

**Careful** · Saving the floor card, the ceiling card or the last card of the five questions again puts your saved floor back on every active room type that counts as a room at once, over any floor set since. Check the **Guardrails** column in the **Rate Simulator** tab afterwards.

On the **Rules** tab, **Get suggestions from my data** reads your booking history again and compares it with your rules and your floors and ceilings. You get cards on the review screen to accept or reject one by one, and your rules, prices and limits stay as they are until you accept one. It can offer starter rules (which ones follows your answer to the last of the five questions), offer to remove a pickup rule a booking speed rule already covers, offer to move an occupancy rule's threshold, and offer a floor or ceiling for a room type still at its default. You can press it before or after going live, and the go-live button stays on the review.

On the **Rules** tab, beside the **Pricing Rules** heading, sits **Get suggestions from my data** (with a handshake symbol in front of it). Pressing it opens a small panel headed "Here's exactly what happens". The panel says MAYA re-reads your booking history and compares it against your current rules and price guardrails, that nothing changes by itself, and that you approve or reject each suggestion individually. Two buttons: the one beginning "Sounds good" starts the read, and **Never mind** closes the panel.

While the read runs, the button turns into a pulsing dot with the line "Reading your history…". MAYA is reading your bookings again and counting. The tab checks on the read every few seconds, so you can leave it open: when the read ends, the button changes by itself.

When a read stops before it finishes, the plain button comes back with a line beside it that says so, and the line stays until a new read starts. A read tries again by itself the way [the history import](@23#import-stopped) does, so the line can say "Your last read paused. We've been told, and it tries again by itself around 3:40 PM." Once it has stopped for good it says "Your last read stopped. We've been told.", or "Your last read stopped. Email us and we'll restart it." when nothing reached us. "Your last read stopped because your property system is no longer connected." means the connection went away: reconnect, then press the button again.

- A Revenue Manager, General Manager or Hotel Admin. Anyone else sees "You need Revenue Manager access or higher to run this."
- A property with a subscription in good standing. Otherwise: "This property's subscription is not active, so MAYA has paused work on it."
- A property with a connected system. Otherwise the message begins "Connect your property system first".
- Five runs per 15 minutes per property. Past that, a message asks you to let the last read finish before starting another. Read [Messages explained](@104).
- One read at a time. If a read is already running (yours, a colleague's, or the first import), pressing the button joins it rather than starting another. If that read is the first import, it finishes as a first import, with no suggestion cards. Press the button again once it is complete. Either way the press counts towards the five runs.

Mews has no history import yet, so on a Mews property the button is greyed out, with the note "Not available for Mews yet. MAYA can't read its booking history." beside it. [Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Suggestions%20on%20Mews) if you would like suggestions for a Mews property. Read [The history import](@23).

**Good to know: Before or after going live** · Either is fine. A read the button starts points the review at the new cards, and the box with your starter rules and **Turn them on for real** stays on the review's second screen.

- Closures are proposed on cards, never recorded on their own. New instances of a season you confirmed earlier are proposed too.
- A duplicate room type with no bookings is proposed, not hidden.
- Cards about rates that look like typos, stays with a $0 rate and stays that point at deleted room types can come back, because each read is a fresh look.
- Room types are never unticked as rooms by a re-read. A type whose name or bookings look unlike a bedroom gets an "Is X actually a room?" card instead.
- Your existing rules and limits are left exactly as they are.

The review reopens with anything from the list above on its first screen, and the suggestion cards on its second. Read [Checking what MAYA found](@26).

Which rules are offered follows your answer to the last of the five questions, as the starter rules do. Read [Your starter rules](@27).

- **No answer.** The five booking speed starter rules, offered only when your property has no booking speed rule at all. A booking speed rule that is switched off counts as one, so pausing the starter rules for the season does not bring five fresh copies. When you have none, all five are offered, one card each, with the rule's own sentence and a line saying nothing currently watches for nights falling behind (or ahead of) their normal pace.
No answer

- **"My pricing works".** The rules copied from your own rates over the past year, such as "Filling-up raise" and "Last-minute cut". On a property that is live, only bookings made two or more days before MAYA first tried to send a price count, so MAYA's own price changes are never copied back as yours. A Filling-up raise is offered only when no rule of yours has a **Sellable occupancy (%)** **Greater than** condition, and a Last-minute cut or raise only when none has a **Booking window (days to stay)** **Less than** condition. Switched-off rules count. The card's first line reads "Your own rates already made this move, and no rule of yours makes it yet.", followed by the rule's sentence saying what your bookings showed. When nothing of yours can be copied, you get the five booking speed cards instead, as with no answer.
"My pricing works"

- **"Find money I'm leaving on the table".** The five booking speed rules, with the bigger raises when your nights filled early, offered only when you have no booking speed rule. And "Nearly-full raise" when your rates stayed flat on nearly full nights, offered only when no rule of yours has a **Sellable occupancy (%)** **Greater than** condition. Its first line reads "Nothing raises your nearly full nights yet."
"Find money I'm leaving on the table"

Buttons: **Add this rule** and **No thanks**. **Add this rule** first opens the window with the days the rule will change: **Apply price adjustments** or **Skip price adjustments** (**Turn it on** when no price would change), or **Cancel** to leave the card as it is. If the window cannot open, the card says "The window didn't open. Try again." and nothing is saved. Read [Turning a rule on, Apply or Skip](@41). An added rule is on and applies every day with no date range, except a copied rule whose name ends in "(Fri and Sat)" or "(Sun to Thu)", which applies only on those nights. It measures every room type that counts as a room and changes every active room type. Starter rules built at import leave unticked types out altogether. It needs at least 60 past nights with a booking, like the starter rules. Read [Your starter rules](@27).

Offered for a pickup count rule that is switched on when a booking speed rule that is also switched on covers everything it does: the same room types or more, in both the measured and the changed sets, the same days, and the same dates or wider. The card explains that the pickup rule reacts to a fixed booking count, that your booking speed rules already cover the same nights by comparing with your own similar past nights, and that keeping both would stack two price changes on the same bookings.

Three buttons:

- **Remove it** deletes the rule and undoes every price change it made.
- **Turn it off, keep it** switches it off. The changes it made stay, and you can switch it back on from the **Rules** tab.
- **Leave it running** changes nothing.

Offered for a rule that is switched on, has an occupancy condition set to **Greater than**, and has no booking speed or pickup condition, when its threshold sits more than 10 points away from what your own history supports. A booking window condition in the same rule does not stop the card. MAYA compares your threshold with how full your own past nights got. It finds two levels: one that most of your nights stay under, and one that only your busiest nights pass. If your threshold is more than 10 points from the nearer of the two, the card says your rule fires above X% occupancy but your history suggests Y% is where nights become scarce, and offers to move the trigger from X% to Y%.

Buttons: **Make that change** and **Leave it as is**. **Make that change** is an edit of that one number, and the rule keeps its name, its other settings and its fire count. On a rule that is on, the window with the days opens first, with **Save changes** as its one button when no price would change (if it cannot open, the card says "The window didn't open. Try again." and nothing is saved). With **Apply price adjustments**, from the next run the rule applies only to nights above the new number, so nights between the old and new numbers lose its change (or gain it, if the number went down). With **Skip price adjustments**, the days the window showed keep their prices until the rule stops being true on a day and then becomes true again, and every other night works as with Apply. On a rule that is off, the new number is saved at once. Read [Change a rule](@72).

Never tuned: a rule whose occupancy condition uses **Less than**, a rule with no occupancy condition (a booking window rule on its own, say), any rule with a booking speed or pickup condition, and a rule named "Filling-up raise" (with or without "(Fri and Sat)" or "(Sun to Thu)") or "Nearly-full raise". Those two names are the ones the rules built from your own bookings for the last question carry, and their threshold came from those bookings. Rename one and it can be tuned like any other rule. A rule that pairs **Greater than** with a booking window condition can be tuned, and the card moves only its occupancy threshold, never the booking window.

Offered for a room type whose floor or ceiling is still at MAYA's default, when there is a number to offer: your answer from the five questions, or enough history (30 nights for a floor, 200 for a ceiling). Room types whose name or bookings look unlike a bedroom never get one, even after you confirm they are rooms.

The defaults are 1.00 for a floor and 99,999.99 for a ceiling, in your property's currency. Only a ceiling of exactly 99,999.99 counts as the default. A ceiling you set yourself, above or below it, never gets a card, so in a currency such as yen a ceiling of 150,000 stays as you set it.

The card gives the reason and a suggested amount in an editable box. Press **Set it to 80** to accept it, or type your own number and the button follows. **No thanks** keeps the default. Read [Floors and ceilings](@28) for where the numbers come from and how to set a limit when no card comes.

Answered cards are counted as "N items already handled" and are not shown again on this read. A later read may ask about typos, $0 rates or deleted room types again, and will offer the rules your answer calls for again while no rule of yours covers them. Press **Finish** or close the page. Read [Checking what MAYA found](@26).

**Not yet** · You cannot ask for one kind of suggestion on its own, or run the read on a schedule. There are no suggestions for a booking window threshold, for occupancy rules that use **Less than**, or for a rule's percentage. And a suggestion never edits a rule's room types or dates.

**Example: Priya runs it at The Harbour Inn**

Priya, the Revenue Manager, built "Busy nights" at Greater than 60. She also built a pickup rule called "Quick pickup" that raises Standard, Deluxe and Suite (the builder's default: the types that count as rooms) by 10% when a night gains more than 4 room nights in 3 days. The five starter rules are on. She presses **Get suggestions from my data**, then the start button, and moves to the **Calendar** tab while the read runs. Later she opens **Rules** again and the button reads "2 suggestions ready →". The review shows "Tune "Busy nights"?", offering to move the trigger from 60% to 75% because that is where the inn's nights become scarce, and "Remove "Quick pickup"?", because Warm-date bump already measures and changes the same room types on every day. Had she added the Meeting Room to Quick pickup, there would be no removal card, because Warm-date bump leaves the Meeting Room out.

Open the **Rules** tab, click **+ Add a rule**, name it, pick a condition, choose raise or lower and by how much, pick the room types, and click **Add Rule**. A window shows the days the rule will change: click **Apply price adjustments** and the rule is on. While your property is in simulation, MAYA shows what the rule would do without sending anything. After you go live, it sends the prices to Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations. Nothing is sent to Mews yet.

A rule is one sentence you write once: when a night looks like this, change its price by that much. MAYA checks every rule against your bookings on a night within about five minutes of them changing, and on every night up to 395 nights ahead once a day, and writes down what it did in the **Change Log** tab.

Rules live on the **Rules** tab. From the top down you will find:

- the heading **Pricing Rules**, with the **Get suggestions from my data** button beside it
- a filter with three choices, **All**, **Enabled** and **Disabled**
- a closed panel called **How rules behave**, which holds three short animations
- the list of your rules
- the **+ Add a rule** button, which opens the rule builder underneath the list

You need to be a Revenue Manager, General Manager or Hotel Admin on the property to add a rule. A Viewer can open the form, but the save is refused.

**Good to know** · If your property had about two months of booking history when you connected, MAYA built starter rules for you and they are already on the list. Which ones depends on your answer to the last of the five questions. You can build your own beside them, turn any of them off, or delete them. Read [Your starter rules](@27) for what each one does.

We will build a rule called "Busy nights" for The Harbour Inn, a made-up 20-room property: when a night is more than 80% full, raise every room type by 10%.

**1. Open the rule builder**

Go to the **Rules** tab and click **+ Add a rule**. The form opens underneath the list of rules.

**2. Name it**

In **Rule name**, type Busy nights. The name is how you will find the rule in the change log later, so choose words you will recognise in a month.

**3. Set the condition**

Under **Conditions**, one row is already there. Leave **Metric** on **Sellable occupancy (%)**, leave **Compare** on **Greater than**, and leave **Threshold** at 80. Read together, the row says: when more than 80% of the rooms you can sell that night are booked.

Under **Apply to room types**, every room type that counts as a room is already selected. Leave them all on. A type tagged "not a room" (The Harbour Inn's Meeting Room, say) stays out unless you click it.

**6. Add it**

Click **Add Rule**. A window opens with a small calendar of the months ahead, the days the rule will change filled in, and a line such as "12 days will be affected by this rule." Click **Apply price adjustments**. The rule appears in the list with its switch on **On**, and the form clears, ready for the next rule. (**Skip price adjustments** also switches it on, but leaves those days' prices as they are. Read [Turning a rule on, Apply or Skip](@41).)

**Careful** · A new rule is on the moment you add it. If your property is live on Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations, its first price changes go to your system on the next cycle. Nothing is sent to Mews. If you would rather look first, build the rule in the **Rate Simulator** tab instead. A rule saved from there arrives on the Rules tab switched off. Read [Trying rules out in the Rate Simulator](@44).

The list has seven columns: **Name**, **Fired**, **Conditions**, **Room Types**, **Price Change**, **Status**, and a **Delete** button at the end of the row.

| Column | What it shows for "Busy nights" |
|---|---|
| Name | Busy nights |
| Fired | A dash until the rule has acted, then a count such as 3× |
| Conditions | Occupancy above 80% |
| Room Types | Standard, Deluxe, Suite |
| Price Change | +10% |
| Status | On |

The **Fired** count goes up once for every night and room type the rule acts on. So if "Busy nights" raises two Fridays for Standard, Deluxe and Suite, **Fired** reads 6×. A new rule whose condition already holds on many nights can show a big number within minutes: 20 nights across 3 room types is 60×. It keeps counting changes that later come off. The list is sorted with the most fired rule first, then rules that are on before rules that are off, then by name. Read [Turning a rule off, deleting it, or changing it](@42) for the rest of the list.

Open the **Change Log** tab. Each pricing run lists the prices that changed, room type by room type. When "Busy nights" acts on a Standard room at The Harbour Inn, the entry reads:

"Busy nights" raised this night 10%, from $150.00 to $165.00.
It was 85% full, past the 80% mark you set.

In simulation the same entries appear. They show what the rule would have sent. After you go live on Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations, the same entries are what was sent.

Twelve rooms, three out of service, eight booked: 89% sellable occupancy, so a Greater than 80 rule fires.

**Example: Busy nights on three nights at The Harbour Inn**

The Harbour Inn has 20 rooms across Standard (12), Deluxe (6) and Suite (2). "Busy nights" measures all 20 together, because occupancy is worked out over the room types the rule measures.
If two Friday guests cancel, Friday drops to 15 of 20, 75%, and on the next check the raise comes off. Standard goes back to $150.

How much a rule raises or cuts is your choice. There is no right number, and MAYA does not pick one for you. The percent box shows "e.g. 10" until you type, and 10% is $15 on The Harbour Inn's $150 Standard. Three things help you settle on yours:

- **Use the starter rules as a reference.** The usual five cut by 7% and 15% and raise by 10% and 25%. Rules copied from your own rates use the sizes your rates showed. Read [Your starter rules](@27).
Use the starter rules as a reference
- **Try it before it counts.** In the **Rate Simulator**, make up a night and see what each room type becomes. Then watch a week of the change log in simulation before you go live.
Try it before it counts

- **Remember what stacks.** Percentages compound: $200 raised 10% and then 25% is $275, not $270. A booking speed rule can fire again after each wait, so two 10% raises on $150 make $181.50. The ceiling stops raises and the floor stops cuts, so check those first. Read [Floors and ceilings](@28).
Remember what stacks

Each of these is a short recipe with exact labels.

1. **A last-minute cut.** When a night is close and still quiet, lower the price. **Booking window (days to stay)** **Less than** 3, plus **Sellable occupancy (%)** **Less than** 50, then **Decrease the rate** by 15%. Read [Price last-minute nights differently](@77).
A last-minute cut

2. **A booking speed raise.** When a night is booking faster than similar past nights did at the same point, raise it. **Booking speed (recommended)**, **Speed** **Faster Than Normal**, **Measured over** **Past week**, then **Increase the rate** by 10%. Read [Booking speed](@34) first, so the levels make sense.
A booking speed raise

3. **Suites that follow your standard rooms.** Tick **Change prices on different room types**, measure Standard, change Suite. Read [Let suites follow your standard rooms](@78).

**Not yet** · Rules run every day of the year, for every night in the window. You cannot yet limit a rule to weekends, a date range or a season. To change a rule once it is saved, click **Edit** on its row. Read [What rules cannot do yet](@45) for each limit and what to do instead.
Suites that follow your standard rooms

- [The rule builder, field by field](@31): every field, every message, and what happens when you click **Add Rule**.
- [How rules run](@39): the five-minute cycle, the 396-night window, and how two rules combine on one night.
- [Simulation mode](@54): what "not sent" means, and how to go live when you are ready.

A rule has a name, one to four conditions that must all be true, a direction and an amount, and the room types it changes. The four conditions are sellable occupancy, booking speed, booking window and pickup count, one of each at most. The amount is a percent or a fixed amount, one or the other. A box under the amount, ticked to start, lets cancellations undo the rule's changes. Click **Add Rule**, and a window shows the days the rule will change: apply or skip the price adjustments, and the rule is on. **Edit** on a saved rule opens it here to change.

**Edit** on a rule's row opens the same form filled with that rule as saved, headed "Edit "Busy nights"" in place of **+ Add a rule**. Every field below is filled in, the undo box included, and the button at the bottom reads **Save changes**, with **Cancel editing** beside it to empty the form without saving. Switching property or deleting the rule also ends the edit. Read [Changing a rule](@42#changing-a-rule).

The **Rule name** box is required. The placeholder reads "e.g. Weekend surge". There is no length limit. The name appears in the rules list, in every change log sentence the rule writes, and in the banner MAYA shows when a rule keeps adjusting a night, so choose something you will recognise later.

The **Conditions** section is headed "Matches when all of the following are true." That sentence is the whole logic: a rule with two conditions acts only on nights where both hold. There is no either/or. If you want "busy or last-minute", make two rules.

A rule needs at least one condition and can have four at most, one of each kind. The first row is there when the form opens, set to occupancy. Click **+ Add condition** to add another row. Each new row starts on the next kind you have not used yet, in this order: occupancy, booking speed, booking window, pickup. Once a kind is used, it is greyed out in the other rows' **Metric** dropdown. When all four are in use, the button disappears.

A cut on low pickup with no booking window row gets one filled in for you. The moment your rule is **Decrease the rate** with a **Pickup count (advanced)** row set to **Less than** and no **Booking window (days to stay)** row, a booking window row appears, **Less than** 60, with a "?" beside its **Metric** label that says why: without it the rule reaches every night of the 396-night window, a far-out night with no bookings yet always counts as quiet, and the cut repeats each time the rule's wait is over. Change the number, or remove the row with its red button. It is offered once per rule you build or edit, never comes back on its own, and saving never adds it: the rule saved is exactly the rows on screen. Rules you saved before are left as they are, and **Edit** on one offers the row the same way. Read [A cut on low pickup, far out](@37#a-cut-on-low-pickup-far-out).

| Metric label | What it measures | Fields on the row | Read more |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Sellable occupancy (%)** | Rooms booked divided by rooms you can sell that night | **Compare** (**Greater than** or **Less than**), **Threshold**, default Greater than 80 | [Sellable occupancy](@32) |
| **Booking speed (recommended)** | How many bookings the night received recently, compared with similar past nights at the same point | **Speed** (seven levels, default **Faster Than Normal**), **Measured over** (default **Past week**), **Then waits (advanced)** (default **1 week**) | [Booking speed](@34) |
| **Booking window (days to stay)** | Days until the stay, on your property's own calendar (today is 0) | **Compare**, **Threshold**, default Greater than 7 | [Booking window](@33) |
| **Pickup count (advanced)** | Room nights (or revenue) the night gained in the last 1, 3 or 7 days | **Compare**, **Threshold** (default Greater than 5), **Lookback window** (default **3 days**), **Then waits (advanced)** (default **Same as the lookback window**), **Pickup measures** (default **Room nights (units)**) | [Pickup count (advanced)](@37) |

A few things about the number fields:

- **Threshold** must be 0 or more. If it is blank or below 0, your browser stops the save and points at the box. A typed 0 is accepted.
- Comparisons are strict. **Greater than** 80 means more than 80, not 80 exactly. **Less than** 7 means 6 or fewer.
- An occupancy threshold above 100 is saved as 100. A booking window threshold is rounded to whole days.
- Booking speed has no **Compare** field. Picking a level above Normal means "that fast or faster", a level below Normal means "that slow or slower", and **Normal** means exactly Normal.

**Adjust by percent (%)** is a number box, empty to start, showing "e.g. 10" until you type. A percent change multiplies the price: 10% on $150 gives $165, and when two percent rules land on the same night they compound (10% then 25% on $200 gives $275, not $270).

**Adjust by fixed amount ($)** is the number box under it, also empty, showing "e.g. 15". A fixed amount adds to or subtracts from the price: $25 on $150 gives $175. The box shows a $ sign whatever your property's currency. The amount is in your property's currency.

A rule has one amount. Type a number in one box and the other is greyed out until you clear it. Whichever box has the number is the amount the rule saves. For a raise of 10% plus $5, make two rules: they stack.

Type the amount as a positive number. The direction dropdown supplies the sign. If you type a negative number, your browser stops the save and points at the box.

Under the amounts is one more checkbox, **Undo the change if cancellations mean this rule is no longer true**, ticked to start. Ticked, a change the rule makes comes off when guests cancel and the rule is no longer true for that night. Unticked, cancellations never take its changes off. The rules list does not show it. To change it on a saved rule, click **Edit** on the rule. Read [The undo box](@40#the-undo-box).

**"Is there a limit on how big a raise or cut can be?"** Not one you would meet: any amount above 0 saves in either box, up to just under 1,000,000. A raise stops at the room type's ceiling. A cut that would take the price below the floor publishes the floor instead. A cut of 100% or more, or a fixed cut as big as the price, takes the price to 0 or below on its own, so the room type's floor is published, and the floor is 1.00 in your property's currency until you set one. A typo such as 150 for 15 on a cut rule does exactly that. Set real floors before you use large cuts, and read the number again before you click **Add Rule**. Read [Floors and ceilings](@28).

When the form opens, every room type that counts as a room is selected. A type you have unticked under **Counts as a room** on the **PMS** tab shows a small "not a room" tag on its chip, and hovering it reads "Meeting Room, not counted as a room (change this in the PMS tab)". It is left out of a new rule unless you click it. You can price it: a rule that changes the Meeting Room changes its price like any other type, and that is what lets MAYA send a price for it once you are live (a price you type for one of its nights on the calendar is sent too). What MAYA never does is measure it. Occupancy, booking speed and pickup are counted only over room types that count as rooms.

To keep a rule away from a room type, click its chip so it is no longer highlighted before you save. A rule with no room types is refused with "Select at least one room type."

With one list, the rule changes every selected type and measures the selected types that count as rooms. If you select only types that do not count as rooms, the rule can still change their prices but has nothing to measure. An occupancy, booking speed or pickup condition then never holds, so the rule never fires. A rule whose only condition is booking window still fires, because it counts days, not bookings. To move the Meeting Room's price with how busy your rooms are, use the split described next: measure your rooms and change the Meeting Room.

Under the chips is a checkbox, **Change prices on different room types**. Ticking it splits the field into a **Measure** list and a **Change** list, so a rule can watch your standard rooms and price your suites. Read [Measure one set of room types, change another](@38).

Click **Add Rule**. If everything is in order, a window opens, headed "Add "Last minute"?", with a small calendar of the months ahead, the days the new rule will change filled in, and "X days will be affected by this rule." Nothing is saved yet. Choose:

- **Apply price adjustments**: the rule is saved, switched **On**, and changes those days from the next pricing run
- **Skip price adjustments**: the rule is saved and **On**, but those days keep their prices until the rule stops being true on a day and then becomes true again. Every other day works as with Apply
- **Cancel**: nothing is saved, and the form keeps what you typed

- it appears in the list above, in the sort order the list uses (most fired first, then on before off, then by name)
- the form clears back to its defaults and stays open, ready for the next rule

The rule runs from the next pricing check, about five minutes away, on tonight and the next 395 nights, the days the window showed first. If the property is in simulation, the change log shows what it would have sent. If the property is live on Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations, changed prices go to your property system on the next cycle. On Mews nothing is sent, and the change log shows what the rule did.

**Save changes**, when you are editing, saves a new name alone at once, and a change to a rule that is **Off** at once too, moving no price. A change to a rule that is **On** opens the same window, headed "Save changes to "Last minute"?". Read [Change a rule](@72).

Priya, the Revenue Manager, wants a cut on quiet nights that are close. She types Last minute as the name. Row one: **Booking window (days to stay)**, **Less than**, 3. She clicks **+ Add condition**. The new row starts on **Sellable occupancy (%)**, because row one no longer uses it, and she sets it to **Less than**, 50. Direction **Decrease the rate**, percent 15. All three room types stay selected. She clicks **Add Rule**. The window shows two of the next three days filled in, "2 days will be affected by this rule.", and she clicks **Apply price adjustments**.

From the next check, a night 0, 1 or 2 days away with fewer than half its sellable rooms booked is lowered by 15%: Standard $150 becomes $127.50. A night that is 2 days away but 60% full is left alone, because both conditions must hold.

| Message | Why | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Your browser's own note beside a field, such as "Please fill out this field." or "Value must be greater than or equal to 0." | The name, a **Threshold** or **Direction (required)** is empty, or a threshold or amount is below 0. The wording depends on your browser | Fill in the field it points at, with a number of 0 or more |
| Enter a percent or a fixed amount. | Both amount boxes are empty | Type a number in one of them |
| Select at least one room type. | No chip selected | Click a room type |
| Pick at least one room type to measure. | The split is on and the **Measure** list is empty, or you switched property in another browser tab, so the room types on this page belong to a different property | Select a room type that counts as a room. After a switch, reload the page, check the **Property** selector and add the rule again |
The window that opens after **Add Rule** or **Save changes** has messages of its own. Read [Turning a rule on, Apply or Skip](@41#messages-you-can-meet).

Revenue Managers, General Managers and Hotel Admins can add, edit, switch and delete rules. A Viewer sees the same form and the same controls, and **Edit** fills the form so they can read a rule, but a Viewer's **Add Rule** or **Save changes** saves nothing: the window with the calendar opens for a moment and closes, and "Only a Revenue Manager or above can change this." appears in red under the form. The same line appears under a rule's switch or **Delete** button when a Viewer clicks them. Read [Roles: who can do what](@64).

**Not yet** · There is no date range, no weekday choice and no priority control in the builder, and editing a rule keeps its saved ones. Read [What rules cannot do yet](@45).

Sellable occupancy is rooms booked divided by rooms you can sell that night. Only room types you have ticked as rooms count, and rooms out of service are taken off first. Twelve rooms, three out of service, eight booked: 89%. **Greater than** 80 means more than 80, not 80 exactly.

For each night, MAYA counts two things over the room types a rule measures:

- **Booked**: how many rooms are on the books for that night. A booking that holds several rooms counts each room.
Booked

- **Sellable**: how many rooms you could sell that night. That is the room type's room count, minus any rooms you have marked out of service for that night.

Sellable occupancy is booked divided by sellable, as a percentage.

**Example: Twelve Standard rooms at The Harbour Inn**

Standard has 12 rooms. Three are out of service for a repair this week. Eight are booked for Friday.

Booked 8, sellable 12 minus 3, which is 9. Eight of nine is 89% sellable occupancy. A rule set to **Greater than** 80 fires.

Without the out-of-service block, the same night is 8 of 12, which is 67%, and the rule does not fire.

The rule builder's label for this condition is **Sellable occupancy (%)**. Its fields are **Compare** (**Greater than** or **Less than**) and **Threshold**, which starts at 80.

Twelve rooms, three out of service, eight booked: 89% sellable occupancy, so a Greater than 80 rule fires.
Sellable

MAYA reads your bookings from your property system about every five minutes. Which bookings count as booked depends on the system.

**Cloudbeds:** Bookings with the status confirmed, checked in, checked out or "Confirmation Pending" (Cloudbeds calls it not confirmed) count as booked. That matches how Cloudbeds' own occupancy counts them. Cancelled bookings and no-shows do not count. Nor does a room that was taken off a booking, or that Cloudbeds lists as cancelled inside a booking whose other rooms are kept.

**ThinkReservations:** Every booking counts as booked except cancelled bookings and no-shows.

**Mews:** Every Mews reservation counts as booked, including enquiries and optional (tentative) and requested ones. Only cancelled reservations are left out. Read [Which bookings count](@14#which-bookings-count).

A booking counts by its status, not its rate, so a comp, house-use or owner stay at $0 counts as a booked room like any other. A day-use booking (in and out the same day) counts as a booked room on its date too: always in ThinkReservations and Mews, and in Cloudbeds when Cloudbeds lists a room rate for that date. Read [Comp, house-use and day-use bookings](@22#comp-house-use-and-day-use-bookings).

Room blocks, allotments and rooms held without a booking are not read from any property system. If you want a held block to reduce what MAYA counts as sellable, enter those rooms as out of service.

Only room types ticked as **Counts as a room** on the **PMS** tab go into the sellable count. A meeting room, a spa slot or a court that you have unticked never adds to the rooms MAYA divides by, and its bookings never add to the booked count. It can still be priced by a rule that changes it. Read [Room types and rooms out of service](@52).

When a rule measures a type that does not count as a room, MAYA leaves that type out of the occupancy figure and says so in the change log: "That 95% leaves out Meeting Room." Read [Measure one set of room types, change another](@38).

On the **PMS** tab, under each room type, **+ Rooms out of service** lets you take some rooms off sale for a stretch of nights. Those rooms come off the sellable count for those nights only, so an occupancy rule reads against what you can sell. Nothing is sent to your property system about the block. Saving or clearing a block re-prices those nights within a few minutes. Read [Room types and rooms out of service](@52).

Sellable occupancy can read above 100%. It happens when you mark rooms out of service after they were already sold, or when your property system has overbooked a night. Twelve rooms, three out of service, ten booked: 111%.

You cannot set a threshold above 100 in the builder. A number above 100 is saved as 100. A rule set to **Greater than** 100 fires on any overbooked night.

The comparison is strict. **Greater than** 80 fires at 80.01% and does not fire at 80.00%. **Less than** 50 fires at 49.9% and does not fire at 50.00%. To include 80% itself, set the threshold to 79.99 (the box takes decimals). A threshold of 79 would also fire at 79.5%, for example 159 of 200 rooms.

Occupancy is worked out over the room types a rule measures, not over the whole property. A rule that measures only Deluxe reads Deluxe's occupancy. The day card on the **Calendar** tab shows occupancy over every room type that counts as a room. So the day card can say 85% while a rule that measures only Standard sees 75% and does not fire. When you wonder why a rule did not fire, check which room types it measures.

- **The day card** on the **Calendar** tab: "17/20 rooms · 85% sellable occupancy · revenue on the books $4,850.00". The room count there is the sellable count over the types that count as rooms. The revenue shows your property's [currency](@106#currency) sign.
The day card

- **The change log**: "It was 83% full, past the 80% mark you set." or "under the 40% mark you set". With a booking window on the same rule: "It was 95% full with 17 days to go, past the 90% and 21-day marks you set."
The change log
- **The Rate Simulator**: you type an occupancy per room type and see what your rules would do with it.
The Rate Simulator

Your property system's occupancy report and MAYA's sellable occupancy answer different questions.

**Cloudbeds:** Cloudbeds' headline occupancy keeps blocked rooms in the total, so a night with 3 rooms blocked and 8 of 12 sold reads 67% there. MAYA does not read Cloudbeds' room blocks at all. It subtracts only the rooms you enter as out of service on the **PMS** tab, and then reads 8 of 9, which is 89%. If the two numbers disagree, that is usually why.

**ThinkReservations:** MAYA counts each room type's rooms from ThinkReservations' list of rooms, leaving out rooms marked there as inactive, as not a room, or as not included in occupancy. It subtracts only the rooms you enter as out of service on the **PMS** tab. Read [ThinkReservations](@13#how-many-rooms-each-room-type-has).

If none of the room types a rule measures has any sellable rooms on a night, occupancy is unknown for that night, and an occupancy condition is treated as not met. This happens when every measured type is fully out of service, or when the only measured types do not count as rooms. The rule stays quiet rather than firing on nothing. A room type with 0 sellable rooms is skipped, and the rest of the measured types are counted as usual.

To build it, follow [Raise prices when you are nearly full](@74).

**Not yet** · There is no way to tell MAYA about room blocks or allotments held in your property system. Enter them as rooms out of service on the **PMS** tab instead.

Booking window is the number of days until the stay, on your property's own calendar. Tonight is 0, tomorrow night is 1. **Booking window (days to stay)** **Less than** 7 covers tonight and the next six nights. The count moves every day, so a night slides into a rule's range as it gets closer.

For each night your rules run on, booking window is the stay date minus today's date, in whole days. "Today" is the calendar date at your property, in your property's time zone, at the moment of the check. A night 30 days away has a booking window of 30. Tonight has a booking window of 0.

The condition has nothing to do with when a guest booked. It is about how far away the night is right now.

The rule builder's label is **Booking window (days to stay)**. Its fields are **Compare** (**Greater than** or **Less than**) and **Threshold**, which starts at 7. A threshold with a decimal is rounded to whole days when you save.

Comparisons are strict, so:

| You set | Nights covered |
|---|---|
| **Less than** 7 | Tonight and the next six nights (0 to 6) |
| **Less than** 3 | Tonight, tomorrow and the night after (0 to 2) |
| **Less than** 1 | Tonight only (0) |
| **Greater than** 45 | Nights 46 days away and further, up to the edge of the 396-night window |
| **Greater than** 0 | Every night except tonight |

Your rules run on tonight and the next 395 nights, so a **Greater than** rule reaches at most night 395. A price you type further out is kept, and your rules price that night once it enters the window. Read [How rules run](@39#the-window).
