The 25% raise already on the night stays. With a longer history, the Saturday that moved up would have had bookings, and nothing would be capped.

MAYA keeps the detail behind a change for 90 days. Within that time the numbers open for any change still on the change log. Since the log shows the 10 most recent runs that changed a price, in practice you will nearly always be inside the 90 days.

**Not yet** · There is no page that lists your seasons, your similar nights or your holidays on their own. They appear only inside this panel, for the night in question. You cannot type a usual number or change the level by hand. The one lever is setting a night aside.

If a past night MAYA compared with was not a normal night (a festival, a buyout, a renovation), set it aside. From the next pricing run it is left out of every comparison. Say it happens every year and, once reports from two different years agree, the whole window around it is skipped every year.

Open the change log, find a change with **Show the numbers** under it, and click it. Open **Which nights were compared?**, then **List the nights**. Each past night in that list has **Not a fair comparison?** on its right. Click it and a short form opens under that night.

There is no page where you type a date in by hand. You set a night aside from the list of nights MAYA compared with, one night at a time. The change log keeps only the 10 most recent runs that changed a price, so this works only while the change is still listed there. [The numbers behind a change](@48) walks through the three layers.

The form asks "What made Fri, Nov 14 2025 not a fair comparison?" and offers a dropdown, **Choose a reason…**, with twelve reasons. Pick one, choose how far it should reach where that choice is offered, and click **Set this date aside**. **Never mind** closes the form without saving. While it saves the button reads **Saving…**.

| Reason | Choices it offers |
|---|---|
| Holiday Not on MAYA's List | this date, every year, seasons |
| Local Event or Festival | this date, every year, seasons |
| Sporting Event or Tournament | this date, every year, seasons |
| Conference or Convention | this date, every year, seasons |
| Renovation or Rooms Out of Service | this date, seasons |
| Utility or Amenity Outage | this date, seasons |
| Group Buyout | this date only |
| Nearby Competitor Closed or Sold Out | this date, seasons |
| Severe Weather | this date, every year |
| Road, Transit, or Flight Disruption | this date only |
| Booking Data Looks Wrong | this date only |
| Other | this date, every year, seasons |

**Other** needs a few words in the box that appears ("Tell us in a few words what happened"), up to 300 characters. When a reason offers only "this date", no choices are shown and the date is set aside on its own.

When a reason allows more than one, its choices appear (two or three, as the table shows). The first is selected, and each one does everything the one above it does.

**Just set aside this one date (recommended).** This night stops being used in comparisons, and in the reading of your seasons, from the next pricing run. It is never treated as a pattern that repeats.
Just set aside this one date (recommended)

**This happens every year around this time.** The night is set aside now, the same as above. On top of that, MAYA counts it as one report of a yearly pattern. Once it holds reports of the same reason, at about the same time of year, from 2 different years, it leaves a window of 5 days either side of that point out of comparisons every year.
This happens every year around this time

**This should also change how our seasons are read (advanced).** The night is set aside now, and it counts toward the yearly pattern too. On top of that, once it holds reports at this level from 3 different years, the same window is also left out when MAYA reads your seasons (the stretches of your year that book differently). One correction can never change how your seasons are read on its own.

Two things about counting years. A report counts as one year however many nights it covers, so a renovation you flag on three nights is one year of evidence, not three. And reports older than 3 years stop counting.

**Good to know** · Weekends are Friday and Saturday nights. A night you set aside is skipped whatever weekday it falls on, and the yearly window is a stretch of dates, not of weekdays.
This should also change how our seasons are read (advanced)

From the next pricing run (about every five minutes) the night is left out of every comparison and out of the reading of your seasons. Any booking speed rule that fires from then on compares against the nights that remain, so the "usual" number for a night can move.

If setting a night aside leaves fewer than 5 compared nights, the reading is held within one step of Normal, so a rule waiting for Much Faster Than Normal, Surging, Much Slower Than Normal or Stalled will not fire on it. A compared night that shows "no history for this night" does not count toward the 5.

MAYA does not go back and redo prices. A price a rule already set stays until that rule next acts, or its change comes off in the usual way.

For a reading built from momentum (nearby nights compared with the same nights a year earlier), the night you set aside is the year-ago night of each pair, and the starting point night. That is where a night that was not normal usually sits.

**Example: The Harbour Inn sets a Saturday aside**

Sam opens **Show the numbers** under a 25% raise to Deluxe on Saturday, November 14, 2026. In the block for the past week, 10 bookings arrived against about 5 usual: Much Faster Than Normal, the level "Hot-week surge" waits for. The compared nights include Sat, Nov 15 2025 with "1 booking in the same stretch". That was the weekend the coast road was closed. Sam clicks **Not a fair comparison?**, picks **Road, Transit, or Flight Disruption** (this date only), and clicks **Set this date aside**.

The row now reads "Set aside". From the next run, that Saturday is left out. The usual number for Saturday, November 14, 2026 stays about 5: the five Saturdays had 1, 4, 5, 5 and 6 bookings, and with five nights the highest and lowest were already left off the average. But only four compared Saturdays remain, so the reading is now held within one step of Normal. The same 10 bookings now read Faster Than Normal, and "Hot-week surge" will not fire on them. The raise it already made stays.

On the **Change Log** tab, under the heading, sits a panel titled **Your corrections**. Click **Show** to open it and **Hide** to close it. Everyone on the property can read it.

Each night you have set aside is one line: the night, then "You told us this date was affected by road, transit, or flight disruption, so we leave it out of comparisons." For **Other**, your own words appear instead of the reason.

Under those, two kinds of note can appear:

- **Still counting.** "We have seen this reported in 1 year of the 2 different years we would want before treating "Local Event or Festival" near June 10 as a pattern that repeats every year." The same shape appears for the seasons choice, ending "as a change to how we read the season around here."
Still counting

- **Now applied every year**, in amber. "Reports across 2 different years flagged "Local Event or Festival" near June 10, so we now leave it out of comparisons every year." For the seasons choice it ends "out of comparisons and out of our seasonal calculations, every year."

When the panel has nothing in it, a short note explains what it is for.
Now applied every year

Each line in **Your corrections** has **Undo**. Click it and the night is compared with again from the next run. Any yearly pattern it counted toward is counted again from the reports that remain, so a window applied every year can go back to "still counting".

If nothing is removed, the panel says "Nothing was removed" and adds that it may already be gone, or that removing it needs manager access.
Setting a night aside, and undoing it, needs Revenue Manager access or higher. Everyone on the property, Viewers included, can open the evidence and read **Your corrections**.

MAYA matches nights around 17 US holidays by their position relative to the holiday rather than by date. It has no other countries' holidays and no local events. When a past night was a holiday or an event MAYA does not have, set it aside with **Holiday Not on MAYA's List** (first in the **Choose a reason…** list) or **Local Event or Festival**, and choose **This happens every year around this time**. After reports from 2 different years, the window is skipped every year. [Which past nights your rules compare with](@36) lists the 17 holidays MAYA has.

A closed period is a stretch you confirmed as closed on the review screen. A card there asks whether you were closed between two dates, or whether your property is normally closed at that time of year. Those nights are left out of comparisons too, and out of the reading of your seasons, without any setting aside. There is no screen to add a closed period by hand, and MAYA does not treat a future closure as closed, so those nights are still priced. [Checking what MAYA found](@26) covers the closure findings.

Click a night on the calendar, type a price in a room type's box and save. That number goes to your property system as typed. Rules that had already moved that night pause for that room type, and rules that fire later stack on top of your price. **Clear** hands the night back to your rules.

Open the **Calendar** tab and click a day. Under the grid, one card per room type appears. At the bottom of each card sits the price editor: a box marked with your property's currency sign ($, € or £, or the currency's code, such as CAD), pre-filled with the night's current price (or the price already typed for it), a **through…** link, **Save**, and a **?** that opens a short explanation titled "Setting a price yourself". **Clear** appears only while a typed price is open on that night, and never on a night that has passed.

Setting or clearing a price needs Revenue Manager access or higher. Everyone on the property can see the prices that have been set.

1. Click the night on the calendar, then find the room type's card.
2. Type the price in the box. Whole numbers or cents are both fine.
3. For a run of nights, click **through…** and pick the last night the price applies to. The × beside it goes back to a single night.
4. Press Enter or click **Save**. A line under the box confirms what happened (see below).

**Save** stays greyed out while the box is empty, not a number, below 0, or while the last night is before the first.

**A comma or a point?** Type a point for cents, as in 180.50, and no thousands separator, as in 1250. The box is your browser's own number box, so whether it also takes a comma (180,50) depends on your browser and its language. If it cannot read what you typed, it counts as empty and **Save** stays greyed out, so nothing wrong is saved. The amount and threshold boxes in the rule builder work the same way.

Your number becomes the starting point for that night and room type, ahead of the rate in your property system and everything else MAYA might have started from. Three things follow.

- **Changes already on the night are taken off.** A standard rule (occupancy or booking window) that was holding a change on that night keeps its place but stops moving the price. A booking speed or pickup rule's change on that night is taken off. The confirmation line counts them: "Paused 2 rules on this night for this room".
Changes already on the night are taken off

- **Rules that fire later stack on top.** Your price is not a lock. A rule whose condition starts holding after you typed, or a booking speed or pickup rule that fires after its wait, changes the price from your number. The change log then reads "Priya set the base rate to $180.00." followed by that rule's sentence.
Rules that fire later stack on top

If you want a night left at your number for good, there is no lock. Type the price, then type it again when a rule moves it, or turn off the rules that would move it. Turning a rule off stops it on every night, not only this one. To stop one rule on this night alone, answer **Stop for this night** when the amber banner asks, which is only after that rule has adjusted the night three times. This works for booking speed and pickup rules only. An occupancy or booking window rule can only be turned off everywhere.
Your price is published as typed

Standard on Friday, November 13, 2026 is at $165: "Warm-date bump" raised it 10% from $150. Priya types $180 and clicks **Save**. The line reads "Saved. Sending to Cloudbeds now. Paused 1 rule on this night for this room; new rules will apply on top." The night now shows "Manual · $180.00" and the change log reads "Priya set the base rate to $180.00."

A week later the night passes 80% full. "Busy nights" (occupancy Greater than 80, Increase 10%) fires and raises it to $198.00, from $180.00. The log reads "Priya set the base rate to $180.00." then ""Busy nights" raised this night 10%, from $180.00 to $198.00."

**Example: The lines after Save and Clear**

| Line | What it means |
|---|---|
| "Saved. Sending to Cloudbeds now." | You are live and MAYA has asked for the price to be sent straight away. |
| "Saved. Sending to Cloudbeds on the next cycle (about 5 min)." | You are live and the price goes with the next pricing run. |
| "Saved (simulation: not sent to Cloudbeds)." | You are still in simulation. The price shows in MAYA and is not sent. |
| "Saved. It will be sent when the date enters the 396-day push window." | Every night you saved is more than 395 nights ahead. MAYA sends a night once it enters the window. |
| "Saved. 12 nights sending to Cloudbeds now; 8 more will be sent as they enter the 396-day window." | Your run of nights crosses the edge of the window. |

The system's name in these lines (Cloudbeds, Think Reservations, Mews) comes from your connection, which MAYA reads when the dashboard opens. With no connection on file, or for a moment while the dashboard opens, the lines and the **?** panel say "your PMS".

**Cloudbeds:** When you are live, MAYA runs your rules on the nights you saved straight away and asks for the price to be sent now. If it cannot ask, the next run sends it within about five minutes. It goes to the room type's base rate in Cloudbeds. A night more than 395 nights ahead is kept, and is priced and sent when it enters the 396-night window.

**Mews:** MAYA does not send prices to Mews. A price you type shows in MAYA, in the change log and on the calendar, and nothing reaches Mews. The confirmation line may still read "Saved. Sending to Mews now." Nothing is sent to Mews whatever that line says. To change a rate in Mews, change it there.

In simulation the price is saved and shown, and nothing is sent. If you go live later, it goes out with the first live send like every other price.

On a live Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations property, the line under the box does not stop at the save. MAYA reads what became of the night about 20 seconds, 1 minute and 3 minutes after a save, and once more when you open a day that already has a typed price. When the save said the price goes on the next cycle, or that Cloudbeds isn't answering, it also reads about 6 and 11 minutes after. It stops early once the answer cannot change by itself (sent, or stopped), and does not keep asking after the last read. While the answer says no more than the save did, the save's line stays. Once it says more, the line changes to one of these:
- **"Sent to Cloudbeds."** Cloudbeds took the price. On ThinkReservations that means accepted, and MAYA reads it back within about an hour.
"Sent to Cloudbeds."
- **"Sending to Cloudbeds now."** The send is under way.
"Sending to Cloudbeds now."

- **"Saved. It couldn't be sent yet. MAYA will retry 3 more times."** Cloudbeds did not take it for a cause that usually clears on its own: slowing down, not responding, never confirmed. MAYA sends it again every cycle, up to 10 tries at this price, and the number is the count left, read from MAYA's own record of the sends. When Cloudbeds could not find the rate MAYA sends to, MAYA reads your rate plans again and sends once more, so the line says "MAYA will retry 1 more time."
"Saved. It couldn't be sent yet. MAYA will retry 3 more times."

- **"This price couldn't be sent to Cloudbeds."** MAYA has stopped retrying on its own: the tries at this price are used, or the cause needs you, such as a rate rule or a permission in Cloudbeds. Two buttons follow. **Try again** sends the price once more now, and the line follows that try: "MAYA will retry 1 more time." while it is on its way, then "Sent to Cloudbeds." or the same line again. Pressing it twice sends once. **See the error log** opens the **Change Log** at the "Prices not reaching Cloudbeds" item for that night, which names the cause and what to do. A cause that usually clears on its own reaches the change log only once it has lasted about two hours, and a night that had already begun may never reach it. Until there is an item, there is no **See the error log**, and the cause is written under the line instead, with what to do when there is something.
"This price couldn't be sent to Cloudbeds."

- **"This price couldn't be sent to Cloudbeds."** with no **Try again**, even for a Revenue Manager: the room type has no rate in Cloudbeds for MAYA to send to, such as no base rate of its own, or only rates that follow another plan. The cause is written under the line, or **See the error log** opens its item. Once you add a base rate in Cloudbeds, the night usually goes out on the next cycle.

**Try again** needs Revenue Manager access or higher, like typing a price. Everyone on the property sees the line, the cause and **See the error log**.
"This price couldn't be sent to Cloudbeds."

A price typed while you simulate, on Mews, on a Disconnected connection, past the window, or while MAYA's work is paused has no line of its own after the save: nothing is sent, and the save's line says so. A night MAYA's own checks held back keeps the save's line too.

| Limit | What the screen says |
|---|---|
| Tonight onwards only, on your property's own calendar | "Manual prices apply to tonight onwards; earlier nights have already sold." |
| Up to 399 days ahead (400 nights counting tonight) | "You can set a price up to 400 nights ahead." |
| At most 366 nights in one save | "One change can cover at most 366 nights." You see it only if you pick 367 nights or more. |
| A number of 0 or more | "Price must be a number of zero or more." |
| Not below the floor (except 0) | "Below this room type's floor of $80.00." |
| Not above the ceiling | "Above this room type's ceiling of $300.00." |
| At most 99,999,999.99 | "That price is more than MAYA can store." |
| 30 saves or clears per person per 10 minutes, shared with room type changes | "That's a lot of price changes at once. Give it a minute and try again." |
| Revenue Manager or higher | "This needs Revenue Manager access or higher on this property." |

A price outside the floor or ceiling is refused, not rounded to the limit. Type a number inside the limits, or change the limits first. [Floors and ceilings](@28) explains where they are set.
Prices in these messages, the price box and the **Manual** badge show your property's currency sign.

Type 0 and the night becomes a comp night for that room type. It is allowed under the floor. No rule raises it, and no rule can cut it, because it is already at the lowest a price can go.

MAYA does not send a price of 0 to any property system. The confirmation says so, and while the night stays at 0 the change log carries an item headed "Prices not reaching Cloudbeds" that reads "MAYA doesn't send a price of 0 to Cloudbeds, so Standard rates set to 0 in MAYA weren't changed there", with the action "If the night is meant to be free, set it to 0 in Cloudbeds yourself." Once your system has the night at 0, the item closes on its own. [Make a night free](@69) has the short version.

**A booking speed or pickup rule waits again from your price.** A rule that existed when you typed the price waits its wait, in whole days from the day you typed, then reads its whole window afresh, as if nothing had happened on the night before. A rule you add after typing the price is not held by it. [How rules run](@39) explains the wait.
A booking speed or pickup rule waits again from your price

**A standard rule holds its place.** An occupancy or booking window rule whose condition already held when you typed stays quiet on that night. When its condition stops and starts again, or when you clear the price, it moves the price again.
A standard rule holds its place

**The three-times question closes.** If the **Rules that keep adjusting** banner was asking about that night and rule, your price takes its changes off and the question closes for that night. It asks again if the rule adjusts your price three times.
The three-times question closes

**Clear** removes your price for that room type on that night. For a run of nights, open **through…**, pick the last night, and click **Clear**: "Cleared 5 nights. Your rules price them again."

Clear reaches tonight onwards only, because your rules never price a night that has passed. A past night has no **Clear** button, and its typed price stays on it as the record of what it sold at. A run of nights that starts before tonight is cleared from tonight.

After a clear, your rules run on the night again straight away. The starting point is the rate MAYA read from Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations for that night. A night your system has no rate for is left unpriced after the clear, and the day card says so, until your system has a rate for it. Mews properties have no rate read, so a cleared Mews night stays unpriced until you type a price again.

A rate you change in your property system, on a night MAYA had sent to, is kept the same way and shows as "Changed in Cloudbeds · $180.00". [Rates you change in your property system](@51) explains that.

**Not yet** · There is no note field: the price is saved without a comment. You cannot upload prices in bulk. One save covers one room type over a run of nights, so a season across three room types is three saves. You cannot set a price per rate plan: MAYA writes one base rate per room type. You cannot type a price on a night that has passed.

On a night MAYA has already sent a price to and confirmed, a rate you change in your property system an hour or more later is kept as your price and marked "Changed in Cloudbeds". On a night MAYA has never sent to, your rate becomes the starting point, and your rules work from it. Setting a night to 0 in your system closes it.

Which case a night falls into depends on one thing: whether MAYA has already sent a price to that night and confirmed it landed.

**MAYA has sent to the night.** Your change is read as a decision. It becomes a manual price for that night and room type, exactly as if you had typed it in MAYA: rules that had already moved the night are paused for that room type, rules that fire later stack on top of your number, and **Clear** hands the night back. [Setting a price yourself](@50) explains what a manual price does.
MAYA has sent to the night

**MAYA has never sent to the night.** That includes every night before you first go live, and any night beyond the 396-night window. Your rate is read as the property's own rate for that night, the starting point. When a rule fires, it works from your number. When no rule fires, your number is the price.

**Example: The Harbour Inn, one change in each case**

Sam changes two Standard rates in Cloudbeds on the morning of Friday, October 2, 2026.

Friday, November 13, 2026: MAYA sent $165.00 to that night two days ago and Cloudbeds confirmed it. Sam changes it to $175.00. Within the hour MAYA reads the change and keeps it. The night shows "Changed in Cloudbeds · $175.00" and the change log reads "The base rate was changed in Cloudbeds to $175.00." When "Busy nights" fires later, it raises the night 10% from $175.00, not from $150.00.
MAYA has never sent to the night

If you change a rate in your system instead, give the night an hour after MAYA last sent to it (an hour or two on ThinkReservations). Change the rate MAYA writes to: the base rate in Cloudbeds, usually the Best Available rate type in ThinkReservations. Then, while you are live, your change on a night MAYA has sent to is kept as your price when MAYA next reads it.

**Example: The exact conditions**

On a night MAYA has sent to, your change is kept only when all of these hold:

- You are live. In simulation nothing is sent, so nothing is read as a change (see "Changes made while simulating" below).
- MAYA's last send to that night landed and was confirmed. Cloudbeds reports that the job applied. ThinkReservations only accepts the price, so MAYA counts it as confirmed once its hourly read finds the price there.

- Your change is on the same rate plan MAYA writes to. In Cloudbeds that is the base rate. In ThinkReservations it is the rate type named Best Available, or, if none is, the standard rate type that covers the most room types. A change to another rate plan is not read.
- The new rate differs from MAYA's price by more than half a cent, and is not MAYA's price rounded to a whole unit.
- No newer price typed in MAYA is still on its way to that night.
- The difference is not one shared by nearly every night. That covers tax, a markup, or a raise of one percentage across the board (see "Prices with tax or a markup" below).
- The send landed after you last went live. A rate changed while simulating is a starting point, not a manual price.

MAYA reads your own rates for every night in the 396-night window about once an hour, and again when your property's date changes. It also reads a night again right before sending a new price to it, when the night was last sent to over an hour ago and the hourly read did not run this cycle. So a change on a sent night is read within about an hour, and usually before MAYA sends a new price to that night. The exceptions are a cycle in which MAYA could not read your system, and a change made within an hour of MAYA's send.

A night beyond the window is not read until it enters the window.

On the calendar, the room type's card shows an amber badge reading "Changed in Cloudbeds · $175.00" (or "Changed in Think Reservations · $175.00"). Hover it for "Seen" and the date and time MAYA read the change, in your browser's clock. A price typed in MAYA shows "Manual" instead, with "Set" on hover.

In the change log the entry names no person: "The base rate was changed in Cloudbeds to $175.00." A rule that fires later on that night adds its sentence after it.

**Clear** on the card works the same as for a typed price. Hover it and it reads "Changed in Cloudbeds. Clear hands the night back to your rules."

Say you meant $150 for a Standard night and typed $15 in Cloudbeds. What happens depends on the same two cases.

**On a night MAYA has sent to**, your $15 is kept as your price, like any change of yours, and the card shows "Changed in Cloudbeds · $15.00". The floor does not catch it. A price you set yourself is published as you set it, even under the floor, so $15 stays in your system. Rules that fire later work from $15.
On a night MAYA has sent to

**On a night MAYA has never sent to**, $15 becomes the night's starting point. Your rules work from it and the floor holds the result: with Standard's $80 floor, MAYA publishes $80 (and sends it when you are live). That is not your $150 either. A floor still at $1.00 would let the $15 through.

A rate typed too high works the same way, with the ceiling in place of the floor. To put it right, do one of these:
On a night MAYA has never sent to
- **Press **Clear** in MAYA** on a night marked "Changed in Cloudbeds". The night goes back to your rules, from the starting point MAYA had before your typo, and MAYA's price is sent over the $15.
Press Clear in MAYA
- **Type the right price in MAYA.** It is kept at once and, when you are live, sent straight away.
Type the right price in MAYA

- **Correct the rate in your system.** MAYA reads it within about an hour. On a night MAYA has sent to, it is kept as your price, the same way the typo was. On any other night it becomes the starting point.

Clearing or typing a price in MAYA needs Revenue Manager access or higher. On Mews, MAYA does not read rates, so a rate mistyped in Mews stays as it is until you correct it there.
Correct the rate in your system

If you were live before and went back to simulation, a rate you change in your system on a night MAYA sent to during the live stretch is not read while you simulate. MAYA's prices for that night keep starting from the old starting point. When you go live again, that rate is read as the night's starting point, and your rules work from it.

Set a night's rate to 0 in your system and MAYA reads it as closed.

- On a night MAYA has sent to, the starting point becomes 0, MAYA stops pricing that night and sends nothing to it. Any manual price on that night is cleared, and the rules it paused are released. This needs you to be live and the 0 to be on the rate plan MAYA writes to. MAYA's last send to the night must also have gone through over an hour ago. It does not need to be confirmed, because MAYA never sends 0 itself.
- On a night MAYA has never sent to, a rate of 0 is left unpriced from the start. MAYA does not open a closed night at the floor.

Open the night again by loading a rate in your system. The next hourly read takes that rate as the starting point, and your rules work from it.

A 0 in your system does not close a night MAYA has sent to in three cases:

- **A comp night you set in MAYA.** A typed price of 0 makes the night free, so a 0 in your system for that night matches your price rather than closing the night. [Setting a price yourself](@50) covers comp nights.
A comp night you set in MAYA

- **A manual price whose last send was never confirmed.** The night is held rather than closed, since that price may never have reached your system. The manual price stays, and MAYA sends nothing new to the night while your system has 0.
A manual price whose last send was never confirmed
- **A newer price typed in MAYA that is still on its way.** Your typed price is kept and sent as usual.
A newer price typed in MAYA that is still on its way

Some systems report rates through a rule of their own: tax included, or a markup on every night. Those rates all differ from MAYA's price by the same ratio, and reading each one as a change of yours would freeze the window at inflated prices.

So when 80% or more of the sent nights MAYA reads (10 nights at least) differ from its price by one shared ratio, MAYA reads that as your system's rule, not as edits. None of those nights is kept, and nothing shows on the calendar. MAYA's next price for each of them is sent as usual. A night that does not fit the ratio is still read as a change of yours. If your prices in your system look like MAYA's plus tax, that is why, and nothing needs doing.

The same check catches a change you make yourself. Say you are live and you raise every rate by 10% in Cloudbeds. Every sent night now differs from MAYA's price by the same ratio, so MAYA reads your raise as your system's own arithmetic, not as your prices. None of the new rates is kept as a manual price, and nothing shows on the calendar.

Your raised rates stay in your system until MAYA's price for a night next changes. MAYA then sends its new price for that night, worked out from the starting point it had before your raise, so your 10% is gone from that night. Nights change at different times, so for a while some nights carry your raise and some do not. A Standard night MAYA sent at $165.00 reads $181.50 in Cloudbeds after your raise, until MAYA's price for that night next moves.

To move a lot of nights at once, type the prices in MAYA. One save covers one room type and a run of nights at one price, using **through…**. Each night is kept at once as a manual price, and rules that fire later stack on it. [Setting a price yourself](@50) has the detail.

Or change rates in your system only on nights MAYA has not sent to yet, such as nights more than 395 nights ahead. Each of those rates becomes the night's starting point when the night enters the window, and your rules work from it.

|  | In MAYA (the calendar) | In your property system |
|---|---|---|
| Takes effect | At once, and sent straight away when you are live | Within about an hour |
| Which nights | Tonight to 399 days ahead | Only nights MAYA has sent to; any other night becomes a starting point instead |
| Who did it | Named in the change log | "The base rate was changed in Cloudbeds", no name |
| A run of nights | One save with **through…** | Night by night, as your system allows |
| Undo | **Clear** | **Clear** in MAYA |

When you mean to set a price, type it in MAYA. Change it in your system when that is where you happen to be, and give MAYA's send an hour first. A change of one percentage to nearly every sent night is not kept (see "Raising every night by the same percentage" above).

**Cloudbeds:** MAYA writes to the base rate of each room type in Cloudbeds, the rate plan that does not follow another plan. Change that rate and MAYA reads it. A change to a derived plan or a package is not read. Cloudbeds confirms MAYA's sends, so the hour starts when the send goes out.

**ThinkReservations:** MAYA writes to the rate type named Best Available, or, if none is, to the standard rate type that covers the most room types. Change that rate and MAYA reads it. ThinkReservations accepts a price without confirming it applied, so MAYA counts a send as confirmed only once its hourly read finds the price there. A change you make before that read is not kept and is written over by MAYA's next price change. Give a night an hour or two after MAYA's send.

**Mews:** MAYA does not read rates from Mews and does not send prices to Mews. A rate you change in Mews is neither shown in MAYA nor written over. To set a price in MAYA for a Mews property, type it on the calendar. To change the rate guests see, change it in Mews.

A rate the front desk gives one guest lives on that guest's booking, not on your base rate. MAYA does not read it as a change to your rates, and it does not change the price MAYA sends for that night.

The booking counts like any other. It adds to the night's occupancy, booking speed and pickup count. Its rate counts in that night's room revenue and in the ADR (the average rate per room booked) on the calendar, at the rate MAYA read with the booking. Occupancy, booking window and booking speed rules, and pickup rules that count room nights, do not look at what a guest paid. A pickup rule set to measure revenue adds up the rates on the night's bookings, special rates included, so a special rate does move that rule's number.

A booking's rate never reaches a price. A night's starting point is your own rate for it, read from Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations, or a price someone typed; a night with neither is not priced at all, whatever its bookings paid. So a special rate on a booking moves nothing but that night's revenue and ADR, and a booking taken at one of MAYA's own prices never becomes the next starting point. On Mews, where no rates are read, a night is priced only once you type a price for it.

**Not yet** · MAYA does not tell you when it has kept a change from your system. The badge on the calendar and the sentence in the change log are the only signs. There is no list of changes it has kept, and no setting to turn this off.

The **PMS** tab lists your room types as your property system reports them, with their unit counts. Untick **Counts as a room** for anything nobody sleeps in, and MAYA leaves it out of occupancy and your bill. It is still priced, and sent when you are live, like any other room type. Add **Rooms out of service** for units off sale for a stretch, so occupancy reads against what you can really sell.

Open the **PMS** tab. Under the connection cards sits a section headed **Room types**, with a **?** beside the heading. Everyone on the property can see it. Changing anything here needs Revenue Manager access or higher.

One row per active room type, in name order. Each row shows the room type's name, its unit count ("12 units"), a small tag when it is unticked, and the checkbox **Counts as a room**. The tag reads "not a room" when the room type has been unticked, and "needs your answer" when nobody has ticked or unticked it yet. A room type that is not ticked is dimmed.

While the list loads you see a grey placeholder. If it cannot load: "Couldn't load room types." with **Try again**. Before the first sync: "No room types have synced yet."

A room type tagged "needs your answer" is one nobody has ticked or unticked yet, whose name reads like something nobody sleeps in (see "How MAYA proposes the answer" below). It shows unticked and is left out of your bill until you answer. Until then it still counts in occupancy and in the calendar's revenue per room. Tick it if guests sleep there and it joins your bill. If they do not, tick it and untick it again: it then shows "not a room" and leaves occupancy and the calendar's count too. The **?** beside the heading says the same in one line.

Untick a room type and it leaves all three. Its bookings also leave the history booking speed reads, so a court selling six slots a night cannot read as the hotel filling up. It is still priced, and sent when you are live, like any other room type, and its revenue still counts in the day card's revenue figure.

A rule cannot measure an unticked room type. A rule that measures only unticked types measures nothing and never fires. When an occupancy rule measured a mix, the change log says which were left out: "That 82% leaves out Meeting Room." [Measure one set of room types, change another](@38) has the detail.

Tick or untick and the change saves at once. If it does not save you see "That didn't save" with a note to try again, and the box goes back to where it was. Your rules then run again across the 396-night window, since every occupancy figure has moved: within a few minutes for the coming nights, and over the next few cycles for the furthest, nearest nights first. Each change is recorded with who made it.

After that, MAYA never unticks a room type on its own. A new room type from your system whose name reads like a bedroom arrives ticked as a room. If its name reads like something nobody sleeps in, it waits for your answer: it shows unticked, tagged "needs your answer", and counts in occupancy (your existing rules do not include it, see "What a new room type starts with" below), but it is left out of your bill until you answer. To answer, tick it if it is a room, or, if it is not, tick it and untick it again. A sync never overwrites an answer you have given. You can change any room type from the **PMS** tab at any time.

Under each room type, click **+ Rooms out of service**. A short form opens:

| Field | What to enter |
|---|---|
| **From** | The first night the rooms are off sale. Required. |
| **To** | The last night. Leave it empty for one night. |
| **Units** | How many rooms, from 1 up to the room type's unit count. |
| **Reason (optional)** | A few words, up to 200 characters. "Renovation" is the hint. |

Click **Save** (it reads **Saving…** while it works) or **Cancel**. The block then lists under the room type as "2 out of service", the first and last night, "· Renovation", and **Clear**.

For those nights only, the units come off the room type's sellable count, for your rules and on the calendar day card. Occupancy then reads against what you can sell, so an occupancy rule does not stay quiet because a renovated wing looks empty. Nothing is sent to your property system. Your rules run again on those nights within a few minutes of saving.

**Example: Two Standard rooms under renovation**

The Harbour Inn takes 2 Standard rooms off sale from November 10 to November 20, 2026. On those nights the property has 18 sellable rooms, so a night with 11 rooms booked reads "11/18 rooms" and 61% instead of 55%. With 15 rooms booked, "Busy nights" (occupancy Greater than 80) fires at 15 of 18, which is 83%. Without the block, 15 of 20 is 75% and the rule would stay quiet.

| Rule | What the screen says |
|---|---|
| One block covers at most 366 nights | "One block can cover at most 366 nights." |
| Units are whole numbers from 1 | "Units must be a whole number of at least 1." |
| Not more units than the room type has | "Standard has 12 rooms" followed by a note that you cannot block more than that. |
| Blocks stack night by night, never past the count | "Standard already has 8 rooms out of service on some of those nights" followed by how many you can still block. |
| Reason under 200 characters | "Keep the reason under 200 characters." |
| Real dates, last night not before the first | "End date can't be before the start date." |
| Revenue Manager or higher | "This needs Revenue Manager access or higher on this property." |
| 30 changes per person per 10 minutes, shared with typed prices | "That's a lot of changes at once. Give it a minute and try again." |

Click **Clear** beside the block. The rooms are back on sale from the next run, within a few minutes. MAYA keeps a record of the block and who cleared it, but it no longer shows. A block already cleared by someone else answers "That block is already cleared."

There is no edit. To change a block's dates or units, clear it and add a new one.

A block changes occupancy only. Booking speed counts the bookings a night has received against what similar past nights had, and a room off sale changes neither count. [Booking speed](@34) explains the count.

MAYA reads bookings and rates from your system, not room blocks, out-of-order rooms or allotments. A wing you close in Cloudbeds, ThinkReservations or Mews still counts as sellable in MAYA until you enter it here. This is also why MAYA's occupancy can differ from your system's headline figure. [Occupancy looks wrong](@99) walks through the differences.

**Cloudbeds:** A new room type appears in MAYA on the next cycle, about five minutes, ticked as a room. If its name reads like something nobody sleeps in, it shows unticked instead, with a "needs your answer" tag: it counts in occupancy but is left out of your bill until you answer on the **PMS** tab. A changed unit count is picked up on the next cycle, from the count Cloudbeds reports for the room type. A renamed room type shows its new name on the next cycle.

**ThinkReservations:** A new room type appears in MAYA on the next cycle, about five minutes, ticked as a room. If its name reads like something nobody sleeps in, it shows unticked instead, with a "needs your answer" tag: it counts in occupancy but is left out of your bill until you answer on the **PMS** tab. A room type you remove stays in MAYA with its history. MAYA counts each room type's units from ThinkReservations' list of rooms on every cycle, leaving out rooms marked there as inactive, as not a room, or as not included in occupancy. A renamed room type shows its new name on the next cycle.

**Mews:** A new space category appears in MAYA as a room type on the next cycle, about five minutes, ticked as a room. If its name reads like something nobody sleeps in, it shows unticked instead, with a "needs your answer" tag: it counts in occupancy but is left out of your bill until you answer on the **PMS** tab. A category you remove stays in MAYA with its history. Mews does not report how many rooms a category has, so MAYA gives every Mews category the same number of units: the number we set with you when we connect Mews, or 100 if it was never set. [Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Mews%20room%20counts) your counts. Once we have set the number, occupancy is right from the next run if your categories are all the same size. A renamed category shows its new name on the next cycle.

Delete a room type in your system and create it again, and your system treats it as a new room type. So does MAYA, even when the name is the same. Nothing carries over from the old one. The old one stays in MAYA as the tabs above describe, so for a while you may see two room types with the same name. [Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Switch%20off%20a%20room%20type) and we switch the old one off.

A brand new room type, or a rebuilt one, starts like this:

- **Your rules do not cover it.** A rule covers the room types that were selected when you saved it. A room type added later is not in any of your rules, not even one that covered every room type you had. That goes for rules you built and for the starter rules. The **Room Types** column on the **Rules** tab shows what each rule changes.
Your rules do not cover it

- **It has no history.** The old type's past stays remain under the old type, so the new one starts with none. A booking speed rule that measures only the new type has nothing to compare with, so it stays quiet at first. Once the type has bookings of its own, readings with fewer than 5 similar nights are capped at one step.
It has no history

- **Occupancy works at once.** An occupancy rule that measures it reads its bookings against its units from the first cycle. A pickup count rule that measures it waits until MAYA has kept a record of the type for the whole lookback (1, 3 or 7 days).
Occupancy works at once

- **Its floor and ceiling are MAYA's defaults**, $1.00 and $99,999.99, which stop nothing in most currencies (where a room sells above 99,999.99, the default ceiling holds its price down). They stay there until real ones are set for it. A suggestion card is the quickest way (below).
Its floor and ceiling are MAYA's defaults
- **Prices you typed stay with the old type.** A manual price belongs to one room type, so the new type starts without any.
Prices you typed stay with the old type

- **On Mews, it gets the same unit count as your other room categories**, as the Mews tab above explains. On Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations its own count is read.

To bring the new type into your pricing, add a rule for it, or change an existing rule to include it. A saved rule cannot take on a room type, so changing one means deleting it and adding it again with the new type selected. [Change a rule](@72) walks through it.
On Mews, it gets the same unit count as your other room categories

Twelve rooms, two out of service, nine booked: 90% sellable occupancy, so a Greater than 80 rule fires.

**Not yet** · You cannot switch a room type off in MAYA or rename it. Names and unit counts come from your property system. The one exception is a duplicate found at import, which the review screen can hide. You cannot edit a block: clear it and add another. Floors and ceilings are not set here. [Floors and ceilings](@28) explains where they are.

The **PMS** tab shows whether your property system is connected, how the last 24 hours of requests to it went, when bookings last synced, the most recent requests MAYA made, and the time zone and currency saved for your property. Problems sending prices are not here. They are in the change log. When the connection breaks on Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations, a General Manager or Hotel Admin sees a **Reconnect** button here, and in a banner at the top of the dashboard whichever tab is open. On Mews, the panel asks everyone to email us to re-enter the keys.

The **PMS** tab is the last of the five tabs. Everyone on the property can open it. The heading reads "Property System (Cloudbeds)", with your system's name in brackets once connected, and one line under it: "Bookings sync automatically on a schedule. This page shows how that connection is doing."

Before it loads: "Loading connection status…". With no property chosen: "Select a property to view status." With no system connected yet: "No property system is connected for this property yet."

The **Time zone and currency** card sits under the request list, and the **Room types** section under that, on the same tab. [Room types and rooms out of service](@52) covers it.

A single word, colour-coded. It is the state of the connection as MAYA last recorded it.

| Word | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Connected (green) | Healthy. MAYA reads bookings and, when you are live, sends prices. | Nothing. |
| Pending (amber) | Connected but not yet paid for. Nothing runs. | Finish setting up payment. |
| Degraded (amber) | Still working. MAYA keeps reading bookings and, when you are live, sending prices. Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations only. | Usually nothing: it tends to clear by itself on the next read. If it is still there in an hour, click Reconnect. It does no harm. |
| Error (red) | Your system rejected MAYA's saved access. On Mews: Mews refused MAYA's keys three reads in a row. Nothing is read or sent while it lasts. MAYA keeps trying, up to an hour between tries, and the card goes back to Connected by itself once a try works. | If it has not cleared within a couple of hours, click Reconnect (on Mews, email us). It does no harm sooner. |
| Disconnected (red) | MAYA's access is gone: the app was uninstalled, its permission removed, or your system refused it. Nothing runs until someone reconnects. | Reconnect. |
| unknown (grey) | MAYA has no status on file for the connection yet. | Open the tab again in a few minutes. If it stays, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Connection%20status%20unknown). |

While the card reads Degraded, one calm line sits above the cards: "Your Cloudbeds connection needs a refresh soon. Prices are still updating." (with your system's name). Yes, your prices are still going out: nothing has stopped and nothing is lost. A General Manager or Hotel Admin also sees a quiet **Reconnect Cloudbeds** link at the end of that line.

When the card has read Error or Disconnected for about an hour, every General Manager and Hotel Admin gets one email saying the connection is down, with a button that opens this tab. Degraded never sends it. Read [emails MAYA sends](@63#the-connection-down-email).

The Health card below has a "Degraded" of its own, about failed requests. The two are separate.

How the requests MAYA made to your system in the last 24 hours went. It counts every request, reads and writes alike.

| Badge | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Healthy | 98% or more of the requests succeeded. |
| Degraded | 80% to under 98% succeeded. |
| Having trouble | Under 80% succeeded. |
| No recent activity | No requests in the last 24 hours. |
| Not tracked for this system | ThinkReservations and Mews. MAYA keeps no log of its requests to them, so there is nothing to count. |

Beside the badge: "97% of 412 requests OK".

A short spell of "Degraded" is normal when your system is slow or asks MAYA to wait. "Having trouble" for more than an hour, with a Connection card that is not green, means it is time to reconnect. [Connection lost](@101) walks through the cases.

The last time MAYA read your bookings successfully, on your own computer's clock with its time zone, for example "Sep 22, 2026, 3:05:12 PM PDT". Someone in another time zone sees the same moment on their own clock. A dash means it has never read them. On a healthy connection this time is at most a few minutes old, because MAYA reads about every five minutes.

Under the cards is a technical list of MAYA's last 50 requests to Cloudbeds, headed "Recent requests to Cloudbeds". You do not need to read it. If you email us about the connection, it helps us. A request that failed shows its status code, or ERR, in red. Its times show the same way as Last sync, on your own clock. Requests are kept for 7 days. When there are none, it reads "No requests recorded yet".

**Cloudbeds:** The table fills with every request MAYA makes to Cloudbeds, and the Health card is built from the same list.

**ThinkReservations:** MAYA keeps no log of its requests to ThinkReservations, so this list and the Health card both read "Not tracked for this system". Read the Connection card and Last sync instead.

Under the request list, a card headed **Time zone and currency** shows both as they are saved for your property. The time zone shows by its name, such as "America/Los_Angeles". The currency shows by its code and sign, such as "USD ($)", "EUR (€)" or "GBP (£)", or by the code alone for any other currency, such as "CAD". Nothing here can be changed. The **?** beside the heading says what each is for: tonight is tonight in this time zone, for your rules and for the prices sent to your system, and amounts across MAYA are in this currency, never converted.

Both are saved when your property connects: read from Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations, and set with you for Mews. When no time zone was read, a property gets UTC, the world reference time, and when no currency was read, US dollars. So when the time zone reads UTC, a line under the two values says so in plain words: "UTC and US dollars are what a property gets when its time zone and currency weren't read from its system. If either is wrong for your property, send us a message and we'll correct it." When the currency is not US dollars, the line speaks of the time zone alone. The link opens an email to us. To change either value at any other time, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Time%20zone%20or%20currency) too. [Time, weekends, currency and holidays](@106) explains what each one changes.

Above the cards, what you see depends on the Connection card and on your role. Broken means the card reads Error or Disconnected. Any other word counts as not broken.

- **Not broken, Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations, General Manager or Hotel Admin:** a quiet link, **Reconnect Cloudbeds**. Use it if you have been asked to, for example after your system's permissions changed.
Not broken, Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations, General Manager or Hotel Admin

Degraded, any role

- **Broken, Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations, General Manager or Hotel Admin:** an amber panel headed "MAYA has lost its connection to Cloudbeds" with the button **Reconnect Cloudbeds**. One click sends you to your system to confirm and brings you back to this tab, with a short note: "Reconnected." Your rules, history and settings are untouched.
Broken, Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations, General Manager or Hotel Admin

Broken, Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations, Revenue Manager or Viewer

Sam opens the **PMS** tab. Connection reads Connected. Health reads Healthy, "99% of 412 requests OK". Last sync reads "Sep 22, 2026, 3:05:12 PM PDT", a couple of minutes ago on Sam's clock at The Harbour Inn. Under the cards, the newest request is from a minute ago. Nothing needs doing.

**Not yet** · The tab does not show whether a price reached your system, or when. Sending problems live in the change log, as "Prices not reaching" items. Every property starts in simulation. MAYA reads your bookings, runs every rule and writes what it would do to the change log, but it sends nothing to your property system. Watch for at least a week if you can. There is no badge for the mode yet: the go-live card on the review screen tells you while it is there, and so does the "would have" wording in the amber banner.

Simulation is the state every property is in from the moment it connects. Nothing you do at sign-up or at the connect step switches it off. It ends when a General Manager or Hotel Admin clicks **Turn them on for real** on the review screen and confirms, or when we switch it live at your request.

In simulation MAYA does everything it would do for a live property except the last step. About every five minutes it reads your bookings. About once an hour it reads your own rates for the nights ahead (Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations). Every cycle it runs every rule on the nights whose bookings changed, and once a day, just after midnight at your property, on every night from tonight to 395 nights ahead, and writes the result to the calendar and the change log. Then it stops. No price leaves MAYA.

No. Connecting starts the history import (Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations) and the first cycles, all in simulation. The rates in your system do not move until someone with General Manager or Hotel Admin access clicks **Turn them on for real** on the review screen and confirms, or we switch the property live at your request. [Going live](@55) has the steps.

There is no separate demo or test property. Simulation is the look before you send: your own bookings, your own rules, real numbers, and nothing sent.

No. There is no step where you approve single prices. Simulation and live are one switch for the whole property.
