Every cycle, about every five minutes, MAYA sends the prices that changed since the last successful send, for nights from today to 395 days out (about 13 months), one nightly rate per room type. Cloudbeds applies each price a few seconds after receiving it and tells MAYA when it is done. ThinkReservations accepts each price and applies it shortly after, and MAYA's hourly read then finds it there. If a price never appears in your system, MAYA does not send it again until the night's price changes, so compare the night in both places and email us. Mews receives nothing.

About every five minutes MAYA runs one cycle for your property. It reads your bookings. If an hour has passed, or your hotel day has changed, it reads your own rates for the window too. It prices again every night whose bookings changed, and every night a change of yours reaches (a price you typed, a rule, a room type). Once a day, in the first cycles after midnight at your property, it prices every night of the window again, tonight and the next 395 nights, nearest nights first. Then, if the property is live, it sends the prices that changed. A cycle where nothing changed prices nothing and sends nothing. About once a day MAYA reads every booking again, so anything missed is picked up within the day. [How rules run](@39) covers what happens inside the rules step.

A price you type does not wait for the cycle. The save runs the rules for those nights at once and, on a live property, asks MAYA to send them now. The confirmation says "Saved. Sending to Cloudbeds now." If that nudge cannot be made, it says "Saved. Sending to Cloudbeds on the next cycle (about 5 min)." While the connection reads Disconnected it says "Saved. It will be sent once you reconnect." and no send is asked for. While it reads Error it says "Saved. Cloudbeds isn't answering MAYA right now. MAYA keeps trying to reach it and sends this price as soon as it answers.": the cycle keeps trying to read, and the first read that works sends the price, so no send is asked for either. If MAYA cannot read the connection or whether you are live at that moment, it says only "Saved." and asks for no send: the next cycle sends the price if you are live and connected.

After a save whose price is on its way, the line follows the send. MAYA reads the night's status about 20 seconds, 1 minute and 3 minutes later (and about 6 and 11 minutes later when the price waits for the next cycle or for the connection), stopping once the answer is final, and once more when you open a day with a typed price. The line changes to "Sent to Cloudbeds.", "Saved. It couldn't be sent yet. MAYA will retry 3 more times." with the real count left, or "This price couldn't be sent to Cloudbeds." with **Try again**, which sends it once more now, and **See the error log** or the cause written under it. [Setting a price yourself](@50#what-the-line-says-afterwards) has the lines.
- **Every cycle**, changed prices only, live properties only.
Every cycle
- **Now**, after you save a typed price. If another run is busy with your property, the nudge waits up to a minute and then leaves the price to the next cycle.
Now
- **Not on a cycle where the read of your bookings failed.** Nothing is priced or sent on stale bookings. The next cycle reads again.
Not on a cycle where the read of your bookings failed

- **Not until a read of your bookings has finished.** Your rules run on what has arrived, but MAYA sends nothing until a read of your bookings has finished. On a large property that read can take more than one cycle.
Not until a read of your bookings has finished

Nights beyond the window are not sent and not priced. Each day, at your property's midnight, one more night enters the window and is priced and sent from then on. Your own base rate is read only inside the window too, so load rates that far ahead. [Setting up your system](@20#rates-loaded-about-13-months-ahead) has the check.

Going live sends every priced night of the window, nearest first.

If your property went live when MAYA sent 60 nights, it now sends up to 396 nights ahead too. Nights 61 to 396 got their first price over the few cycles after the window grew, and each is sent again whenever its price changes. Once MAYA has sent to one of those nights, a rate changed by hand in your system on it is kept as a manual price, as it always was inside the 60.

A price you type can reach a little further, up to 399 days ahead. It is saved and shown with its **Manual** badge, and priced and sent once its night enters the window. The confirmation says "Saved. It will be sent when the date enters the 396-day push window." For a range that crosses the edge it says how many nights go now and how many wait: "Saved. 12 nights sending to Cloudbeds now; 8 more will be sent as they enter the 396-day window." Until then it has no Current price.

Nights before your property's today are never sent. Tonight stays in the window, priced and sent like any other night, until midnight at the property. After that it leaves the window.

A night is sent again only when MAYA's price for it changes. If the last successful send to that night was at the same price, to the same rate plan, the night is skipped. That is why a quiet property can go hours with nothing sent, and why the change log's runs often read "Prices checked" with no change.

One exception: a night is sent again at the same price when the rate plan behind its room type changes in your system, for example after a base rate is replaced or the rate catalogue is rebuilt. MAYA re-reads which plan each room type maps to and sends the night to the new one. If you have renamed or rebuilt your rate plans and prices have stopped landing, [Prices are not reaching your property system](@100) has the steps.

**Cloudbeds:** MAYA writes one nightly rate per room type, to that room type's **base rate**: the rate plan that does not follow another plan and has no public name of its own. Every other plan for the room type is left alone. A package, a long-stay plan or any other independent plan is never written, even when the room type has no base rate. A room type with no base rate is left out, and the change log tells you (see "MAYA can't find a base rate" on [When your property system does not accept a price](@57)).

Plans that follow the base rate (derived plans) move by Cloudbeds' own rules when the base rate moves. Booking channels take their rates from Cloudbeds as before. MAYA does not talk to channels.

**ThinkReservations:** MAYA writes one nightly rate per room type, to the property's **Best Available** rate type. ThinkReservations marks a rate type as standard or derived, and a non-refundable rate or a package is standard too, so the rate type MAYA writes to is set by its name. MAYA writes to the standard rate types whose name includes "Best Available". If none has that name, it writes to the one standard rate type that covers the most room types. If two cover the same number, it writes to neither, and nothing is sent until you name one Best Available.

A room type that no base rate type covers is left out, and the change log tells you. Derived rate types reprice themselves from their parent, so writing the parent is the whole job.

**Mews:** Nothing is sent to Mews. MAYA reads Mews bookings and room categories, runs your rules and shows the prices it would send, and stops there. It does not read Mews rates either, so a Mews night is priced only once you type a price for it; nothing is ever priced from what a guest paid.

A price you type on a Mews property is saved and shown but not sent. On a live Mews property the confirmation still says it is sending, for example "Saved. Sending to Mews now." That is wrong: nothing is sent. Ignore it. [Mews: what works today](@14) has the full picture.

Whatever your system, it is one price per room type per night. MAYA cannot send a different price to each rate plan, and it never creates a rate plan, a restriction, a minimum stay or a close-out.

**Cloudbeds:** Cloudbeds applies each price a few seconds after receiving it and tells MAYA when it is done. Right after sending, MAYA asks Cloudbeds how each send went, waits a few seconds for any still being applied, and keeps asking on later cycles for up to 60 minutes.

- A send Cloudbeds reports as applied cleanly counts as landed.
- A send Cloudbeds reports as failed, or applied with a complaint, counts as refused. A cause that clears on its own is retried. A cause that needs you is held. [When your property system does not accept a price](@57) lists each cause and when you are told.
- A send still listed as unfinished 45 minutes after it went out is treated as not applied and the night is sent again.

**ThinkReservations:** ThinkReservations answers each send with "accepted" and applies it shortly after. It tells MAYA nothing more after that. MAYA's check that the price is there comes with its next hourly read of your rates. If a price never appears, MAYA does not send it again until the night's price changes, so compare the night in both places and [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Price%20not%20in%20ThinkReservations).

Until that read, MAYA cannot tell whether the rate is there yet. Two things follow. MAYA does not promise the write is instant, only that it is accepted and then checked within about an hour. And a rate you change in ThinkReservations on that night before MAYA has read its own price back is not kept: the next price change writes over it. [Rates you change in your property system](@51) has the rule.

MAYA's part ends at your property system. A price that changes is sent on that cycle, to the room type's base rate there, and to nothing else. Your booking engine, your channel manager, Booking.com, Expedia and every other channel take their rates from your system, on their own timing, as they did before MAYA. MAYA does not talk to any of them, so it cannot hurry them and cannot tell you how long they take.

So when MAYA shows a new price and a channel still shows the old one, check your property system first. Look at the room type's base rate for that night.

- **Your system still has the old rate.** The price has not reached it yet. A price that changed in the last few minutes may not have gone out. If it is older than that, read [Prices are not reaching your property system](@100).
Your system still has the old rate
- **Your system has MAYA's price.** MAYA's part is done, and the wait is on the channel's side. Ask your channel manager, or your system's support, how often that channel picks up a rate change.
Your system has MAYA's price

- **The channel sells a rate plan MAYA does not write.** A plan that follows your base rate moves by your system's own rules. A plan that does not follow it, such as a package, keeps its own price whatever MAYA sends.

**Cloudbeds:** Compare the room type's base rate in Cloudbeds with the night's Current price in MAYA. Cloudbeds applies a send a few seconds after it goes out, so the two should match within a minute of it.

**ThinkReservations:** Compare the rate on the rate type MAYA writes to (Best Available, as above) with the night's Current price in MAYA. ThinkReservations applies a send shortly after accepting it, so allow a little longer than you would for Cloudbeds.

**Mews:** Nothing is sent to Mews, so MAYA never changes what a channel shows. Your channels show your Mews rates, as they always have.
The channel sells a rate plan MAYA does not write

Before every send MAYA checks each room type and night once more, against the room type as it is now. A night that fails a check is held back and recorded, and never sent. The checks:

| Held back when | Why |
|---|---|
| The night is outside the window | Only nights the cycle priced go out. |
| The room type is switched off in MAYA | A duplicate room type hidden at import, or one you confirmed as a duplicate on the review screen. A room type your system has removed is not switched off. On Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations it is reported in the change log instead (see the next section). |
| The price is 0 | A comp night. No property system is confirmed to take a 0 from MAYA, so you set 0 in your system yourself. You are told in the change log. |

Only two of these are shown to you: the price of 0 and the missing base rate, because those need you. The rest are MAYA's own checks, and most clear on a later cycle without you. A room type switched off as a duplicate is never meant to be sent, and a night your system has at 0 waits until you load a rate there.

**Good to know: A price of 0 is never sent** · Type 0 for a night and the confirmation reads "Saved. MAYA doesn't send a price of 0 to Cloudbeds, so set the night to 0 there yourself." The change log then carries the same reminder until your system has the night at 0. No rule raises a night set to 0.

**Counts as a room** on the PMS tab changes what MAYA divides by for occupancy, what you are billed for, and whether a price is sent for the type. A room type you untick there (a parking bay, a meeting room, a court) is still priced in MAYA whenever it has a starting price, but nothing is sent to your system for it unless one of your rules ticks it under **Apply to room types**, or you type a price for one of its nights. Your own rate for it stays as it is. The floor and ceiling answers from setup are not written onto it either. Tick it in a rule, and its price is sent like any other room type's. Type a price for a night of it on the calendar, and that night is sent as you typed it, with any rule that ticks the type on top; its other nights stay held.

The exception is a duplicate. A room type the review screen hides as a duplicate is switched off in MAYA, and nothing is sent for it. MAYA hides one at import, or you confirm one there later.

A room type your system has removed is not switched off in MAYA. On Cloudbeds its prices cannot land. Once you are live, the change log reports its nights as "Cloudbeds can't find the rate MAYA changes for" that room type. On ThinkReservations its prices cannot land either, and once MAYA's hourly read finds it gone, the change log reports it as "MAYA can't find a base rate for" that room type. [Room types and rooms out of service](@52) says how to have it switched off.

The first time MAYA sends to a night, it writes over the rate you had there. So MAYA makes sure the price it sends was built on a rate it has read recently. A night MAYA has never sent to is held until the cycle's read of your rates has succeeded, or a read within the last hour did. That is why the first send after going live, and the first send to each new night entering the window, can take one cycle longer than you expect.

If the read keeps failing, those nights keep waiting. Once a night has waited an hour, the change log says so at the top: "MAYA couldn't read your current rates in Cloudbeds, so its first prices for Deluxe haven't been sent." The item closes by itself on the first cycle whose read works, when the nights go out. [When your property system does not accept a price](@57#every-cause-and-what-to-do) has what to check.

Once MAYA has sent to a night it stops reading that night's rate as yours. What your system reports back is MAYA's own price, and storing it as your rate would build price on price. Instead MAYA compares. If the rate there differs from what MAYA sent, on a night MAYA sent to and confirmed at least an hour ago, MAYA keeps it as your manual price: your rules start from it, and a rule that fires on that night later moves the price on from your number and sends it. Some changes are not kept this way, for example when nearly every night differs from what MAYA sent by the same percentage.

Nothing is priced or sent on that cycle. MAYA tries again about ten minutes after the first failed read, then every fifteen minutes. The first read that works puts the property back on the normal cycle, prices it and sends what changed.

While reads are failing, the rates already in your system stay exactly as they are. MAYA never sends a rate to undo an earlier one.

MAYA reads your rates as far ahead as your system returns them. A night with no rate on record, and no price typed in MAYA, is not priced and nothing is sent for it, whatever its bookings paid; the day card says "No rate in Cloudbeds for this night yet". When a later read returns a rate for the night, it is priced on it and sent on that run. A night the last read did not return, though an earlier one did, counts the same way until a read returns it again. A price you type for such a night is sent as typed.

If only the hourly read of your rates fails, rules still run and changed prices still go out. Only nights MAYA has never sent to wait for the next successful read, and you are told in the change log once they have waited an hour.

Your prices are made from the prices you typed, your own rates, your room types, your closed periods, your "not a fair comparison" dates and your bookings. A pricing run reads all of them from MAYA's records before it works out a price. If one of them cannot be read, the run stops before it changes any price. It does not carry on without the part it could not read, so a night is never priced as if you had typed no price, or as if your property had never been closed.

The prices already published stay as they are, and nothing new is sent for the nights that run was pricing. The next cycle prices the same nights again and sends what changed. A night that has waited more than 30 minutes to be priced is held back from sending until it is priced, as the table under [What is never sent](#what-is-never-sent) says.

When the latest run could not finish and either three runs in a row have failed or no pricing run has priced anything for your property for 15 minutes, an automatic alert goes to our team, and a second line tells them when a run has priced again. A cycle that ran and found nothing to price does not count as one that priced, so a run that keeps failing is not hidden by the quiet cycles between its tries.

A separate check runs inside MAYA's database every 10 minutes, apart from the pricing cycles, so it still speaks when the cycles stop altogether. It alerts our team when no pricing run has finished for your property in 30 minutes, or when your daily pass has not finished two hours into your hotel day, and says so again once pricing is running normally. It watches live and simulating properties alike, and repeats itself no more than once every six hours for the same property.

On a large property the daily re-read of your bookings can take more than one cycle too. Until it finishes, rules still run but nothing is sent. Sending resumes on the cycle it completes.

When your system is busy it can ask MAYA to slow down, and MAYA waits and tries again. A busy hour at your system can make a large send take a few minutes longer. You do not need to do anything. If it lasts, the change log says so, for example "Cloudbeds asked MAYA to slow down, so Standard rates are taking longer than usual to update". [When your property system does not accept a price](@57) explains that message.

To check a night, compare its Current price in MAYA with the rate in your system. On Cloudbeds they should match within a minute of a send. On ThinkReservations, allow a little longer. For "is it working right now?", start at [Start here: the four questions people ask first](@95).

**Not yet** · MAYA cannot show you what it sent next to what your system has, and there is no per-night "landed" mark. Compare the night in both places, or read the change log for problems.

**Inside my system, how can I tell which rate changes MAYA made and which a colleague made?** MAYA writes through the connection your property approved. On Cloudbeds that is the MAYA app connected from the Marketplace, and on ThinkReservations the ThinkReservations login used to connect it. It sends only the rate for each night, with no note or tag. How your system's own rate history or audit log labels those changes (by the app's name, or by the person who connected it) is up to your system, so look there for which name appears beside them. MAYA's change log is the record of what MAYA set: each change with its night, room type, price and reason. A rate that matches the change log's latest price for that night came from MAYA. On Mews, MAYA writes nothing, so every rate change there is someone else's.

**Does MAYA pick up new bookings instantly?** No. A booking made in your system is read on the next cycle, within about five minutes. The rules price that night again on that cycle, and any price that changes is sent on the same cycle.
Does MAYA pick up new bookings instantly?
**Why did MAYA send a night again at the same price?** The rate plan behind that room type changed in your system, so MAYA sent the night to the new plan.
Why did MAYA send a night again at the same price?

**What does "Last sync" mean?** The time of the last successful read of your bookings. It says nothing about sending. [The PMS tab: connection health](@53) explains the rest of that tab.

**Example: One cycle at the Harbour Inn**

Tuesday, 3:05 PM cycle (your browser's clock). MAYA reads the Harbour Inn's bookings and finds one new booking for Friday, November 13, 2026. That night is now 17 of 20 rooms, 85% full. "Busy nights" (occupancy Greater than 80, Increase 10%) fires on every room type: Standard's $150 becomes $165, Deluxe's $200 becomes $220 and Suite's $300 becomes $330.

The send has three changes, all for November 13: Standard $165, Deluxe $220, Suite $330. Each goes to its room type's base rate in Cloudbeds. MAYA asks Cloudbeds what became of the send a few seconds later and records the prices as landed. The other 395 nights are unchanged and are not sent.
What does "Last sync" mean?

If a price does not land for a reason that usually clears on its own, MAYA sends it again every cycle, up to 10 times at one price, then once a day. If the reason needs you, such as a rate rule, the night is held and tried again after a day, when its price changes, or (for a connection or permission problem) after a reconnect. A missing base rate is different: MAYA looks for one again every cycle, so the night usually goes out on the cycle after you add it. You are told in the change log, in an item headed "Prices not reaching Cloudbeds", straight away for a cause that needs you, otherwise after 2 hours and 5 tries. Nights whose first price is waiting for a read of your own rates are reported after an hour. Each item names the cause and, when there is something for you to do, says what.

Sending problems live in one place: the **Change Log** tab. There is no email and no badge for them. The exception is a lost connection: the connection banner shows when Cloudbeds stops accepting MAYA's connection, and once the connection has read Error or Disconnected for about an hour, the General Managers and Hotel Admins get one email ([emails MAYA sends](@63#the-connection-down-email)). While a problem is ongoing its item sits at the top of the log, above every pricing run, with an amber border. Once it is over it drops into the timeline at the point it ended, and only while the log still shows runs from that time.

Only a live property has these items. In simulation nothing is sent, so nothing can fail to land. Anyone on the team who can open the change log can read them.

An item has four parts, and a fifth you can open.

1. **The header**: "Prices not reaching Cloudbeds", then the date it opened and, in brackets, how long ago. The name is your system's: "Prices not reaching Think Reservations" for ThinkReservations.
The header
2. **The cause**, one sentence, for example "Cloudbeds refused MAYA's price for Deluxe because it breaks a rate rule set in Cloudbeds, such as a minimum or maximum rate."
The cause
3. **The size and the state**: "6 nights, 2 room types · Still happening", or "· Resolved <when>" once the prices landed, or "· Ended <when>" when something else closed it.
The size and the state
4. **What to do**, one line, shown only while the problem is ongoing and only for causes where there is something for you to do: "Check the rate limits for this room type in Cloudbeds."
What to do

5. **Show 12 tries** opens the list of tries behind it, oldest first, one line per group that went the same way: "12 tries, Sep 17, 10:05 AM to 10:50 AM, 6 nights: Cloudbeds refused them". Hover a line to read your system's own words. When every line is a check MAYA made without reaching your system, the button reads **Show 12 checks**. A footer such as "3 other tries not shown" means more tries were counted than listed.

The words at the end of a try line say how it went: "Cloudbeds refused them", "Cloudbeds accepted them, then rejected them", "Cloudbeds never confirmed them", "Nothing to send to in Cloudbeds", "Couldn't read the rates in Cloudbeds", "Waiting to read your rates in Cloudbeds", "MAYA held them back", or "Went through".
Show 12 tries

The sentences below are exactly what the change log says, with Cloudbeds and the Deluxe room type as the example. For ThinkReservations the name changes and nothing else.

| The item says | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Cloudbeds stopped accepting MAYA's connection, so Deluxe rates can't be changed. | Your system no longer accepts MAYA's connection, so nothing can be written. The connection banner appears at the same time. | "Reconnect Cloudbeds on the PMS tab." A General Manager or Hotel Admin clicks **Reconnect Cloudbeds**. Held prices go out on the next cycle after. |
| Cloudbeds won't let MAYA change Deluxe rates because MAYA doesn't have permission to update rates. | Your system lets MAYA read but refuses the write. Someone changed MAYA's permissions there. | "Give MAYA permission to update rates in Cloudbeds, then reconnect on the PMS tab." |

**Good to know: How a refusal gets its cause** · When your system refuses a price, MAYA matches its words against a fixed list of phrases and answer codes. A message on the list gets its cause. Anything else is filed as "couldn't tell why". Your system's own words are behind the hover on the try line, so you can check the match yourself.

There is no screen for changing one room type's floor or ceiling in MAYA. So when your system's minimum sits above MAYA's floor (or its maximum below MAYA's ceiling), you have three ways to line them up. They differ in what else they change.

1. **Change your system to match MAYA.** Lower the minimum, or raise the maximum, for that room type in your system. Only that room type is touched. MAYA's floor and ceiling for each room type are in the **Guardrails** column on the **Rate Simulator** tab.
Change your system to match MAYA

2. **Answer the floor question again.** Your answer becomes the floor of every room type that counts as a room at once, not only this one. Use it when one floor suits them all. A new ceiling answer goes only to room types that have never sold above it. [Set or change a floor or ceiling](@81) has the steps and the catches.
Answer the floor question again

3. **Email us for one room type.** [Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Floor%20and%20ceiling) with the room type and the numbers.

The night that was refused waits. MAYA is not told about a change you make in your system, so the night goes again within a day, or sooner if its price changes. To send it now, type a price on it that sits inside both your system's limits and MAYA's.
Email us for one room type

MAYA counts days on your property's own calendar, using the time zone it read from your system when you connected. If the time zone in your system has since changed, or was wrong then, the two can disagree about when tonight ends. If midnight comes first in your system's time zone, your system counts tonight as over until midnight comes in MAYA's. It refuses any new price MAYA sends for tonight in those hours.

Don't wait for the change log to tell you, because it will usually not show this cause at all. A refused night is held rather than sent every cycle, and at midnight in MAYA's time zone it leaves the 396-night window. An item appears only once one night has had at least 5 tries over 2 hours or more. A held night rarely gets there before midnight.

Look at your rates instead. The sign is a new price for tonight, set in those hours, that shows as the **Current price** in MAYA but never reaches your system. Prices for later nights go through as normal. If you see it, check the property's time zone in your system first. To change the time zone MAYA uses, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Time%20zone). [Time, weekends, currency and holidays](@106) explains how MAYA counts days.

**Example: Eastern in Cloudbeds, Pacific in MAYA** · Say Cloudbeds is set to US Eastern and MAYA has US Pacific. From 9:00 PM to midnight Pacific time, Cloudbeds already counts tonight as over and refuses any new price for tonight. Later nights go through as normal.

- A price that fails for a cause that clears on its own (slowing down, not responding, never confirmed, cause unrecognised) is sent again every cycle, up to 10 tries at that price, then once a day. For a price you typed, the line under the price box on the calendar counts them down: "Saved. It couldn't be sent yet. MAYA will retry 3 more times."

- A price that fails for a cause that needs a person (connection, permission, a rate rule, a night already begun) is held. It is not sent again until the price changes, the rate plan behind it changes, a day has passed, or, for a connection or permission problem, the connection has been reconnected. MAYA is not told about a change you make in your system. So after you do what the item asks there, the held night goes again within a day, or sooner if its price or rate plan changes. You do not have to touch the price. A different price you type goes out now; typing the same price again does not, because the tries are counted per price. To send the same price again now, use **Try again** under the price box on the calendar: it appears once the line there reads "This price couldn't be sent to Cloudbeds.", and sends that price once more, whatever held it.

- A room type with no base rate, or whose only rates follow another plan, is not held. While its nights have nowhere to go, MAYA reads your system's rate plans again on every cycle. So once you add a base rate, the nights usually go out on the next cycle. For a price you typed on such a room type, the line under the price box reads "This price couldn't be sent to Cloudbeds." with the cause, and no **Try again**.
- A rate MAYA cannot find is looked up again once, after re-reading your catalogue, and then held.
- A price of 0 is never sent. MAYA checks each cycle whether your system now has the night at 0, and closes the item when it does.
- A night is never given up on for good. Every held or exhausted night gets one more try each day, so a fix nobody told MAYA about, such as a rate rule loosened in your system, is picked up within a day.

- **At once** for a cause that needs you: a connection or permission problem, a derived-only rate, a missing base rate, a rate rule, a price of 0. And for a rate MAYA cannot find, once its second try has failed.
At once

- **After 2 hours and at least 5 tries** for the causes that usually clear on their own. A price that lands on a retry before then is never mentioned. That is deliberate: an item you cannot act on is noise.
After 2 hours and at least 5 tries

- **Usually not at all** for a night that had already begun. Such a night leaves the window at midnight, nearly always before it reaches 5 tries. [The time zone case](#the-time-zone-case) says what to look for instead.

An item that closed within the last hour and then fails again is reopened rather than duplicated.
Usually not at all

An item is over when no night is still failing for that cause. The second line then says how it ended:

- **Resolved** when your system took the prices (for ThinkReservations, when it accepted them).
Resolved

- **Ended** when something else closed it: a new price replaced the failing one, the night left the 396-night window, the night is no longer priced, or the property stopped sending (it went back to simulation, or its subscription lapsed).

A resolved or ended item is not deleted. It sits in the timeline at the point it ended, for as long as the log shows runs from that time.
Ended

The cause sentence names which system did what: "Cloudbeds refused", "Cloudbeds isn't responding", "MAYA doesn't send". The hover shows your system's own words. As a rule:

- A refusal that names a setting (a rate rule, a permission, a plan that follows another) is settled in your system. For Cloudbeds, Cloudbeds Support can see those settings; we cannot.
- Slowing down, not responding and never confirmed are your system being busy or down. Wait.
- "MAYA couldn't tell why" and anything you cannot place: email us with the sentence, the hover text and your property name.

[Contact support](@111) has our address and the link to Cloudbeds Support.

Only when the item has an action line. An item with no action line is MAYA keeping you informed while it retries. If the action line asks you to add a base rate, the nights usually go out on the next cycle after you do. If it asks for another change in your system, such as a rate limit, make the change, and the held nights go again within a day, or sooner if their price changes. If it asks for a reconnect, a General Manager or Hotel Admin reconnects on the PMS tab, and the held prices go out on the cycle after. [Reconnect your property system](@92) has the clicks.

**Cloudbeds:** Everything on this page applies as written. A refused write for a gone connection also marks the connection disconnected, so the reconnect banner appears at the same time.

**ThinkReservations:** The sentences read "Think Reservations" in place of "Cloudbeds". Three differences:

- A refused write never disconnects ThinkReservations. It is held as a permission problem and the connection stays up for reading. So the cause "stopped accepting MAYA's connection" is never filed for ThinkReservations; you see "won't let MAYA change ... because MAYA doesn't have permission to update rates" instead.

- If ThinkReservations quietly drops an accepted batch, the night keeps showing MAYA's price in MAYA while ThinkReservations keeps the old rate, until the price next changes and is sent again. Compare a night in both places if you suspect this.

**Mews:** Nothing is sent to Mews, so a Mews property never has a "Prices not reaching" item.

Before every send MAYA checks each night against the room type as it is now: inside the window, room type still active, price above 0, inside the floor and ceiling, backed by a recent pricing run, and your system not holding the night at 0 with no typed price. A night held by one of those checks is recorded but not shown to you, except a price of 0, which needs you. Most of the others clear on a later cycle without you. A room type switched off as a duplicate is never meant to be sent, and a night your system has at 0 waits until you load a rate there. [How prices reach your property system](@56) lists the checks.

Sam sets a minimum rate of $120 on Deluxe in Cloudbeds. MAYA's floor for Deluxe is $110, lower than that minimum. On Monday, "Last minute" (booking window Less than 3 and occupancy Less than 50, Decrease 15%) cuts Deluxe for a quiet Wednesday night from $140 to $119. That is above MAYA's floor, so it goes out, and Cloudbeds refuses it.

Because a rate rule is a cause that needs a person, the change log shows at once: "Prices not reaching Cloudbeds", then "Cloudbeds refused MAYA's price for Deluxe because it breaks a rate rule set in Cloudbeds, such as a minimum or maximum rate." and "1 night, 1 room type · Still happening", with "Check the rate limits for this room type in Cloudbeds."

To pause, turn your rules off: the prices they set stay where they are. To undo what a rule did, delete it. To hold a price on some nights, type it. To put the whole property back into simulation, email us; only we can switch it. Turning rules off, typing a price or going back to simulation never puts back a rate MAYA has replaced. Deleting a rule is the one route that does: its changes come off and the new prices are sent.

| You want to | Do this | Prices already in your system |
|---|---|---|
| Stop every rule acting from now on | Turn each rule **Off** on the **Rules** tab | Stay as they are |
| Undo everything one rule did | **Delete** the rule | Go back to what they would be without it, and are sent |
| Stop one rule on certain nights | Answer **Stop for this night** on the amber banner | Stay as they are, unless the rule's undo box is ticked and cancellations mean the rule is no longer true |
| Hold a price on a night or a stretch | Type the price on the **Calendar** tab, with **through…** for a range | Become the price you typed |
| Stop sending altogether, keep everything else | Email us to go back to simulation | Stay as they are |

Every rule on the **Rules** tab has an **On** / **Off** switch. Click it and the rule is off from the next pricing run. There is no confirmation for switching off.

Off freezes. The rule stops acting, and every change it has already made stays on the price: a raise stays raised, a cut stays cut. Those prices are already in your system and MAYA does not send them again or send anything to undo them. Turn the rule **On** again and a window first shows the days it will change. With **Apply price adjustments** it resumes from the next run, starting from the prices as they are. With **Skip price adjustments** those days keep their prices until the rule stops being true on a day and then becomes true again, and every other night works as with Apply. Read [Turning a rule on, Apply or Skip](@41).

To pause everything, turn every rule off. Nothing else happens: MAYA keeps reading your bookings and your rates, and sends a price only when one changes. With every rule off, a price changes when you type or clear one, or when a floor or ceiling you change moves it. And each morning one new night enters the window. It goes out at your own rate, kept between your floor and ceiling. [Pause everything for a while](@71) is the short version.

**Careful: Off does not undo** · Turning a rule off keeps every price it set. If a rule has set prices you do not want, delete it, or type the prices you want. Off alone leaves them in place.

The red **Delete** button on a rule opens a dialog headed "Delete "Busy nights"?". It says: "Deleting this rule also undoes the price changes it has already made. Any night it adjusted goes back to what the price would be if this rule had never run." It then offers the other choice, turning the rule off instead, with the prices it set staying exactly as they are. And it warns: "Deleting cannot be undone."

Three buttons: **Delete Rule and Undo Its Changes**, **Turn It Off and Keep Its Changes** (which does the same as the switch and closes the dialog), and **Cancel**.

Once three of a booking speed or pickup rule's changes are on the same night, the amber Rules that keep adjusting banner asks you what to do. **Stop for this night** stops that rule on that night. What it already changed there stays, unless its undo box is ticked and cancellations mean the rule is no longer true. Your other rules keep working there. The rule then shows a "Stopped on 3 nights" chip on the **Rules** tab, and **Let it run again** puts it back. [Rules that keep adjusting](@43) explains the banner. There is no way to stop a rule on one night before the banner asks, other than turning the rule off everywhere. A typed price takes off what the rule already did on that night, but the rule can fire on it again.

Click a night on the **Calendar** tab, type a price for a room type, click **through…** to pick the last night if you want a range, and click **Save**. On a live property, nights inside the 396-night window go to your system as typed, now. Nights further ahead are sent as they enter the window. In simulation nothing is sent. Rules that had already moved those nights pause for that room type. Rules that fire later still apply on top of your price, so a typed price is a starting point, not a lock. A range can run from tonight up to 399 days ahead (366 nights at most in one save).

**Clear** takes your price off the night, and your rules set its price again. [Setting a price yourself](@50) has every detail, and [Hold a price for a wedding or event weekend](@68) is the short version.

There is no switch in MAYA to put a property back into simulation. Going live is one-way in the app. To go back, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Back%20to%20simulation) from your MAYA sign-in address with your property name. We switch it for you.

What happens once we do:
- **Sending stops on the next cycle.** Everything else carries on: bookings are read, rules run, the change log fills, the calendar shows what MAYA would send.
Sending stops on the next cycle

- **The prices already in your system stay.** MAYA never sends a rate to undo an earlier one. If you want different rates, set them in your system, or wait until you are live again and type them in MAYA.
The prices already in your system stay

- **On a night MAYA never sent to, a rate you change in your system becomes the base.** For example, a night that entered the window after we switched you back. MAYA reads your rate again within the hour (Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations) and uses it as the night's starting price. It is not kept as a manual price.
On a night MAYA never sent to, a rate you change in your system becomes the base

- **On a night MAYA sent to while you were live, a rate you change in your system waits.** While you simulate, your rules keep working from the base that night already had. When you go live again, MAYA reads your rate as that night's base (next point).
On a night MAYA sent to while you were live, a rate you change in your system waits

- **When you go live again**, from the button on the review screen if it is still there (otherwise email us and we switch you live again), MAYA reads your rates once more before its first send, and your rules work on top of them. A night whose rate you changed while simulating starts from that rate. A rate you changed in your system on a night MAYA had sent to, and that MAYA had already kept as a manual price ("Changed in Cloudbeds"), stays a manual price.
When you go live again

- **Your rules, limits, history, manual prices and team are untouched.**

[Simulation mode](@54) describes the state you go back to.
Your rules, limits, history, manual prices and team are untouched

Cancelling your subscription is a different thing from pausing. It is done in the billing portal or by email, takes effect at the end of the paid period, and MAYA keeps working until then. After that, reading, pricing and sending stop, and the rates in your system stay as they are. Your rules and history stay too, and **Restart your subscription** brings MAYA back. [Cancelling, restarting and leaving](@62) has the steps.

MAYA does not read future closures from your system, and there is no screen to enter one. Nights you are closed are priced and sent like any others while they are inside the 396-night window. Three ways to handle a closed stretch, from simplest:

1. **Close the nights in your system.** Set the rate to 0 there (or close the night the way your system does, if that reports as a rate of 0). On a night MAYA has already sent to, MAYA reads the 0 on its next hourly read, your rules stop running on that night, and any manual price there is cleared. On a night MAYA has never sent to, a rate of 0 means the night is not priced at all. Either way nothing more is sent for it. When you reopen and load a rate, MAYA reads it as the night's base and your rules work on top of it. This works for Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations. Nothing is sent to Mews in any case.
Close the nights in your system
2. **Turn your rules off** for the closed stretch and back on afterwards. Simple to do, but it pauses every night, open or closed.
Turn your rules off

3. **Type a price** for the closed nights as a range. A typed price is sent as typed, so this only helps if a placeholder rate is what you want in your system.

A closure in the past is a separate matter: it should not skew comparisons. MAYA finds long stretches of zero occupancy in your history and asks on the review, "Were you closed ...?". Confirming keeps those nights out of comparisons. [Checking what MAYA found](@26) explains that card.
Type a price
On February 1 Sam loads $150 for Standard from February 15 onwards. MAYA reads $150 as the base for those nights and "Busy nights" raises the ones over 80% full to $165 as usual.

Click **Billing** at the top right of the dashboard. General Managers and Hotel Admins see it. Everyone else sees a line saying who to ask. The top card says where you stand in one sentence. **Your plan** lists status, price and next charge. **Update card, receipts & cancellation** opens Stripe's billing portal, where your card, invoices and cancellation live. Your room count is changed on this page, never in Stripe.

**Billing** is a button at the top right of the dashboard, beside **Team** and **Sign Out**. The page is headed "Billing" with three links: **Help**, **Your team** and **← Back to MAYA**.

Only a General Manager or Hotel Admin can see the plan and act on it. A Revenue Manager or Viewer who opens the page sees one line instead: "Billing is handled by this property's General Manager or Hotel Admin. Ask one of them for access if you need to change it." Everyone on the property, Viewers included, still sees the dashboard banner when something needs attention, so nobody is left wondering why prices stopped. [Roles: who can do what](@64) has the full table.

One sentence at the top of the page says where you stand. MAYA shows the sentence that matters most, in this order, and colours the card to match: plain, amber for a warning, red when work has stopped.

| Title | Colour | What it means and what to do |
|---|---|---|
| "MAYA has paused work on this property" | red | "Your rules no longer run on a schedule and nothing is sent to your PMS." If the status is "Unpaid", the card says to update your card and the subscription restarts where it left off. If it is "Paused", the card says "Your subscription is on hold. Email us and we'll get it running again.", with our email address under it and no restart button ([Your plan](#your-plan) explains). For any other status it says the subscription was cancelled and starting again means a new one, and a green **Restart your subscription** button sits under it. |
| "Your last payment did not go through" | amber | The bank is retrying the payment, and your rules keep running while it does. Update your card to avoid an interruption. |

The amount in the last two rows is Stripe's own total for your whole next invoice. It includes any code. After a room count change it also includes the part-period difference: more after a raise, less (down to nothing) after a credit from lowering the count. So for one invoice it can differ from your usual price. If Stripe cannot be reached within a moment, the bracket price for your room count shows instead, which can be higher or lower than the invoice. That is also why the number can differ from the calculator on get-maya.com.

Four rows at most.

- **Status.** One of "On trial", "Active", "Payment overdue", "Unpaid (stopped)", "Cancelled", "Never completed" (a checkout that was never finished) or "Paused" (explained under this list).
Status

- **Price**, or **Was** once the subscription is over (the status reads "Cancelled" or "Never completed"). An "Unpaid" or "Paused" subscription can still come back, so it keeps **Price**. Under **Price** it is the same number as the top card, Stripe's total for your next invoice, followed by "per month" or "per year". After a room count change that total includes the part-period difference, so it may not be your monthly (or yearly) price. The hint reads, for example, "20 rooms at MAYA's monthly rate." It adds "with your code applied" while a discount from your code is on that next invoice. Otherwise, when that total before any tax differs from the bracket price, it adds "adjusted for a recent room count change". Tax on its own never adds it.
Price
- **Trial ends.** The date, only during a trial.
Trial ends

- **Next charge**, or one of its other names: **Access ends** (set to cancel: MAYA works until this date, then stops), **Retrying payment until** (a payment failed and the bank is retrying), **Unpaid since** (the retries ran out) or **Ended** (the status reads "Cancelled" or "Never completed"). Under **Unpaid since** the date is when the first invoice still unpaid was raised. An "Unpaid" subscription is not over: update your card in the portal and it restarts where it left off. If Stripe cannot be reached within a moment, the row is left out. Under every other name the date is the end of the current billing period. So while a payment is being retried, the date is not when the retries stop: they usually stop well before it, after about two weeks. A "Paused" subscription has no date row.
Next charge

**What "Paused" means.** The subscription is on hold in Stripe. No invoices are made, and work on the property stops, as it does for "Unpaid". You cannot pause a subscription from MAYA or from the billing portal, so this status is rare. The top card says "Your subscription is on hold. Email us and we'll get it running again." with our email address under it. [Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Paused%20subscription) and we get it running again with you. There is no **Restart your subscription** button, because a paused subscription still exists in Stripe and a second one beside it would bill you twice.
What "Paused" means

This amber section appears only after a card check has failed: "We checked it on" the date "and your bank declined it", with the bank's short reason in brackets, then "Nothing has failed yet" and a note that updating the card now avoids an interruption. Nothing has been charged and nothing has stopped. [Cards, payments and invoices](@61) explains the check and how the warning clears.

The button **Update card, receipts & cancellation** (it reads "Opening…" while the link is made) opens Stripe's billing portal, and the line under it says why: "Opens Stripe, where your card, invoices and cancellation all live." When you are done, Stripe returns you to this page.

**Not yet** · No invoices, receipts or billing history inside the app. They live in the Stripe portal. No pause. No way to see a property's billing until its system is connected. The code you used at checkout is not shown. The page shows US dollars whatever your property's currency.

MAYA charges per room and counts your rooms from your property system on every sync, leaving out room types you have unticked as rooms. Up to 500 rooms, if it finds more rooms than you pay for, you get a banner, an email and 7 days to set the count yourself before MAYA raises it and adjusts your next invoice. It never lowers the count for you: if you run fewer rooms, lower it on the **Billing** page and your next invoice drops.

About every five minutes, when MAYA reads your bookings, it also adds up the rooms in your active room types. Two kinds of type are left out:

- **Types you have unticked as rooms.** On the **PMS** tab, each room type has a **Counts as a room** box. Untick it for anything nobody sleeps in, such as a meeting room, a spa slot or a court. An unticked type is left out of the count whatever its name. A ticked one is counted whatever its name. Your answer is final in both directions.
Types you have unticked as rooms

Some words leave a type out whatever else its name says, such as meeting, conference, boardroom, banquet, parking, massage, treatment, storage and day use. Others leave a type out only when its name has no bedroom word in it (room, suite, king, queen, villa or cabin, for example). Spa, pool, cabana, court, event, hall, package and fee are words of this second kind. So "Spa Suite" is counted, while "Meeting Room", "Garden Cabana" and "Pool House" are left out.

If the **Billing** page lists a type as not counted and guests do sleep there, tick it on the **PMS** tab and it joins the count.
Types you have not answered for, whose name reads like something nobody sleeps in

**Cloudbeds:** Cloudbeds reports how many rooms each room type has, so the count MAYA measures is the count Cloudbeds holds.

**ThinkReservations:** ThinkReservations lists every room at your property, and MAYA counts the rooms of each room type from that list on every sync. A room ThinkReservations marks as inactive, as not a room, or as not included in occupancy is left out. So the count MAYA measures is the rooms ThinkReservations holds in the types ticked as rooms: The Harbour Inn's 12 Standard, 6 Deluxe and 2 Suites measure as 20.

If the count looks wrong, check those settings on the rooms in ThinkReservations. MAYA reads the change on the next sync. If ThinkReservations cannot send the list of rooms on a sync, MAYA keeps the counts it already has.

**Mews:** Mews does not report how many rooms each category has, so MAYA gives every category one number, which we set with you when we connect (100 until then). We cannot set a separate number for each category, and there is no field in MAYA for you to set it yourself.

So the count is that one number times the categories counted as rooms, and it may not match what you run: at 100, three such categories read as 300 rooms. Check the **Room count** section of the **Billing** page in the days after connecting, and if the measured number is higher than what you run, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Mews%20room%20counts) before the 7 days pass. If they have already passed and your count was raised, [you can put it right](#if-the-100-rooms-number-has-already-raised-your-count).

The **Room count** section of the **Billing** page starts with "Your plan covers 20 rooms. We check this against your property management system." Then, depending on your property:

- "Not counted, because they don't look like guest rooms:" followed by the names. MAYA read these names and left the types out. If one of them is a guest room, tick it under **PMS**, then Room types, and it joins the count. Each of them shows unticked there.
- "You've marked these as not rooms:" followed by the names. Your own unticks. Change them on the same tab if one is wrong.
- "Every room type is marked as not a room, so we can't measure your count." in amber. Tick the types guests sleep in.

**1. First a banner, then an email**

The moment MAYA measures more rooms than you pay for, the top card on the **Billing** page and the dashboard banner turn amber: "You're billed for 20 rooms but running 24", then "MAYA charges per room, so 4 rooms are not being paid for." At first it adds "Set the count right below. We'll email you before anything changes." (above 500 rooms it says something else, as [Over 500 rooms](#over-500-rooms) explains). Once the email is out it says how many days remain: "Set the count right below within 7 days and nothing else happens. After that we'll update it to 24 for you and adjust your next invoice."

The email follows at the next daily check (once a day), so it can arrive the day after the banner. Above 500 rooms it never comes, as [Over 500 rooms](#over-500-rooms) explains. It goes to the address on your billing account, the one that receives invoices. Its subject is "Your MAYA plan covers 20 rooms, and your PMS shows 24", with your own numbers. Its heading is "Your room count has changed", and it says what your system lists, what your plan covers, what you pay today and what you would pay at the measured count ("$110 today, $120 at 24 rooms"), that you have 7 days to set the number yourself, and the date after which MAYA updates it. A button, **Set your room count**, opens the **Billing** page. It also names any types that were left out and why, so your own count and MAYA's reconcile.

That is how the correction works today. The Terms (clause 7.5) also allow the difference to be charged separately, and allow us to invoice for rooms that were in use but not paid for during the previous 12 months. MAYA does neither on its own: the raise above is the only change it makes to your bill, and it charges only from the day of the raise. [Terms and legal](@110) lists the clauses.

Any shortfall counts. There is no tolerance band: one extra room is a real amount every month, so one extra room triggers the email.

The Harbour Inn pays for 20 rooms at $5.50, $110 a month. Sam opens a 4-room annex in Cloudbeds as a new room type. On the next sync MAYA measures 24. The banner reads "You're billed for 20 rooms but running 24", the email says "$110 today, $120 at 24 rooms" (24 rooms sits in the next bracket, at $5.00 a room). Sam can type 24 in **Rooms billed** today, or let MAYA do it in a week. Either way the next invoice is $120 plus the part-month difference, and the property's team grows from 2 seats to 4.

MAYA never lowers the count for you. A wing closed for a fortnight's refurbishment would otherwise cut the bill without anyone asking, and put it back up with a warning email when the wing reopened. Instead, the **Room count** section says "Your PMS currently shows 16 active rooms." and "You're paying for more than that", and you lower it yourself if you want to.

Lowering the count gives a credit for the unused part of the current period, taken off future invoices. It is never a cash refund.

On Mews, the 7 days can run out before your real count is set. MAYA then raises your billed count to the measured number: The Harbour Inn would go from 20 rooms at $110 a month to 300 rooms at $750. Here is how to put it right.

**1. Email us your real room counts**

[Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Room%20count%20raised) with your property's name and how many rooms each room type has. We set your property's rooms-per-type number. Within about five minutes the **Room count** section of the **Billing** page shows the new measured number.

**2. Lower Rooms billed to that number**

Once the new measured number shows, type it in **Rooms billed** and click **Change**. Two things bring the email back, and a new raise 7 days later: lowering the count while it still reads 300, and lowering it below the new measured number.
If you want those days looked at too, say so in the same email. Anything beyond the credit is up to us, case by case. The Terms call it a one-off courtesy, so we cannot promise it.

**1. Open Billing and find Room count**

The section is there while the subscription is running. A General Manager or Hotel Admin can change it.

**2. Type the new number in Rooms billed**

Any whole number from 1 to 500. Anything else shows "Enter a whole number between 1 and 500." **Change** stays greyed out until the number is valid and different from today's.

**3. Read the quote**

Before you save, a line shows what the new bill will be, from the same brackets Stripe bills: "$110 up to $120 per month. Your next invoice is adjusted for the part of this period you have already paid." Going down, it adds in green "That is $22 less." If the new count lands in the same price, it reads "Still $110 per month."

**4. Click Change**

It reads "Saving…", then "Room count updated." Stripe confirms the change to MAYA a moment later, so the number on the page can take a moment to catch up.
- **"This property has no subscription to change."** Set up payment for the property first.
"This property has no subscription to change."
- **"This subscription has nothing to change."** [Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Room%20count) and we look at the subscription.
"This subscription has nothing to change."
- **"Could not change the room count. Try again shortly."** Wait a moment, then try again.
"Could not change the room count. Try again shortly."

- **"This property's subscription is not active, so MAYA has paused work on it."** The subscription has lapsed. Fix the payment first.

The count is changed here and only here. Stripe's billing portal does not offer a quantity control, because MAYA measures the count and would correct a number typed there.

**Careful: Lowering below what you run brings the email back** · If you lower the count below what your system shows, the next sync measures the shortfall again, the email goes out, and after 7 days MAYA raises it back. Lower it only when the rooms really are gone from your system, or untick the types that are not rooms.
"This property's subscription is not active, so MAYA has paused work on it."

How many people can be on your team depends on the rooms you pay for: 2 seats up to 20 rooms, 4 up to 40, 5 up to 60, 6 up to 80, 8 up to 500. Raising the count raises the seats at the same moment. [Inviting and removing people](@65) has the details.

Self-serve stops at 500. If MAYA measures more than 500 rooms, the banner still turns amber, for example "You're billed for 20 rooms but running 600", and ends "That's above what we sell self-serve. Email us and we'll set it up with you." The banner's button reads **Email us** and opens an email to us. On the **Billing** page our email address sits under it. You pay by card, and Stripe holds it. MAYA checks the card with a zero-amount check right after checkout and again 48 hours later. No money moves. If a payment fails, your rules keep running while your bank retries, and a live Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations property keeps sending prices as normal. Nothing is sent to Mews yet, or while a property is in simulation. If the retries run out, work stops until the card is updated, and your rates, rules and history stay as they are. Invoices and receipts live in Stripe's billing portal, which opens from the **Billing** page.

You pay by card. Stripe hosts the payment page and holds the card, and MAYA never sees the card number. Paying from a US bank account (ACH) is switched off, because the two card checks below are made for a card. Every payment is taken automatically, so there is no bank transfer and no invoice to pay by hand. Prices are in US dollars whatever your property's currency.

If the bank's answer is inconclusive (it wants the cardholder present, say), MAYA asks again. It asks up to 4 times in all for each check, about 6 hours apart, and then records that check as failed. A card removed from the billing account after checkout counts as failed too.

A failed check never stops MAYA working. It raises two things: the top card on the **Billing** page reads "Your saved card stopped working" with "Nothing has failed yet, but the next charge will. Update it before your renewal to keep pricing running.", and an amber section headed "Your card needs attention" says "We checked it on" the date "and your bank declined it", with the bank's short reason in brackets. The dashboard shows the amber **Fix it** banner to everyone on the property.
The warning clears by itself the next time a payment goes through. Saving a new card does not clear it on the spot. The next successful charge does.

**1. The bank retries and MAYA keeps working**

Stripe retries the card over a period (about two weeks). During the retries the status on the **Billing** page reads "Payment overdue" and the date row is renamed **Retrying payment until**. The top card reads "Your last payment did not go through", and says your rules keep running while the bank retries and that updating your card now avoids an interruption. The date on it is the end of the current billing period, not the last retry: the retries usually stop well before it (about two weeks). The dashboard shows the amber **Fix it** banner. Your rules keep running as normal, and a live Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations property keeps sending prices. Nothing is sent to Mews yet, or while a property is in simulation, whether or not a payment has failed.

**2. If the retries run out, work stops**

The status becomes "Unpaid (stopped)". The top card turns red: "MAYA has paused work on this property" with "Your rules no longer run on a schedule and nothing is sent to your PMS. Update your card and the subscription restarts where it left off." The dashboard shows the red **Restart MAYA** banner. There is no **Restart your subscription** button in this state, because the subscription is still alive in Stripe. Update the card in the portal and save it as your default. MAYA then pays the open invoice with that card straight away, and moves the subscription onto it so later charges come from it too. Once the payment goes through, the status goes back to "Active" and work picks up again. If the new card is declined too, the status stays "Unpaid". Save a different card as your default and MAYA tries that one.

In a group of properties on one card, each property is charged on its own renewal date, so each one fails and retries on its own. The owner fixes them by moving them onto a working card. Read [If the shared card fails](@10#if-the-shared-card-fails).

When work has stopped, for a lapsed payment or a cancellation:

- The scheduled reads of your bookings and the scheduled runs of your rules stop, and nothing is sent to your system. This is the same for Cloudbeds, ThinkReservations and Mews.
- If you type or clear a manual price, MAYA still runs your rules again on those nights, and the new prices show on the calendar. Nothing is sent. A change to **Counts as a room** or **Rooms out of service** is saved, and priced from the first cycle after work starts again. The line after a save says so: "Saved. Nothing is sent while MAYA's work is paused. Update your card on the Billing page." When the subscription reads Cancelled or Never completed it ends "Restart your subscription on the Billing page." instead, and when it is on hold, "Email us and we'll get it running again."

- The rates already in your property system stay exactly as they were last sent. Nothing is reverted, and nothing new goes out. [Rates you change in your property system](@51) has what to do with them.
- Your rules, floors and ceilings, history, manual prices, team and settings all stay.
- You can still sign in and read the calendar, the change log and the team page.

**1. Open Billing**

Click **Billing** at the top right of the dashboard. General Manager or Hotel Admin only.

**2. Click Update card, receipts & cancellation**

Stripe's billing portal opens. Choose the option to update the payment method, enter the new card, and save it as your default.

**3. Come back**

Stripe returns you to the **Billing** page. If the status was "Unpaid", there is nothing more to do: MAYA pays the open invoice with the new card and moves the subscription onto it. Otherwise your subscription may keep charging the card it started with, including when Stripe retries an overdue payment. To be sure the new card is used, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Move%20to%20a%20new%20card) and we move the subscription onto it. A card warning clears after the next successful payment, not the moment you save.

In a group of properties from the Cloudbeds Marketplace, the card belongs to the owner's billing account. A General Manager or Hotel Admin of one property who does not also manage the others cannot reach the card from their **Billing** page. The owner updates it, or [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Group%20card). [Paying for a group of properties](@10) explains.

Each billing period is charged at its start, in advance, on its renewal date: a monthly plan pays for the month ahead, a yearly plan for the year ahead. After a free trial, the first charge falls on the day the trial ends. The **Billing** page shows the date under **Next charge**. A change to your room count is not charged on the day: the difference for the rest of the period goes on your next invoice, as a charge or a credit.

Your renewal date comes from the day the subscription started, or the day its trial ended. There is no setting in MAYA to move it, and Stripe's portal cannot move it either. In a group, each property keeps its own renewal date, so the properties are charged on different days. If you need them lined up, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Renewal%20date).

Every invoice and receipt lives in Stripe's billing portal, under the same button. There is no invoice list inside MAYA. They stay in the portal after you cancel, as [Cancelling, restarting and leaving](@62#your-invoices-after-you-cancel) explains. Stripe, not MAYA, sends any receipt or failed-payment email, to the email address on the billing account.

An accountant who only needs invoices does not need a MAYA login: forward the receipts, or change the billing email in the portal to an address they read. A login for the **Billing** page itself needs General Manager or Hotel Admin, which also grants the power to go live and change the team, so it is rarely the right fit.

Before you commit, two screens show the price: the calculator on the get-maya.com home page, and the price panel on the payment screen, which re-prices the moment you type a code. MAYA does not produce a formal quote, a pro-forma invoice or supplier forms such as a W-9. If your accounts team needs any of these, or our company details for supplier set-up, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Supplier%20paperwork) and say what they need. A vendor form or purchase order you send does not change the Terms. Read [Terms and legal](@110).

A charge for MAYA shows under MAYA's business name, as your bank prints it. Banks often shorten the name. The first charge after a free trial ends is marked once so you can spot it: it begins "MAYA" and ends "TRIAL OVER".

The charge is in US dollars, so a card in another currency shows the amount your bank converted. The card checks above are not charges. To match a statement line to an invoice, compare its date and amount with the invoices in the billing portal.

Prices exclude tax, and under the Terms (clause 7.7) any tax is yours to pay. Whether tax is added at checkout, with a full billing address and a business tax ID asked for, depends on how billing is set up at the time, not on anything you choose. Each invoice in the billing portal shows whether tax was added. The portal also lets you add or change a billing address and a business tax ID.

In the portal. A switch starts a new billing period on the day you make it, and Stripe charges for that period straight away, less a credit for the unused part of the old one.

From monthly to yearly, a full year is charged that day, less the unused days of your month. From yearly to monthly, the credit for the unused year is usually more than a month costs, so the rest stays as a credit on your billing account and comes off later invoices. A switch during a free trial ends the trial that day and charges the new plan at once.

Yearly is 10% cheaper from 21 rooms up, and the same price as twelve monthly payments for 1 to 20 rooms. [What it costs](@3) has the brackets.

Add the new card in the portal and save it as your default, as in the steps above. A subscription can keep the card it was set up with at checkout, so the old card may still be charged. To be sure it is not, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Move%20to%20a%20new%20card) and we move your subscription onto the new card. A subscription whose status reads "Unpaid" is the exception: saving the new card as your default pays its open invoice and moves it onto the new card, with nothing to email.

You can, in Stripe's billing portal. Open it with **Update card, receipts & cancellation** on the **Billing** page, add the second card, and choose which card is the default.

Each payment comes from one card: the card on your subscription (the one from checkout), or your default card if the subscription has none. If a payment fails, Stripe retries that same card and does not switch to the spare by itself. Making the spare your default may not move a subscription that has its own card, so to switch to the spare, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Move%20to%20a%20new%20card) and we move it. Under the Terms there are no refunds for part of a billing period, unused rooms, downgrades, suspensions or time when the Service or your property system was unavailable. Apart from any refund the law requires, there are two exceptions: if we discontinue the Service entirely, or end your agreement for our own reasons on 30 days' warning, we refund the unused part of the current paid period. Lowering your room count gives a credit against future invoices, never cash. Any other credit is a one-off courtesy.

If a charge looks wrong, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Disputed%20charge) with the invoice number within 60 days of the charge, and we look into it. Under the Terms, a charge you have not raised with us in writing within 60 days is final.

Please [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Disputed%20charge) before you ask your bank to reverse a charge. We can usually sort it out faster. Under the Terms, reversing a correct charge makes you liable for the fees it causes. [Terms and legal](@110) has the clauses on disputes and overdue amounts.

**Example: The card on file expires at The Harbour Inn**

The card on file expires in June. The 48-hour check passed months ago, so nothing warns in advance. On the June renewal the charge fails: the status reads "Payment overdue" and the **Fix it** banner appears for everyone, Priya included. Sam, the Hotel Admin, opens **Billing**, clicks **Update card, receipts & cancellation**, saves the new card as the default and returns, then emails us to move the subscription onto it. Stripe's next retry succeeds, the status goes back to "Active", and prices never stopped.

Cancel from Stripe's billing portal (opened from the **Billing** page) or by emailing us. It takes effect at the end of the paid period, and MAYA keeps working until then. Your rules, floors and ceilings, history and settings stay, and **Restart your subscription** brings MAYA back. Cancelling does not disconnect your property system, and disconnecting does not cancel. **1. Open Billing and click Update card, receipts & cancellation**

Choose to cancel, pick a reason from Stripe's list, and confirm. MAYA keeps the reason category for its own records and never any comment you type. Stripe returns you to the **Billing** page.

The top card now reads "This subscription is set to cancel" with "MAYA keeps working until" the date "then stops." The **Next charge** row is renamed **Access ends**. Nothing else changes yet.

Your role is set on each property separately, by that property's General Manager or Hotel Admin. The same person can be Hotel Admin on one property and Viewer on another. [Several properties on one account](@7) has the switch.

One difference: managing Hotel Admins. A General Manager can hand out any role up to General Manager, change or remove anyone up to that level (other General Managers included), and cannot touch a Hotel Admin. A Hotel Admin can do all of that and also make, demote or remove other Hotel Admins. Both can go live, reconnect, see billing and manage the team. Two rank rules hold for everyone: you can give a role at your own level or below, never above ("You can't give someone a role above your own."), and you cannot change or remove someone above you ("That's above your own access level.").

Can a General Manager remove another General Manager? Yes. A General Manager can change another General Manager's role or remove them, as they can for anyone up to their own level.

If you have a General Manager, they can still keep things running: open **Billing** and Stripe's billing portal, change the room count, go live, reconnect, and invite, change or remove anyone up to General Manager. What they cannot do is make someone Hotel Admin or remove the one who left. For that, email us.

**1. Email us from the right address**

[Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Our%20Hotel%20Admin%20has%20left) from the address of a General Manager on the property, or from the address that receives the property's invoices from Stripe (usually the owner's). Say which property it is, who has left, and who should become Hotel Admin. If that person is not on the team yet, a General Manager can invite them first as a General Manager.

Before we change anything, we check that the address you wrote from belongs to a General Manager on that property, or is the billing email on its account in Stripe. Then we reply to that address and wait for you to confirm.

**3. We make the change**

We make the person you named Hotel Admin and take the old login off the property. From then on your new Hotel Admin manages everything from the **Team** page.

If nobody on the team can write from either address, email us anyway from your work address and explain. We reply with what we need to confirm that you run the property. Write promptly either way: until the old login is removed, it still opens the property.

Whoever creates the account and pays, or claims the property after **Connect App** in Cloudbeds, becomes its Hotel Admin. They invite everyone else. If a colleague signed up first, ask them to invite you.
Give front-desk colleagues the Viewer role: they see every night's price and the change log and can change nothing. [Give the front desk view-only access](@88) is the two-minute version.

The Terms ask for one login per individual, and each person on the team takes a seat. Do not share a login. Invite each person with the role they need. The change log names the person who answered a **Rules that keep adjusting** banner, which only works when each person has their own login.

Yes. Modern Hospitality Solutions staff can open your property and look at everything on it, to check a price with you or to see what a rule did. **Team** is a button at the top right of the dashboard, beside **Billing**. The page is headed "Your team", with links to **Help**, **Billing** and **← Back to MAYA**. It has two parts: **Add someone**, and the list **On this property**.

How many people can be on a property follows the rooms you pay for, in the same bands as the price.

| Rooms billed | Seats |
|---|---|
| 1 to 20 | 2 |
| 21 to 40 | 4 |
| 41 to 60 | 5 |
| 61 to 80 | 6 |

The band uses the room count you are billed for, not the one MAYA measured, so a seat cannot vanish because a room type was switched off overnight. Raising the billed count on the **Billing** page raises the seats at the same moment. [Your room count and what you pay](@60) explains the count.

There are no seats to buy on their own. Seats come only from the room count you pay for, so the one way to add people is to pay for more rooms. That is allowed.
