**1. Go to the Change Log tab**

It opens on changes only. Each entry is headed **Pricing run** with the time of the run in your browser's local time, such as "Sat, Nov 14, 2026, 3:05 PM PST", and how long ago it was, such as "(12 min ago)". Ongoing problems, headed **Prices not reaching Cloudbeds** (or your system's name), sit above every run.

**2. Find the night**

Inside a run, each change starts with a bold line in the shape "Standard · stay 2026-11-14: $150.00 up to $165.00 (+10%)". Look for the stay date. Down moves read "down to" with a minus percentage.

**3. Read the sentence under it**

The first sentence names the rule and the move: "Busy nights" raised this night 10%, from $150.00 to $165.00. The next sentence gives the reason in your own numbers: It was 85% full, past the 80% mark you set.

**4. Show the numbers for a booking speed change**

When a booking speed rule acted, a **Show the numbers** link sits under the entry. It shows how many bookings the night received, how many a night like it usually has by that point, and the level that reads as. **Which nights were compared?** lists which past nights were compared and why, and **List the nights** lists them one by one.

| You read | It means |
|---|---|
| "Busy nights" raised this night 10%, from $150.00 to $165.00. | That rule acted on this night and room type. |
| Then "Hot-week surge" raised it 25%, from $165.00 to $206.25. | A second rule acted on top. Percentages compound, so the 25% is applied to $165.00. When the same rule acts again after its wait, the sentence says "another". |
| It was 85% full, past the 80% mark you set. | The condition that made an occupancy rule true. |

The tab covers the 10 most recent runs that changed a price, however long ago they ran. On a busy day that may be the last hour, on a quiet week several days. A change older than the tenth is no longer listed. The runs in between that changed nothing are counted into one quiet line per stretch, shown under **Show All Cycles**.

If no run has changed a price yet, no runs are listed. Within a run you see the 40 biggest moves. When a run had more, a line under them counts the rest, such as "And 23 more changes in this run."

When the price moved before the oldest run on screen, its run has dropped off the list (see above). You can still narrow it down yourself. Open the night on the **Calendar** tab and check three things:

- **A badge on the room type's card.** "Manual · $180.00" means someone typed that price in MAYA. "Changed in Cloudbeds · $180.00" (or your system's name) means the rate was changed in your property system and MAYA kept it. Either way, the starting price did not come from your rules. Hover the badge for the time it was set (or, for a rate changed in your system, when MAYA read it).
A badge on the room type's card

- ****Current price** against your own rate.** Current price is your rate for that night after your rules and your floor and ceiling. A gap between the two is what they added or took off. (MAYA reads no Mews rates, so on Mews the starting point is always a price you typed.)
Current price against your own rate

- **Which of your rules could apply.** On the **Rules** tab, hold each rule that is **On** up against the night: how full it is, how many days away it is, and whether the rule changes that room type.

For the exact reason, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Why%20did%20a%20price%20change) the night and room type within 90 days. The detail behind every change is kept for 90 days, and we can read it for you.

If the price did not move, most runs change nothing. Click **Show All Cycles** to include the quiet lines, such as "Prices checked 47 times from Sep 24, 10:05 AM to 1:55 PM, nothing needed to change". That is normal: about every five minutes MAYA reads your bookings and runs your rules on the nights that changed, and a price only moves when a rule's condition changes.
Which of your rules could apply

Type the price you want for the night on the **Calendar** tab, or delete the rule to undo everything it did on every night. Switching a rule off undoes nothing. On Mews, change the rate in Mews itself, because MAYA does not send prices to Mews yet.

**1. Open the night**

Go to the **Calendar** tab and click the night. One card per room type appears under the grid.

**2. Type the price**

In the room type's box, type the price you want. To cover several nights, click **through…** and pick the last night.

**3. Save**

Press Enter or click **Save**. The line under the box says what happens next, for example "Saved. Sending to Cloudbeds now." (with your system's name). Rules that had already moved that night are paused for that room type.

Your number becomes that night's starting point. Rules that fire later still stack on top of it, so this is a correction, not a lock. If a rule keeps adjusting the night, the amber banner asks you once three of its changes are on the night, and you can answer **Stop for this night**. To hand the night back to MAYA afterwards, click **Clear**.

**ThinkReservations:** When you are live, your price is sent to ThinkReservations straight away, or with the next run about five minutes later. A night more than 395 nights ahead is sent when it enters the 396-night window (tonight and the next 395). When every night you saved is that far out, the line reads "Saved. It will be sent when the date enters the 396-day push window." In simulation nothing is sent.

**Mews:** MAYA does not send prices to Mews yet, live or not. Your typed price shows in MAYA, on the calendar and in the change log, and nothing reaches Mews. The line under the box may still read "Saved. Sending to Mews now." That line is wrong for Mews. To change the rate guests see, change it in Mews itself.

Setting a price needs Revenue Manager access or higher. A price under the room type's floor or over its ceiling is refused, except 0, which makes the night a comp night. A 0 is never sent to your system, so set that night to 0 there yourself.

**1. Find the rule**

On the **Rules** tab, find the rule in the list and click **Delete** at the end of its row.

**2. Confirm**

A dialog asks "Delete "Busy nights"?" and explains that deleting also undoes the price changes it has already made. Click **Delete Rule and Undo Its Changes**.

From the next run, about five minutes away, nearest nights first, every night the rule adjusted goes back to what its price would be if the rule had never run. If you are live on Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations, the changed prices are sent, and a night more than 395 nights ahead goes when it enters the window. Nothing is sent to Mews. The rule's old entries stay in the change log, where it now reads as "Pricing rule".

When three of a booking speed or pickup rule's changes are on the same night, an amber banner at the top of the app asks what to do. **Stop for this night** means the rule makes no more changes there. It does not put the price back: what the rule already did stays, unless its undo box is ticked and cancellations mean the rule is no longer true. Pair it with a typed price if you want a particular number.

The banner only appears at three changes. Before that, a typed price resets the night to your number, but it does not hold it there. Your price starts the rule's wait again (the days it leaves a night alone). Once the wait is over, the rule can move the price again. To keep your number, switch the rule **Off** on the **Rules** tab, which stops it on every night, not only this one.

Some changes undo themselves, so check the change log before you act.

- A standard rule (occupancy or booking window) takes its change off the moment its condition stops holding. With its undo box ticked, as it is on every new rule, a cancellation that drops a night under the mark takes the raise off.
- A booking speed or pickup rule's change comes off when its undo box is ticked and cancellations mean the rule is no longer true. If bookings made since keep the rule true, the change stays.
- A cut made because a night was booking slowly never comes off this way, because cancellations only make the rule truer.
- With the undo box unticked, cancellations never take a change off. Read [When a price change comes off](@40).

Open the first night on the **Calendar** tab, type the price on each room type card, click **through…** to pick the last night of the weekend, and **Save**. That price goes to Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations as typed (on Mews, set it in Mews itself), and rules that had already moved those nights are paused. Rules that fire later still stack on top, so to keep your number, go to the **Rules** tab and switch off the rules that would move those nights. Rooms held in your system without bookings are invisible to MAYA: enter them as rooms out of service.

**2. Type the price on a room type card**

In the box on the Standard card, type the price you want for the weekend, say 250.

**3. Cover the whole weekend**

Click **through…** and pick the Saturday as the last night. The × beside the date goes back to a single night.

**4. Save, then repeat for each room type**

Click **Save**. The line under the box confirms it: "Saved. Sending to Cloudbeds now." on a live property, or "Saved (simulation: not sent to Cloudbeds)." while you are simulating. Each room type has its own card, so do the same on Deluxe and Suite.

Setting a price needs Revenue Manager access or higher. Prices apply from tonight up to 399 days ahead, and one save covers at most 366 nights. A price under the room type's floor or over its ceiling is refused with the limit named, for example "Above this room type's ceiling of $300.00."

On Mews, MAYA does not send prices yet, so set the weekend's rate in Mews itself. Typing it in MAYA only changes what MAYA shows, even when the line under the box reads "Saved. Sending to Mews now." Switching rules off changes nothing in Mews either. Read [Nothing is sent to Mews](@14#nothing-is-sent-to-mews).

Your typed price becomes the starting point for those nights and room types. Rules that had already raised or cut them are paused for that room type, and the confirmation counts them: "Paused 2 rules on this night for this room".

It is not a lock. A rule that fires afterwards stacks on top of your number. A booking speed rule waits its wait, in whole days from the day you typed, then reads its whole window again, bookings from before your price included. An occupancy or booking window rule whose condition starts holding later applies on top too.

The reliable way to keep your number today is to type the price and then switch off the rules that would move those nights. On the **Rules** tab, click a rule's switch so it reads **Off**. Click it back to **On** once the weekend has passed, and apply or skip the price adjustments in the window that opens.

Off stops the rule on every night, not only the weekend, and what it already did stays. For a weekend held as a block, the rules to switch off are usually the ones that cut, because a block adds no bookings (see below). Read [Off, delete or change](@42).

If you would rather keep a rule on, type the price again whenever it moves one of those nights. Each save takes the rule's change off that night again.

**Stop for this night** on the amber banner cannot keep your number. The banner asks only once a booking speed or pickup count rule (the two kinds that fire, then wait before firing again) has three of its changes on a night, and your typed price takes its changes off, so that count starts again from zero. So by the time it asks, the rule has already moved the night three times from your price. Answering **Stop for this night** then prevents a fourth adjustment, and does not undo the three.

**Not yet** · Rules cannot be limited to a date range or told to skip a weekend, and there is no lock on a night. To hold an event weekend today, type the price and switch off the rules that would move those nights until the weekend has passed.

MAYA reads bookings from Cloudbeds, ThinkReservations and Mews. It does not read blocks, allotments or rooms held without a booking. A wedding pencilled in as a block adds nothing to occupancy and nothing to booking speed, so the night can read as slow and a cut rule can fire.

Two fixes. First, type the price as above and switch off the cut rules that would act on those nights. Your price alone does not stop them: the block keeps the night reading slow, so a booking speed cut can still fire on top of your price once its wait has passed.

Second, on the **PMS** tab, under the room type, click **+ Rooms out of service** and enter the held rooms for those dates, so sellable occupancy reads against what you can still sell. This changes occupancy only. Booking speed counts bookings, and a block has none. Read [Tell MAYA rooms are out of service](@83).

**Example** · The Harbour Inn has a wedding on Fri, Nov 13 2026 and Sat, Nov 14 2026, held as a block in Cloudbeds. Sam types $250 on Standard through the Saturday, $320 on Deluxe and $450 on Suite. "Slow-date trim" had already cut the Saturday, so the line under the Standard box reads "Paused 1 rule on these 2 nights for this room" and the Standard card shows the badge "Manual · $250.00". Open the night on the **Calendar** tab and click **Clear** on the room type card. The line reads "Cleared. Your rules price this night again." Your rules price the night again straight away. It works the same for a price you typed and for a rate you changed in your property system that MAYA kept.

**1. Open the night**

When you typed the price, rules already on the night were paused for that room type. Clear lets them back in, with one difference between the two kinds of rule.

- An occupancy or booking window rule that was holding a change keeps its place and moves the price again straight away, if its condition still holds.
- A booking speed or pickup rule's earlier change stays off. While your price was on, the rule waited from the day you typed it. Clear ends that wait, and the changes your price took off never shorten what the rule counts. So the rule can act again as soon as its condition holds, on the price MAYA now works out. If the rule is off, the change saves at once and moves no price until you switch it on.

**1. Open it in the builder**

On the **Rules** tab, click **Edit** at the end of the rule's row. The row stays highlighted while you edit.

**2. Change what you want**

Any field the builder has: a condition's threshold, speed or window, the amount, the room types, the undo box. A rule's date window, weekdays and priority are not in the builder, and are kept as saved. A booking speed condition saved as exactly a level below or above Normal, as some starter rules are, keeps its compare unless you pick another speed.

**3. Save changes**

Click **Save changes**. A new name alone saves at once. For a rule that is **On**, the window opens with the days the changed rule will affect. **Cancel editing**, under the form, empties the builder without saving. Rules need Revenue Manager access or higher.

**Apply price adjustments.** Every change the rule has on the price is judged against the edited rule from the next pricing run. A standard rule's change stays, at the new amount, where the edited rule holds, and comes off where it does not, on room types you took off the rule and nights it no longer covers too. A booking speed or pickup rule's earlier changes come off ("the rule was edited, so MAYA started it fresh" in the change log), and the edited rule reads its whole window again, with no wait. The days the window showed are the ones whose prices move.
Apply price adjustments

**Skip price adjustments.** The days the window showed keep their prices, each until the rule stops being true there and then becomes true again. Every other day works as Apply. On those days a standard rule's change stays at its old amount: where the edited rule is true it stays, still stays once the rule stops being true (undo box ticked or not), and moves to the new amount the next time the rule is true; where the edited rule is not true, it waits for the rule to be true there and then moves to the new amount. On a room type or night you took off the rule, it comes off at that point instead. A booking speed or pickup rule's changes on those days stay, are not checked for cancellations, and still cover the rules they covered; once the rule has stopped and started being true on such a day, they come off and the edited rule acts there in that same run.

Changing the conditions, amount or room types also clears the rule's "Stop for this night" answers: they belonged to the rule as it was. Read [Turning a rule on, Apply or Skip](@41) and [A rule that is changed](@40#a-rule-that-is-changed).

**Example: Moving 'Busy nights' from 80% to 90% at The Harbour Inn**

"Busy nights" raises Standard 10%, from $150 to $165, on nights more than 80% full. Priya edits it to more than 90%. Friday is 17 of 20 booked (85%), Saturday 19 of 20 (95%). With **Apply price adjustments**, the window shows Friday among the affected days: on the next run Friday goes back to $150 and Saturday keeps $165. With **Skip price adjustments**, both stay at $165. Friday's raise then waits until Friday is over 90% full, and Saturday's comes off when Saturday drops to 90% or below.

If the rule is on, the same window opens first, with Apply and Skip. Only occupancy thresholds are offered this way, and only when yours is more than 10 percentage points away from what your own history supports. A rule named "Filling-up raise" or "Nearly-full raise", as the starter rules built from your own bookings are, never gets one, since its threshold came from those bookings. To move every night by the same percentage, add one rule on the **Rules** tab: **Booking window (days to stay)** **Less than** 396, then **Increase the rate** or **Decrease the rate** by the percentage you want. It covers tonight and the next 395 nights, which is every night MAYA prices, and it stacks with your other rules. A rule cannot be limited to a season, so for a stretch of dates, type the new price for each room type on the **Calendar** tab with **through…**, or change your rates in your property system on nights MAYA has not sent a price to yet.

A season here is any stretch of dates you choose, such as your summer or the winter holidays.

| You want to move | Do this | Keep in mind |
|---|---|---|
| Every night MAYA prices | Add a booking window rule | Moves every night by the same percentage, on top of your other rules. It cannot stop at a date. |
| A season, at one price per room type | Type the price on the calendar with **through…** | One amount for every night in the run. You work out the new price. |
| A season, keeping each night's own rate | Change the rates in your property system | Only on nights MAYA has never sent to: every night before you first go live, then nights more than 395 nights ahead. Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations only. |

**1. Open the builder and name the rule**

On the **Rules** tab, click **+ Add a rule**. In **Rule name**, type a name you will recognise in the change log, such as All nights up 10%.

**2. Set the condition**

In the first row, change **Metric** to **Booking window (days to stay)**. Set **Compare** to **Less than** and **Threshold** to 60.

**3. Set the percentage**

Under **Rate adjustment**, choose **Increase the rate** (or **Decrease the rate**) and type 10 in **Adjust by percent (%)**. For a flat amount, leave the percent empty and type it in **Adjust by fixed amount ($)** instead.

**4. Pick the room types and add it**

Under **Apply to room types**, leave every room type ticked, or untick any you want left alone. Click **Add Rule**. The window that opens shows every night the change reaches: click **Apply price adjustments**, and the rule is **On**.

Booking window is the number of days until the stay, on your property's own calendar: tonight is 0. **Less than** 396 covers 0 to 395, the whole window MAYA prices, and each new night as it comes into the window. This is a standard rule (one with only occupancy or booking window conditions): it makes its change once on each night and room type and holds it until the night has passed. The change comes in from the next pricing run, about five minutes away, nearest nights first.

On the Rules tab the row reads "Booking window below 396 days" with "+10%". In the change log a change reads: "All nights up 10%" raised this night 10%, from $150.00 to $165.00.

A raise or cut from a standard rule like this does not change which bookings your booking speed rules count. It does not open a night you closed at 0 in your system, and it does not raise a comp night (a night you typed as 0).

- **To change 10% to 15%**, click **Edit** on its row, type 15 and click **Save changes**, then **Apply price adjustments**: every night it had moved goes to 15% from the next run. Read [Change a rule](@72).
To change 10% to 15%
- **To take it off**, click **Delete** on its row, then **Delete Rule and Undo Its Changes**. From the next run every night goes back to what it would be without the rule.
To take it off
- **Switching it Off does not take it off.** Nights it already moved keep the change and new nights do not get it, so the window ends up mixed. Use Delete to end it.
Switching it Off does not take it off

The price box on the calendar takes an amount, not a percentage, so work out each room type's new price first. The Harbour Inn's Standard is usually $150, so 10% up is $165.

**1. Open the first night**

On the **Calendar** tab, click the first night of the season. The room type cards appear under the grid.

**2. Type the price and cover the season**

In the box on the Standard card, type 165. Click **through…** and pick the last night of the season.

**3. Save, then repeat for each room type**

Click **Save**. Do the same on the Deluxe and Suite cards, each with its own new price.

- One save puts one amount on every night in the run. If Friday and Saturday nights normally sell higher, save them as runs of their own, or use your property system (below).

- Your price becomes the starting point. Rules that had already moved those nights pause, rules that fire later stack on top, and booking speed and pickup rules wait again from your price. Read [Setting a price yourself](@50).
- When you are live it goes to your property system as typed, and nights more than 395 nights ahead go as they come into the window. Nothing is sent to Mews.
- To hand the season back, open its first night, pick the last one with **through…** and click **Clear**.

Change rates in your property system only on nights MAYA has never sent a price to. Before you first go live, that is every night. Once you are live, it is every night more than 395 nights ahead.

MAYA reads your rate for each night in the window about once an hour, and again when your property's date changes. On a night it has never sent to, your rate is the starting point, so a night you raised 10% starts 10% higher and your rules work on top. Each night keeps its own rate, so weekends stay above weekdays.

On a night MAYA has already sent to, a change in your system is kept as your own price once MAYA's last send there has landed and is an hour old ("Changed in Cloudbeds" on the calendar). That works for part of the window, not for nearly all of it. [Rates you change in your property system](@51) has every condition.

**Careful: Changing the whole window in your system once you are live** · If you are live and change 80% or more of the nights MAYA has sent to (10 at least) by one percentage in your system, MAYA reads it as your system's own arithmetic, like prices shown with tax, and keeps none of it. Your new rates stay in your system only until MAYA's price for each night next changes. For the whole window, use the rule above.

**Cloudbeds:** Change each room type's base rate, the rate plan that does not follow another plan. MAYA reads and writes that rate. A change to a derived plan or a package is not read.

**ThinkReservations:** Change the Best Available rate type. MAYA reads and writes that rate. A change to another rate type is not read.

The rule works on top of whatever starting point a night has, a rate you raised in your system included. With a price you typed (or one MAYA kept from your system as yours), it depends on timing:

- If the rule was already acting on the night when you typed, your price stands and the rule stays off that night until you click **Clear**.
- A price typed for a night more than 395 nights ahead gets the rule's change on top once the night comes into the window.
- A rule added after you typed a price applies on top of that price.

**Example: The Harbour Inn, all nights up 10% and the winter holidays**

On Friday, October 2, 2026, Sam adds "All nights up 10%". On the next run every night from October 2 to November 30 moves: Standard from $150 to $165, Deluxe from $200 to $220, Suite from $300 to $330.

Sam wants the winter holidays higher still, Friday, December 18, 2026 through Sunday, January 3, 2027. Those nights are 77 to 93 nights away, so MAYA has never sent to them, and Sam raises each one's base rate 10% in Cloudbeds. On October 20, December 18 comes into the window. MAYA reads $165 as the Standard starting point, and the rule adds its 10%: $181.50, which is 21% above the old $150.

**Not yet** · A rule cannot be limited to a date range or a season, and a booking window counts days from today, so it cannot pick out fixed dates. The calendar takes an amount, not a percentage, and there is no bulk upload.

On the **Rules** tab, click **+ Add a rule**, leave **Metric** on **Sellable occupancy (%)**, set **Greater than** 85, choose **Increase the rate** by 10%, keep every room type ticked, click **Add Rule** and then **Apply price adjustments**. From the next run, any night in the 396-night window with more than 85% of its sellable rooms booked is raised 10%. When the night drops back to 85% or under, the raise comes off.

**1. Open the builder**

On the **Rules** tab, click **+ Add a rule**. In **Rule name**, type Nearly full.

**2. Set the condition**

The first condition row is already **Sellable occupancy (%)**. Leave **Compare** on **Greater than** and change **Threshold** from 80 to 85.

**3. Set the change**

Under **Rate adjustment**, choose **Increase the rate** in **Direction (required)**. Type 10 in **Adjust by percent (%)**. For a fixed amount instead, leave the percent empty and type it in **Adjust by fixed amount ($)**. A rule has one amount, so the box you leave empty greys out.

The row reads "Occupancy above 85%" under **Conditions** and "+10%" under **Price Change**. When a night crosses the mark, the change log shows a line such as "Standard · stay 2026-11-14: $150.00 up to $165.00 (+10%)" with the sentences "Nearly full" raised this night 10%, from $150.00 to $165.00. It was 90% full, past the 85% mark you set.

This is a standard rule: it switches on when the condition starts holding, holds one raise while it holds, and switches off when it stops. With its undo box ticked, as it is on every new rule, a cancellation that takes the night to 85% or under takes the raise off on the next run. Untick it and falling occupancy never takes the raise off. It never stacks on itself.

A sold-out night keeps the raise and is still priced like any other night. Once you are live on Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations, a room freed by a cancellation goes back on sale at the night's current price, raised as long as the night stays above 85%. On Mews it sells at the rate you set in Mews, because MAYA sends no prices there yet. A booking speed cut rule can still cut a sold-out night, because a full night takes no new bookings. Read [A price looks wrong](@96#we-are-sold-out-tonight-why-is-the-price-still-changing).

**Example** · The Harbour Inn has 20 rooms that count. On Saturday, November 14, 2026, 18 are booked: 90%, so the rule fires and Standard goes from $150 to $165. A cancellation leaves 17 booked: 85% exactly, which is not more than 85, so the raise comes off and Standard returns to $150.

On the **Rules** tab, add a rule with **Metric** set to **Booking speed (recommended)**, **Speed** **Slower Than Normal**, **Measured over** **Past month**, **Then waits (advanced)** **1 week**, and **Decrease the rate** by 7%. A night whose bookings over the past month are slower than similar past nights had by the same point is cut 7%. After a week the rule counts only the bookings made since that cut, and cuts again if those are still slow. This rule is not a copy of the starter rule "Slow-date trim", which cuts only nights that read exactly Slower Than Normal.

On the **Rules** tab, click **+ Add a rule**. In **Rule name**, type Slow nights.

**2. Choose booking speed**

In the condition row, change **Metric** to **Booking speed (recommended)**. The row changes to a **Speed** dropdown: pick **Slower Than Normal**.

**3. Set the window and the wait**

Under the row, set **Measured over** to **Past month** and **Then waits (advanced)** to **1 week**. The **?** beside each explains what it does in the app's own words.

**4. Set the cut, pick the room types, add it**

Under **Rate adjustment**, choose **Decrease the rate** and type 7 in **Adjust by percent (%)**. Leave every room type ticked and click **Add Rule**. A window shows the days the rule will change: click **Apply price adjustments**, or **Skip price adjustments** to leave those days' prices as they are. Read [Turning a rule on, Apply or Skip](@41).

For each night in the window (tonight and the next 395), MAYA counts the bookings that night received over the 30 full days up to yesterday and compares the count with what similar past nights (same weekday, same time of year, up to 3 years back) had received over the same stretch of their own run-up. A rule that cuts judges complete days only, so a quiet morning never counts against a night. A booking counts once, however many rooms it holds. Only the room types the rule measures are counted.

How a wedding block counts depends on how it was booked. On Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations, one reservation that holds several rooms counts as one booking. When guests book their own rooms from the block, each of their reservations counts as a booking. On Mews every room is its own reservation, so a group counts once per room. For occupancy, every booked room counts either way.

**Slower Than Normal** means that slow or slower: the rule fires on Slower Than Normal, Much Slower Than Normal and Stalled. With an expected count of 5, a night with 1 booking reads as Much Slower Than Normal and fires. With 5 or 6 it reads Normal and does not. When the difference is small, or there are fewer than 5 similar nights to compare with, MAYA keeps the call close to Normal, so the rule fires less often rather than wrongly.

The cut stays on the price. Cancellations only make a slow night slower, so they never take it off. For 1 week the rule leaves that night alone for that room type. When the wait is over it counts only the bookings made in the full days after the newest cut still on that night by this rule or a stronger one, up to yesterday. A cut from a weaker rule, or from a standard rule such as "Last minute", does not restart the count. It compares those bookings with the same days on the similar nights, and if they read slow on their own, it cuts another 7%, and the change log reads: Then "Slow nights" lowered it another 7%. Once three of its cuts are on the same night, the amber banner asks whether to keep adjusting or stop.

**Good to know** · The usual five starter rules include "Slow-date trim" (Slower Than Normal only, past month, cut 7%, waits 1 week) and "Slow-date rescue" (Much Slower Than Normal or Stalled, past month, cut 15%, waits 1 week). This rule is not a copy of either: it cuts 7% on all three slow levels. If both starter rules are on, you do not need this one: together they already cover every slow level. To keep a nearly full night from ever being cut, click **+ Add condition** and add **Sellable occupancy (%)** **Less than** 60: the rule then needs both to be true.

On the **Rules** tab, add a rule with **Metric** **Booking speed (recommended)**, **Speed** **Surging**, **Measured over** **Past day**, **Then waits (advanced)** **1 day**, and **Increase the rate** by 25%. A night that received far more bookings today than similar nights had on the same day of their run-up is raised 25%. The next day the rule counts only the bookings made since that raise, and raises again if those still read Surging. This is the starter rule "Sudden-spike catcher", so check your list first.

**1. Open the builder and name it**

On the **Rules** tab, click **+ Add a rule**. In **Rule name**, type Sudden rush.

**2. Choose Surging over the past day**

Change **Metric** to **Booking speed (recommended)** and pick **Surging** in **Speed**. Set **Measured over** to **Past day** and **Then waits (advanced)** to **1 day**.

**3. Set the raise, pick the room types, add it**

Under **Rate adjustment**, choose **Increase the rate** and type 25 in **Adjust by percent (%)**. Leave every room type ticked and click **Add Rule**. A window shows the days the rule will change: click **Apply price adjustments**, or **Skip price adjustments** to leave those days' prices as they are. Read [Turning a rule on, Apply or Skip](@41).

**Past day** counts the bookings dated today, on your property's own calendar, so a reading soon after midnight has almost nothing in it yet. MAYA compares that count with what similar past nights received on the same single day of their own run-up. Surging is the top of seven levels: the night needs at least 3.5 times the usual count, and at least 4 more bookings than usual, to read as Surging. With an expected count of 5, that is 18 bookings or more in one day. With fewer than 5 similar nights to compare with, the call is capped at one step from Normal and Surging cannot be reached.

Picking **Surging** means the rule fires on Surging only. To fire on a broader rush, pick **Much Faster Than Normal** (at least twice the usual count) or **Faster Than Normal**, which fire on that level and everything above it.

A raise by a weaker rule, or by an occupancy or booking window rule, does not restart that count. One burst of bookings raises a night once, not once per rule. Once three of its raises are on the same night, the amber banner asks whether to keep adjusting or stop.

The rule's undo box, **Undo the change if cancellations mean this rule is no longer true**, starts ticked. With it ticked, a raise comes off when bookings it counted cancel and the ones still booked no longer read Surging, unless bookings made since keep the rule true. The change log then reads: Cancellations meant "Sudden rush" was no longer true, so its 25% raise came off. Untick the box and cancellations never take the raise off. Read [When a price change comes off](@40).

**Careful** · Set a ceiling first. A rule that raises stops at the room type's ceiling, and MAYA's default of $99,999.99 stops nothing in most currencies. Read [Set or change a floor or ceiling](@81).

**Good to know** · The usual five starter rules include "Sudden-spike catcher" (Surging, past day, raise 25%, waits 1 day), "Hot-week surge" (Much Faster Than Normal, past week, raise 25%, waits 2 days) and "Warm-date bump" (Faster Than Normal, past month, raise 10%, waits 3 days). Together they step up as the pace climbs. If you answered "Find money I'm leaving on the table" and your nights filled early, they raise 30%, 30% and 15%.

On the **Rules** tab, add a rule with two conditions: **Booking window (days to stay)** **Less than** 3, and **Sellable occupancy (%)** **Less than** 50, then **Decrease the rate** by 15%. Tonight, tomorrow night and the night after are cut 15% while fewer than half their sellable rooms are booked. When a night fills to 50% or more, the cut comes off.

**1. Open the builder and name it**

On the **Rules** tab, click **+ Add a rule**. In **Rule name**, type Last minute.

**2. Set the booking window condition**

In the first row, change **Metric** to **Booking window (days to stay)**. Set **Compare** to **Less than** and **Threshold** to 3.

**3. Add the occupancy condition**

Click **+ Add condition**. The new row is **Sellable occupancy (%)**. Set **Compare** to **Less than** and **Threshold** to 50. The line under **Conditions** says it: the rule matches when all of its conditions are true.

Booking window is the number of days until the stay, on your property's own calendar: tonight is 0, tomorrow night is 1. **Less than** 3 covers 0, 1 and 2, so tonight and the next two nights. The count moves every day, so each night slides into the rule's range as it gets closer, and out again once it has passed.

The occupancy condition is what keeps this from cutting a night that is already selling. A night at 50% or more is left alone. Both conditions must hold at the same time.

The row on the Rules tab reads "Occupancy below 50% · Booking window below 3 days" with "-15%". In the change log a change reads: "Last minute" lowered this night 15%, from $150.00 to $127.50. It was 40% full with 1 day to go, under the 50% mark and past the 3-day mark you set.

This is a standard rule. It holds one cut while both conditions hold and takes it off when either stops: when the night fills to 50% or more, or when the night passes. It never cuts the same night twice.

**Example** · It is Tuesday at The Harbour Inn. Wednesday night has 8 of 20 rooms booked (40%) and is 1 day away, so Standard drops from $150 to $127.50, Deluxe from $200 to $170 and Suite from $300 to $255. Two more bookings on Wednesday morning take it to 10 of 20 (50%), which is not less than 50, so on the next run the cut comes off.

**Not yet** · A rule cannot be limited to certain weekdays or dates, so this rule runs every night of the year. To keep a weekend or event out of it, type those nights' prices and switch this rule off (which stops it on every night) until the nights have passed. A typed price alone does not stop a rule that starts to hold later. Read [Hold a price for a wedding or event weekend](@68).

In the rule builder, tick **Change prices on different room types**. The room type list splits in two: **Measure**, the room types whose occupancy or bookings the rule reads, and **Change**, the room types whose prices it moves. Tick Standard under **Measure** and Suite under **Change**. When Standard is more than 80% full, the Suite price rises.

**1. Open the builder and set the condition**

On the **Rules** tab, click **+ Add a rule**. Name it Suites follow Standard. Leave the condition on **Sellable occupancy (%)** **Greater than** 80, and under **Rate adjustment** choose **Increase the rate** by 10%.

**2. Split the room type lists**

Under the room types, tick **Change prices on different room types**. The single **Apply to room types** list becomes two lists, **Measure** and **Change**. The **?** beside the box explains: you watch occupancy, pickup and booking speed on the Measure room types, and when the rule fires you change prices on the Change room types.

**3. Pick Measure and Change**

Under **Measure**, click **Clear** and then tick Standard only. Under **Change**, click **Clear** and tick Suite only.

Occupancy is measured over the **Measure** list alone. The Harbour Inn's Standard has 12 rooms, so 10 booked reads as 83% and the rule fires: Suite goes from $300 to $330, while Standard's own price is untouched. Booking speed and pickup conditions work the same way, counting only bookings in the measured room types.

Only room types that count as rooms are offered under **Measure**. A Meeting Room, unticked as a room on the **PMS** tab, can be changed by a rule but never measured. Under **Change**, every room type is offered, rooms or not.

The change log names both sides: Standard was 83% full, past the 80% mark you set, on a line for Suite.

In the rule builder, the chips under **Apply to room types** are the room types the rule covers. Every type that counts as a room starts ticked. Click a chip to untick it and the rule leaves that room type alone, in what it measures and in what it changes. For a saved rule, click **Edit** on its row, change the chips and click **Save changes**.

**1. Open the builder**

On the **Rules** tab, click **+ Add a rule** and fill in the name, condition and rate adjustment as usual.

**2. Untick the chips you want left out**

Under **Apply to room types**, each room type is a chip. A ticked chip is highlighted. Click Suite to untick it. The summary beside the label counts what is left, for example "2 of 4 room types". **Select all** ticks every chip and **Clear** unticks them all.

**3. Add the rule**

Click **Add Rule**, then **Apply price adjustments** in the window that opens. The row's **Room Types** column lists the types it covers: "Standard, Deluxe".

At least one room type must be ticked. Leaving none gives "Select at least one room type."

With the single list, the rule measures and changes the same room types. It measures the ticked types that count as rooms, and it changes every ticked type. So a rule ticked on Suite alone measures Suite's occupancy on its own (The Harbour Inn has 2 Suites, so 1 booked is 50%) and moves Suite's price only.

A chip tagged "not a room" is a type you have unticked as a room on the **PMS** tab, such as a Meeting Room. It starts unticked in the builder. Tick it and the rule changes its price, and once you are live that price is sent to your system; leave it out of every rule and MAYA sends nothing for it, apart from a price you type for one of its nights on the calendar, which is sent as you typed it. A rule never measures it: a court or meeting room has no occupancy to read.

So tick at least one type that counts as a room as well, unless booking window is the rule's only condition. The rule then changes the price of every type you tick, rooms included. Read more in [Take a meeting room out of occupancy](@82).

**Good to know** · To measure one set of room types and change another, tick **Change prices on different room types** under the chips. For example, measure Standard and change only the Meeting Room. Read [Let suites follow your standard rooms](@78).

Click **Edit** on the rule's row. The rule builder opens with its chips as saved. Change them and click **Save changes**. On a rule that is on, a window shows the days that change: with **Apply price adjustments**, the room types you unticked lose the rule's changes from the next run, and the ones you ticked get them where the rule holds. With **Skip price adjustments**, the prices on those days stay as they are until the rule stops being true on a day and then becomes true again, and every other night works as with Apply. The starter rules MAYA built from your history cover every room type that counts as a room; to keep one of them off your suites, edit it the same way. Read [Change a rule](@72).

Open the **Rate Simulator** tab, set up a made-up night, click **+ Build a test rule** and fill it in. The **What would happen** table shows what each room type would become. Nothing is saved and no price reaches your property system until you click **Save This Rule**, and even then the rule arrives on the **Rules** tab switched **Off**. Turn it **On** when you are ready: the switch first shows the days it will change on your real calendar, and you apply or skip the price adjustments.

**1. Set up the night**

On the **Rate Simulator** tab, under **The night**, pick a **Stay date** (it starts 30 days ahead) and a **Booking speed** level. Leave it on **Not enough history** and booking speed rules stay quiet, which is what happens on a night MAYA cannot measure.

**2. Set up the rooms**

Under **Your rooms**, each room type that counts as a room has a **Base price** (starting at the nearest price MAYA has published), an **Occupancy** percentage (starting at 70%) and a **Picked up** count. Its floor and ceiling show under **Guardrails**. Change the numbers to the night you want to test.

The **What would happen** table shows each room type's **Base**, what it **Becomes**, the **Change**, and **Because**, which names the rules that fired. A price held at a limit is tagged "held at your floor" or "held at your ceiling". The **Didn't fire** list says why a rule stayed quiet, for example "Conditions not met" with what it saw.

The math is the same a real run uses, so the numbers are what your rules would produce for the night you typed. Your existing rules are all ticked under **Rules in play**, switched-off ones included, so you can see what turning one on would do. Untick any to leave it out of the test.

Three things it simplifies, as the note at the foot of the page says:

- A standard rule (occupancy or booking window) fires on the way into its condition and holds, so the table shows where the night settles rather than each step.
- When several booking speed or pickup rules match, a real run lets only one of them act on each night and room type, while the simulator adds them all.
- A booking speed or pickup rule that is still true once its wait is over adjusts the night again, which the simulator shows only once.

It is one run, not where a night ends up over a week.

There is no floor and ceiling editor yet. Setup sets them from your answers and your own past rates: check them in the **Guardrails** column on the **Rate Simulator** tab. A limit still at $1.00 or $99,999.99 can be set from a **Get suggestions from my data** card. To change one already set, answer the floor and ceiling questions again, or email us the numbers.

Before you set anything, look at what you already have. Setup fills in floors and ceilings for you, so do not assume yours are still at $1.00 and $99,999.99.

Your answers to the floor and ceiling questions go on first. The floor goes to every room type that counts as a room, and the ceiling to each such room type whose highest sold rate is at or below it, unless the two clash (see below). A type unticked as a room keeps its own limits.

A limit stays at the default when the room type had sold too few room nights, or looked like it might not be a room. A ceiling needs far more room nights than a floor, and a room type with few rooms gets there more slowly. At The Harbour Inn, Standard has 12 rooms and reaches 200 room nights after about 17 full nights. Suite has 2 rooms and needs at least 100. So a room type can have a floor and still carry the $99,999.99 ceiling. To see yours, open the **Rate Simulator** tab and read the **Guardrails** column. It shows the floor and ceiling of every room type that counts as a room.

**1. Ask for suggestions**

On the **Rules** tab, click **Get suggestions from my data** beside the **Pricing Rules** heading. A panel headed "Here's exactly what happens" says that nothing changes by itself. Click **Sounds good**. The button shows a waiting message while MAYA reads your history again.

**2. Open the review**

When it is done, the button reads "3 suggestions ready →". Click it to open the review page, under the heading "Recommendations from your data".

**3. Edit the amount and set it**

A card reads "Set a floor for "Standard"?" with the reason under it, for example: Standard has typically sold for $150 a night, so MAYA suggests a floor of $60. The amount sits in a box labelled **Amount to set**. Leave it, or type your own number. The button reads **Set it to 60** and follows what you typed. Click it. **No thanks** leaves the room type as it is.

Cards only fill gaps: a floor still at $1.00 or a ceiling still at $99,999.99. A limit that is already set, by your answers, the import or an earlier card, gets no card, whatever its number. So if setup filled every limit, you will see no floor or ceiling cards. The amount on a card is your own answer where it fits, and otherwise a number from the room type's past rates, worked out the same way as during the import.

Accepting a suggestion needs Revenue Manager access or higher. Reading your history again is limited to 5 runs in 15 minutes, needs a paid property with a connected system, and can take a while on a large property. It is not available on Mews yet, where the button is greyed out.

The floor and ceiling questions from setup can be answered again at any time, at maya-rms.com/onboarding/questions once your property is connected. They are the same five cards, all skippable. Skip to the floor card, answer it, then the ceiling card, then skip the rest.

- **The floor** you type replaces the floor of every active room type that counts as a room, except where it clashes. A type you have unticked as a room, such as a parking bay or a meeting room, is left alone.
The floor

- **The ceiling** you type goes only to room types whose highest sold rate is at or below it, so a property-wide ceiling never pins a suite below what it already sells for. Other room types keep their ceiling.
The ceiling

- **A clash is skipped, and the card says so.** A room type takes the new numbers only if its floor still ends up at or below its ceiling. If your floor is above a room type's ceiling, or your ceiling is below its floor, that room type keeps the floor and ceiling it had. The card stays up and names it, for example "Your floor of $200 wasn't saved for Deluxe King: its ceiling is $150, and a floor can't be above the ceiling." Type another number, or skip the card to leave it that way.
A clash is skipped, and the card says so

- **Your saved answers go on again each time.** Saving the floor card, the ceiling card or the fifth card writes both of your saved answers again, by the same rules. So answering only the ceiling card still puts your saved floor answer, if you gave one, back on every room type that counts as a room. Skipping a card changes nothing.

A card names a skipped room type only for the answer you just gave. When it writes your other saved answer again, a room type that cannot take that one is skipped without being named again. Check the **Guardrails** column on the **Rate Simulator** tab afterwards.

To give one room type a floor of its own, or to lower a ceiling under a room type's past rates, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Floor%20and%20ceiling) with the room type and the numbers.
Your saved answers go on again each time

Every price your rules produce is held inside the room type's floor and ceiling. So is your system's own rate on a night where no rule has fired: under the floor, the floor is published, and over the ceiling, the ceiling. The change log says so when a limit stops a rule: "That would have gone past your $300.00 ceiling for Standard, so it stopped there." A booking speed or pickup rule that cannot move the price in its own direction against a limit does not fire.

**Good to know** · When the amber banner says a rule keeps adjusting a night and your limit is still the default, it offers **Ask MAYA for a ceiling** or **Ask MAYA for a floor**. The link takes you to the **Rules** tab, where **Get suggestions from my data** is the next click.

**Not yet** · No per-room-type editor, no floor or ceiling per night or per season, and no way to lower a ceiling under a room type's past rates yourself. The floor cannot be 0: use a comp night for a free night.

Open the **PMS** tab, scroll to **Room types**, and untick **Counts as a room** on the meeting room's row. It saves at once. From then on that type is left out of sellable occupancy, the calendar's room counts, booking speed and the room count you are billed for. It can still be priced if a rule changes it.

**1. Open the room types**

Go to the **PMS** tab. Under the connection cards is a section headed **Room types**, one row per active room type with its unit count and a **Counts as a room** checkbox.

**2. Untick Counts as a room**

On the Meeting Room's row, untick the box. It saves straight away, with no confirmation. The row dims and gains a "not a room" tag. If it did not save, the box snaps back and a short error shows.

If the box is already unticked with a "needs your answer" tag, nobody has answered for that type yet, and it still counts in occupancy. Tick the box, then untick it: the tag changes to "not a room".

- **Sellable occupancy.** Only ticked types, and types still tagged "needs your answer", are divided by. The Harbour Inn has 20 rooms plus a Meeting Room. With it ticked, 18 booked rooms read as 18 of 21 (86%). Unticked, they read as 18 of 20 (90%).
Sellable occupancy
- **The calendar.** The day card's "18/20 rooms" and its percentage leave out types tagged "not a room". Revenue on the card still sums every type.
The calendar
- **Booking speed.** Bookings for an unticked type are not counted, and it is never measured by a rule.
Booking speed

- **Sending.** MAYA sends no price to your property system for an unticked type unless one of your rules ticks it under **Change**, or you type a price for one of its nights on the calendar (that night is sent as you typed it). Your own rate for the Meeting Room stays as it is there. The floor and ceiling answers from setup are not written onto it either.
Sending

- **Rules.** In the rule builder the type is tagged "not a room" and starts unticked. A rule that ticks it can still change its price, and that price is sent. A rule that measures only unticked types (the Meeting Room alone, say) never fires on occupancy, pickup or booking speed. A booking window condition counts days, not bookings. So a rule whose only condition is booking window still fires and changes the room types it is set to change.
Rules

- **Your bill.** The room count MAYA measures from your system leaves out unticked types. Lowering the count never lowers your bill on its own: set it on the **Billing** page. Read [Change the room count you pay for](@89).

**Good to know** · During setup MAYA unticks types whose names are plainly not bedrooms (parking, meeting, conference, spa treatment and the like) and asks about softer cases on the review page with a card headed "Is "Pool Cabana" actually a room?". Your answer is final either way, and you can change it here any time.
Your bill

Go to the **PMS** tab, find the room type under **Room types**, click **+ Rooms out of service**, enter the dates and the number of rooms, and **Save**. Those rooms come off the sellable count for those nights only, so occupancy reads against what you can sell. Nothing is sent to your property system, and rooms you block there are not read by MAYA, so enter them here.

**1. Find the room type**

On the **PMS** tab, scroll to **Room types** and find the row. Under it, click **+ Rooms out of service**.

**2. Fill in the block**

**From** is the first night. **To** is the last night and defaults to the same night. **Units** is how many rooms of that type are off sale, from 1 up to the type's count. **Reason (optional)** takes a few words, such as Renovation.

**3. Save**

Click **Save**. The block lists under the row as "3 out of service", the dates, and the reason, with a **Clear** link. MAYA re-prices the nights of the block from the next cycle, within a few minutes.

Adding or clearing a block needs Revenue Manager access or higher. One block can cover at most 366 nights. Blocks on the same nights add up, and the total cannot exceed the type's units: MAYA tells you how many you can still block.

Sellable occupancy is rooms booked divided by rooms you can sell that night. A rule reads it over the room types it measures, and a new rule measures every type that counts as a room. At The Harbour Inn that is Standard, Deluxe and Suite: 20 rooms, or 17 with 3 Standard rooms out of service.

Take a night with 8 Standard, 5 Deluxe and 1 Suite booked. A rule that measures all three reads 14 of 17, or 82%, instead of 14 of 20, or 70%. A rule that measures Standard alone (only Standard ticked) reads 8 of 9, or 89%, instead of 8 of 12, or 67%. Either way, an occupancy rule set at **Greater than** 80 fires with the block and not without it.

The calendar shows the same reduced counts. On this night the day card reads "14/17 rooms", and the day detail reads "Booked 8/9" for Standard.

**Good to know** · A block held in your system for a wedding or a group, with no bookings behind it, is invisible to MAYA in the same way. Entering those rooms as out of service keeps the night from reading as empty. Read [Hold a price for a wedding or event weekend](@68).

Click **Clear** beside the block. The rooms come back into the sellable count from the next run. Cleared blocks are kept for the record but no longer shown. A block whose last night has passed needs no clearing: it only ever counted for its own nights.

**Not yet** · Blocks are per room type, not per room, and MAYA does not read blocks, allotments or out-of-order rooms from any property system. A whole-property closure that is still to come is not a closed period either: those nights are still priced. Closed periods only come from your setup review.

Find the change in the **Change Log** tab, click **Show the numbers**, then **Which nights were compared?** and **List the nights**. On the night that was not normal, click **Not a fair comparison?**, choose a reason such as **Local Event or Festival**, keep **Just set aside this one date (recommended)** and click **Set this date aside**. From the next run that date is left out of comparisons for 3 years. **Undo** under **Your corrections** puts it back.

**2. Show the nights it compared**

Click **Which nights were compared?**, then **List the nights**. One row per past night appears, such as "Fri, Jul 18 2025" with "12 bookings in the same stretch" and why it was picked.

**3. Flag the odd one**

On the row that was not normal, click **Not a fair comparison?**. Under "What made Fri, Jul 18 2025 not a fair comparison?", choose a reason from the list: **Local Event or Festival**, **Sporting Event or Tournament**, **Conference or Convention**, **Renovation or Rooms Out of Service**, **Utility or Amenity Outage**, **Group Buyout**, **Nearby Competitor Closed or Sold Out**, **Severe Weather**, **Road, Transit, or Flight Disruption**, **Booking Data Looks Wrong**, **Other** (which asks for a few words), or **Holiday Not on MAYA's List**, covered in [Handle a holiday MAYA does not have](@85).

Leave **Just set aside this one date (recommended)** selected and click **Set this date aside**. The row now reads "Set aside. Not used from the next run on."

Setting a date aside needs Revenue Manager access or higher. Anyone on the property can open the panel and read the nights.

From the next pricing run the date is left out of every comparison and out of the reading of your seasons. The expected count for the night you started from is worked out again from the nights that remain, and any booking speed rule reads the new figure on its next check. Nothing about the past is changed and no price is moved by the correction itself.

Some reasons offer two more scopes. **This happens every year around this time** starts a yearly pattern: once the same reason is reported near the same time of year from 2 different years, a window of about 5 days either side is left out every year. **This should also change how our seasons are read (advanced)** needs reports from 3 different years before it changes anything about seasons. Until those counts are reached, only the single date is set aside.

**Example** · Priya opens a cut on Fri, Nov 13 2026 at The Harbour Inn. One of the eight nights compared is Fri, Nov 15 2024, with 14 bookings in the same stretch, the weekend of a food festival that has since moved. She sets it aside with **Local Event or Festival**. On the next run the usual count for a night like this drops from 6 to 5, and the cut rule reads the night as Normal.

At the top of the **Change Log** tab, **Your corrections** lists every date you have set aside, each with **Undo**. Undo makes the date comparable again from the next run. A flagged date can also be seen on the row itself the next time you open that night's comparisons.

**Not yet** · Dates can only be set aside from a change's comparisons, so you cannot flag a date before it has been used. Closed periods (a stretch when the whole property was shut) are confirmed on the setup review, not here.

MAYA uses 17 US holidays for every property, wherever it is, and has no screen to add another or switch one off. The workaround: when a change's comparisons include a past night that fell on your holiday, click **Not a fair comparison?** on it, choose **Holiday Not on MAYA's List** (the first in the list), pick **This happens every year around this time** and click **Set this date aside**. The date is left out at once. After the same report from 2 different years, the days around it are left out of comparisons every year, for as long as those reports are under 3 years old. If your holiday never shows up in a comparison, email us its dates and we can set them aside for you, or type prices for the holiday nights yourself.

Holidays are used to pick which past nights a night is compared with: a night near Thanksgiving is compared with the same position around Thanksgiving in earlier years, not the same calendar date. The list is New Year's Day, Martin Luther King Jr. Day, Valentine's Day, Presidents' Day, St. Patrick's Day, Easter, Mother's Day, Memorial Day, Father's Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day, Labor Day, Indigenous Peoples' Day, Halloween, Veterans Day, Thanksgiving and Christmas (whose stretch runs through New Year's Eve). Nothing outside the US is on it.

Your own holidays are different. A night on one that falls outside every US stretch is compared with ordinary nights of the same weekday and time of year. A past night on it can also turn up as a comparison for an ordinary night and make it read slow.

**Good to know: Some of your holidays already line up** · A few holidays outside the US fall inside a US stretch every year, so they are already compared by their position around it: Good Friday and Easter Monday (Easter), Boxing Day (Christmas), the UK's late May bank holiday (Memorial Day), and Canada's Labour Day, Thanksgiving and Remembrance Day (Labor Day, Indigenous Peoples' Day and Veterans Day). Under **Which nights were compared?** the line names the US holiday.

**1. Find a comparison that used your holiday**

On the **Change Log** tab, open a booking speed change with **Show the numbers**, then **Which nights were compared?** and **List the nights**. Look for a past date that fell on your holiday.

**2. Flag it with the holiday reason**

Click **Not a fair comparison?** on that row and choose **Holiday Not on MAYA's List**.

**3. Choose the yearly scope**

Select **This happens every year around this time**. The hint under it says the date is set aside now, and that treating it as a yearly pattern needs reports like this one from 2 different years.

**4. Set it aside**

Click **Set this date aside**. Repeat when a comparison uses the same holiday from another year.

Setting a date aside needs Revenue Manager access or higher.

These steps only work on a past night that is listed among a change's compared nights, and only while that change is still on the change log (its 10 most recent runs that changed a price). You cannot choose which nights are compared, so your holiday may never come up. If it does not:

- **Email us the dates.** [Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Set%20a%20holiday%20aside) your holiday's dates in the last few years and we can set them aside for you with the holiday reason, every year. With dates from 2 different years, the days around your holiday are left out of comparisons every year, as if you had set them aside yourself.
Email us the dates

- **Hold the holiday night's own price.** Type a price for it on the **Calendar** tab, with **through…** for a run of nights. Setting dates aside never gives the holiday night holiday comparisons of its own, so a typed price is the way to hold it.
Hold the holiday night's own price
- **At once:** that date is left out of comparisons and out of the reading of your seasons, from the next run.
At once

- **After 2 different years** report the same reason near the same time of year: a window of about 5 days either side of the centre is left out of comparisons every year, past and future, for as long as reports from at least 2 different years are under 3 years old. **Your corrections** at the top of the change log shows the count, for example "We have seen this reported in 1 year of the 2 different years we would want", and then the promoted line once it repeats.
After 2 different years

- **3 years after you make a report,** it stops counting. When that leaves reports from fewer than 2 different years, the promoted line goes away and the holiday is compared again, so set it aside again when it comes up in newer comparisons. **Your corrections** still lists your old reports.
3 years after you make a report,

- **The holiday night itself** is still priced by your rules like any other night. Setting it aside stops it being used as a comparison for other nights. It does not give it holiday comparisons of its own. Hold its price with a typed price if you want to.

**Example** · The Harbour Inn's sister property in Halifax sees a cut on Mon, Aug 2 2027, Nova Scotia's civic holiday. Among the nights compared is Mon, Aug 3 2026, the same holiday a year earlier, with 9 bookings against a usual 4. Priya sets it aside with the holiday reason, every year. When another comparison brings up Mon, Aug 4 2025, the holiday two years earlier, she does the same. The days around that Monday are then left out of comparisons every year, until her first report is 3 years old.
The holiday night itself

Once three of a booking speed or pickup rule's changes are on the same night, an amber banner at the top of every tab asks what to do, and the rule keeps adjusting until you answer. **Keep adjusting** lets it carry on and stops the question for that night. **Stop for this night** means no more changes there, while what it already did stays. A stopped night shows under the rule on the **Rules** tab, where **Let it run again** puts the rule back on it.

The banner is headed with the rule and the count, for example "Hot-week surge" has 3 raises on Sat, Nov 14 2026., and the line under it: It keeps raising these nights until you stop it. For several nights it reads "Hot-week surge" has 3 raises on each of 4 nights. The count is the rule's changes still on the price, so one that came off, for cancellations or because you typed a price, is not counted.

**1. Choose for one night or for all of them**

With several nights, two buttons come first: **Keep adjusting on all 4 nights** and **Stop on all 4 nights**. Under them the nights are listed. Click **Answer night by night** to open a card per night, each with **Keep adjusting** and **Stop for this night**.

**2. Keep adjusting**

The rule carries on as it is, and MAYA stops asking about that night. Other rules are unaffected.

**3. Stop for this night**

The rule makes no more changes on that night. What it already changed there stays, unless its undo box is ticked and cancellations mean the rule is no longer true. Your other rules keep working on the night.

Answering needs Revenue Manager access or higher. Anyone else sees the banner with "Only a Revenue Manager or above can answer this." The **?** beside the buttons repeats what each answer does.

A rule you stopped on nights still to come shows an amber chip under its switch on the **Rules** tab: "Stopped on 4 nights", with a **?** that names them and a **Let it run again** link. One click clears the stop on every stopped night of that rule. The rule can adjust them again from the next run, starting from the price it left, and MAYA asks again after three more changes on the night.

**Good to know** · The question is per rule and per night. It can arrive a few minutes after the third adjustment. A price you type on the night, or deleting the rule, closes the question without an answer. Deleting and re-adding a rule starts its count at zero.

There is no badge on the dashboard yet. Open the review page: where it shows your starter rules, the green pill "✓ Live: your rules are now managing prices" means you are live, and the button **Turn them on for real** means you are in simulation. Then compare one night's price in MAYA with the same night in your property system. If you are still unsure, email us and we check.

**1. Open the review page**

Open maya-rms.com/onboarding/review, or click **Review →** on the blue banner when it is showing. Under "While you were here, we built your first pricing rules", a simulating property shows the button **Turn them on for real** and the line "Or leave them in simulation and watch for a while. That works too." A live property shows the green pill "✓ Live: your rules are now managing prices" instead. This box only appears when MAYA built starter rules for you during setup, which needs about 60 days of history. It stays after someone runs **Get suggestions from my data** on the **Rules** tab. If it is missing, use the clues below or [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Am%20I%20live) and we check.

If you have typed a price for a real reason lately, its confirmation said which mode you were in: "Saved (simulation: not sent to Cloudbeds)." in simulation, "Saved. Sending to Cloudbeds now." or "Saved. Sending to Cloudbeds on the next cycle (about 5 min)." when live. "Saved. It will be sent once you reconnect." and "Saved. Cloudbeds isn't answering MAYA right now. MAYA keeps trying to reach it and sends this price as soon as it answers." mean live too, with the connection down. "Saved. Nothing is sent while MAYA's work is paused." says nothing about the mode. Do not type a price only to test this. On a live property it sends the price, and it takes any booking speed or pickup change off that night for good.

**Cloudbeds:** Look at the room type's base rate in Cloudbeds. The **Change Log** tab shows a "Prices not reaching Cloudbeds" item if sends are failing. A simulating property never has one, because nothing is sent.

**ThinkReservations:** Look at the Best Available rate for the room type in ThinkReservations. ThinkReservations accepts MAYA's prices and applies them shortly after, so allow a little longer than with Cloudbeds. MAYA reads the rate back within about an hour.

A typed price's confirmation still talks about sending. On a live Mews property it reads "Saved. Sending to Mews now." or "Saved. Sending to Mews on the next cycle (about 5 min)." Nothing is sent to Mews. Read that line as a sign you are live, not as proof a price went out.

**Good to know** · Everything except sending runs in both modes: bookings are read about every five minutes, rules run on the nights that changed and on every night of the 396-night window once a day, the calendar shows the prices and the change log fills with what MAYA did or would have done. A General Manager or Hotel Admin goes live from the review page, or [asks us to](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Go%20live) when its **Turn them on for real** button is not there. Click **Team** at the top right of the dashboard. Under **Add someone**, enter their email, set **What they can do** to **Viewer** and click **Send invitation**. They get an email with a single-use link to set a password. A Viewer sees everything on the property and can change nothing.

**1. Open the Team page**

Click **Team** in the dashboard header. You need General Manager or Hotel Admin access. The counter at the top right reads how many seats are used, for example "1 of 2 seats used · 20 rooms".

**2. Fill in Add someone**

In **Their email**, type their work address. In **What they can do**, choose **Viewer**. The line under the form reads the role's description: "Can look, cannot change anything."

**3. Send it**

Click **Send invitation**. The page reads "Invitation sent to [name@yourhotel.com](mailto:name@yourhotel.com). They'll get an email with a link to join." They are on the property from that moment, before they open the email. Their address appears straight away under **On this property** as a Viewer, with a role dropdown and **Remove**, like everyone else. The email's link is only how they set their password.

An email with the subject "You have been invited to The Harbour Inn on MAYA" and a button **Accept the invite**. The link is single-use and expires. It opens a page headed "Set your password" with an optional full name, a password of at least 8 characters, the Terms checkbox and **Set password & continue**. Then they are on the dashboard.

If they have signed in to MAYA before, from another property say, no email goes out: they are added to the property at once and see it in the **Property** dropdown the next time they open MAYA. The page says "Added. [name@yourhotel.com](mailto:name@yourhotel.com) already uses MAYA and will see this property next time they sign in."

A Viewer can view every price but cannot change any of them. They see all five tabs, the prices on the calendar, every change log entry including **Show the numbers**, the **PMS** tab, and any banner.
