The **Billing** and **Team** pages show them a line saying who handles those. A Viewer who tries to add a rule sees an error, and the rule switches and **Delete** buttons do nothing for them.

**Good to know** · Seats follow your billed room count: 2 seats for 1 to 20 rooms, 4 for 21 to 40, 5 for 41 to 60, 6 for 61 to 80 and 8 for 81 to 500. Everyone under **On this property** uses a seat, including someone who has not set a password yet. When every seat is used the form is replaced by a note: remove someone, or raise your room count on the **Billing** page. The Terms ask for one login per person, so a front desk of three people needs three seats.

Under **On this property**, each member has a role dropdown, which saves the moment you change it, and a **Remove** button. That includes someone who has not opened the email yet, so **Remove** is also how you take an invitation back.

There is no resend button, and inviting the same address again while they are a member does nothing new: the page answers "That person is already on this property." If their link expired or the email went astray and they have never signed in, click **Remove** and invite them again as a Viewer: a new email goes out with a fresh link. Or [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=New%20invitation%20link) with their address and we send a new link.

Click **Billing** at the top right, scroll to **Room count**, type the new number under **Rooms billed** and click **Change**. A quote shows the new price before you commit, and the difference is adjusted on your next invoice, never charged the same day. If your system shows more rooms than you pay for, MAYA tells you and gives you 7 days before it raises the count for you. It never lowers the count on its own.

**1. Open the Billing page**

Click **Billing** in the dashboard header. You need General Manager or Hotel Admin access. Scroll to the **Room count** section: "Your plan covers 20 rooms. We check this against your property management system."

**2. Type the new number**

Under **Rooms billed**, type a whole number from 1 to 500. A quote appears from the same brackets Stripe bills. For example, going from 20 rooms to 21 (the cheaper bracket) reads "$110 down to $105 per month. Your next invoice is adjusted for the part of this period you have already paid." When the price goes down, the quote adds "That is $5 less."

**3. Click Change**

The page reads "Room count updated." Stripe confirms a moment later and the new number shows on the page. Nothing is charged today: the unused part of the period is credited and the difference lands on the next invoice.

MAYA counts the rooms in your property system on every cycle: the units of every active room type ticked as **Counts as a room**, leaving out types you have unticked and, until you answer, types whose names are plainly not bedrooms. The section shows what it found: "Your PMS currently shows 22 active rooms."

- **Running more rooms than you pay for.** The billing page and a dashboard banner say "You're billed for 20 rooms but running 22", and an email goes to the address that gets your invoices. Set the count yourself within 7 days of that email. After that MAYA raises it to the measured number and adjusts the next invoice. Nothing is charged separately.
Running more rooms than you pay for

- **Paying for more rooms than you run.** The page says so and invites you to lower it here. It is never lowered for you, so a wing closed for a fortnight does not quietly cut your bill: lower it yourself if you want to.

On ThinkReservations, MAYA counts each room type's rooms from ThinkReservations' list of rooms. A room marked there as inactive, as not a room, or as not included in occupancy is left out. If the measured number looks wrong, check those settings on your rooms in ThinkReservations, and **Counts as a room** on the **PMS** tab: the next cycle measures again.
Paying for more rooms than you run

**Good to know** · The room count changes on MAYA's billing page, not in Stripe: the Stripe portal does not offer it. Your seats on the **Team** page follow the billed count too. Prices are per room per month in US dollars: $5.50 for 1 to 20 rooms, $5.00 for 21 to 40, $4.00 for 41 to 60, $3.00 for 61 to 80, $2.50 for 81 to 500, with the whole property at its bracket's rate.

**Not yet** · Over 500 rooms is not sold self-serve. Lowering the count gives a credit against future invoices, never a refund. While a subscription has lapsed the field is refused with "This property's subscription is not active, so MAYA has paused work on it."

Click **Billing** at the top right, then **Update card, receipts & cancellation**. That opens Stripe, where your card, invoices and cancellation live. Save the new card there as your default and you are sent back to the Billing page. Then email us so we move your subscription onto it, because a subscription can keep charging the card it started with. If work has paused because the payments failed, there is no need to email: MAYA pays the open invoice with the new card and moves the subscription onto it. MAYA never holds your card: Stripe does.

**1. Open the Billing page**

Click **Billing** in the dashboard header, or **Fix it** on the amber banner when one is showing. You need General Manager or Hotel Admin access.

**2. Open Stripe**

Under **Manage**, click **Update card, receipts & cancellation**. The button reads "Opening…" and Stripe's portal opens for your property's subscription.

**3. Change the payment method and come back**

In the portal, update the payment method and save the new card as your default. Stripe returns you to the Billing page. The portal also holds your invoices and receipts, and the switch between monthly and yearly.

| The Billing page says | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Your saved card stopped working | MAYA checks the card with a zero-amount check that moves no money, once after checkout and again about 48 hours later. This one was declined. Nothing has failed yet. | Before the next charge, update the card, then email us so we move your subscription onto it. The warning clears by itself the next time a payment succeeds. |
| Your last payment did not go through | The bank declined a real charge. Stripe is retrying, and your rules keep running in the meantime. The status row reads "Payment overdue". | Update the card, then email us so we move your subscription onto it. The next retry then uses the new card. |
| MAYA has paused work on this property | The retries ran out. Your rules no longer run on a schedule and nothing is sent to your PMS. The status row reads "Unpaid" and the dashboard shows the red **Restart MAYA** banner. | Update the card and save it as your default. MAYA pays the open invoice with it straight away and moves the subscription onto it, so there is no need to email us. Once the payment goes through, the subscription restarts where it left off. Your rules, settings and history are untouched. If the new card is declined too, the status stays "Unpaid": save a different card. |

The retry period is a Stripe setting, about two weeks.

**Good to know** · Receipts, failed-payment emails and expiring-card emails come from Stripe, not from MAYA, to the email address on your billing account. MAYA cannot resend them. MAYA itself sends five emails: the team invitation, the account ready email after you pay, the room count email, a nudge before a charge when your property system is not connected, and an email to your General Managers and Hotel Admins when the connection to your property system has been down about an hour.

**Not yet** · Every payment is taken automatically, so there is no invoice to pay by hand. US bank debit (ACH) is switched off when you subscribe, and Stripe's portal shows the ways you can pay. There is no way to update a card from inside MAYA, and no card details are shown there beyond the decline reason when a check fails.

Click **Billing** at the top right, then **Update card, receipts & cancellation**, and cancel in Stripe's portal. MAYA keeps working until the end of the period you have paid for, then stops reading, pricing and sending. The prices already in your property system stay as they are. Cancelling deletes nothing: disconnect in your system if you want to, and email us if you want your data removed.

**1. Open the Billing page**

Click **Billing** in the dashboard header. You need General Manager or Hotel Admin access.

**2. Open Stripe and cancel**

Under **Manage**, click **Update card, receipts & cancellation**. In the portal, choose to cancel and give a reason if asked. Stripe returns you to the Billing page.

**3. Check the page**

The headline reads "This subscription is set to cancel" with "MAYA keeps working until November 30, 2026, then stops." and the period row is labelled **Access ends**.

You can also cancel in writing: [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Cancel%20my%20subscription) from a General Manager's or Hotel Admin's address. A property that has paid but is not connected yet has no Billing page: use the **Manage billing or cancel** link on the setup screen instead.

MAYA stops reading your bookings, running your rules and sending prices. The status row reads "Cancelled" and the dashboard shows the red banner "MAYA has paused work on this property". You can still sign in and read the calendar, the change log and the team page.

- **Prices in your system stay as they are.** MAYA never reverts them. On Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations, if you want your own rates back, set them in your system, or before the period ends delete your rules in MAYA so the reverted prices are sent. On Mews, MAYA never sent prices, so your rates are already your own.
Prices in your system stay as they are

- **Rules, settings and history stay** in MAYA, so a restart picks up where you left off. (One exception, for a Cloudbeds Marketplace property that never paid, is under [Delete your data](#delete-your-data-if-you-want-that).)
Rules, settings and history stay
- **No refund for the rest of the period**, and no pause instead of cancelling.
No refund for the rest of the period

Cancelling does not disconnect your property system, and disconnecting does not cancel billing. To stop completely, cancel first, then disconnect.

**Cloudbeds:** In Cloudbeds, open **Marketplace**, then **My Apps**, and disconnect MAYA there. Cloudbeds tells MAYA, and the **PMS** tab reads **Disconnected**. There is no disconnect button inside MAYA.

**ThinkReservations:** There is no disconnect button inside MAYA. Once the subscription has ended MAYA no longer reads ThinkReservations. To remove MAYA's access on the ThinkReservations side, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Disconnect%20ThinkReservations) and we walk through it with you.

**Mews:** Mews is connected by us with keys from your Mews dashboard. [Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Disconnect%20Mews) and we remove the keys.

Nothing is deleted when you cancel or disconnect, and there is no delete button in MAYA. A Hotel Admin or General Manager emails [info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Close%20my%20account) with the subject "Close my account". We delete or de-identify the property's data within 90 days, keeping only what the Terms and Privacy Policy list, such as billing records. It is permanent, and a later reconnection starts from scratch.

One exception applies to a property that came from the Cloudbeds Marketplace and never paid (cancelled during the free trial, say). After 180 days with nobody using MAYA for it, its booking history and its connection to Cloudbeds can be removed. Your rules and settings stay, and reconnecting imports the history again. A property that has ever paid is never touched this way.

**Good to know** · To come back, click **Restart your subscription** on the **Billing** page: a new subscription at the same prices, with your rules and settings in place. While sign-up for your system is still invite-only, you need a new code from us (the first cannot be used again), so [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Restart%20code) for one. A connection you removed stays removed until you [reconnect your property system](@92).

When the connection breaks, an amber panel headed "MAYA has lost its connection to Cloudbeds" appears with a **Reconnect Cloudbeds** button. A General Manager or Hotel Admin clicks it, signs in at Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations, and lands back on the MAYA dashboard with the panel gone. Nothing about your rules, history or settings changes. Mews connects with keys we enter, so email us.

**1. Find the panel**

Open the **PMS** tab. When the connection is broken (the **Connection** card reads **Error** or **Disconnected**), an amber panel sits above the cards: "MAYA has lost its connection to Cloudbeds" and "Your prices aren't updating while this is down." The same panel appears as a banner at the top of the dashboard, whichever tab is open. When the card reads **Degraded**, MAYA is still reading and sending, and you see one calm line instead: "Your Cloudbeds connection needs a refresh soon. Prices are still updating." If it is still there in an hour, click the quiet **Reconnect Cloudbeds** link at the end of that line. It does no harm.

**2. Click Reconnect**

Click **Reconnect Cloudbeds** (or **Reconnect Think Reservations**). You are sent to your system's own sign-in page. Sign in and approve. The link is good for 15 minutes and finishes only for you, signed in to MAYA in the same browser: the person who clicked the button. If you take longer, you see "That sign-in link ran out after 15 minutes. Start again from MAYA." If someone else opens the link, or you have signed out of MAYA in between, you see "This reconnect link was started from a different account. Sign in as the person who started it, or start the reconnect again from MAYA." Nothing has changed either way: click **Open MAYA** and reconnect again.

**Cloudbeds:** Another way: in Cloudbeds, open **Marketplace** and click **Connect App** on MAYA again. For a property that started in the Marketplace, Cloudbeds sends you to MAYA's sign-in page with the line "Your Cloudbeds connection is active again. Sign in to pick up where you left off." For a property you connected from inside MAYA, sign in to MAYA first as its General Manager or Hotel Admin, and you come back to its **PMS** tab with "Reconnected." Anyone else sees "This property is already in MAYA, so nothing new was added." MAYA never adds the property a second time. This is also the way back if you uninstalled the app by accident. If someone removed MAYA's permission to update rates rather than uninstalling it, restore the permission in Cloudbeds first, then reconnect.

**Mews:** The panel reads "Mews needs its keys re-entered" with no button, for every role, because Mews connects with keys we enter rather than a login. It appears once Mews has refused MAYA's keys three reads in a row, or after we remove the keys. It says "Ask us to re-enter the Mews keys: email [info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com).", and the address opens an email to us. [Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Mews%20keys) and we arrange new keys with you.

The banner shows only while the **Connection** card reads **Error** or **Disconnected**. If the change log says to reconnect and there is no banner, your system is most likely refusing the price write while it still lets MAYA read, so the card reads **Connected**. Open the **PMS** tab: a General Manager or Hotel Admin always finds the **Reconnect Cloudbeds** link there.

**Good to know** · A property that came from the Cloudbeds Marketplace, never paid and sat unused for 180 days can have its booking history removed. Its panel reads "Your rules and settings are still here, and your booking history comes back once you reconnect." Reconnecting starts a fresh import, and pricing resumes once it completes.

**Not yet** · The email waits until the connection has been down about an hour, never comes for **Degraded**, and there is no text message. There is no manual "sync now" button.

Open the **Change Log** tab: each change a rule makes names the rule and the reason. To fix a night now, type the price you want. To undo a rule's changes everywhere, delete the rule. Most runs change nothing, and nothing is sent until you go live.

One of your rules may have. Open the **Change Log** tab and find the night. Each change names the rule that acted and the reason, in one or two sentences. The change log only reaches back about 50 minutes. For an older change, check the night's **Current price** and any **Manual** badge on the calendar, and [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Why%20did%20a%20price%20change) the night and room type: the detail behind every change is kept for 90 days, and we can read it for you. If a booking speed rule cut the night, the sentence reads something like "Bookings came in much slower than normal this past month: 1, against the 5 a night like this usually has by now."

That reading can be right and still feel wrong, for two reasons.

First, a wedding booked as one reservation is one booking. For booking speed, a booking counts once however many rooms it holds. A 20-room wedding on your Saturday is 20 booked rooms for occupancy and one booking for booking speed. If similar Saturdays had received 5 bookings by this point, one booking reads as much slower, and a cut rule that measures only booking speed fires. It does not look at how full the night is unless you gave it an occupancy condition.

Second, MAYA reads bookings, not blocks or allotments, from Cloudbeds, ThinkReservations and Mews. A wedding held as a block in your property system, with no booking behind it, adds nothing to the count and nothing to occupancy.

**Fix it now.** On the **Calendar** tab, open the night, and on the room type card type the price you want. Use **through…** to cover the whole weekend in one save. On a live Cloudbeds property that price goes to your system now, and ThinkReservations applies it shortly after. With Mews a typed price is never sent, although the confirmation says "Sending to Mews now". Rules that had already moved the night are paused for that room type. Read [Setting a price yourself](@50).
Fix it now

**Keep the rules off those nights.** Your typed price is not a lock. Once its wait is over, a booking speed rule reads the night again and can cut on top of your price. To keep your number, switch off the cut rules on the **Rules** tab until the weekend has passed. Off stops a rule on every night, and what it already did stays. Read [Hold a price for an event](@68).
Keep the rules off those nights

**Prevent it next time.** Give your cut rules an occupancy condition, so a full night can never read as one to cut. Click **Edit** on the rule, add **Sellable occupancy (%)** **Less than** 50 as a second condition and click **Save changes**. **Apply price adjustments** takes its cuts off the full nights, and **Skip price adjustments** leaves them and keeps new cuts off. Read [Change a rule](@72).

For a block held in your system without bookings, enter those rooms as out of service on the **PMS** tab so occupancy reads against what you can sell.

**Careful** · A cut made because a night was booking slowly never comes off for cancellations, because guests cancelling only make it truer. It stays until you type a price or delete the rule. Other rules stack on top of it.
Prevent it next time

Most pricing runs change nothing, and the change log hides them by default. Press **Show All Cycles** and each stretch of those runs shows as one line, such as "Prices checked 47 times from Sep 24, 10:05 AM to 1:55 PM (4 min ago), nothing needed to change." A quiet property is a property whose rules were checked and found no reason to act.

The usual reasons a rule stays quiet:
- **A standard rule holds.** A rule with only occupancy or booking window conditions changes the price once when its condition starts to hold, then holds it. It does not fire again every day.
A standard rule holds

- **A booking speed rule is waiting.** After it acts on a night it leaves that night alone for its wait, from 1 day to 2 weeks. When the wait is over it counts only bookings made since the newest change still on that night by itself or a stronger rule moving the price the same way, so a burst already acted on cannot make it act again.
A booking speed rule is waiting

- **Not enough history.** A booking speed rule stays quiet only when there are neither similar past nights nor enough nearby nights to read momentum from (how nearby nights are filling now). Then **Show the numbers** under a change says "Booking speed wasn't rated for this night, so rules that watch booking speed left it alone." Occupancy and booking window rules work from day one.
Not enough history

- **A read failed.** A run whose booking read failed prices nothing and sends nothing. **Last sync** on the **PMS** tab shows the last read that worked. On Cloudbeds, **Health (last 24 hours)** also counts the requests that failed. On ThinkReservations and Mews that card reads "Not tracked for this system", so check **Last sync**.
A read failed

- **The subscription lapsed.** A red banner at the top of the app reads "MAYA has paused work on this property". Nothing runs until the subscription restarts. After failed payments, update your card. After a cancellation, start a new subscription. The banner says which, and its **Restart MAYA** button opens the **Billing** page. A paused subscription is on hold in Stripe: its banner has an **Email us** button instead, and we get it running again.
The subscription lapsed

- **The connection is lost.** Open the **PMS** tab to check. The amber banner at the top of the dashboard, "MAYA has lost its connection to Cloudbeds" (or your system's name), shows whichever tab is open once the connection is marked as lost. While the card reads Error or Disconnected, nothing is read, priced or sent. Disconnected waits for someone to reconnect. Error can clear by itself, because MAYA keeps trying, up to an hour between tries.
The connection is lost

- **Rules are switched Off.** The **Rules** tab shows each rule's **Status**.

In simulation the log still fills. Every run happens, every change is written down, and nothing is sent. So a quiet log is quiet for one of the reasons above, not because you are simulating.

Read [A rule did not fire](@97) for the full checklist.
Rules are switched Off

Yes, three ways, and one that does not work.

1. **Type the price you want.** On the **Calendar** tab, open the night, type the price on the room type card and press **Save**. On a live Cloudbeds property it is sent now, and ThinkReservations applies it shortly after. With Mews it is never sent. This is the fastest fix for one night or a range.
Type the price you want

2. **Delete the rule.** On the **Rules** tab, **Delete** undoes every price change the rule made, on every night. The dialog offers **Delete Rule and Undo Its Changes**. Deleting cannot be undone, and the rule's history stays in the change log under the name "Pricing rule".
Delete the rule

3. **Stop it on that night.** When the amber banner asks, **Stop for this night** means the rule makes no more changes there. What it already did stays.

Switching a rule **Off** does not undo anything. Its changes stay exactly where they are, which is the point: you can pause a rule without prices jumping. The delete dialog's other button, **Turn It Off and Keep Its Changes**, does exactly that.

Read [Undo a price change](@67) for the steps, and [When a change comes off](@40) for what comes off on its own.
Stop it on that night

MAYA sends prices only when you have gone live, and only for nights whose price changed since the last send. There is no "sending" light on the dashboard, and no badge that says live or simulation. The word live beside the time at the top right of the calendar ("Updated 3:05:12 PM · live") only means the calendar refreshes by itself. It shows in simulation too. Here is how to tell.

- **The go-live card.** Open the review screen at maya-rms.com/onboarding/review. The card appears only when MAYA built starter rules for you during setup, which needs about 60 days of history, and it stays after someone clicks **Get suggestions from my data**. Without it, read [Going live](@55).
The go-live card

- **A price you typed.** If you typed a price for a real reason lately, its confirmation read "Saved. Sending to Cloudbeds now." on a live property and "Saved (simulation: not sent to Cloudbeds)." while simulating. Do not type a price only to test this: on a live property it sends the price, and it takes any booking speed or pickup change off that night for good.
A price you typed
- **The alert banner.** In simulation the amber banner says a rule "would have 3 raises" on a night. Live, it says "has 3 raises".
The alert banner

- **Compare a night.** Open a night in your property system and in MAYA. Live, the rate there matches MAYA's **Current price** within a few minutes of a change.

Sending problems show in the **Change Log** tab as an item headed "Prices not reaching Cloudbeds" (or your system's name). Success is silent. **Last sync** on the **PMS** tab is the last time bookings were read, not the last time a price was sent.

Mews: nothing is ever sent, live or not. MAYA reads Mews bookings and shows prices, and sending to Mews is not built yet.
