Start in the **Change Log** tab: every change names the rule and the reason. A big jump is usually two rules stacked (percentages compound). A $1 or $99,999 price is the default floor or ceiling, which stop nothing in most currencies, so set real ones. A change with no rule named is your own rate changing in your property system, or a price someone typed. A night with no price is past the 396-night window (tonight and the next 395), closed in your system, or not run yet.

The change log shows the chain with running prices, each step followed by its own reason:

"Busy nights" raised this night 10%, from $200.00 to $220.00.
It was 85% full, past the 80% mark you set.
Then "Hot-week surge" raised it 25%, from $220.00 to $275.00.
Bookings came in much faster than normal this past week: 12, against the 5 a night like this usually has by now.

Once three of one booking speed rule's changes are on the same night, the amber **Rules that keep adjusting** banner asks you whether to carry on or stop. Until you answer, it keeps going. Read [Rules that keep adjusting](@43).

If the jump is bigger than you want, set a ceiling. The default ceiling is $99,999.99, which stops nothing in most currencies. Read [Floors and ceilings](@28).

Deluxe is $200. "Busy nights" (occupancy Greater than 80, Increase 10%) takes it to $220. "Hot-week surge" (Much Faster Than Normal, Increase 25%) takes it to $275. The Deluxe ceiling is $400, so $275 is published. Had the ceiling been $250, the log would add "That would have gone past your $250.00 ceiling for Deluxe, so it stopped there."

Because booking speed compares a night with what similar past nights had received at the same point before arrival, not with how full it is. A night 50 days out is compared with how its similar nights were booking when they were 50 days out. If those nights had received none at all by then, 2 or 3 bookings in a week read Much Faster Than Normal, or Faster Than Normal when there are fewer than 5 similar nights to compare with. If they had averaged a fraction of a booking, 0.4 say, it takes 3, because a difference of less than 2 bookings always reads Normal.

To keep raises off empty nights, add **Sellable occupancy (%)** **Greater than** as a second condition to your raise rules. A rule needs every condition true at once. Click **Edit** on the rule, click **+ Add condition**, and click **Save changes**. The window then shows the nights that change: **Apply price adjustments** takes the rule's raises off the nights the new condition rules out, and **Skip price adjustments** leaves them and keeps new raises off. An edited starter rule keeps its place above the rules you build.

A cut rule with only a booking speed condition does not look at occupancy. It counts bookings made in its window (past day, week or month, in full days up to yesterday) and compares them with similar nights over the same stretch. A night that filled up months ago and received one booking this month reads slower than a night like it usually books, and the cut fires.

A wedding or group booked as one reservation makes this more likely: for booking speed, a booking counts once however many rooms it holds. Twenty rooms in one reservation are 20 rooms for occupancy and one booking for booking speed.

Fix the night by typing a price on the **Calendar** tab. Read [Start here](@95) for the wedding weekend case in full.

MAYA does not read how many rooms your system still has for sale. A full night is priced like any other: your rules run on it whenever its bookings change and once a day, and once you are live its price is sent whenever it changes (Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations). That is on purpose. A cancellation puts a room back on sale, and it sells at the rate your system has at that moment, which is MAYA's latest price once you are live.

On a sold-out night:

- **An occupancy raise stays.** A rule such as "Busy nights" keeps its one raise while the night stays above its mark, and, with its undo box ticked, takes it off if cancellations bring the night back down to the mark or under.
An occupancy raise stays
- **A booking speed cut can still fire.** A full night takes no new bookings, so its recent count can read slow against similar nights that were still selling at the same point (the question above).
A booking speed cut can still fire

- **Raises already made stay on the price**, as they do on any night.

To keep cuts off full nights, add a **Sellable occupancy (%)** row set to **Less than** (70, say) to each cut rule: **Edit** on its row, **+ Add condition**, **Save changes**. For an exact price on a sold-out night, type it on the **Calendar** tab.

Editing a starter rule keeps the rest of it exactly as it is, its rank above rules you built included, and "Slow-date trim" keeps its exactly **Slower Than Normal** unless you pick another speed. Read [Change a rule](@72).
Raises already made stay on the price

That is the default floor, $1.00, and it stops nothing in practice. A cut rule that fires again after each wait, on a night that keeps reading slow, walks the price down until the floor catches it. With no floor set, the floor is $1.

Set a floor for each room type. On the **Rules** tab press **Get suggestions from my data**. MAYA offers a floor only for a room type whose floor is still the $1.00 default. It also needs your answer to the floor question during setup, or at least 30 sold nights for that room type. Accept the amount, or type your own, then press **Set it to**. On the amber banner, **Ask MAYA for a floor** takes you to the **Rules** tab for the same button.

Once a floor is set, a cut rule stops firing on a night that is already at the floor, because it cannot move the price in its own direction. The price stays at the floor until you type a price, delete the rule, or bookings change what the rules read.

That is the default ceiling, $99,999.99. In most currencies it has the same effect as no ceiling at all. Raise rules that keep firing on a night that keeps reading fast climb until the ceiling stops them.

In a currency where rooms sell for more than 99,999.99 (yen, won, rupiah or dong, for example), a price stuck at 99,999.99 is the default ceiling holding it down, even below your own rate. Set a real ceiling for that room type before you go live. Read [Floors and ceilings](@28#when-your-rates-are-above-the-default-ceiling).

**Good to know: The banner tells you when a limit is still the default** · When three of a rule's changes are on a night and the limit is still the default, the banner's night card says so: "Your ceiling for Suite is still MAYA's $99,999.99 default, so the price can climb that far."

Every published price is held between the room type's floor and ceiling. When the rules ask for less than the floor, the floor is published and the change log says "That would have dropped under your $80.00 floor for Standard, so it stopped there."

While the price sits at the floor, a cut rule does not fire again (it cannot move the price down), and a standard rule's cut holds while its condition holds. The price stays at the floor until something changes what the rules read, or until you act.

To lift it: type the price you want on the **Calendar** tab, or delete the cutting rule (which undoes its changes). Turning the rule **Off** keeps its changes, so the price stays at the floor. A typed price below the floor is refused rather than moved: "Below this room type's floor of $80.00." The one exception is 0, which is a comp night.

Three shapes of entry have no rule name.

**"The rate moved from $200.00 to $210.00."** MAYA had nothing else to say: no rule fired, no rule came off, no limit stepped in. Nearly always your own rate changed in your property system. MAYA reads your rates about once an hour, and again when your property's date changes, and prices from that base. On a night MAYA has never sent to, a rate you change in Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations becomes the new starting point. Read [Rates changed in your property system](@51).

Mews: MAYA reads no rates from Mews, so a Mews night's starting price is always one someone typed, and this line does not appear there.
"The rate moved from $200.00 to $210.00."
**"Sam set the base rate to $180.00."** A person typed a price on the **Calendar** tab. The entry is labelled "Manual price". "A manager" appears when the name is not on file.
"Sam set the base rate to $180.00."

**"The base rate was changed in Cloudbeds to $180.00."** On a live property, a rate you changed in your system on a night MAYA had already sent to, an hour or more after the send, is kept as a manual price. The day card shows "Changed in Cloudbeds · $180.00". No name is attached.

A fourth shape names a rule you cannot find: **"Pricing rule"**. That is a rule someone has deleted. The history stays; the name does not.
"The base rate was changed in Cloudbeds to $180.00."

Four reasons, and the change log names each.

- **A standard rule switched off.** A rule with only occupancy or booking window conditions holds its change while the condition holds. With its undo box ticked, a cancellation that drops occupancy under the mark stops the condition holding, and the change comes off on the next run.
A standard rule switched off

- **A change came off after cancellations.** "Cancellations meant "Warm-date bump" was no longer true, so its 10% raise came off." With a rule's undo box ticked, a booking speed or pickup change comes off when bookings it counted cancel and the rule is no longer true for the night, unless bookings made since keep it true. A cut made because a night was booking slowly never comes off this way, and nor does any change from a rule with its undo box unticked.
A change came off after cancellations
- **A rule was deleted.** Deleting undoes every change the rule made, from the next run.
A rule was deleted

- **A manual price was cleared.** **Clear** on the room type card hands the night back to your rules. Standard rules (occupancy and booking window) that the typed price had paused apply again at once, if their condition still holds. Booking speed and pickup changes it took off stay off. Those rules change the night again only by firing anew, which they are free to do from the next run.

Read [When a change comes off](@40).
A manual price was cleared

The room type card shows "Current price" followed by a dash when no price has been published for that night and room type. Reasons, most common first:

1. **Beyond 396 nights.** Your rules price tonight and the next 395 nights, so a night further out gets no price. A price you typed further out is kept, and the night is priced and sent once it enters the window.
Beyond 396 nights

2. **Closed in your system.** A night whose rate is 0 in Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations, with no price typed in MAYA, is left unpriced. MAYA does not open a closed night at the floor. Type a price if you want the night priced.
Closed in your system

3. **No rate in your system for the night.** A night Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations has no rate for, for example one further ahead than you have loaded rates, is not priced and nothing is sent for it, whatever its bookings paid. The card reads "No rate in Cloudbeds for this night yet" (or your system's name) under the dash. Load a rate for it in your system and the next hourly read picks it up, or type a price in MAYA, which is sent as typed. MAYA reads your rates as far ahead as your system returns them; a night past that is treated the same way until a read returns it.
No rate in your system for the night
4. **Not run yet.** A property that connected minutes ago has no runs until its first cycle. Give it about five minutes.
Not run yet
5. **A past night.** Past nights are never priced or changed.
A past night

6. **A room type switched off in MAYA.** A room type hidden during the review (an empty duplicate), or one we switched off after you removed it from your system, is not priced and has no card on the **Calendar** tab. A room type you only removed in your system stays priced until we switch it off, but nights that enter the 396-night window after you removed it have no rate to start from and show a dash. [Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Switch%20off%20a%20room%20type) its name and we switch it off. Read [Room types and rooms out of service](@52).

Mews: a Mews property has no rate read, so a night stays unpriced until you type a price for it.
A room type switched off in MAYA

Because it keeps going until you answer. Once three of a booking speed or pickup rule's changes are on the same night, the amber **Rules that keep adjusting** banner appears at the top of every tab: ""Hot-week surge" has 3 raises on Fri, Nov 13 2026." and "It keeps raising these nights until you stop it."

Answer **Keep adjusting** and MAYA stops asking about that night. Answer **Stop for this night** and the rule makes no more changes there. Only a Revenue Manager or above can answer. Read [Rules that keep adjusting](@43).

Stop means no more changes from that rule on that night. What it already did stays: "What it already changed there stays, unless cancellations mean the rule is no longer true." For a rule with its undo box unticked: "What it already changed there stays."

To put the price where you want it, type it on the **Calendar** tab. To undo everything the rule did on every night, delete the rule. Read [Undo a price change](@67).

""Slow-date trim" lowered this night 7%, from $200.00 to $186.00." and, after its reason, "Then "Slow-date trim" lowered it another 7%, from $186.00 to $172.98." is one rule that fired, waited its wait, and fired again. A booking speed rule can act on the same night more than once. After the first change it counts only bookings made in the full days since the newest cut still on the night by itself or a stronger rule, up to yesterday, compared with similar nights over the same days, and if those still read slow it cuts again. Three of its changes on one night bring the amber banner.

Three things clear a manual price.

- **Someone pressed **Clear**.** The confirmation reads "Cleared. Your rules price this night again." Any Revenue Manager or above on the property can do it.
Someone pressed Clear

- **Your system reported the night at 0.** On a live property, a night MAYA has sent to that your system now has at 0 is read as you closing it. The night is left unpriced and the manual price there is cleared. When you load a rate again, MAYA reads it as the starting point.
Your system reported the night at 0
- **The night passed.** Manual prices apply to tonight onwards.
The night passed

A rule fires only when every one of its conditions is true on the room types it measures, and only where nothing holds it back: a wait, a stronger rule, a ceiling or floor already reached, or history it does not have. The day card shows the whole property, while a rule reads only its own room types, and **Greater than** 80 means more than 80, not 80 exactly. The **Fired** column on the **Rules** tab tells you whether it has ever acted.

Two things to check.

**Which room types the rule measures.** The day card's big percentage is sellable occupancy over every room type ticked as a room. A rule reads occupancy over the room types in its own list. If a rule such as "Busy Standard" measures only Standard, and Standard is 75% full while Deluxe and Suite are full, the property reads 85% and the rule reads 75%. The **Room Types** column on the **Rules** tab shows the list, and "Watches Standard · Changes Suite" when the rule measures one set and changes another.
Which room types the rule measures

**The comparison is strict.** **Greater than** 80 fires at 80.01% and not at 80.00%. **Less than** 50 fires at 49.9% and not at 50.00%. To fire at exactly 80% as well, set the threshold to 79.99 (the box takes decimals).

Also check the rule's other conditions. A rule with occupancy and a booking window needs both true at once. "Busy nights" with a booking window **Less than** 7 added does nothing on a night 20 days out, however full it is.
The comparison is strict

Work down this list. Most are visible on screen.

1. **The rule is Off.** The **Status** switch on the **Rules** tab. An Off rule is skipped on every night.
The rule is Off

2. **It measures nothing.** Only room types ticked as **Counts as a room** are measured. A rule whose measured list holds only a meeting room, a court or a spa slot reads nothing, so its conditions can never be true. A room type switched off in MAYA (an empty duplicate hidden during the review, or one we switched off after you removed it from your system) is dropped from the list too.
It measures nothing

3. **It changes nothing.** A rule needs at least one room type to change, and the builder refuses to save without one. A room type switched off in MAYA is never priced, so a rule that changes only that type does nothing. A room type you only removed in your system stays priced until we switch it off, but nights that enter the 396-night window after you removed it have no rate to start from, so nothing fires on them (item 10).
It changes nothing

4. **It is waiting.** A booking speed or pickup rule leaves a night alone for its wait after acting on it, from 1 day to 2 weeks, per night and room type. A price you type on the night restarts the wait from that moment for every rule that existed when you typed it.
It is waiting

5. **It counts only what came in after the latest raise.** Once a night has been raised, a booking speed rule that raises counts from the newest raise still on that night by itself or a stronger rule. A weaker rule's raise never moves where it counts from. On the day of the raise, only the bookings that arrived after it count. A rule that raises on a fast pace needs those alone to beat what similar nights get in its whole window; any other rule compares them with similar nights over the same days. Cuts work the same way among the rules that cut, in full days up to yesterday. A raise by a rule with only occupancy or booking window conditions never moves where counting starts. After a price you type, the rule reads its whole window again.
It counts only what came in after the latest raise

6. **A stronger rule holds the night.** Only one booking speed or pickup rule fires on a night and room type in a run. A waiting rule whose condition still holds keeps the night, so nothing weaker fires under it. When two are ready at once, higher priority wins first (starter rules before yours, and every rule you build has the same priority). Then the one with more conditions wins, then, for two pickup rules with the same **Compare**, the stricter threshold, then the larger money move, then the older rule. Read [which one fires when several match](@39#which-one-fires-when-several-match).
A stronger rule holds the night
7. **The price is already at the limit.** A raise does not fire on a night already at its ceiling. A cut does not fire on a night at its floor. Neither counts as a fire.
The price is already at the limit

8. **Not enough history.** A booking speed rule needs similar past nights, or failing those enough nearby nights to read momentum from. Momentum is how nearby nights are booking now compared with the same nights a year earlier. With neither it stays quiet. The change log's **Show the numbers** says "Booking speed wasn't rated for this night, so rules that watch booking speed left it alone."
Not enough history

9. **No pickup reading from the window's start.** A pickup count rule compares booked rooms now with booked rooms when its lookback window opened (1, 3 or 7 days ago). MAYA needs a reading from that moment for every room type the rule measures. A property that connected two days ago has no reading from 3 days ago, so a 3-day pickup rule stays quiet until it does, and a room type ticked as a room today has none either. A reading more than 12 hours older than the window's start does not count.
No pickup reading from the window's start

10. **The night has no starting price.** A night your system has at 0, or has no rate for at all, with no price typed in MAYA, is not priced, so nothing can fire on it. A booking's rate is never a starting price.
The night has no starting price

11. **A standard rule is already holding.** A rule with only occupancy or booking window conditions fires once when its condition starts to hold, then holds. It does not fire again while the condition stays true, and the **Fired** count does not climb.
A standard rule is already holding

12. **The night is outside the window.** Your rules price tonight and the next 395 nights. Past nights are never touched.

**Good to know: The Fired column** · **Fired** shows how many times a rule has acted, once per night and room type, including changes that later came off. A dash means never. Its **?** explains the count.
The night is outside the window

Rules act per room type, so every hold in the list above applies room type by room type.

- **Different ceilings and floors.** Standard's $300 ceiling may already be reached while Deluxe has room under its $400.
Different ceilings and floors
- **Different waits.** Each room type waits on its own. Standard may still be inside its wait from an earlier fire while Deluxe is free.
Different waits

- **Different counts.** One rule reads the same count for every room type it changes, taken over the room types it measures. A booking speed rule's count differs between two room types only when the newest change it counts from, by itself or a stronger rule, was made at a different time on each, or you typed a price on one of them after that, which sends the rule back to its whole window there. To read each room type on its own, make one rule per room type, each measuring and changing only itself.
Different counts

- **A stronger rule holds Standard.** Another rule may be waiting on Standard with its condition still true, which keeps weaker rules off that room type.

The change log lists each room type's change separately, so you can read the reason for the one that fired and look for the hold on the one that did not.
A stronger rule holds Standard

Your rules price a window of 396 nights: tonight and the next 395, counted on your property's own calendar. A night 397 days out is not priced or sent, and no rule reads it. It enters the window the day after tomorrow, and rules act on it then.

You can type a price up to 399 days ahead. It is kept, and the night is priced and sent once it enters the window.

Only room types ticked as **Counts as a room** are measured. Occupancy is rooms booked over rooms you can sell, and booking speed counts bookings, and neither is worked out for a court, a meeting room or a spa slot. A rule whose measured list holds only such types measures nothing and never fires.

It can still price the court. Tick **Change prices on different room types** in the builder, put a real room type under **Measure** and the court under **Change**. The rule then reads the room type's occupancy or booking speed and changes the court's price. Read [Measure one set of room types, change another](@38).

When a rule measures a mix, MAYA drops the non-rooms from the figure and says so in the change log: "That 95% leaves out Pickleball Court."

The **Rate Simulator** tab lists every rule that did not fire under "Didn't fire", with one of these reasons:

| Reason | What it means |
|---|---|
| "Conditions not met" | The rule's conditions were false for the numbers you typed. The line adds what it saw: "(it saw 70% occupancy, 30 days out)". |
| "No occupancy for its signal room types" | None of the room types the rule measures counts as a room, or you gave them no rooms. |
| "Rule has no room types attached" | The rule has nothing to change. |
| "Outside the rule's date window" | The rule has a date range. Rules you make in the app have none, so you should not see this. |
| "This day of the week is excluded" | The rule runs only on some days. Rules you make in the app run every day. A starter rule whose name ends in "(Fri and Sat)" or "(Sun to Thu)" runs only on those nights, because it copies a move you made only on them. |

The simulator's **Booking speed** select starts on "Not enough history", which keeps booking speed rules quiet, exactly as your booking speed rules do on a real night when there is not enough history. Pick a level to see what they would do.

The simulator differs from a real run in three ways it states on screen: a standard rule shows where the night settles rather than each step, every matching booking speed rule is added rather than one winner chosen, and a rule that would fire again after its wait is shown once. Read [The Rate Simulator](@44).

The room type list in the builder does two jobs. Unticked, **Apply to room types** is both the set the rule measures and the set it changes. Ticked, **Change prices on different room types** splits it into **Measure** and **Change**. The rule card reads "Watches Standard, Deluxe · Changes Suite" when the two differ.

If a rule changed a room type you did not expect, it is in that rule's **Change** list. Click **Edit** on the rule, untick it and click **Save changes**. With **Apply price adjustments**, the rule's changes come off that room type from the next run. Read [Change a rule](@72).

Viewers can look but not change. A Viewer who presses **Add Rule** or **Save changes**, flips a switch or presses **Delete** sees "Only a Revenue Manager or above can change this." in red, under the form or under the rule, and nothing is saved. Rules need Revenue Manager access or higher. Ask a General Manager or Hotel Admin to change your role on the **Team** page. Read [Roles](@64).

Turning a rule **Off** freezes what it has done: its changes stay on the price. A change made by a booking speed or pickup rule that is Off also still marks where weaker rules start counting, because the bookings behind it were already acted on. Once a night carries a change, a booking speed or pickup rule counts only bookings made since the newest change still on that night by itself or a stronger rule moving the price the same way, switched-off rules included. Delete the rule if you want its changes and its marks gone.

Booking speed compares how many bookings a night received in the past day, week or month with how many similar past nights had received by the same point before arrival. A booking counts once, however many rooms it holds. Small numbers read the way small numbers do: 2 bookings on a far-out night can be Much Faster Than Normal, and a big count can still read Normal when the difference is within the ordinary ups and downs. The **Show the numbers** panel under a change shows the count, the expected count and the nights compared.

MAYA compares the bookings a night received with the bookings a night like it usually has by now, and reads the gap as one of seven levels. The smaller the numbers, the bigger the gap has to be before a night reads anything but Normal. With 5 expected you need 9 to read Faster Than Normal. With 20 expected you need 27. The outer levels, Stalled and Surging, need a bigger gap still. With fewer than 5 similar nights to compare with, the level stays within one step of Normal.
Expected 5, received 9, with 5 similar nights: Faster Than Normal.

Because the nights it was compared with had received almost none by that point. A night 50 days out is compared with how its similar nights were booking when they were 50 days out, which is often close to nothing. When the similar nights had received none at all, 2 or 3 bookings read Much Faster Than Normal and 4 or more read Surging, provided there are at least 5 similar nights. Against an expectation of 0.4, 2 bookings still read Normal: it takes 3 to read Much Faster and 5 to read Surging. One booking stays Normal against either, because a difference of one is inside the first check.

With fewer than 5 similar nights, or a momentum reading, the reading stops at Faster Than Normal. That is how 2 bookings against none end up reading Faster Than Normal.
If you would rather raise rules stayed off far-out nights, add a **Booking window (days to stay)** **Less than** condition, or a **Sellable occupancy (%)** **Greater than** condition, to the rule.

One of the three checks kept the reading nearer Normal, and the **Show the numbers** panel names which:

- "The numbers leaned away from Normal, but by too little to matter at this many bookings, so it stays Normal." The gap was too small for the numbers involved. With 20 expected, 26 received is 1.3 times as many, which would read Faster, but at that size it takes 27 to leave Normal, so it stays Normal.
- "The numbers pointed one step further from Normal, but not clearly enough, so it reads one step closer to Normal." A Surging or Stalled reading without enough difference behind it.
- "Only a few similar nights were found, so it stays within one step of Normal however strong the numbers look." Fewer than 5 similar nights. A momentum reading (below) always counts as one, so it is always capped.

Under **Show the numbers**, **Which nights were compared?** names the nights that were added: "Too few other Friday nights matched, so Saturday nights were compared too, since they are also weekend nights. Friday and Saturday nights count as weekend nights, the rest as weekday nights." and then "Fewer than 4 nights matched closely, so the search was widened. Check the nights below and set aside any that were not normal." Under **List the nights** each compared night carries its reason, for example "a Saturday, similar to a Friday". As your history grows, widening happens less.

Because nobody had told MAYA that weekend was unusual. Open the change, press **Show the numbers**, then **Which nights were compared?**, then **List the nights**. Beside the festival night press **Not a fair comparison?**, choose a reason such as **Local Event or Festival**, and press **Set this date aside**.

From the next run that night is left out of every comparison. Choosing "This happens every year around this time" also counts toward a yearly pattern: once the same reason has been reported from 2 different years, a window of 5 days either side is set aside every year. Read [Not a fair comparison](@49). Setting a date aside needs Revenue Manager access or higher.

MAYA has 17 US holidays and no others, and there is no screen to add one. A night near one of those holidays is compared with the same position around the same holiday in earlier years. A night near any other holiday is compared like an ordinary night.

**Not yet** · You cannot add a holiday. The workaround is to set the night aside from the **Show the numbers** panel with the reason **Holiday Not on MAYA's List** and the scope "This happens every year around this time". After reports from 2 different years, MAYA leaves that stretch out of comparisons every year.

Read [Handle a holiday MAYA does not have](@85).

No. For booking speed a booking counts once, however many rooms it holds, on the night it is made and on every past night it is compared with. A 10-room group booked as one reservation is one booking. For occupancy it is 10 booked rooms. For a pickup count rule it is 10 room nights.

A room added to a group later is not a new booking. The group is counted at the earliest booking date across its rooms on that night.

**Cloudbeds:** Each room of a Cloudbeds reservation is stored as its own room-night, and MAYA groups them back into their reservation for booking speed. A group made as separate reservations counts as separate bookings.

**ThinkReservations:** Each room of a ThinkReservations reservation is stored as its own room-night, and MAYA groups them back into their reservation for booking speed. A group made as separate reservations counts as separate bookings.

On Cloudbeds, a booking with the status Confirmation Pending (Cloudbeds calls it not confirmed) holds a room, and Cloudbeds' own occupancy counts it as sold. MAYA counts it the same way, for occupancy and for booking speed. Cancelled bookings and no-shows do not count, and a booking that cancels disappears from the count on the next read.

On Mews, every reservation counts except a cancelled one. Optional, Enquired and Requested reservations count as booked, for occupancy and for booking speed, exactly like a Confirmed one. On ThinkReservations every booking counts except cancelled bookings and no-shows.

Because it is an average. The usual number, the expected count, is the trimmed average of what the similar nights had received over the same stretch: a plain average with fewer than 5 nights, and with 5 or more the single highest and lowest are dropped first. An expected count of 0.4 is a true statement about a quiet far-out night: most similar nights had none, one or two had one. On screen it reads "almost no bookings" when it is under 1, and "about 3 bookings" otherwise. A similar night with no bookings at all in your history is left out of the average, not counted as zero.

Yes, but the count never goes below zero. It counts the bookings for the night that were made during the window and are still on the books. A booking that cancels drops out on the next read, so cancellations lower the count, down to none at the lowest. A booking made before the window that cancels during it was never in the count, so it changes nothing.

The nights it is compared with are counted the same way: a past booking that cancelled is not in their counts either. When bookings a change counted cancel, the change can come off, if the rule's undo box is ticked and the rule is no longer true. Read [When a change comes off](@40).

When a night has no usable similar nights at all, MAYA falls back to momentum: how the 10 nights either side of it are booking now compared with the same nights a year earlier. The **Show the numbers** panel opens like any other reading, with the count, the usual number and the level.

Under **Which nights were compared?** it explains "Your history has no usable similar nights for this one, so the usual number comes from booking momentum instead." Then comes "Momentum here means how nights near this one are filling now, compared with how the same nights were filling at this point last year." After that it says how many nearby nights could be paired, whether they are filling faster or slower than a year ago, where the starting point came from, and that a momentum reading is a best effort.

After a night has been raised, a rule that raises counts only the bookings made from the newest raise still on that night by itself or by a stronger rule, a rule you have switched off included. A weaker rule's raise does not change where it counts from, and nor does a raise by a standard rule, one with only occupancy or booking window conditions. A raise that has come off no longer counts.

The change log sentence names the shorter stretch: "Bookings came in faster than normal in the 4 days since this rule or a stronger one's latest raise still on this night: 6, against the 2 a night like this usually gets in a whole week." The **Show the numbers** panel opens with "The newest raise still on this night's price, by the rule behind this reading or a stronger rule, was made on Fri, Nov 13 2026. In the 4 days from that raise on, 6 bookings arrived for it, with 20 days still to go before arrival." That raise is always one made by a booking speed or pickup rule.

When the raise was made today, the stretch is that one day: the change log says "later on the day of this rule or a stronger one's latest raise still on this night" and the panel starts "Later that day,".

A rule reads bookings across every room type it measures, then changes every room type in its change list. "Hot-week surge" measuring Standard, Deluxe and Suite reads one count for all three. Six bookings on Standard and Deluxe against an expectation of 2 read Much Faster, and the rule raises Suite too, with no Suite booking in sight.

If you want each room type read on its own, make one rule per room type, each measuring and changing only itself. Each such rule also has its own expected count, worked out from that room type's own history. A small set has a small expected count, and a difference of fewer than 2 bookings always reads Normal, so it stays at Normal more often. When it does leave Normal, a few bookings can be enough.

Sellable occupancy is rooms booked divided by rooms you can sell that night, counting only room types ticked as rooms and taking rooms out of service off first. It differs from Cloudbeds' headline number because Cloudbeds keeps blocked rooms in its count while MAYA removes only rooms you enter as out of service. It can read over 100%. On Mews, where Mews gives no count, a room category is counted as 100 rooms until we change that number, so email us your counts. On ThinkReservations the counts come from your list of rooms there.

Two reasons. Both can make MAYA's number higher than Cloudbeds', and the second can also make it lower.

**Blocked rooms.** Cloudbeds' own headline occupancy keeps blocked rooms in the count it divides by. MAYA does not read room blocks, allotments or out-of-order rooms from Cloudbeds. It divides by the room type's room count minus any rooms you have entered as out of service in MAYA. So a block you enter in MAYA can only make MAYA's number higher than Cloudbeds', and a block you hold only in Cloudbeds does not make them differ.
Blocked rooms

**Which room types count.** MAYA counts only room types ticked as **Counts as a room** on the **PMS** tab. If Cloudbeds lists a meeting room or a parking space as a room type and MAYA has it unticked, the two numbers divide by different room counts. MAYA's number reads higher when those types are emptier than your rooms, and lower when they are fuller.

Which bookings count is the same in both: bookings with the status confirmed, checked in, checked out or Confirmation Pending count as booked. Cancelled bookings and no-shows do not.

Read [Sellable occupancy](@32) for the definition.
Which room types count

Because nobody has told MAYA. Rooms out of order in your property system are not read. Enter them in MAYA: on the **PMS** tab, under the room type, press **+ Rooms out of service**, fill in **From**, **To**, **Units** and an optional **Reason (optional)**, and press **Save**. Those rooms come off the sellable count for those nights only, and your rules run on those nights again from the next cycle if they fall within the 396-night window. Nothing is sent to your property system about the block.

Standard has 12 rooms, 3 are out of service, 8 are booked: 8 of 9, which is 89%. Without the block it reads 8 of 12, which is 67%.

Read [Tell MAYA rooms are out of service](@83).

Because more rooms are booked than MAYA reads as sellable. It happens when you mark rooms out of service after they were already sold (12 rooms, 3 out of service, 10 booked reads 111%), or when your property system has overbooked the night. MAYA does not cap the number.

A rule's threshold cannot go above 100, so a rule set to **Greater than** 100 fires on any overbooked night.

On Mews, every room category Mews sends no room count for gets the same number of rooms, one number for your whole property, 100 until we change it. A category with 6 rooms and 5 booked reads 5% instead of 83%, and occupancy rules that need a full night never fire.

[Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Room%20counts) your room categories and their room counts. We can change that one number for you, not set a count for each category. Once we have set it, occupancy is right from the next run if the categories without a count are all the same size. If they differ, it reads wrong for at least one of them. Read [Mews](@14).

Booking window rules are not affected. Booking speed counts bookings, not rooms, but it compares within seasons read from how full past nights were. Send us your counts before relying on booking speed too.

On ThinkReservations, MAYA counts each room type's rooms from ThinkReservations' list of rooms. Occupancy reads low when that list holds rooms you do not sell: mark them there as inactive, as not a room, or as not included in occupancy, and the next cycle leaves them out. Read [ThinkReservations](@13#how-many-rooms-each-room-type-has).

The **PMS** tab's **Room types** list shows "100 units" for a room type whose room count MAYA does not have. On Cloudbeds the count is read from your system on every cycle, so this is rare and means Cloudbeds reported none. On ThinkReservations it is read from your list of rooms on every cycle, so it shows only when MAYA could not read that list when the room type first appeared, and the next cycle that reads the list puts the real count in. On Mews it is every room category Mews sends no room count for, until we set the one number for your property: email us the real count.

They are reading different room types. The day card's percentage is the whole property: every room type ticked as a room. A change log sentence such as "It was 92% full, past the 80% mark you set." is the occupancy over the room types that rule measures. A rule measuring only Standard reports Standard's occupancy.

When a rule's measured list includes a type that is not a room, MAYA leaves it out of the figure and says so: "That 92% leaves out Meeting Room." Read [A rule did not fire](@97) for how a rule reads its own room types.

Yes, for occupancy. A booking that holds 10 rooms is 10 booked rooms on each of its nights. That is different from booking speed, where a booking counts once however many rooms it holds. Read [Booking speed reads oddly](@98).

The day card's revenue figure sums every room type, including ones you have unticked as rooms. Occupancy and the "12/20 rooms" line use only the ticked ones. So a meeting room booking adds to revenue and not to occupancy.

They value a booked night differently. The day card values each booked night at the booking's rate as it was imported, falling back to its current rate, and at 0 when neither is on file. A pickup count rule set to **Revenue (currency)** sums each booked night's current rate as your system reports it. The two can differ for the same night. Neither figure is sent anywhere.

MAYA adds up the nightly rates your system reports for booked nights. It never adds tax or takes off a booking site's commission, and what the rate includes depends on your system: in Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations it is the room rate on the same basis as your own rates, and in Mews it is the booking total, taxes included, split across its nights. A report that adds taxes, fees or extras, or takes off commission, will differ. [The calendar](@46#one-day-line-by-line) has the detail for each system.

**Not yet** · Booked revenue is shown per night on the calendar and used by revenue pickup rules. There is no revenue report and no export. The day card shows occupancy and room revenue for each night, not the bookings behind them.

Give a new price two cycles, about ten minutes, then open the **Change Log** tab. A problem that needs you, such as a lost connection or a rate rule in your system, sits at the top at once as "Prices not reaching Cloudbeds", with the cause and what to do. One that clears on its own is shown only if it lasts 2 hours, first prices waiting for a read of your own rates after an hour, and a time zone mismatch usually not at all. Nothing is sent while you are simulating, nothing is ever sent to Mews, a price of 0 is never sent, and a night past the 396-night window (tonight and the next 395) waits until it enters it.

Check these in order.

1. **Wait two cycles.** Prices go out about every five minutes, and only prices that changed since the last send. The first send to a night MAYA has never sent to also waits until a fresh read of your own rates has succeeded, within the last hour, so that MAYA writes over a rate it has freshly read. The first live cycle reads your rates before it sends. If that read has not worked for an hour, the change log says "MAYA couldn't read your current rates in Cloudbeds" at the top.
Wait two cycles

2. **Check that you are live.** There is no badge on the dashboard. Open the review page and find the card headed "While you were here, we built your first pricing rules". The green pill "✓ Live: your rules are now managing prices" in it means you are live, and the button **Turn them on for real** means you are simulating. The card appears only when MAYA built starter rules for you at setup, which needs at least 60 days of booking history. If your review page has no such card, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Am%20I%20live) and we check. [Going live](@55#where-the-button-is) says how to go live without the card, and [Tell whether you are live or in simulation](@87) has the other clues.
Check that you are live

3. **Look for a problem item.** On the **Change Log** tab, an ongoing problem sits above every run, headed "Prices not reaching Cloudbeds" (or "Prices not reaching Think Reservations"), with the cause and what to do. [When your property system does not accept a price](@57) explains each. For a price you typed, the line under the price box on the calendar says the same for that one night: "Sent to Cloudbeds.", the real count of tries left, or "This price couldn't be sent to Cloudbeds." once MAYA has stopped retrying it, with **Try again** and either **See the error log** or the cause written under it. [Setting a price yourself](@50#what-the-line-says-afterwards) has the lines.
Look for a problem item

4. **Check the connection.** Open the **PMS** tab and read the **Connection** card. Error or Disconnected means your system stopped accepting MAYA's connection, and nothing is read from it or sent to it while that lasts. Disconnected lasts until a General Manager or Hotel Admin reconnects. On Error MAYA keeps trying, and the card goes back to Connected by itself once a try works. If it has not cleared within a couple of hours, reconnect. Do not wait for the amber banner at the top of the dashboard, "MAYA has lost its connection to Cloudbeds": it shows only once the connection is marked as lost, and some breaks never are. [Connection lost](@101) explains each status, and what an old **Last sync** means.
Check the connection

5. **Check the subscription.** A red banner reading "MAYA has paused work on this property" means your rules no longer run on a schedule and nothing is sent to your PMS until the subscription is running again. Read [Account and billing problems](@103).

**Cloudbeds:** MAYA writes one nightly rate per room type to that room type's base rate: the rate plan that does not follow another plan and has no public name. Cloudbeds takes the write as a job, and MAYA asks Cloudbeds whether the job applied. Packages and derived plans are never written; derived plans follow the base rate by Cloudbeds' own rules.
Check the subscription

**Mews:** Nothing is sent to Mews, live or not. MAYA reads Mews bookings and shows prices on the calendar and in the change log. The go-live dialog says so: "MAYA doesn't send rates to Mews yet, so nothing is sent. The hotel only shows as live." A manual price saved on a Mews property is not sent either, whatever the confirmation says.

Five reasons, most common first.

- **It has not gone yet.** A price changed in the last few minutes goes on the next cycle. The first send to a night waits for a fresh read of your rates.
It has not gone yet
- **You are simulating.** Prices are worked out and shown, and never sent. See the check above.
You are simulating
- **A problem is holding it.** Look for "Prices not reaching Cloudbeds" at the top of the change log. The item says what is wrong and what to do.
A problem is holding it

- **Cloudbeds took it and never finished.** Cloudbeds applies a rate write as a job. If a job is still unfinished 45 minutes later, MAYA treats it as not applied and sends the night again. You are told only if it keeps happening.
Cloudbeds took it and never finished
- **ThinkReservations applies it later.** ThinkReservations accepts a write and applies it afterwards. MAYA confirms it on the next hourly read.
ThinkReservations applies it later

MAYA writes one rate per room type and no other: the base rate in Cloudbeds, the Best Available rate type in ThinkReservations. Your non-refundable rate, like every other plan, moves only by your system's own rules. MAYA never writes to it.

Check three things in your system.

1. **The base rate itself.** Open the night. If the base rate still shows the old price, the new one has not landed yet. Read [the five reasons above](#maya-shows-a-new-price-but-cloudbeds-still-has-the-old-one).
The base rate itself

2. **Whether the non-refundable rate follows the base.** A plan set to follow another is what both systems call derived. Only a derived plan moves when the rate it follows moves. A plan with prices of its own stays where you set it, whatever MAYA sends.
Whether the non-refundable rate follows the base

3. **What it follows, and by how much.** A derived plan follows one rate, by the amount set in its own settings. If it follows a different plan, or the amount is not what you expect, change that in your system.

At The Harbour Inn, "Non-refundable" follows Standard Rate at 10% off. On Fri, Nov 13 2026, "Busy nights" raises Standard from $150 to $165, and MAYA sends $165 to Standard Rate. Cloudbeds moves Non-refundable from $135 to $148.50 on its own. MAYA wrote only the $165.

To make your non-refundable rate move with MAYA's price, set it in your system to follow the rate MAYA writes to. Your system then works it out from each new base rate.
What it follows, and by how much

**ThinkReservations:** ThinkReservations marks each rate type as standard or derived. A non-refundable rate type can be standard, with prices of its own. MAYA never writes to it, so it does not move with Best Available. A derived one moves once ThinkReservations has applied the new price to the rate type it follows. Check that it follows the rate type MAYA writes to, which the ThinkReservations tab near the top of this page describes.

**Mews:** Nothing is sent to Mews, so no rate moves there, base or derived.

On a live property, a rate you change in your system is kept as a manual price when all of these hold: the night is one MAYA had already sent to, MAYA's send there was confirmed, the send is at least 60 minutes old, and your rate differs from MAYA's price by more than rounding. The day card then reads "Changed in Cloudbeds · $180.00", rules that had already moved the night are paused, and MAYA does not write over it. Read [Rates changed in your property system](@51).

Your change was written over for one of these reasons:

- **Within the hour.** You changed it less than 60 minutes after MAYA's send. MAYA reads your rates about once an hour, and again before re-sending a night it last sent to over an hour ago, so a change made inside that hour can be written over when MAYA's own price for the night changes.
Within the hour

- **A night MAYA had never sent to.** Your rate there is read as the night's starting point, not as a manual price. Your rules work from it, and MAYA sends the result. This is also what happens to every rate you change while simulating.
A night MAYA had never sent to

- **A ThinkReservations night MAYA had not read back yet.** A send to ThinkReservations counts as confirmed only once MAYA's hourly read finds it. Until then a different rate there is not read as your change.
A ThinkReservations night MAYA had not read back yet

- **Nearly every night differs by the same ratio.** When 80% or more of the nights MAYA sent to (10 at least) differ from MAYA's price by one shared ratio (a system reporting prices with tax included, or a markup), MAYA reads that as your system's own arithmetic, not as edits, and keeps sending its own prices.

**Good to know: Change prices in MAYA when you can** · A price typed on the **Calendar** tab is sent now, shows who set it, and pauses the rules already on that night at once. A change made in your system is picked up within the hour, and only on nights MAYA has already sent to.
Nearly every night differs by the same ratio

A night whose rate is 0 in your system, with no price typed in MAYA, is left unpriced. MAYA never opens a closed night at the floor.

The timing matters. MAYA reads your rates about once an hour and when your property's date changes. A night you close after MAYA has sent to it is read within the hour: its starting price becomes 0, the night is left unpriced, and any manual price on it is cleared. Between your change and that read, MAYA's price may still be there. A night closed before MAYA ever sent to it is left unpriced from the first run.

MAYA does not send a price of 0 to any property system. A manual price of 0 is a comp night: no rule raises it, and the save confirmation says "Saved. MAYA doesn't send a price of 0 to Cloudbeds, so set the night to 0 there yourself." The change log carries an item that says the same until your system has the night at 0. Set it there yourself. Read [Make a night free](@69).

A night your system has no rate for, and nobody has typed a price for in MAYA, is not priced and not sent, whatever its bookings paid. The day card reads "No rate in Cloudbeds for this night yet". Load a rate for it in your system and it is priced and sent within the hour, or type a price in MAYA, which is sent as typed. Read [Nights your system has no rate for](@56#nights-your-system-has-no-rate-for).

MAYA prices and sends tonight and the next 395 nights, on your property's own calendar. A night 70 days out is not priced, refreshed or sent until it enters the window. A manual price you type further out is saved now and sent when the night enters the window, and the confirmation says so: "Saved. It will be sent when the date enters the 396-day push window."

A new price for tonight that never lands, while later nights go through, usually means your system and MAYA hold different time zones for your property. This one rarely shows in the change log. [The time zone case](@57#the-time-zone-case) has what to check.

**Not yet** · There is no per-night "sent" or "confirmed" mark on the calendar, and no email or notification for a sending problem. Problems live in the change log only. The one email is for a lost connection, once it has been down about an hour. To confirm a price landed, open the night in your system.

Sam sets a minimum of $120 on Deluxe in Cloudbeds. MAYA's floor for Deluxe is $110. On a slow Tuesday, "Last minute" cuts Deluxe from $140 to $119. The floor lets that through, and Cloudbeds refuses it. The change log shows at once: "Prices not reaching Cloudbeds", "Cloudbeds refused MAYA's price for Deluxe because it breaks a rate rule set in Cloudbeds, such as a minimum or maximum rate.", "1 night, 1 room type · Still happening", and "Check the rate limits for this room type in Cloudbeds."

Priya types $120 on that night on the **Calendar** tab, and it is sent. Cloudbeds takes it. The item then reads "Ended" with the time, because a new price replaced the refused one.

An amber banner reading "MAYA has lost its connection to Cloudbeds" means your system stopped accepting MAYA's connection: a General Manager or Hotel Admin presses **Reconnect Cloudbeds** and signs in at Cloudbeds again. When the **PMS** tab reads Degraded instead, MAYA is still reading and sending, and one calm line says "Your Cloudbeds connection needs a refresh soon. Prices are still updating." While the connection is down nothing is read, priced or sent, and the rates already in your system, your rules, history and settings stay as they are. Mews connects with keys rather than a login, so email us and we re-enter them with you. If the connection reads Error or Disconnected for about an hour, the General Managers and Hotel Admins get one email about it.

The banner shows when the connection reads Error or Disconnected. Here is what stops: reading bookings, running rules and sending prices, all of it. Disconnected stays that way until someone reconnects. Error does not have to: MAYA keeps trying on its own, about ten minutes after the first failed try and then every fifteen minutes. The first try that works turns the card back to Connected, and reading, pricing and sending carry on by themselves, including any prices that were held back. If your system goes on refusing, the card stays at Error until someone reconnects. What stays: the rates already in your system (MAYA reverts nothing), your rules, your history, your room type answers and your manual prices. A price you type meanwhile is saved, and the line under the price box tells the two apart: "Saved. It will be sent once you reconnect." on Disconnected, and "Saved.

What to do: a General Manager or Hotel Admin presses **Reconnect Cloudbeds** on the banner or on the **PMS** tab. It sends you to Cloudbeds to sign in and confirm, then back to MAYA. The banner text says the same: "Reconnecting takes one click and sends you to Cloudbeds to confirm. Your rules, history and settings are all untouched." Read [Reconnect your property system](@92).

After you reconnect, the next cycle reads your bookings again and sends any prices that were held back.

**Cloudbeds:** Cloudbeds tells MAYA when you uninstall or disable the app, usually within seconds. Otherwise MAYA reads the refusal on its next call, within about five minutes. Either way the banner appears, and nothing is read, priced or sent until someone reconnects. You can also reconnect from the Cloudbeds Marketplace by pressing **Connect App** again.

**ThinkReservations:** ThinkReservations does not tell MAYA when access is revoked. MAYA finds out when its calls fail, and shows the banner once the connection's status changes. Until then the **PMS** tab may still read "Connected" while **Last sync** falls behind. A refused rate write does not disconnect ThinkReservations; it appears in the change log as a permission problem instead.

**Mews:** Mews connects with keys rather than a login, and we enter them for you. When Mews refuses MAYA's keys three reads in a row, about half an hour after the first refusal, the connection reads Error and everyone on the property sees "Mews needs its keys re-entered", with no button and the line "Ask us to re-enter the Mews keys: email [info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com)." A read that fails for another reason, such as Mews being down, leaves the status alone, so the **PMS** tab can keep reading "Connected" with no banner. **Health (last 24 hours)** reads "Not tracked for this system" on Mews, so then **Last sync** is the one sign. If **Last sync** on the **PMS** tab is more than an hour old, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Mews%20keys).

The **Connection** card on the **PMS** tab reads Degraded. The full line is "Your Cloudbeds connection needs a refresh soon. Prices are still updating.", and it means what it says: MAYA is still reading your bookings and, when you are live, sending prices. Nothing has stopped and nothing is lost.

It usually clears by itself on the next read. If it is still there in an hour, a General Manager or Hotel Admin clicks the quiet **Reconnect Cloudbeds** link at the end of the line and signs in with a login for this property only. It does no harm. Everyone else sees the line without the link.

Only a General Manager or Hotel Admin can reconnect Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations. Everyone else sees the same banner with "Ask this property's General Manager or Hotel Admin to reconnect it" and no button, so they can tell the right person. A reconnect link someone forwards does not get round this: it stops with "Reconnecting needs General Manager access or higher on this property." Read [Roles](@64).

Go back to the Cloudbeds Marketplace and press **Connect App** for MAYA again. For a property that started in the Marketplace, you land on MAYA's sign-in page with "Your Cloudbeds connection is active again. Sign in to pick up where you left off." Sign in, and the property is back on the schedule. For a property you connected from inside MAYA, sign in to MAYA first as its General Manager or Hotel Admin: **Connect App** then brings you to its **PMS** tab with "Reconnected." Anyone else sees "This property is already in MAYA, so nothing new was added." and nothing changes. Nothing was deleted by the uninstall. The **Reconnect Cloudbeds** button in MAYA works too.

Reading still works, so no connection banner appears. Instead the change log shows "Prices not reaching Cloudbeds" with "Cloudbeds won't let MAYA change Deluxe rates because MAYA doesn't have permission to update rates" and the action "Give MAYA permission to update rates in Cloudbeds, then reconnect on the PMS tab." Restore the permission in your system, then press **Reconnect Cloudbeds** on the **PMS** tab. Held prices go out on the next cycle. Read [Prices are not reaching your property system](@100).

When Cloudbeds answers with its wording for an app that is no longer connected, MAYA marks the connection disconnected at once and shows the banner. A change to your Cloudbeds subscription or apps can cause that. Reconnect as above. If a change to your Cloudbeds login stops the connection, the same banner appears and **Reconnect Cloudbeds** fixes it.

One refused read does not disconnect you. When Cloudbeds refuses a read, MAYA renews its sign-in and asks once more, and carries on if that works. The connection is marked disconnected only when Cloudbeds refuses the renewed sign-in too, or when the sign-in could not be renewed and three reads in a row were refused. An error page that does not come from Cloudbeds itself, such as a security filter in front of it, counts as Cloudbeds being down: that read fails, MAYA tries again later, and the connection stays Connected.

MAYA shows the banner and the **Reconnect Think Reservations** button when the connection stops working and its status changes. Because ThinkReservations does not tell MAYA, that can lag: MAYA's reads fail first and are retried with a growing gap of up to an hour, and the banner follows once the status is marked. If **Last sync** on the **PMS** tab is hours old and no banner shows, press **Reconnect Think Reservations** there anyway, with a login for this hotel only. It is harmless on a working connection.

Mews uses keys rather than a sign-in, and only we can enter them. The banner has no button, and everyone on the property sees the same words, whatever their role: "Ask us to re-enter the Mews keys: email [info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com)." Click the address, or [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Mews%20keys), and it takes a couple of minutes together.

This banner shows once Mews has refused MAYA's keys three reads in a row, and after we remove the keys. For about the first half hour after the keys stop working, and whenever reads fail for another reason, no banner appears and the **PMS** tab can keep reading "Connected". Watch **Last sync** on the **PMS** tab then. If it is more than an hour old, email us.

The **Connection** card on the **PMS** tab shows one of these.

| Status | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Connected | Healthy. Bookings are read every cycle. | Nothing. |
| Pending | Connected but not yet paid for. Nothing is read or priced until the subscription starts. | Finish setting up payment. |

| Error | Your system rejected MAYA's saved sign-in (on Mews, refused MAYA's keys three reads in a row), or, on Cloudbeds, reads have failed for about an hour for any other reason, such as Cloudbeds not answering. Nothing is read, priced or sent while it lasts. MAYA keeps trying every fifteen minutes or so, and the card goes back to Connected by itself once a try works. | If it has not cleared within a couple of hours, press **Reconnect** (on Mews, email us). Reconnecting sooner does no harm. |
| Disconnected | The connection is gone. The property is off the schedule. | Press **Reconnect**. |
| unknown | MAYA has no status on file. | Open the tab again in a moment, then reconnect if it stays. |

The banner appears for Error and Disconnected. Degraded shows the calm line instead. A Mews connection never reads Degraded. It reads Error once Mews has refused MAYA's keys three reads in a row, and keeps reading Connected while reads fail for any other reason, so on Mews watch **Last sync** too. A Cloudbeds connection reads Error after about an hour of failed reads of any kind, and our team is alerted after three failed reads in a row or half an hour without a good one.

Yes, once the connection has read Error or Disconnected for about an hour. Every General Manager and Hotel Admin on the property gets one email, headed "MAYA has lost its connection to Cloudbeds" (or your system), saying when it went down, what happened, what it means for your prices and how to reconnect. Its button, **Open the PMS tab**, opens the tab where you reconnect. On Mews, reply to it and we arrange new keys with you.

One email per outage. There is none for Degraded, for a break that leaves the card at Connected, for a property whose subscription has stopped, or when we remove Mews keys at your request. If you have reconnected since it was sent, the **PMS** tab shows the connection as it is now. Read [emails MAYA sends](@63#the-connection-down-email).

**Last sync** is the last time bookings were read successfully. On a healthy connection it is a few minutes old. After a failed read MAYA waits longer before each retry, doubling each time up to an hour, so a system that is down for a while leaves **Last sync** up to an hour behind before it catches up. A disconnected property stops reading altogether until someone reconnects. A paused subscription stops it too.

**Health (last 24 hours)** counts MAYA's requests to your system over the last day: "Healthy" when 98% or more succeeded, "Degraded" from 80%, "Having trouble" below that, with the figure beside it, for example "76% of 412 requests OK". "Having trouble" usually means your system was down or refusing for part of the day. If the connection card reads Connected and **Last sync** is recent, the trouble has passed. If not, reconnect.

"No recent activity" means no requests were recorded in the last 24 hours. On ThinkReservations and Mews the card reads "Not tracked for this system" instead, because MAYA keeps a log of its requests to Cloudbeds only. Read [Calendar and change log questions](@102).

The banner shows only while the connection itself is marked as lost. When Cloudbeds refuses to let MAYA change rates, reading still works and the connection stays Connected, so the change log's line is the only prompt. MAYA reads the connection when the dashboard opens, when you switch property and when you open the **PMS** tab, so a connection that broke while the page was open shows once you reload or open that tab. Open the **PMS** tab: a General Manager or Hotel Admin always finds **Reconnect Cloudbeds** there.

A successful reconnect brings you back to the dashboard's **PMS** tab, on the property you reconnected, with a short note: "Reconnected." Close it with the ×. The banner stops showing once the connection reads Connected, and a few minutes later **Last sync** shows a fresh time.

If you land on a page with a sentence instead, the reconnect did not go through and nothing changed. The sentence says why, for example "This login is for a different property.", "That sign-in link ran out after 15 minutes. Start again from MAYA." or "This reconnect link was started from a different account." (the link finishes only for the person who clicked **Reconnect**, signed in to MAYA). Read [Messages you might see, explained](@104).

A property on Cloudbeds must be reconnected with a Cloudbeds login that reaches the same Cloudbeds property, however it was first connected. The login you used reaches a different one, so the reconnect stopped before anything changed: the old connection is exactly as it was. A General Manager or Hotel Admin presses **Reconnect Cloudbeds** in MAYA again, then signs in at Cloudbeds with a login for this property. Any Cloudbeds login that can reach it works, a group login included, not only the one that first connected it. Three related messages: "Cloudbeds didn't answer. Try connecting again in a moment." (Cloudbeds was unreachable, so try again), "We couldn't check this login just now. Try connecting again in a moment." (try again) and "Reconnect this property from the Cloudbeds Marketplace." (use **Connect App** there).

**Careful: On ThinkReservations, reconnect with a login for this hotel only** · There is no screen for moving a MAYA property to a different property in your system. Cloudbeds reconnects check this for you. ThinkReservations reconnects do not: reconnecting with a login that reaches one other hotel moves MAYA onto it, and nothing on screen warns you. Always reconnect ThinkReservations with a login for this hotel only.

There is no disconnect button in MAYA. To disconnect, remove the app in Cloudbeds. Disconnecting does not cancel your subscription and deletes nothing.

Nothing is read, priced or sent. The rates already in your system stay exactly as they are. After you reconnect, the next cycle reads your bookings, prices again and sends what changed. Any price held back by a permission problem goes out then too.

The calendar colours compare each night's room revenue per room with your own other nights, so a busy night can be red, and every day is amber when there are fewer than 10 nights to compare. The calendar, the price box, the Rate Simulator and the sentences under each change use your currency's symbol. The bold line of each change in the change log shows $ whatever your currency. The change log holds the 10 most recent runs (roughly the last 50 minutes) and 40 changes per run, in your browser's time zone, and hides quiet runs unless you press **Show All Cycles**.

Colours need something to compare with. Each night's room revenue is divided by the property's room count to give revenue per room, and past nights are ranked against your other past nights, future nights against your other future nights. With fewer than 10 nights on a side, MAYA borrows both sides together, and with fewer than 10 in total there is no scale and every night is amber. A new property, or a property whose history is still importing, is amber until it has enough nights. The legend under the grid says "measured by revenue per room, relative to this property's own results".

Because the colour is revenue per room, not occupancy. A full night at low rates can earn less per room than a half-full night at high rates. Red is the bottom third of your nights, amber the middle third, green the top third, each side (past, future) ranked on its own. The colour tells you how the night's revenue ranks against your own nights, and nothing else.

The booked counts and revenue on the visible month are always fresh, but the ranking they are coloured against is kept for up to 5 minutes. A colour can lag a new booking by that long. The calendar also refreshes itself every 5 minutes on the **Calendar** tab and when you return to the browser tab.

In the change log, one line shows $ whatever your currency: the bold line of each change. So a property in euros sees "$150.00 up to $165.00" in a change's bold line and "€150.00" in the sentence under it, for the same price. The numbers are in your own currency. Only that symbol is off. Your currency comes from your property system when you connect and cannot be changed in the app.

**Not yet** · The change log's bold lines cannot show your currency's symbol yet, and the currency cannot be changed on a screen. If MAYA has the wrong currency for your property, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Currency).

The room type card's ADR (average daily rate: that night's room revenue divided by the rooms booked) needs at least one booking. When **Booked** reads 0 there is nothing to average, so the line reads "ADR –". Look at **Current price** for the price your rules have set.

The day detail reads "revenue on the books" for today and later, and "revenue" for past days. At properties in the Americas, today's heading can switch from "revenue on the books" to "revenue" in the evening. It is only a label and changes no price. Pricing always uses your property's own date.
The month grid has none. Click a day and its heading names the weekday: "Friday, November 13, 2026". The grid starts on Sunday.
Nights before your property's imported history have nothing to show. The year picker runs from the first month with a booking or a price to the last.

Pressing **Show All Cycles** adds the quiet lines, and a run happens about every five minutes whenever bookings were read. Each line counts a stretch of runs that changed nothing: "Prices checked 47 times from Sep 24, 10:05 AM to 1:55 PM, nothing needed to change." That is MAYA checking your rules and finding no reason to act. Press **Show Changes Only** to go back to the default view, which keeps only runs that changed something, sending problems and your answers.
- **Nothing has changed yet.** The default view hides the quiet lines. Press **Show All Cycles** to see them. A new property with rules that have not fired shows only quiet lines.
Nothing has changed yet
- **No run has happened yet.** A property that connected minutes ago runs its first cycle within about five minutes.
No run has happened yet
- **The subscription lapsed.** A red banner reads "MAYA has paused work on this property". No runs happen until it is fixed.
The subscription lapsed
- **Reads are failing.** A run whose booking read failed prices nothing and writes nothing. Check **Health (last 24 hours)** and **Last sync** on the **PMS** tab, and look for the connection banner.
Reads are failing

- **It could not load.** "Couldn't load your price history." with a **Try again** link means the page could not fetch the log. Press **Try again**.

Simulation is not a reason: while simulating, every run happens and is written down.
It could not load

The change log holds the 10 most recent runs that changed a price, with the quiet runs between them counted into lines. An older run drops off the bottom as new changes arrive, so on a busy day a change from this morning may already be gone.

A sending problem that is still going on stays at the top of the log until it ends, however long ago it started. Once it has ended, it shows only while it ended within the time those 10 runs cover. Your answers to the amber banner work the same way: each one shows only while it falls within that time.

For an older change, check the night's **Current price** and any **Manual** badge on the calendar, and [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Why%20did%20a%20price%20change) the night and room type. The detail behind every change is kept for 90 days, and we can read it for you.

A run lists its 40 biggest moves, largest percentage first. A run that changed more nights than that shows 40, then a line counting the rest, such as "And 23 more changes in this run." In a very large run the count can be a minimum: "And at least 23 more changes in this run." The rest are not listed anywhere in the app. To see where a night stands now, open it on the **Calendar** tab.

**Not yet** · There is no export, no search and no filter by night or room type in the change log, and no way to see runs older than the 10 shown. For a change older than those, email us the night and room type and we read it for you.

Under those changes the reading is background, not the reason the price moved. The sentence under the change names what moved it. The button shows how the night was booking at the time of that run.

The button is missing when that run took no booking speed reading for the night. That happens when none of the rules you have switched on uses booking speed, and on the occasional night no booking speed rule was checking in that run. A booking speed rule that measures only some room types leaves its reading on the room types it adjusts, and nowhere else.

Your browser's. "Pricing run · Fri, Sep 18, 2026, 3:05 PM PDT" is the time on your computer's clock, with its zone abbreviation. Hover the time for the exact moment, to the second, on the same clock. **Last sync** and the request times on the **PMS** tab use your clock too. Pricing itself works in your property's own time zone, and the "Updated 3:05:12 PM · live" time on the calendar is also your browser's clock.

The **Health (last 24 hours)** card and the **Recent requests** table are filled from a log of MAYA's requests, and MAYA keeps that log for Cloudbeds only. On a ThinkReservations or Mews property both read "Not tracked for this system", however healthy the connection is. Use **Connection** and **Last sync** on those properties instead.

The amber **Rules that keep adjusting** banner loads when the page opens and when you switch property, and not on a timer. A night you answered in another tab, or a night that has since passed, stays on screen until you reload the page.

The billing, connection and review banners load the same way: when the page opens and when you switch property. A banner for the property you left goes as soon as you switch. Reload the page to see a change made since.

If the switch fails, a short red line under the **Property** dropdown says so, such as "Couldn't switch to Sea View Inn. You're still on The Harbour Inn. Try again in a moment.", and the property you had stays open. Try again, and reload the page if it keeps failing. Only properties that are paid for and set up appear in the **Property** dropdown: a property you set aside with "Not now" is listed under **Properties not set up yet** on the billing page, where **Set up** brings it back.

Most sign-in and billing problems have a one-line fix, and the message on screen says what to do. A forgotten password is reset from **Forgot password?** on the sign-in page. A card check moves no money, so you were not charged twice. The billing page and the Team page need General Manager or Hotel Admin access, and a property that is not paid for never appears in the property dropdown.

The sign-in card shows "Invalid login credentials" when the email or password is wrong. Check the email address you signed up with and retype the password. Passwords are at least 8 characters.

If you have forgotten your password, click **Forgot password?** under the **Sign In** button, type your email and click **Send reset link**. If the address has an account, an email with a link to set a new password arrives. Read [Reset your password](@93).

**Not yet** · There is no way to change your email address inside the app, no two-factor sign-in and no Google or single sign-on.

You pressed **Create Account** with an address that already has a MAYA login. The card has switched to sign-in mode for you. Sign in with that address. If you do not know its password, click **Forgot password?** and a link to set one goes to that address.

You may be asked to confirm your address when you create an account. The card reads "Check your email" with "A confirmation link is on its way to" your address. Look in spam. For a Cloudbeds Marketplace arrival the property waits for you: "Your Cloudbeds property is saved and will be waiting." If nothing arrives after a few minutes, press **Back to sign in** and try to sign in. If that fails, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Confirmation%20email).
