Another MAYA account already owns that Cloudbeds property. Ask whoever set it up to invite you from the **Team** page. If you set it up yourself with a different email, sign in with that one.

They invite you. On the **Team** page they enter your email, pick your role and press **Send invitation**. You get an email with a link to set a password and join. If you have signed in to MAYA before, you are added at once with no email, and the property appears the next time you open MAYA. Read [Inviting and removing people](@65).
The page has been open long enough for your sign-in to lapse. Sign in again and retype the code.

The message under the field says why:

- "We don't recognize that code" (check it for typos): the code is not one we issued. Codes are letters, digits and dashes, 3 to 40 characters, and capitals do not matter.
- "That code has been turned off." or "That code has expired.": that code is no longer valid. Ask us for a current one.
- "That code has already been used the maximum number of times.": the same.
- "This property already used that code.": one redemption per property. Restarting a cancelled subscription cannot reuse the old code.
- "Too many code attempts. Wait a few minutes and try again.": 20 checks per person per 10 minutes.

Codes come from us. A property arriving from the Cloudbeds Marketplace needs none. Read [Codes and the free trial](@9).

Because a property attached to your account is connected but not paid for. A Cloudbeds Marketplace property is connected first and paid for second, so until payment is set up, signing in lands on the subscribe screen. Set up payment, or press "Not now" if it is one of several properties and you want to come back to it. Read [Setting up payment](@8).
Your account has no property that is set up and active yet. Onboarding is where you pay, connect and review. If a colleague has the property, ask them to invite you.

After Stripe confirms, MAYA usually takes you straight on. When confirmation is slow you see "Payment received" with "Setting up your account" and a moving bar. After 25 seconds it reads "Your payment went through, but our side is taking longer than usual to catch up." with a **Check again** button, and after 5 minutes it stops checking.

Your payment went through and you have not been charged twice. You can leave the page and sign in again later; the property is waiting. The screen also says we will email you when it is ready, and we do: once the payment is recorded, an email headed "Your account is ready" goes to the address you sign in with, and its button takes you to the next step. If the screen is still stuck an hour later and no email has come, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Payment%20received%20stuck).

No. MAYA checks your saved card twice with a zero-amount check that moves no money: once right after checkout, and again 48 hours after the subscription starts. Some banks briefly show a pending line that then disappears. It is never charged. The receipt for a real charge comes from Stripe.

Your card did not pass one of the two card checks: the one right after checkout or the one 48 hours later. Nothing has been charged and nothing has failed yet, but the next charge will. The billing page says when it was checked and the bank's short reason. Press **Update card, receipts & cancellation** to open Stripe and update the card. The warning clears by itself when a payment goes through. MAYA keeps working meanwhile. Read [Cards, payments and invoices](@61).

On every cycle MAYA adds up the rooms in your room types ticked as rooms. When that measured count is higher than the count you pay for, the banner appears, and an email with the same numbers goes to the address on your billing account. You have 7 days from that email to put it right. After the 7 days MAYA raises the count you pay for to the measured number, and the difference lands on your next invoice. Nothing is charged today and nothing is charged separately.

If the banner shows a count you do not have, check those settings on the rooms in ThinkReservations before the 7 days run out: the next cycle measures again. Typing your real count on the billing page does not clear the banner while the measured count is higher.

**Mews:** Where Mews gives no room count for a room category, that category gets one rooms-per-type number that we set for your whole property, 100 unless we change it. The measured count then adds that number once for each such category ticked as a room, so it can be far from the rooms you run.

[Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Mews%20room%20counts) your real room counts before you rely on this number. If the banner shows a count you do not have, email us straight away, before the 7 days run out. We can change that one number, not set a count for each category.

Typing your real count on the billing page does not clear the banner while the measured count is higher, and after the 7 days MAYA raises your count to the measured number. If that has already happened, [Your room count and what you pay](@60#if-the-100-rooms-number-has-already-raised-your-count) shows how to put it right. The same number sets your occupancy, so read [Occupancy looks wrong](@99) too.

The subscription is not paying. Nothing is read, priced or sent until it is. Three cases, and what the banner says after "Your rules no longer run on a schedule and nothing is sent to your PMS." tells them apart:

- "Update your card and the subscription restarts where it left off." The last payments failed and the bank's retries ran out. Press **Restart MAYA**, then **Update card, receipts & cancellation**, and save the new card as your default. MAYA pays the open invoice with it straight away and moves the subscription onto it, and the subscription restarts where it left off. If the status still reads "Unpaid" a few minutes later, the new card was declined too. Save a different card as your default, or [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Still%20unpaid).

- "Your subscription is on hold. Email us and we'll get it running again." The status reads "Paused": the subscription is on hold in Stripe. There is no restart button, because a second subscription beside it would bill you twice. The dashboard banner's button reads **Email us** and opens an email to us. Seats come with your room count: 2 seats for 1 to 20 rooms, 4 for 21 to 40, 5 for 41 to 60, 6 for 61 to 80, 8 for 81 to 500. Three common reasons.

- **They already use MAYA.** Someone who has signed in to MAYA before gets no email. They are added to the property at once, and the page says "Added." with "already uses MAYA and will see this property next time they sign in." Ask them to sign in. The property is in their **Property** dropdown.
They already use MAYA
- **Sending failed.** The page said "Could not send that invitation. Try again in a minute." and nobody was added. Send the invitation again. It goes out with a fresh link.
Sending failed

- **The link expired or went to spam.** Ask them to check their spam folder first. The invitation link works once and expires. There is no resend button, but as long as they have never signed in, you can click **Remove** beside their name and invite them again: a new email goes out with a fresh link, and the old link stops working. Or [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=New%20invitation%20link) with the address and we send a new link.
The link expired or went to spam
You cannot demote or remove the last Hotel Admin, or a property could end up with nobody able to manage its team or billing. Make someone else a Hotel Admin first, then change or remove the original.

MAYA uses a small set of words on screen and in these docs. Each is defined here in a few plain sentences, in alphabetical order, with a link to the page that explains it fully. A word marked (screen) is a label you will see in the app, written here exactly as it appears there.

**ADR** (screen: ADR $160.00). Average daily rate: a room type's room revenue for a night divided by the rooms of that type booked that night. It is on the room type cards in the calendar's day detail. With nothing booked it shows a dash: "ADR –". Read [The calendar](@46).

**Apply price adjustments** (screen). One of the two choices in the window that opens before a rule starts acting (switched on, added, or saved with changes while on): the rule changes the days the window showed from the next pricing run. Read [Turning a rule on, Apply or Skip](@41).
Apply price adjustments

**Base price.** The price a rule starts from on a night and room type. It is your typed price if you set one, else your own rate as read from your property system, else the newest booking's rate for that night, else the last base price MAYA recorded for that night. Read [How prices reach your property system](@56).
Base price

**Base rate** (screen, Cloudbeds). The one rate plan per room type that MAYA writes to in Cloudbeds: the plan that does not follow another plan and has no public name. Derived plans follow it by Cloudbeds' own rules. In ThinkReservations, the Best Available rate type. The change log also says "set the base rate" for a price someone typed. There it means the night's starting price. Read [What MAYA reads and writes](@15).
Base rate

**Best Available** (ThinkReservations). The standard rate type whose name contains "Best Available". It is the rate type MAYA sends its prices to in ThinkReservations. If no rate type has that name, MAYA uses the one standard rate type that covers the most room types. If two tie, neither is used and nothing is sent until you name one Best Available. Read [ThinkReservations](@13).
Best Available

**Booking.** For booking speed, one reservation for one night, however many rooms it holds: a 20-room wedding booked as one reservation in Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations is one booking. In Mews each room is its own reservation, so each room counts as a booking, and so does each separate reservation made from a group block. For sellable occupancy and pickup count, each room counts, so the same wedding is 20 booked rooms. Read [Booking speed](@34).
Booking

**Booking speed** (screen). How many bookings a night received in the past day, week or month, compared with how many similar past nights had received by the same point before arrival. Seven levels, from Stalled to Surging. Read [Booking speed](@34).
Booking speed

**Booking speed and pickup rules.** Any rule with a Booking speed or Pickup count condition. It fires, the change stays on the price, and after its wait it can fire again on the same night, so raises stack on raises and cuts on cuts. At most one of them fires on a night and room type per run. Read [How rules run](@39).
Booking speed and pickup rules
**Booking window** (screen: Booking window (days to stay)). The number of days until the stay, on your property's own calendar. Tonight is 0, tomorrow night is 1. Read [Booking window](@33).
Booking window

**Ceiling** (screen). The highest price MAYA will publish for a room type. Setup fills it from your answer to the five questions where it fits, or else from your own rates if the room type has at least 200 room nights sold. Otherwise it stays at $99,999.99 (a number in your own currency), which stops nothing in most currencies, until you set one. Where rooms sell above 99,999.99, as they can in yen or rupiah, the default ceiling holds prices down, so set one before you go live. Read [Floors and ceilings](@28).
Ceiling

**Change Log** (screen). The tab that shows the 10 most recent pricing runs and, for each change, which rule acted and why. A run happens about every five minutes and quiet runs count toward the 10, so it covers about the last 50 minutes. By default it lists only the runs among them that changed a price. Read [The change log](@47).
Change Log

**Changed in Cloudbeds** (screen: Changed in Cloudbeds · $123.00). The badge on a room type card for a rate you changed in your property system on a night MAYA had already sent to. MAYA keeps it like a manual price. Read [Rates changed in your property system](@51).
Changed in Cloudbeds
**Closed period.** A stretch when the whole property was shut, confirmed on the setup review. Its nights are left out of every comparison. Read [Checking what MAYA found](@26).
Closed period

**Code.** A signup code we give you that opens self-serve signup for a property system, or grants a trial or a discount. One code per property. A code's own free days replace the Marketplace trial rather than adding to it, while a discount code with no free days keeps the trial and discounts the invoices after it. Read [Codes and the free trial](@9).
Code
**Comp night.** A night with a manual price of 0. No rule raises it. MAYA does not send 0 to any property system, so you set it there yourself. Read [Make a night free](@69).
Comp night

**Connected** (screen, on the PMS tab). The connection to your property system is working: MAYA reads your bookings and, once you are live, sends prices. The other words the **Connection** card can show are Pending, Degraded, Error and Disconnected, each defined here. Read [The PMS tab](@53).
Connected

**Counts as a room** (screen). The checkbox on the PMS tab that says a room type is somewhere guests sleep. Ticked types are what MAYA divides by for sellable occupancy, and what you are billed for. A type tagged "needs your answer" has not been ticked or unticked yet: it counts in occupancy but not in your bill until you answer. Read [Room types and rooms out of service](@52).
Counts as a room
**Current price** (screen). The price MAYA has worked out for a room type on a night, after rules and limits. It is what the calendar shows and what is sent. Read [The calendar](@46).
Current price

**Cycle.** One run of MAYA for your property, about every five minutes: read bookings, refresh your rates if due, run your rules on every night whose bookings changed or that a change of yours reaches (and on every night once a day, after midnight at your property) and, once you are live, send the prices that changed. For Mews, MAYA does not read rates or send prices yet. Cycles run on MAYA's side, day and night, whether or not anyone has MAYA open, and your own internet being down does not stop them. Only MAYA being unable to reach your property system's service does, or a stopped subscription. Read [How rules run](@39).
Cycle

**Degraded** (screen, on the PMS tab). Two meanings. On the **Connection** card (Cloudbeds and ThinkReservations only): MAYA is still reading and sending, and one calm line says "Your Cloudbeds connection needs a refresh soon. Prices are still updating." It usually clears by itself on the next read. If it is still there in an hour, a General Manager or Hotel Admin reconnects, which does no harm. On the **Health (last 24 hours)** card: 80% to under 98% of MAYA's requests to your system succeeded. Read [Reconnecting and disconnecting](@16).
Degraded

**Derived rate plan.** A rate plan in your property system that follows another plan by a rule of its own, such as 10% off the base rate. MAYA never writes to one. It moves when the base rate moves, by your system's own rules. ThinkReservations calls it a derived rate type. Read [How prices reach your property system](@56).
Derived rate plan

**Disconnected** (screen, on the PMS tab). MAYA's access to your property system is gone: the app was uninstalled, its permission was removed, or your system refused it. Nothing is read or sent until a General Manager or Hotel Admin reconnects. Nothing is deleted. Read [Reconnecting and disconnecting](@16).
Disconnected

**Error** (screen, on the PMS tab). Your property system refused MAYA's saved access, so reading has stopped for now. MAYA keeps trying, up to an hour between tries, and the card goes back to Connected by itself once a try works. If it does not clear, a General Manager or Hotel Admin reconnects. Read [Connection lost](@101).
Error

**Fired** (screen). The number of times a rule acted, counted once per night and room type, including changes that later came off. A booking speed or pickup rule can act on the same night more than once. Read [The rule builder](@31).
Fired

**Floor** (screen). The lowest price MAYA will publish for a room type. Setup fills it from your answer to the five questions, or else from your own rates if the room type has at least 30 room nights sold. Otherwise it stays at $1.00, which stops nothing, until you set one (a floor cannot be 0). Read [Floors and ceilings](@28).
Floor
**General Manager** (screen, a role). Everything except managing Hotel Admins: pricing, going live, the property system connection, billing and the team. Read [Roles](@64).
General Manager

**Go live.** Switching a property from simulation to live, so its changed prices are sent to Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations every cycle (nothing is sent to Mews yet). A General Manager or Hotel Admin does it with **Turn them on for real**, in the starter rules box on the review screen. The box is there only if setup added starter rules, and it stays after someone uses **Get suggestions from my data** on the **Rules** tab. Without it, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Go%20live) and we switch the property live. One way in the app: only we can switch a property back. Read [Going live](@55).
Go live
**Guardrails** (screen, in the Rate Simulator). A room type's floor and ceiling, shown together as a range.
Guardrails

**Hold My Hand / Let Me Drive** (screen). The two setup paths. **Hold My Hand** asks five optional questions and walks you through the review. **Let Me Drive** goes straight to the dashboard, and the review stays available. Read [Hold my hand or let me drive](@24).
Hold My Hand / Let Me Drive

**Holiday.** One of 17 US holidays MAYA uses to pick similar nights: a night near Thanksgiving is compared with the same position around Thanksgiving in earlier years. No other holidays exist yet. Read [Time, weekends, currency and holidays](@106).
Holiday
**Hotel Admin** (screen, a role). Everything, including managing General Managers. The person who creates the account and pays is a property's first Hotel Admin. Read [Roles](@64).
Hotel Admin

**Hotel day.** A calendar date in your property's own time zone. The window, booking windows, "past week", pickup count lookbacks and rule waits all count in hotel days. Read [Time, weekends, currency and holidays](@106).
Hotel day

**Last sync** (screen, on the PMS tab). The last time MAYA read your bookings from your property system successfully, about every five minutes on a healthy connection. It says nothing about sending prices. Read [The PMS tab](@53).
Last sync
**Level.** One of the seven booking speed readings: Stalled, Much Slower Than Normal, Slower Than Normal, Normal, Faster Than Normal, Much Faster Than Normal, Surging. Read [Booking speed](@34).
Level

**Live.** The state after going live. Every cycle, prices that changed are sent to Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations. Nothing is sent to Mews yet, so a Mews property only shows as live. Read [Simulation mode](@54).
Live

**Manual price** (screen: Manual · $123.00). A price you typed for a room type on a night on the Calendar tab. It becomes the night's base price. Once you are live, it is sent as typed to Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations (a night beyond the 396-night window goes when it enters the window). Nothing is sent to Mews yet, and a price of 0 is never sent. Rules already on that night pause for that room type, and rules that fire later stack on top. Read [Setting a price yourself](@50).
Manual price

**Marketplace.** The Cloudbeds Marketplace, where a Cloudbeds property installs MAYA with **Connect App**. Properties that arrive this way get the free trial and can come in as a group. Read [Cloudbeds](@12).
Marketplace

**Measure / Change** (screen). The two room type lists of a rule that watches one set of room types and prices another, shown when **Change prices on different room types** is ticked. Read [Measure one set, change another](@38).
Measure / Change
**Measured over** (screen). The booking speed window: **Past day**, **Past week** or **Past month**, counted in booking dates on your property's calendar, today included. Read [Booking speed](@34).
Measured over

**Momentum** (in explanations). The fallback reading when a night has no similar past nights: how nearby dates are filling now compared with the same dates a year earlier. Always treated as thin evidence. Read [Similar nights](@36).
Momentum
**Not a fair comparison?** (screen). The link on a compared night that lets you set it aside with a reason. Read [Not a fair comparison](@49).
Not a fair comparison?

**Package.** A rate plan that sells the room together with something else, such as breakfast or parking. MAYA never writes to a package. A package built on the base rate moves when the base rate does, by your system's own rules. Read [What MAYA reads and writes](@15).
Package

**Paused.** A word with four meanings, so these docs keep them apart. A rule you set to **Off** on the **Rules** tab is "switched off": it stops acting and its changes stay on the price (the switch says On and Off, and the list's filter says Enabled and Disabled). Rules on a night where you typed a price are "held": their changes come off that night, and the save's confirmation counts them, as in "Paused 2 rules on this night for this room". "MAYA has paused work on this property" is the banner shown while the subscription is not active, and "Paused" as a status on the Billing page means the subscription is on hold in Stripe. Read [Turning a rule off, deleting it, or changing it](@42), [Setting a price yourself](@50) and [The billing page](@59).
Paused
**Pending** (screen, on the PMS tab). Connected but not paid for yet, or set up and not switched on yet. Nothing runs until then. Finish payment, or wait for us. Read [The PMS tab](@53).
Pending

**Pickup count** (screen: Pickup count (advanced)). How many room nights, or how much revenue, a night gained over 1, 3 or 7 whole days at your property, cancellations subtracted: today so far and the days before it, or for a rule that looks for low pickup, the full days up to yesterday. Read [Pickup count](@37).
Pickup count
**PMS** (screen). Your property management system: Cloudbeds, ThinkReservations or Mews, where your bookings and rates live. In these docs, "property system". Read [Which systems work](@11).
PMS
**Price and rate.** In these docs, a price is what MAYA works out and sends. A rate is what lives in your property system, such as your base rate or a rate you changed there.
Price and rate
**Pricing run** (screen). One evaluation of every night and every rule for your property. The change log shows the 10 most recent, one entry per run. Read [The change log](@47).
Pricing run

**Rate Simulator** (screen). The tab where you make up a night and see what your rules would do to it. Nothing there is saved or sent unless you click **Save This Rule**, and a rule saved from there arrives switched Off. Read [The Rate Simulator](@44).
Rate Simulator

**Revenue Manager** (screen, a role). Day-to-day pricing: rules, typed prices, floors and ceilings, room types and rooms out of service, answering the Rules that keep adjusting banner, and setting dates aside. A Revenue Manager cannot go live, reconnect the property system, see billing or change the team. Read [Roles](@64).
Revenue Manager
**Revenue on the books** (screen). Room revenue from bookings already made for that night, shown on the calendar day card. Read [The calendar](@46).
Revenue on the books

**RevPAR** (screen). Revenue per available room: the whole property's room revenue for a night divided by the number of rooms in room types ticked **Counts as a room**. The calendar's colours rank your nights by it (the legend says "revenue per room"). Unticking a room type takes its rooms out of it. Read [The calendar](@46).
RevPAR
**Room count.** The number of rooms you are billed for. MAYA measures it from your property system every cycle, counting only room types ticked as rooms. Read [Your room count](@60).
Room count

**Room night.** One room for one night. A booking of 2 rooms for 3 nights is 6 room nights. Pickup count and the import's progress bar count room nights. For a single night, room nights are the rooms booked.
Room night

**Rooms out of service** (screen). Rooms you take off sale for a stretch, entered on the PMS tab. They come off the sellable count for those nights only. Nothing is sent to your system. Read [Room types and rooms out of service](@52).
Rooms out of service

**Rule.** One sentence you write once: when a night looks like this, change its price by that much. MAYA checks every rule on a night within about five minutes of its bookings changing, and on every night once a day. Read [Build your first rule](@30).
Rule
**Rules that keep adjusting** (screen). The amber banner that asks you what to do once three of a booking speed or pickup rule's changes are on the same night. Read [Rules that keep adjusting](@43).
Rules that keep adjusting

**Skip price adjustments** (screen). The other choice in that window: the rule is on, but the days the window showed keep their prices, each until the rule stops being true there and then becomes true again. Every other day works as with Apply, and a booking speed or pickup rule counts every booking on the books, the ones made before it included. Read [Turning a rule on, Apply or Skip](@41#skip-price-adjustments).
Skip price adjustments
**Season.** A stretch of your year that books differently, found from your own history and never set by hand. It only ever appears inside an explanation. Read [Similar nights](@36).
Season
**Seats.** How many people can be on a property's team, members plus pending invitations: 2, 4, 5, 6 or 8, following your room count. Read [Inviting and removing people](@65).
Seats

**Sellable occupancy** (screen). Rooms booked divided by rooms you can sell that night, counting only room types ticked as rooms, with rooms out of service taken off first. Twelve rooms, three out of service, eight booked: 89%. Read [Sellable occupancy](@32).
Sellable occupancy
**Set aside** (screen: Set this date aside). Marking a past night as not a fair comparison so it is left out of comparisons from the next run. Read [Not a fair comparison](@49).
Set aside

**Show the numbers** (screen). The link under a booking speed change in the change log. It opens the counts behind the change, the nights MAYA compared with, and the way to set one aside. Read [The numbers behind a change](@48).
Show the numbers

**Similar nights.** The up to eight past nights MAYA compares a night with, from the last three years: same weekday (or, near a holiday, the same position around it) and same time of year. When too few match, other nights of the same kind are added: weekend nights (Friday and Saturday) for a weekend night, the other weekday nights for a weekday night. A night near a holiday has at most three, one a year. Read [Similar nights](@36).
Similar nights
**Simulation mode.** The starting state of every property. Everything runs and is written to the change log, and nothing is sent to your property system. Read [Simulation mode](@54).
Simulation mode

**Standard rule** (screen, in the How rules behave panel). A rule with only occupancy and booking window conditions. It holds one change while its condition holds and takes it off when the condition stops. It never stacks on itself. Read [How rules run](@39).
Standard rule

**Starter rules.** The five booking speed rules MAYA adds at setup when your property has about two months of history and no rules yet: Slow-date rescue, Slow-date trim, Warm-date bump, Hot-week surge and Sudden-spike catcher. Every property gets the same settings, and each rule compares a night's bookings with your own similar past nights. Read [Your starter rules](@27).
Starter rules

**Stopped on N nights** (screen). The chip under a rule's switch that counts the nights still to come on which you told it to stop, with **Let it run again** beside it. Read [Rules that keep adjusting](@43).
Stopped on N nights

**Then waits** (screen: Then waits (advanced)). How long a booking speed or pickup rule leaves a night alone after acting on it: 1 day to 2 weeks. A booking speed row waits 1 week when unset, and a pickup count row waits its lookback window (**Same as the lookback window**) unless you choose another. A rule with both waits the longer of the two. Read [Booking speed](@34).
Then waits
**Three-times question.** Another name for the Rules that keep adjusting banner.
Three-times question

**Turn it on** (screen). The one button in that window, beside **Cancel**, when it reads "0 prices will be affected by this rule.": the rule is saved on and changes nothing now. For an edit to a rule that is on, the button reads **Save changes** and does the same. Read [Turning a rule on, Apply or Skip](@41#what-the-days-mean).
Turn it on

**Trial.** Free days before your first charge. Properties that arrive from the Cloudbeds Marketplace get a 7-day free trial at their first signup, never on a restart. A code can carry its own trial, which replaces the Marketplace one rather than adding to it, and also counts at the first signup only: a restart gets no trial of any kind. A card is taken and nothing is charged until the trial ends. Read [Codes and the free trial](@9).
Trial

**Usual number** (in explanations). What similar past nights had received over the same stretch of their own run-up, averaged with the highest and lowest dropped once there are five or more. It can be a fraction, such as 0.4. On screen it reads "nights like this one usually get about 5 bookings", or "almost no bookings" under 1, and is rounded to a whole number otherwise. Read [Similar nights](@36).
Usual number
**Viewer** (screen, a role). Can look at everything and change nothing. Read [Roles](@64).
Viewer

**Wait.** See Then waits. The wait is counted per rule, night and room type, from that night's last counted change, or from a price you typed if it came later, in whole days at your property: a 2-day wait from a change made any time on Monday is over as Wednesday begins.
Wait
**Weekend.** Friday and Saturday nights. Used when similar nights are chosen and seasons are read. Rules have no weekday control yet. Read [Time, weekends, currency and holidays](@106).
Weekend

**Window (396 nights).** Tonight and the next 395 nights on your property's calendar, about 13 months: the nights your rules price and, once you are live, the nights whose prices are sent to Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations. A price you type further ahead is sent when its night enters the window. Read [How prices reach your property system](@56).
Window (396 nights)
**Your corrections** (screen). The panel at the top of the change log that lists every date you have set aside, each with **Undo**. Read [Not a fair comparison](@49).
Your corrections

If you have used another revenue tool, these are the words you may be looking for, and what MAYA calls them.

**Comp set** (competitive set). Not used. MAYA reads no competitor rates and no data from other hotels, only your own bookings and rates. Read [What MAYA does](@0).
Comp set
**Lead time.** MAYA calls it the booking window: the number of days from today until the night. A rule uses it through the **Booking window (days to stay)** condition. Read [Booking window](@33).
Lead time

**Length of stay (LOS).** Not used by rules. There is no condition for how long a guest stays, and MAYA writes one nightly rate per room type. Keep length-of-stay prices and minimum stays in your property system. Read [What rules cannot do yet](@45).
Length of stay (LOS)

**Pace.** MAYA calls it booking speed: how many bookings a night received in the past day, week or month, compared with what similar past nights had received at the same point before arrival. Read [Booking speed](@34).
Pace

**STLY** (same time last year). There is no STLY report. The nearest thing is similar nights: each night is compared with similar past nights from the last three years, read at the same distance before arrival. When none can be found, momentum compares nearby nights now with the same nights a year ago. Read [Similar nights](@36).
STLY

**Yield rules.** MAYA calls them rules: one sentence you write once, such as "when a night is more than 80% full, raise every room type by 10%". If your property system has yield rules of its own that change the base rate, switch them off before you go live. Read [Build your first rule](@30).
Yield rules

MAYA works on your property's own calendar, using the time zone read from your system when you connected. Tonight is today's date there, and weekends are Friday and Saturday nights. The holidays MAYA uses are 17 US holidays, and any other can be set aside. Prices are in your property's currency, worked out to two decimal places, while billing is in US dollars.

MAYA counts days on your property's calendar. "Today" is the date at your property, in its time zone, at the moment MAYA checks. The docs call that a hotel day.

Everything that counts nights starts from it:
- **Tonight** is night 0 of the booking window, and tomorrow night is night 1. [Booking window](@33)
Tonight
- **The 396-night window** your rules price is tonight and the next 395 nights. Every night in it is priced again once a day, in the first cycles after midnight at your property. [How rules run](@39)
The 396-night window
- **A typed price** can be set from tonight onwards, never on a night that has passed. [Setting a price yourself](@50)
A typed price
- **Past day, past week and past month** in booking speed are counted in hotel days. [See how they are counted](#past-day-past-week-and-past-month).
Past day, past week and past month

- **Waits and pickup lookbacks** are counted in hotel days too. [See how](#waits-and-pickup-lookbacks-whole-days).

**Example: Midnight at The Harbour Inn**

The Harbour Inn is on US Pacific time. A check at 11 pm on Friday still treats Friday night as tonight, night 0. A check at 12:30 am on Saturday treats Saturday night as tonight and Friday as past, so Friday leaves the window and a price can no longer be typed for it.

An illustration with made-up numbers, not your property.
Waits and pickup lookbacks

MAYA reads your property's time zone once, when you connect, and keeps it.

**Cloudbeds:** The time zone set on your property in Cloudbeds.

**ThinkReservations:** The time zone set on your hotel in ThinkReservations.

**Mews:** MAYA does not read it from Mews. We set it with you when we connect the property.

If your system gave none, or it could not be read when you connected, MAYA uses universal time (UTC) until we set yours. The **PMS** tab shows the time zone MAYA has, under **Time zone and currency**, and says so in plain words when it is UTC. It cannot be changed from the app. [Email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Time%20zone) to change it. Changing it in your system later does not change it in MAYA.
- **Pricing** always uses your property's date.
Pricing

- **Times on screen** use your own browser's clock: the time of each run in the **Change Log** (with its zone, such as PDT), the "Updated" time on the calendar, and **Last sync** on the **PMS** tab. Two people in different places see different clock times for the same run.
Times on screen

- **One label** follows universal time (UTC): the day detail's "revenue on the books", which switches to "revenue" at midnight UTC. At a property in the Americas that happens in the evening. It changes no number. [Calendar and change log questions](@102)
One label

These are the choices under **Measured over** in a booking speed rule. They count booking dates, today included:

| Choice | Counts bookings dated |
|---|---|
| **Past day** | today only |
| **Past week** | today and the 6 days before it (7 dates) |
| **Past month** | today and the 29 days before it (30 dates) |

So **Past day** is not the last 24 hours. Shortly after midnight at your property it has almost nothing in it yet, and it fills up through the day. [Booking speed](@34)

**Booking dates.** A booking counts on the date it was made:

**Cloudbeds:** The creation date exactly as Cloudbeds records it. MAYA does not convert it to another time zone.

**ThinkReservations:** The moment ThinkReservations recorded the booking, put on your property's own calendar. An 11 pm booking in California is dated that day.

**Mews:** The moment Mews recorded the booking, put on your property's own calendar.

If a booking's date looks a day off from what your system shows, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Booking%20date) with the booking and we check it.

Both are counted in whole hotel days:

- **A rule's wait.** After a booking speed or pickup rule changes a night, it leaves that night alone for its wait: 1 day to 2 weeks, set in **Then waits (advanced)**. A pickup rule waits its lookback window unless you choose another. A wait of 2 days from a change made at any time on Monday is over as Wednesday begins at your property. [How rules run](@39)
A rule's wait

- **A pickup lookback.** A rule set to **Greater than** counts today so far and the days before it: 3 days is today, yesterday and the day before. A rule set to **Less than** counts the 3 full days up to yesterday. [Pickup count](@37)
A pickup lookback

Hotel days follow your property's local calendar, so the change to or from daylight saving time moves no night: tonight is still tonight. Waits and pickup lookbacks count hotel days too, so they still end at midnight at your property. The day of the change is 23 or 25 hours long, and nothing else moves.

Weekends are Friday and Saturday nights, and Sunday night counts as a weeknight. That is how MAYA reads them when it picks similar past nights: a Friday is compared with other Fridays and, if too few are found, with Saturdays, but never with a weeknight. (Near a holiday, nights are matched by their place around the holiday instead.) It is also how MAYA reads the weekly shape of your seasons. [Similar nights](@36)

Rules have no weekday setting: every rule runs every night. For a weekend price, type it on those nights. [What rules cannot do yet](@45)

MAYA uses 17 US holidays: New Year's Day, Martin Luther King Jr. Day, Valentine's Day, Presidents' Day, St. Patrick's Day, Easter, Mother's Day, Memorial Day, Father's Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day, Labor Day, Indigenous Peoples' Day, Halloween, Veterans Day, Thanksgiving and Christmas. Each has a stretch of days around it.

A holiday never changes a price by itself, and there is no holiday rule. It changes which past nights a night is compared with: the Saturday after Thanksgiving is compared with the Saturday after Thanksgiving in earlier years, not with the same date. [Similar nights](@36) has each holiday's stretch.
Seasons are stretches of your year that book differently, found from your own history, never set by hand. They only ever show inside an explanation under **Show the numbers**. [Similar nights](@36)

Your property's currency is read once, when you connect: from Cloudbeds or ThinkReservations, and set with you for Mews. If none could be read, MAYA uses US dollars until we set yours. MAYA never converts anything. Every price is a number in your own currency.

The symbol depends on the screen:

**The default floor and ceiling are numbers in your currency.** Every room type starts with a floor of 1.00 and a ceiling of 99,999.99, whatever the currency. In most currencies they stop nothing. Where a room type sells above 99,999.99 (yen, won, rupiah or dong, for example), the default ceiling holds its prices down to 99,999.99, and a price you type above it is refused, until a real ceiling is set. Set ceilings before you go live: through the five questions, a suggestion card, or by email. Read [Floors and ceilings](@28#when-your-rates-are-above-the-default-ceiling).
The default floor and ceiling are numbers in your currency

**Typing amounts.** The price box on the calendar and the amount and threshold boxes in the rule builder are your browser's number boxes. Type a point for decimals, as in 180.50, and no thousands separator, as in 1250. Whether a box also takes a comma (180,50) depends on your browser and its language. If it cannot read what you typed, the box counts as empty: **Save** stays greyed out, or the rule is not added, so nothing wrong is saved.
Typing amounts

MAYA works out every price to two decimal places, whatever the currency, and sends it that way. A price you type, a floor and a ceiling are rounded to two decimal places too. There is no setting to round to whole units.

For a currency with no cents, such as Japanese yen, that means a percentage rule can produce a price with decimals. MAYA sends that number as it is. If your system keeps whole units, it rounds the price its own way. When MAYA reads the rate back, a whole number less than 1 away from the price MAYA sent counts as MAYA's own price, rounded, and not as a rate you changed. So the rounding never turns into a manual price, and MAYA does not keep sending the price again.

To keep prices whole, set rules to change by a fixed amount rather than a percentage, and use whole numbers for floors, ceilings and typed prices. As long as your own rates are whole, prices then stay whole. The starter rules change prices by percentages, so they can produce decimals.

MAYA keeps the shape of each booking (dates, room type, rate, channel, party size as a count) and never guest names, emails, phone numbers, addresses or card details. **From your property system.** Your bookings: the nights, the room type, the nightly rate and the status. Your property system's answers can carry guest names, contact details and payment details. MAYA keeps only the fields on a short fixed list and drops everything else before anything is stored. A dropped field is never stored, shown or used. A new field your system adds later is dropped by default.

What is left does not identify a guest to us. You could link a booking number to a guest using your own records, though, so the Privacy Policy treats booking records as personal data wherever the law does.

If a guest asks about their data, they should contact your property first, since we hold no names or contact details and usually cannot tell who a booking belongs to. If a guest contacts us, we answer as the law requires and may ask you to help find the records (Privacy Policy section 1).

Modern Hospitality Solutions is based in the United States, and your data is processed on servers in the United States (Privacy Policy section 9). The database and its backups are on Amazon Web Services servers in Ohio (Privacy Policy section 8). There is no option to keep it in another country or region.

MAYA takes customers worldwide, including in the European Economic Area, the UK and Switzerland.

**Transfers to the United States.** When personal data protected by the GDPR, the UK GDPR or Swiss law comes to us, it is covered by the European Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses: the ready-made contract terms Europe provides for sending personal data abroad. MAYA uses Module One (for one controller passing data to another), with the UK Addendum and the Swiss amendments. They are built into the Terms (section 8.9), so you agree to them when you agree to the Terms. Nothing extra needs signing. You are the data exporter and we are the data importer. The Clauses are governed by Irish law.
Transfers to the United States

**A data processing agreement.** A data processing agreement is the contract a customer signs with a supplier that handles data only on the customer's instructions (a "processor"). We are not your processor. We handle booking data as an independent controller, as the next section explains, so the Terms do not include one. Unless we both sign a separate agreement that says otherwise, we are neither your processor nor a joint controller with you (Terms 8.5).

**Why we hold the data.** Account and billing information, to run our contract with you and meet tax rules. What needs our written consent first is a benchmark, performance or comparative test of MAYA, such as measuring its results against the other tool's (9). If you are not sure whether what you plan is a test, [email us](mailto:info@modern-hospitality-solutions.com?subject=Comparing%20MAYA) before you start. [Switching from another revenue tool](@1#switching-from-another-revenue-tool) explains how the two run side by side.

Write from the email address you sign in to MAYA with. We match it against your account, so an email from another address needs a second step. If you have more than one property, name the one you mean.

We aim to answer within one business day. That is an aim, not a guarantee. The Terms of Service (section 3.7) say support is given by email on a reasonable-efforts basis, with no set response time unless we have agreed one with you in a signed document.

Business days are Monday to Friday. We are based in Austin, Texas, so they run on US Central time, and weekends and US public holidays do not count towards the aim. An email sent on a Friday evening or a Saturday is usually answered the following Monday. There is no out-of-hours cover, and answers are in English, the language of MAYA and these docs. Your rules keep running the whole time: MAYA does not wait for us.

Most of what we need is already on your screen. The more of it you copy into your email, the fewer questions we send back.

| Anything | Your property's name and the property system it uses |
| A price | The night, the room type, the price you see and the change log entry: the bold line and the sentences under it |

Every page describes MAYA as it works today. We check each page against the app before it is published, and we change it when the app changes. Where MAYA cannot do something yet, the page says so plainly and says what to do instead. We do not promise dates.

The Harbour Inn has 20 rooms: 12 Standard, 6 Deluxe and 2 Suites, plus a meeting room that does not count as a room. It is on US Pacific time and prices in US dollars. Sam is its Hotel Admin and Priya its Revenue Manager. It is not a real hotel, and no example uses a real guest.

If you are signed in to MAYA in this browser, the names of places in MAYA on these pages open that place in a new tab, with a small arrow after the words. Some how-tos also show a button that opens MAYA with the rule, filter or choice from the page already filled in.

A link never saves or changes anything. You still click **Add Rule**, **Save This Rule** or **Send invitation** yourself, and MAYA still checks what your role allows. A link opens your active property. Signed out, you see the same words without links.

It works the other way too. **Help** at the top of MAYA's screens opens the page about the screen you are on, and **Learn more** in a "?" panel opens the passage that explains it in full.

The **Ask MAYA docs** button sits at the bottom right of every docs page, the docs home and the support page. On a phone, tap **Ask** in the bar at the top. It opens a panel with a box to type in. While the panel is empty, it offers a few common questions to start from.

To see how it works, open it and ask "Is there a status page?", then compare the answer with the page it links to.

The docs helper does not write anything. Every answer is a passage copied from these pages, word for word, or one of a few short replies written in advance for general questions such as "hi", "what can I ask?" or "can I talk to a person?". Ask "how does this work?" or "what is this page?" and it answers about the page you are on, with its In plain words box and its headings.

When you ask a question, it compares your words with:

- the words in every section of every page,
- the questions each page lists as the ones it answers,
- a list of words people use for the same thing, such as "price" and "rate", "undo" and "put back", or "wedding" and "group".

When the match is weak, it says so. It shows the closest section under "This might help", followed by "Not quite it? Send us your question." and a **Send** button, which works like the one below. When nothing matches, it shows no section, only the message below.

**Example: What an answer looks like**

Sam types "forgot my password". An answer looks like this. First, word for word, the In plain words box of [Reset your password](@93). Then a link to that page, and "Did this help?" with **Yes** and **No**.

The panel says "No clear answer in the docs.", links the pages that came closest (when any came close) and a few good places to start, and gives you two ways forward:

- **Send** sends your question to us so we can write the missing page. It carries no name or email address, so we cannot reply to it.
Send
- **The email link** opens an email to us with the subject "Docs question". Use it when you want an answer. We aim to reply within one business day.
The email link

Your question is matched inside your browser. Your words reach us only if you press a button that sends them. Each question asked is also counted, without its words.

| When you | What reaches us |
|---|---|
| Ask a question | A count, never your words: the kind of reply (a passage, a set reply, "This might help" or no answer), the part of the docs you were in, whether you were signed in to MAYA and, if **Help** in MAYA opened the docs, which screen it was on |
| Press **Yes** under "Did this help?" | Nothing |
| Press **No** under "Did this help?" | Nothing yet. A box opens for an optional note, with a **Send** button |
| Press **Send** | Your question, your note if you wrote one, the page you were on and which sections were shown |
| Press a button under "Was this page useful?" at the foot of a page | Which page it was and which button you pressed. No text |

Before anything you send is stored, email addresses, phone numbers and long runs of digits (such as a card number) are replaced with "[removed]". It is kept as text only, with no name, account, IP address or cookie attached. The only other thing noted is whether you were signed in to MAYA when you sent it. Treat that clean-up as a safety net, not a reason to type personal details. The count is stored with the day, not the time, and with no name, account, IP address or cookie.

Your conversation stays in the browser tab you asked it in, and is gone when you close the tab. Apart from that count of questions, these pages run no visitor counting, and they set no cookies of their own. The [Privacy Policy](https://www.get-maya.com/privacy) explains the rest.

The docs helper answers from these pages, not from your account, so it never needs:

- guest names, or anything about a guest,
- card numbers or bank details,
- passwords, yours or your property system's.

It has no access to your property. It has these pages and nothing else: not your prices, bookings, rules, bill or change log. Ask "why did Deluxe go up on November 13?" and it can only show you a page such as [Find out why a price changed](@66). Your property's own reasons are in the change log and behind the **Show the numbers** button.

It cannot do anything for you either. It cannot reset a password, switch a property back to simulation or change a setting. A password is reset from **Forgot password?** on the sign-in page. For the rest, [contact support](@111).
